```json
  "old_string": "    private func poster3DView(poster: ImageData, index: Int, size: CGSize) -> some View {\n        let rawOffset = CGFloat(index - currentIndex)\n        let dragItems = dragOffset / (size.width + posterSpacing)\n        let offset = rawOffset - dragItems\n        let absOffset = abs(offset)\n\n        let xTranslation = offset * (size.width * 0.55 + posterSpacing)\n        let scale: CGFloat = max(0.65, 1.0 - absOffset * 0.15)\n        let rotationY: Double = Double(offset) * -35\n        let opacity: Double = max(0.25, 1.0 - Double(absOffset) * 0.3)\n        let zIndex: Double = 100 - Double(absOffset)\n\n        let loader = ImageLoaderCache.shared.loaderFor(path: poster.file_path, size: .medium)\n        return BigMoviePosterImage(imageLoader: loader)\n            .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)\n            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10))\n            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.5), radius: 12, x: 0, y: 8)\n            .scaleEffect(scale)\n            .rotation3DEffect(\n                .degrees(rotationY),\n                axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0),\n                anchor: .center,\n                perspective: 0.6\n            )\n            .offset(x: xTranslation)\n            .opacity(opacity)\n            .zIndex(zIndex)\n            .onTapGesture { goTo(index) }\n    }",
  "new_string": "    private func poster3DView(poster: ImageData, index: Int, size: CGSize) -> some View {\n        let rawOffset = CGFloat(index - currentIndex)\n        let dragItems = dragOffset / (size.width + posterSpacing)\n        let offset = rawOffset - dragItems\n        let absOffset = abs(offset)\n\n        let xTranslation = offset * (size.width * 0.55 + posterSpacing)\n        let scale: CGFloat = max(0.65, 1.0 - absOffset * 0.15)\n        let rotationY: Double = Double(offset) * -35\n        let opacity: Double = max(0.25, 1.0 - Double(absOffset) * 0.3)\n        let zIndex: Double = 100 - Double(absOffset)\n\n        return CarouselImageView(path: poster.file_path, size: size)\n            .scaleEffect(scale)\n            .rotation3DEffect(\n                .degrees(rotationY),\n                axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0),\n                anchor: .center,\n                perspective: 0.6\n            )\n            .offset(x: xTranslation)\n            .opacity(opacity)\n            .zIndex(zIndex)\n            .onTapGesture { goTo(index) }\n    }"
```

```json
  "old_string": "#if os(macOS)\nimport AppKit\n#endif",
  "new_string": "#if os(macOS)\nimport AppKit\n#endif\n\n/// Renders a remote image at an arbitrary size without the fixed-aspect\n/// portrait framing BigMoviePosterImage bakes in. Used by the carousel\n/// so both posters (portrait) and backdrops (landscape) fill the size\n/// the carousel computes from each image's aspect ratio.\nstruct CarouselImageView: View {\n    let path: String\n    let size: CGSize\n\n    @StateObject private var loader: ImageLoader\n\n    init(path: String, size: CGSize) {\n        self.path = path\n        self.size = size\n        self._loader = StateObject(wrappedValue: ImageLoaderCache.shared.loaderFor(path: path, size: .medium))\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let data = loader.image {\n                DataImage(data: data, renderingMode: .original)\n                    .aspectRatio(contentMode: .fill)\n            } else {\n                Rectangle().foregroundColor(.gray)\n            }\n        }\n        .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)\n        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10))\n        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.5), radius: 12, x: 0, y: 8)\n    }\n}"
}
```

```
12	    /// The selected sidebar menu. When `UI_TEST_SELECT_MENU` is set in the
13	    /// environment (e.g. by XCUITest `launchEnvironment`), the initial selection
14	    /// is driven by that value — working around headless CI where `tap()` on
15	    /// SwiftUI `List(selection:)` rows does not reliably trigger the binding.
16	    @State private var selectedMenu: OutlineMenu? = initialMenu()

19	    var body: some View {
20	        NavigationSplitView {
21	            List(selection: $selectedMenu) {
22	                ForEach(OutlineMenu.allCases, id: \.self) { menu in
23	                    OutlineRow(item: menu, isSelected: selectedMenu == menu)
24	                        .frame(height: 50)
25	                        .tag(menu)
26	                        .contentShape(Rectangle())
27	                        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
28	                        .accessibilityIdentifier("sidebar.\(menu.title)")
29	                }
30	            }
31	            .listStyle(.sidebar)
32	            .navigationTitle("Movies")
33	            .frame(minWidth: 260, idealWidth: 300)
34	        } detail: {
35	            if let selectedMenu {
36	                selectedMenu.contentView(isRunningUISmokeTests: isRunningUISmokeTests)
37	                    .padding(.leading, selectedMenu == .settings ? 0 : 12)
38	            } else {
39	                Text("Select a section")
40	                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
41	            }
42	        }
43	        .navigationSplitViewStyle(.balanced)
44	        .focusedSceneValue(\.selectedOutlineMenu, $selectedMenu)
45	    }
46	
47	    private static func initialMenu() -> OutlineMenu {
48	        if let menuTitle = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["UI_TEST_SELECT_MENU"],

51	        }
52	        return .popular
```

```
221	                                                                    nextPage: nextPopularPage,
222	                                                                    popularLoading: props.popularLoading,
223	                                                                    popularInitialLoadCompleted: props.popularInitialLoadCompleted) else {
224	            return
225	        }

227	        props.dispatch(PeopleActions.FetchPopular(page: page))
228	    }

231	        guard let page = FanClubPaginationPolicy.nextPopularPage(popular: props.popular,
232	                                                                 lastTriggeredPopularId: lastTriggeredPopularId,
233	                                                                 nextPage: nextPopularPage) else {
234	            return
235	        }
236	        lastTriggeredPopularId = lastPopularId
237	        nextPopularPage += 1
238	        props.dispatch(PeopleActions.FetchPopular(page: page))
239	    }
```

```json
  "new_string": "enum GenresListState {\n    static func genres(from state: AppState) -> [Genre] {\n        state.moviesState.genres\n    }\n}\n\n/// Maps each TMDB genre to an SF Symbol + accent color so the Genres\n/// grid reads visually like the rest of the app (which leans on\n/// imagery) even though TMDB doesn't ship genre artwork.\nenum GenrePresentation {\n    static func iconName(for genre: Genre) -> String {\n        switch genre.name.lowercased() {\n        case \"action\":            return \"flame.fill\"\n        case \"adventure\":         return \"mountain.2.fill\"\n        case \"animation\":         return \"sparkles\"\n        case \"comedy\":            return \"face.smiling.inverse\"\n        case \"crime\":             return \"exclamationmark.shield.fill\"\n        case \"documentary\":       return \"doc.text.fill\"\n        case \"drama\":             return \"theatermasks.fill\"\n        case \"family\":            return \"figure.2.and.child.holdinghands\"\n        case \"fantasy\":           return \"wand.and.stars\"\n        case \"history\":           return \"book.closed.fill\"\n        case \"horror\":            return \"moon.stars.fill\"\n        case \"music\":             return \"music.note\"\n        case \"mystery\":           return \"magnifyingglass\"\n        case \"romance\":           return \"heart.fill\"\n        case \"science fiction\":   return \"star.square.fill\"\n        case \"tv movie\":          return \"tv.fill\"\n        case \"thriller\":          return \"bolt.fill\"\n        case \"war\":               return \"shield.lefthalf.filled\"\n        case \"western\":           return \"mappin.and.ellipse\"\n        default:                  return \"film.fill\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Two-color gradient per genre. Derived from genre.id so the\n    /// palette is stable between runs but feels varied across the grid.\n    static func gradient(for genre: Genre) -> LinearGradient {\n        let palette: [(Color, Color)] = [\n            (Color(red: 0.85, green: 0.26, blue: 0.32), Color(red: 0.55, green: 0.08, blue: 0.16)), // red\n            (Color(red: 0.95, green: 0.58, blue: 0.21), Color(red: 0.66, green: 0.32, blue: 0.04)), // orange\n            (Color(red: 0.97, green: 0.78, blue: 0.26), Color(red: 0.72, green: 0.47, blue: 0.08)), // gold\n            (Color(red: 0.35, green: 0.65, blue: 0.42), Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.37, blue: 0.21)), // green\n            (Color(red: 0.26, green: 0.55, blue: 0.82), Color(red: 0.09, green: 0.27, blue: 0.52)), // blue\n            (Color(red: 0.48, green: 0.34, blue: 0.74), Color(red: 0.25, green: 0.13, blue: 0.48)), // violet\n            (Color(red: 0.79, green: 0.36, blue: 0.66), Color(red: 0.49, green: 0.12, blue: 0.39)), // magenta\n            (Color(red: 0.35, green: 0.45, blue: 0.52), Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.21, blue: 0.28)), // slate\n        ]\n        let pair = palette[abs(genre.id) % palette.count]\n        return LinearGradient(colors: [pair.0, pair.1],\n                              startPoint: .topLeading,\n                              endPoint: .bottomTrailing)\n    }\n}\n\n#if os(macOS)\nprivate struct GenreCard: View {\n    let genre: Genre\n    let isHighlighted: Bool\n\n    var body: some View {\n        ZStack {\n            GenrePresentation.gradient(for: genre)\n            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {\n                Image(systemName: GenrePresentation.iconName(for: genre))\n                    .font(.system(size: 32, weight: .semibold))\n                    .foregroundColor(.white)\n                Spacer(minLength: 0)\n                Text(genre.name)\n                    .font(.title3)\n                    .fontWeight(.semibold)\n                    .foregroundColor(.white)\n                    .lineLimit(2)\n                    .multilineTextAlignment(.leading)\n            }\n            .padding(16)\n            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, Color.white.opacity(0.9) : Color.white.opacity(0.08),\n                        lineWidth: isHighlighted ? 3 : 1)\n        )\n        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isHighlighted ? 0.35 : 0.2),\n                radius: isHighlighted ? 12 : 6,\n                y: isHighlighted ? 6 : 3)\n        .scaleEffect(isHighlighted ? 1.02 : 1.0)\n        .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.15), value: isHighlighted)\n    }\n}\n#endif"
```

Build succeeded. The Genres view now shows a **2-column grid of colored cards**:

- Each card has a **gradient background** picked from a stable palette (red, orange, gold, green, blue, violet, magenta, slate) keyed off `genre.id`, so each genre gets the same color every launch

- **Genre name** in bold at the bottom-left
- **White outline** highlight when keyboard-focused + slight scale, shadow bump
- Unknown genres fall back to `film.fill`

**Arrow navigation now 2D**:
- Left / Right → adjacent card
- Up / Down → skip `columnCount` (moves between rows)
- Return / Space → push `MoviesGenreList`

```
169	        guard let action = DiscoverSwipeActionPlan.action(for: decision,
170	                                                          currentMovieId: props.currentMovie?.id) else {
171	            return
172	        }
173	        let currentMovieId: Int
174	        switch action {
175	        case let .wishlist(movieId):
176	            currentMovieId = movieId
177	            props.dispatch(MoviesActions.AddToWishlist(movie: movieId))
178	        case let .seenlist(movieId):
179	            currentMovieId = movieId
180	            props.dispatch(MoviesActions.AddToSeenList(movie: movieId))
181	        }
182	        previousMovie = currentMovieId
183	        #if os(iOS)
184	        hapticFeedback.impactOccurred(intensity: 0.8)
185	        #endif
186	        props.dispatch(MoviesActions.PopRandromDiscover())
187	        willEndPosition = nil
188	        fetchRandomMovies(props: props, force: false, filter: props.filter)
189	    }
190	    
191	    private func fetchRandomMovies(props: Props, force: Bool, filter: DiscoverFilter?) {
192	        if DiscoverFetchPolicy.shouldFetchRandomMovies(currentMovieCount: props.movies.count,
193	                                                       force: force,
194	                                                       isRunningUISmokeTests: isRunningUISmokeTests) {
195	            props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchRandomDiscover(filter: filter))
196	        }
197	    }
```

Build succeeded. The Discover view now:

**Visual — card deck**:
- ZStack of up to 4 poster cards, each slightly scaled down (0.04 per layer) and offset down (6pt per layer), with progressively weaker shadows — reads as a stack
- Clicking the top card opens the detail popover
- Spring animation when the current movie changes

**Actions row — 4 labeled buttons**:
Each button has a big circular icon, a **name label** below it, and a **keyboard hint**:

| Icon | Label | Key | Action |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| ♥ pink | Wishlist | ← | Add to wishlist |
| ⓘ blue | Info | ↩ | Open detail popover |
| ✕ gray | Skip | esc | Pop and fetch next |
| 👁 green | Seenlist | → | Add to seenlist |

- Each button uses `.keyboardShortcut(shortcut, modifiers: [])` so the key fires the exact same closure, no separate `.onKeyPress` handler
- Each Button is a standard SwiftUI button → **Tab-navigable** for keyboard-only activation
- Visible hint text under each button means the shortcuts are self-documenting

**Reset button** moved to the top-right so it doesn't clutter the main action row.

Give it a try — Tab through the buttons, or press ←/→/Enter/Escape.

Both platforms build. Test it:

1. Go to Fan Club in the sidebar
2. Type in the search field at the top
3. As you type (with a 500ms debounce), the view replaces the fan-club + popular sections with actor search results from TMDB
4. Clear the text or click out of the field and the original view returns
5. Clicking a search result pushes into `PeopleDetail` just like before, so you can tap the **Add to fan club** button from there

A few implementation notes:
- The existing `PeopleActions.FetchSearch` is reused (already wired to `/search/person`)
- `MoviesSearchTextWrapper` is reused for the debounced search — same wrapper `MoviesList` uses
- While searching, arrow-key navigation highlights search results; clearing the search snaps highlight back to the first fan-club or popular person

Let me know how it feels — I can add an inline "Add to fan club" button on each search result row if you want to skip the detail push.

> AGENT

`steam_blue` is a single universal color (RGB 128/172/169 — a desaturated teal) with no light/dark variants, so it's the same tone in both modes. In dark mode it reads as a clear blue highlight; in light mode it comes across as a washed-out gray-teal and loses contrast.

Two clean options:

1. **Switch the focus ring to `Color.accentColor`** — adapts to the user's macOS accent preference (blue by default, respects whatever the user picks in System Settings)
2. **Make `steam_blue` a two-variant asset** with a brighter blue in light mode

Option 1 is the native-macOS pattern for "selected" / focus indicators and requires no asset edits. Let me apply it:

Both platforms build. **My Lists** on macOS is now redesigned:

**Top — segmented picker with icons**:
| Wishlist ♥ | Seenlist 👁 | Custom Lists 📌 |

Clean, matches the app's section switching on other views, keyboard-arrowable via the native Picker.

**Body — ScrollView + LazyVStack**:
- **Wishlist** — `MovieRow` cards with `macFocusHighlight` for the keyboard-selected row, sort-count subheader at top
- **Seenlist** — same layout
- **Custom Lists** — `CustomListRow` cards plus a `Create custom list` button at the top with a blue ➕ icon; empty-state message when none exist

**Navigation**:
- **Arrow up/down** moves highlight through the current section, auto-scrolling into view
- **Return / Space** on a movie pushes `MovieDetail`
- **Return / Space** on a custom list pushes `CustomListDetail`
- **Double-click** does the same
- **Switching section via picker** resets the highlight to the first item
- **`Cmd+[` / Escape** pops the detail via `.macBackKeyboardShortcut`

**Toolbar** — Sort menu (by title / release date / added date) in the top-right corner.

iOS path is untouched. Let me know how the layout feels and I'll tune spacing / colors.

Color.accentColor : .clear,\n                                lineWidth: 2)\n                )\n        }\n        .buttonStyle(.plain)\n        .focusable()\n        .focused($focusedSection, equals: section)\n        .focusEffectDisabled()\n        .accessibilityIdentifier(\"myLists.section.\\(section.title)\")\n    }\n\n    private func moveSection(offset: Int) -> KeyPress.Result {\n        let all = MyListsSection.allCases\n        guard let current = focusedSection,\n              let idx = all.firstIndex(of: current) else {\n            return .ignored\n        }\n        let nextIdx = idx + offset\n        guard all.indices.contains(nextIdx) else { return .ignored }\n        let next = all[nextIdx]\n        focusedSection = next\n        selectedList = next.rawValue\n        return .handled\n    }\n\n    private enum MyListsSection: Int, CaseIterable, Identifiable, Hashable {"

```
168	                moviesListDestinationView(for: route)
169	            }
170	            .onAppear {
171	                listener.dispatchPage = { menu, page in
172	                    props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(list: menu, page: page))
173	                }
174	                listener.loadPage()
175	            }
176	            // SplitView's .id(selectedMenu) is supposed to tear this
177	            // whole subtree down when the user picks a new sidebar
178	            // menu, but on macOS the NavigationStack hangs on to its
179	            // pushed view. Clear navigationRoute explicitly so the
180	            // stack pops back to its root before the new menu's
181	            // content is shown.
182	            .onChange(of: menu) { _, _ in
183	                navigationRoute = nil
184	            }
```

> AGENT

The lift refactor is done and builds clean on both macOS and iOS:

**What changed**
- `SplitView`: added `@State private var detailNavigationRoute: MoviesListNavigationRoute?` — the lifted state. The sidebar `Button` action now sets `detailNavigationRoute = nil` *first*, before bumping `detailRebuildKey` and changing `selectedMenu`.
- `OutlineMenu.contentView(isRunningUISmokeTests:navigationRoute:)` now takes a `Binding<MoviesListNavigationRoute?>` and threads it down through `moviesList(menu:isRunningUISmokeTests:navigationRoute:)`.
- `OutlineMoviesMenuList`: replaced its `@State private var navigationRoute` with `@Binding var navigationRoute`. The `.navigationDestination(item:)` now uses the parent-owned binding, so the explicit `nil` set in `SplitView`'s click handler reaches it before SwiftUI tears the subtree down.
- Wrapped the whole `SplitView` struct in `#if os(macOS)` since it uses `NSApp` for the key-view loop and is only consumed by `MovieSwiftMacApp` (the iOS build was failing on `NSApp`).

The DEBUG banners and prints are still in. Please run the macOS app, push a `MovieDetail` from any menu, then click another sidebar menu (e.g. Popular → Top Rated) and confirm the right pane actually swaps to the new menu's content. Once you confirm it works I'll strip the banners/prints, add a test, and commit.

NavigationSplitView on macOS used to hold on to\n        // the pushed view across menu changes; SplitView now lifts the\n        // navigationRoute up and nils it before swapping menus.\n        let app = launchApp()\n\n        // Push MovieDetail from the default Popular menu.\n        let addToListButton = openFirstMovieDetail(in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(addToListButton.exists,\n                      \"MovieDetail should be visible after tapping the first movie\")\n\n        // Switch sidebar to Top rated.\n        let topRated = app.identifiedElement(\"sidebar.Top rated\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(topRated.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout))\n        topRated.tap()\n\n        // The pushed MovieDetail must be gone and the new menu's\n        // movie list must be at the root.\n        let detailGone = NSPredicate(format: \"exists == false\")\n        let detailDismissed = expectation(for: detailGone, evaluatedWith: addToListButton)\n        wait(for: [detailDismissed], timeout: timeout)\n\n        let firstMovie = app.identifiedElement(\"moviesList.movie.0\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(firstMovie.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout),\n                      \"Expected the new menu's movies list to be visible at the root\")\n    }\n\n    func testMovieDetailGenreChipExists() {"

> AGENT

Committed as `934e564`. Summary of what shipped:

- **`SplitView.swift`**: lifted `detailNavigationRoute` to the parent; sidebar `Button` action nils it *before* mutating `selectedMenu`, so `.navigationDestination(item:)` pops the pushed `MovieDetail` instead of leaving it stranded in the `NavigationSplitView` column. Also wrapped the struct in `#if os(macOS)` (it uses `NSApp` and is only consumed by `MovieSwiftMacApp`).
- **`OutlineMenu.swift`**: `contentView(...)` now takes a `Binding<MoviesListNavigationRoute?>` and threads it down to `OutlineMoviesMenuList`, which converts its old `@State` to `@Binding`. Debug print removed.
- **`MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift`**: added `testSidebarMenuChangePopsPushedMovieDetail` — opens a movie, taps `sidebar.Top rated`, asserts `movieDetail.addToListButton` disappears and `moviesList.movie.0` reappears at the root.

Both targets build clean; all 264 redux/unit tests still pass. The new UI test compiles in `build-for-testing`; running it with xcodebuild from this shell hits a sandbox runner-bootstrap error that affects every existing UI test too — when you run it from Xcode it should exercise the regression directly.

```
208	    private func sectionTabButton(section: MyListsSection) -> some View {
209	        let isSelected = selectedList == section.rawValue
210	        return Button {
211	            selectedList = section.rawValue
212	            focusedSection = section
213	        } label: {
214	            Label(section.title, systemImage: section.systemImage)
215	                .font(.subheadline)
216	                .fontWeight(isSelected ? .semibold : .regular)
217	                .foregroundColor(isSelected ? .white : .primary)
218	                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
219	                .padding(.vertical, 7)
220	                .padding(.horizontal, 12)
221	                .background(
222	                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8, style: .continuous)
223	                        .fill(isSelected ? Color.accentColor : Color.clear)
224	                )
225	                .overlay(
226	                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8, style: .continuous)
227	                        .stroke(focusedSection == section ? Color.accentColor : .clear,
228	                                lineWidth: 2)
229	                )
230	        }
231	        .buttonStyle(.plain)
232	        .focusable()
233	        .focused($focusedSection, equals: section)
234	        .focusEffectDisabled()
235	        .accessibilityIdentifier("myLists.section.\(section.title)")
236	        // Tab from any section tab moves focus into the movies / lists
237	        // below; arrow keys still navigate between the three tabs.
238	        .onKeyPress(.tab, phases: .down) { press in
239	            guard !press.modifiers.contains(.shift) else { return .ignored }
240	            focusedSection = nil
241	            isListFocused = true
242	            return .handled
243	        }
244	        .onKeyPress(.rightArrow) { moveSection(offset: 1) }
245	        .onKeyPress(.leftArrow) { moveSection(offset: -1) }
246	    }
247	
248	    private func moveSection(offset: Int) -> KeyPress.Result {
249	        let all = MyListsSection.allCases
250	        guard let current = focusedSection,
251	              let idx = all.firstIndex(of: current) else {
252	            return .ignored
253	        }
254	        let nextIdx = idx + offset
255	        guard all.indices.contains(nextIdx) else { return .ignored }
256	        let next = all[nextIdx]
257	        focusedSection = next
258	        selectedList = next.rawValue
259	        return .handled
260	    }

281	    private func macOSListView(props: Props) -> some View {
282	        VStack(spacing: 0) {
283	            sectionSwitcher
284	                .padding(.horizontal, 16)
285	                .padding(.top, 12)
286	                .padding(.bottom, 10)
287	
288	            ScrollViewReader { scrollProxy in
289	                ScrollView {
290	                    LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
291	                        currentSectionContent(props: props)
292	                    }
293	                    .padding(.horizontal, 4)
294	                    .padding(.bottom, 24)
295	                }
296	                .focusable()
297	                .focused($isListFocused)
298	                .focusEffectDisabled()
299	                .onKeyPress(.downArrow) {
300	                    let ids = currentSectionItemIds(props: props)
301	                    return moveHighlight(ids: ids, forward: true, scrollProxy: scrollProxy)
302	                }
303	                .onKeyPress(.upArrow) {
304	                    let ids = currentSectionItemIds(props: props)
305	                    return moveHighlight(ids: ids, forward: false, scrollProxy: scrollProxy)
306	                }
307	                .onKeyPress(.return) { openHighlighted(props: props) }
308	                .onKeyPress(characters: .init(charactersIn: " ")) { _ in openHighlighted(props: props) }
309	                // Shift+Tab (delivered as the back-tab character U+0019 on macOS)
310	                // moves focus back to the currently selected section tab.
311	                .onKeyPress(characters: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "\u{19}"), phases: .down) { _ in
312	                    isListFocused = false
313	                    focusedSection = MyListsSection(rawValue: selectedList) ?? .wishlist
314	                    return .handled
315	                }
316	            }
317	        }
318	        .onChange(of: selectedList) { _, _ in
319	            // When the user switches section, reset the highlight to the

444	    private func currentSectionItemIds(props: Props) -> [Int] {
445	        switch MyListsSection(rawValue: selectedList) ?? .wishlist {
446	        case .wishlist:    return props.wishlist
447	        case .seenlist:    return props.seenlist
448	        case .customLists: return props.customLists.map { $0.id }
449	        }
450	    }
451	
452	    private func moveHighlight(ids: [Int],
453	                               forward: Bool,
454	                               scrollProxy: ScrollViewProxy) -> KeyPress.Result {
455	        guard !ids.isEmpty else { return .ignored }
456	        if let current = highlightedItemId,
457	           let idx = ids.firstIndex(of: current) {
458	            let nextIdx = idx + (forward ? 1 : -1)
459	            if ids.indices.contains(nextIdx) {
460	                let next = ids[nextIdx]
461	                highlightedItemId = next
462	                withAnimation { scrollProxy.scrollTo(next, anchor: .center) }
463	            }
464	        } else {
465	            let first = ids.first
466	            highlightedItemId = first
467	            if let first { withAnimation { scrollProxy.scrollTo(first, anchor: .center) } }
468	        }
469	        return .handled
470	    }
471	
472	    private func openHighlighted(props: Props) -> KeyPress.Result {
473	        guard let id = highlightedItemId else { return .ignored }
474	        let section = MyListsSection(rawValue: selectedList) ?? .wishlist
475	        switch section {
476	        case .customLists:
477	            selectedCustomList = CustomListNav(id: id)
478	        case .wishlist, .seenlist:
479	            selectedMovie = MovieNav(id: id)
480	        }
481	        return .handled
482	    }
```

```
72	struct SoftSelectionButtonStyle: ButtonStyle {
73	    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
74	        configuration.label
75	            .softSelectionRow(configuration.isPressed)
76	            .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12), value: configuration.isPressed)

81	/// Replaces SwiftUI's default blue focus ring with a sidebar-style
82	/// rounded-rectangle highlight on macOS.
83	struct MacFocusHighlight: ViewModifier {
84	    var isFocused: Bool
85	
86	    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
87	        content
88	            .background(
89	                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10, style: .continuous)
90	                    .fill(isFocused ? Color.steam_white.opacity(0.10) : .clear)
91	            )
92	            .shadow(color: isFocused ? Color.steam_white.opacity(0.16) : .clear,
93	                    radius: 14,
94	                    x: 0,
95	                    y: 0)
96	            .shadow(color: isFocused ? Color.black.opacity(0.18) : .clear,
97	                    radius: 6,
98	                    x: 0,
99	                    y: 4)
100	            .scaleEffect(isFocused ? 1.01 : 1.0)
101	            .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.14), value: isFocused)
102	            .background(
103	                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous)
104	                    .fill(isFocused ? Color.black.opacity(0.12) : .clear)
105	            )
106	            .focusEffectDisabled()
107	    }
108	}
109	
110	extension View {
111	    func macFocusHighlight(isFocused: Bool) -> some View {
112	        self.modifier(MacFocusHighlight(isFocused: isFocused))
113	    }
114	}
115	
116	/// A reusable wrapper that provides a focusable, keyboard-navigable
117	/// Button for macOS list rows.
118	struct MacFocusableLink<Label: View, ID: Hashable>: View {
119	    let id: ID
120	    var focusedId: FocusState<ID?>.Binding
121	    let action: () -> Void
122	    @ViewBuilder let label: () -> Label
123	
124	    var body: some View {
125	        Button(action: action) {
126	            label()
127	        }
128	        .buttonStyle(.plain)
129	        .focusable()
130	        .focused(focusedId, equals: id)
131	        .onKeyPress(.return) { action(); return .handled }
132	        .onKeyPress(characters: .init(charactersIn: " ")) { _ in action(); return .handled }
133	        .macFocusHighlight(isFocused: focusedId.wrappedValue == id)
134	    }
135	}
136	#endif
137
```

> AGENT

Both targets build, all 7 settings unit tests still pass, and the macOS UI test target builds.

**What changed**

Settings on macOS is now built as a `ScrollView` of grouped cards instead of the system `Form`:

- **Section headers** in `FjallaOne` 14pt small-caps, tinted `.steam_gold` with letter-spacing — matches the rest of the app's typographic voice.
- **Grouped cards** are `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14)` filled with `Color.primary.opacity(0.06)` plus a 1pt hairline stroke, separated by inset dividers. Same card language as My Lists' section switcher.
- **Region preferences card**: globe icon + `.steam_blue` glyph, region picker with `.menu` style, original-title toggle tinted `.steam_gold`.
- **App data card**: trash icon and label in `.steam_rust` for the destructive Clear-cached-data row, "Coming soon" rows show a subtle pill-shaped "Soon" badge instead of generic gray text.
- **Debug info card**: matching info-circle icons, monospaced-digit values.
- Page background is `Color.steam_background`, content-width capped at 720pt so labels don't stretch on wide windows.
- Footnotes for the region and app-data sections live below the card in `.footnote .secondary`, so explanation text reads as commentary rather than form chrome.

iOS still uses the system `Form` (matches platform conventions there). All accessibility identifiers (`settings.regionPicker`, `settings.alwaysOriginalTitleToggle`, `settings.alwaysOriginalTitleRow`, `settings.clearCachedDataButton`, `settings.cancelButton`, `settings.saveButton`) are preserved, so existing UI tests still target the right elements.

Run the macOS app and let me know if the Settings view matches the rest of the app's feel. Once confirmed I'll commit.

```
6	import Foundation
7	
8	enum AppPersistence {
9	    private static var savePath: URL?
10	    private static let encoder = JSONEncoder()
11	    private static let decoder = JSONDecoder()
12	
13	    private static func resolvedSavePath() throws -> URL {
14	        let icloudDirectory = FileManager.default.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier: nil)
15	        let documentDirectory = try FileManager.default.url(for: .documentDirectory,
16	                                                            in: .userDomainMask,
17	                                                            appropriateFor: nil,
18	                                                            create: false)
19	        if let icloudDirectory {
20	            try FileManager.default.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at: icloudDirectory)
21	        }
22	
23	        return (icloudDirectory ?? documentDirectory).appendingPathComponent("userData")
24	    }
25	
26	    private static func ensureSavePath() -> URL? {
27	        if let savePath {
28	            return savePath
29	        }
30	
31	        do {
32	            let path = try resolvedSavePath()
33	            savePath = path
34	            return path
35	        } catch {
36	            return nil
37	        }
38	    }
39	
40	    static func loadState() -> AppState? {
41	        guard let savePath = ensureSavePath(),
42	              let data = try? Data(contentsOf: savePath),
43	              var savedState = try? decoder.decode(AppState.self, from: data) else {
44	            return nil
45	        }
46	
47	        savedState.ensurePlaceholderData()
48	        return savedState
49	    }
50	
51	    static func archive(state: AppState) {
52	        guard let resolvedSavePath = ensureSavePath() else {
53	            return
54	        }
55	
56	        DispatchQueue.global().async {
57	            write(state: AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state), to: resolvedSavePath)
58	        }
59	    }
60	
61	    static func archiveNow(state: AppState) {
62	        guard let resolvedSavePath = ensureSavePath() else {
63	            return
64	        }
65	
66	        write(state: AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state), to: resolvedSavePath)
67	    }
68	
69	    static func archivedStateSizeDescription() -> String {
70	        guard let resolvedSavePath = ensureSavePath() else {
71	            return "0 KB"
72	        }
73	        do {
74	            let resources = try resolvedSavePath.resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey])
75	            let formatter = ByteCountFormatter()
76	            formatter.allowedUnits = .useKB
77	            formatter.countStyle = .file
78	            return formatter.string(fromByteCount: Int64(resources.fileSize ?? 0))
79	        } catch {
80	            return "0"
81	        }
82	    }
83	
84	    private static func write(state: AppState, to path: URL) {
85	        guard let data = try? encoder.encode(state) else {
86	            return
87	        }
88	        do {
89	            try data.write(to: path)
90	        } catch let error {
91	            print("Error while saving app state :\(error)")
92	        }
93	    }
94	}
```

```
9	import Foundation
10	import SwiftUIFlux
11	
12	enum AppActions {
13	    struct ClearCachedData: Action { }
14	}
15	
16	enum AppStateCacheReset {
17	    static func persistentSnapshot(from state: AppState) -> AppState {
18	        var snapshot = AppState()
19	        let preservedMovieIds = preservedMovieIds(from: state)
20	
21	        snapshot.moviesState.movies = state.moviesState.movies.filter { preservedMovieIds.contains($0.key) }
22	        snapshot.moviesState.wishlist = state.moviesState.wishlist
23	        snapshot.moviesState.seenlist = state.moviesState.seenlist
24	        snapshot.moviesState.moviesUserMeta = state.moviesState.moviesUserMeta.filter {
25	            preservedMovieIds.contains($0.key)
26	        }
27	        snapshot.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters = state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters
28	        snapshot.moviesState.discoverFilter = state.moviesState.discoverFilter
29	        snapshot.moviesState.customLists = state.moviesState.customLists
30	
31	        snapshot.peoplesState.peoples = state.peoplesState.peoples.filter {
32	            state.peoplesState.fanClub.contains($0.key)
33	        }
34	        snapshot.peoplesState.fanClub = state.peoplesState.fanClub
35	
36	        return snapshot
37	    }
38	
39	    private static func preservedMovieIds(from state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {
40	        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist
41	        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)
42	
43	        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {
44	            ids.formUnion(list.movies)
45	            if let cover = list.cover {
46	                ids.insert(cover)
47	            }
48	        }
49	
50	        return ids
51	    }
52	}
53	
54	func appStateReducer(state: AppState, action: Action) -> AppState {
55	    if action is AppActions.ClearCachedData {
56	        return AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state)
57	    }
58	
59	    var state = state
60	    state.moviesState = moviesStateReducer(state: state.moviesState, action: action)
61	    state.peoplesState = peoplesStateReducer(state: state.peoplesState, action: action)
62	    return state
63	}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataExport.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  AppDataExport.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Builds a JSON-encoded export of the user's persistent app data —\n//  wishlist, seenlist, custom lists, fan club, and the cached metadata\n//  for those movies / people. Wraps the snapshot in an envelope with a\n//  format version, export date, and app version so future imports can\n//  detect format drift.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\n/// Versioned envelope around an `AppState` snapshot, written out as JSON.\n///\n/// The envelope is intentionally a separate type from `AppState` so the\n/// import side can read the version field before attempting to decode\n/// the snapshot body — letting older or newer formats fail with a clear\n/// error instead of silently corrupting state.\nstruct AppDataExportEnvelope: Codable, Equatable {\n    /// Bumped when the on-disk export format changes in a way that\n    /// would prevent older readers from understanding the file.\n    static let currentFormatVersion: Int = 1\n\n    let formatVersion: Int\n    let exportDate: Date\n    let appVersion: String\n    let appBuild: String\n    let snapshot: AppState\n}\n\nenum AppDataExport {\n    /// Default JSON encoder used for exports. Pretty-printed and ISO 8601\n    /// dates so the file is human-inspectable.\n    static func makeEncoder() -> JSONEncoder {\n        let encoder = JSONEncoder()\n        encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]\n        encoder.dateEncodingStrategy = .iso8601\n        return encoder\n    }\n\n    static func makeDecoder() -> JSONDecoder {\n        let decoder = JSONDecoder()\n        decoder.dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601\n        return decoder\n    }\n\n    /// Builds the export envelope from the live app state. Reuses\n    /// `AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from:)` so transient\n    /// caches (search results, popular lists, recommended sets, etc.)\n    /// are stripped — only the user's actual data ships.\n    static func envelope(from state: AppState,\n                         exportDate: Date = Date(),\n                         appVersion: String = bundleVersion(),\n                         appBuild: String = bundleBuild()) -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        AppDataExportEnvelope(\n            formatVersion: AppDataExportEnvelope.currentFormatVersion,\n            exportDate: exportDate,\n            appVersion: appVersion,\n            appBuild: appBuild,\n            snapshot: AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state)\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Encodes the envelope as pretty-printed JSON.\n    static func data(from envelope: AppDataExportEnvelope,\n                     encoder: JSONEncoder = makeEncoder()) throws -> Data {\n        try encoder.encode(envelope)\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience: build the envelope and encode in one step.\n    static func data(from state: AppState,\n                     exportDate: Date = Date()) throws -> Data {\n        try data(from: envelope(from: state, exportDate: exportDate))\n    }\n\n    /// \"MovieSwift-Export-2026-05-02.json\" style filename based on the\n    /// export date, without spaces or path separators.\n    static func suggestedFilename(for date: Date,\n                                  calendar: Calendar = .init(identifier: .gregorian),\n                                  timeZone: TimeZone = .current) -> String {\n        let formatter = DateFormatter()\n        formatter.calendar = calendar\n        formatter.timeZone = timeZone\n        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: \"en_US_POSIX\")\n        formatter.dateFormat = \"yyyy-MM-dd\"\n        return \"MovieSwift-Export-\\(formatter.string(from: date))\"\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Bundle helpers\n\n    static func bundleVersion(bundle: Bundle = .main) -> String {\n        bundle.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: \"CFBundleShortVersionString\") as? String ?? \"0.0\"\n    }\n\n    static func bundleBuild(bundle: Bundle = .main) -> String {\n        bundle.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: \"CFBundleVersion\") as? String ?? \"0\"\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

```json
  "content": "//\n//  UserDataDocument.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Thin FileDocument wrapper around exported user-data JSON so the\n//  cross-platform `.fileExporter` modifier in SwiftUI can write it to\n//  disk on macOS / iOS / tvOS without dropping into platform-specific\n//  NSSavePanel / UIActivityViewController code.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\nimport UniformTypeIdentifiers\n\nstruct UserDataDocument: FileDocument {\n    static var readableContentTypes: [UTType] { [.json] }\n    static var writableContentTypes: [UTType] { [.json] }\n\n    let data: Data\n\n    init(data: Data) {\n        self.data = data\n    }\n\n    init(configuration: ReadConfiguration) throws {\n        guard let raw = configuration.file.regularFileContents else {\n            throw CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile)\n        }\n        self.data = raw\n    }\n\n    func fileWrapper(configuration: WriteConfiguration) throws -> FileWrapper {\n        FileWrapper(regularFileWithContents: data)\n    }\n}\n"
```

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift",
  "old_string": "    private func clearCachedData(props: Props) {\n        SettingsFormCacheResetPolicy.clearCachedData(state: store.state,\n                                                     dispatch: props.dispatch)\n    }",
  "new_string": "    private func clearCachedData(props: Props) {\n        SettingsFormCacheResetPolicy.clearCachedData(state: store.state,\n                                                     dispatch: props.dispatch)\n    }\n\n    private func startExport() {\n        let now = Date()\n        do {\n            let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: store.state, exportDate: now)\n            exportDocument = UserDataDocument(data: data)\n            exportSuggestedFilename = AppDataExport.suggestedFilename(for: now)\n            isExportPresented = true\n        } catch {\n            exportErrorMessage = \"Couldn't build the export file: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func handleExportResult(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {\n        // Drop the in-memory document either way — the user has either\n        // saved it or cancelled, and we don't want to keep ~20 KB of\n        // their state in @State for the lifetime of the view.\n        exportDocument = nil\n        if case .failure(let error) = result {\n            // The user cancelling is reported as a CancellationError on\n            // some OS versions, so don't surface that as a real error.\n            if (error as NSError).domain != NSCocoaErrorDomain || (error as NSError).code != NSUserCancelledError {\n                exportErrorMessage = \"Export failed: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n            }\n        }\n    }"
}
```

> AGENT

Shipped as `aae26a7`. Summary:

**What changed**

- **`Shared/flux/state/AppDataExport.swift`** — new pure-logic enum that builds a versioned `AppDataExportEnvelope` (formatVersion, exportDate, appVersion, appBuild, persistent snapshot) and encodes it as pretty-printed JSON. Uses `AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from:)` so transient caches (search results, popular/recommended lists) are stripped — only your wishlist, seenlist, custom lists, and fan club end up in the file.
- **`MovieSwift/views/components/settings/UserDataDocument.swift`** — small `FileDocument` wrapper around the JSON `Data` so SwiftUI's cross-platform `.fileExporter` can handle the save dialog.
- **`SettingsForm.swift`** — added export `@State`, `startExport()`, and `handleExportResult(_:)`. The macOS card-style "Export my data" row and the iOS Form button both now trigger `.fileExporter`. Default filename is `MovieSwift-Export-2026-05-02.json`. Errors (other than user cancellation) surface in an alert.
- **`MovieSwiftTests/AppDataExportTests.swift`** — 7 new tests covering persistent-only snapshot inclusion, transient-cache stripping, fan-club person inclusion, metadata stamping (formatVersion/date/version/build), JSON round-trip, pretty-printing, and ISO date filename formatting. Registered in MovieSwiftTests, MovieSwiftMacTests, and MovieSwiftTVTests.
- **`MovieSwift.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`** — registered the three new source files in the appropriate target Sources phases (`AppDataExport.swift` in iOS/macOS/tvOS, `UserDataDocument.swift` in iOS/macOS, `AppDataExportTests.swift` in all 3 unit-test targets).

All 3 targets build clean and all 271 tests pass (was 264 — 7 new). Next time you tap "Export my data" you'll get a save panel with a sensibly-named JSON file containing your actual data, ready for safekeeping or future re-import.

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataImport.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  AppDataImport.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Inverse of AppDataExport: reads a JSON envelope produced by Export\n//  my data, validates the format version, and merges the imported user\n//  data (wishlist, seenlist, custom lists, fan club, cached movie /\n//  people metadata) into the live AppState.\n//\n//  The merge is intentionally non-destructive — current user data is\n//  preserved and the imported data is unioned in. This prevents an\n//  accidental import from wiping a user's collection. To replace\n//  state outright a caller would clear it first, then import.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum AppDataImport {\n\n    /// Errors surfaced to the UI when an import can't proceed.\n    enum ImportError: LocalizedError {\n        case decodeFailed(underlying: Error)\n        case unsupportedFormatVersion(found: Int, supported: ClosedRange<Int>)\n\n        var errorDescription: String? {\n            switch self {\n            case .decodeFailed(let error):\n                return \"Couldn't read the export file: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n            case .unsupportedFormatVersion(let found, let supported):\n                return \"Export file format version \\(found) isn't supported by this version of MovieSwift (supported: \\(supported.lowerBound)–\\(supported.upperBound)).\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format versions this build of MovieSwift can read. Bump the\n    /// upper bound when introducing breaking schema changes; bump\n    /// `AppDataExportEnvelope.currentFormatVersion` to write them.\n    static let supportedFormatVersions: ClosedRange<Int> = 1...AppDataExportEnvelope.currentFormatVersion\n\n    /// Preview of what a merge would change. Surfaces in the import\n    /// confirmation alert so the user sees the scope of the change\n    /// before they commit to it.\n    struct Counts: Equatable {\n        let wishlistAdded: Int\n        let seenlistAdded: Int\n        let customListsAdded: Int\n        let customListsUpdated: Int\n        let fanClubAdded: Int\n\n        var total: Int {\n            wishlistAdded + seenlistAdded + customListsAdded + customListsUpdated + fanClubAdded\n        }\n\n        var hasAnyChanges: Bool { total > 0 }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Decoding\n\n    /// Decodes a JSON-encoded export envelope and validates that this\n    /// build can read its format version.\n    static func decodeEnvelope(from data: Data,\n                               decoder: JSONDecoder = AppDataExport.makeDecoder()) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        let envelope: AppDataExportEnvelope\n        do {\n            envelope = try decoder.decode(AppDataExportEnvelope.self, from: data)\n        } catch {\n            throw ImportError.decodeFailed(underlying: error)\n        }\n        guard supportedFormatVersions.contains(envelope.formatVersion) else {\n            throw ImportError.unsupportedFormatVersion(\n                found: envelope.formatVersion,\n                supported: supportedFormatVersions\n            )\n        }\n        return envelope\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Preview\n\n    /// Counts what `merge(envelope:into:)` would add to `state`,\n    /// without mutating anything. `customListsUpdated` counts\n    /// imported lists whose id matches an existing list (those get\n    /// overwritten on merge).\n    static func previewCounts(for envelope: AppDataExportEnvelope,\n                              against state: AppState) -> Counts {\n        let imported = envelope.snapshot\n\n        let wishlistAdded = imported.moviesState.wishlist\n            .subtracting(state.moviesState.wishlist).count\n        let seenlistAdded = imported.moviesState.seenlist\n            .subtracting(state.moviesState.seenlist).count\n        let fanClubAdded = imported.peoplesState.fanClub\n            .subtracting(state.peoplesState.fanClub).count\n\n        let importedListIds = Set(imported.moviesState.customLists.keys)\n        let currentListIds = Set(state.moviesState.customLists.keys)\n        let customListsAdded = importedListIds.subtracting(currentListIds).count\n        let customListsUpdated = importedListIds.intersection(currentListIds).count\n\n        return Counts(wishlistAdded: wishlistAdded,\n                      seenlistAdded: seenlistAdded,\n                      customListsAdded: customListsAdded,\n                      customListsUpdated: customListsUpdated,\n                      fanClubAdded: fanClubAdded)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Merge\n\n    /// Returns a new AppState with the imported snapshot merged in.\n    ///\n    /// Merge rules:\n    /// - `wishlist`, `seenlist`, `fanClub` — set union with current.\n    /// - `customLists` — upsert by id; imported wins on conflict so\n    ///   the user gets the version they intentionally exported.\n    /// - `movies`, `peoples` reverse caches — current wins on conflict.\n    ///   Current entries are likely fresher; imported only fills in\n    ///   the entries needed to render the imported lists.\n    /// - `moviesUserMeta` — current wins on conflict, same reasoning.\n    /// - `savedDiscoverFilters` — append imported filters that aren't\n    ///   already present (compared by JSON encoding to dodge the\n    ///   missing Equatable conformance on DiscoverFilter).\n    /// - `discoverFilter` (the active selection) — preserved as-is.\n    static func merge(envelope: AppDataExportEnvelope, into state: AppState) -> AppState {\n        var state = state\n        let imported = envelope.snapshot\n\n        // User collections.\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.formUnion(imported.moviesState.wishlist)\n        state.moviesState.seenlist.formUnion(imported.moviesState.seenlist)\n        state.peoplesState.fanClub.formUnion(imported.peoplesState.fanClub)\n\n        // Custom lists — imported wins on conflict.\n        for (id, list) in imported.moviesState.customLists {\n            state.moviesState.customLists[id] = list\n        }\n\n        // Reverse caches — only fill in entries the current state\n        // doesn't already have.\n        for (id, movie) in imported.moviesState.movies {\n            if state.moviesState.movies[id] == nil {\n                state.moviesState.movies[id] = movie\n            }\n        }\n        for (id, meta) in imported.moviesState.moviesUserMeta {\n            if state.moviesState.moviesUserMeta[id] == nil {\n                state.moviesState.moviesUserMeta[id] = meta\n            }\n        }\n        for (id, person) in imported.peoplesState.peoples {\n            if state.peoplesState.peoples[id] == nil {\n                state.peoplesState.peoples[id] = person\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Saved discover filters — append any that don't already\n        // exist in the current state. DiscoverFilter doesn't conform\n        // to Equatable, so compare by encoded JSON.\n        let encoder = JSONEncoder()\n        let existingEncodings = Set(state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters\n            .compactMap { try? encoder.encode($0) })\n        for filter in imported.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters {\n            if let encoded = try? encoder.encode(filter),\n               !existingEncodings.contains(encoded) {\n                state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters.append(filter)\n            }\n        }\n\n        return state\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
```

```json
  "old_string": "        // Saved discover filters — append any that don't already\n        // exist in the current state. DiscoverFilter doesn't conform\n        // to Equatable, so compare by encoded JSON.\n        let encoder = JSONEncoder()\n        let existingEncodings = Set(state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters\n            .compactMap { try? encoder.encode($0) })\n        for filter in imported.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters {\n            if let encoded = try? encoder.encode(filter),\n               !existingEncodings.contains(encoded) {\n                state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters.append(filter)\n            }\n        }",
  "new_string": "        // Saved discover filters — append any that don't already\n        // exist in the current state. DiscoverFilter doesn't conform\n        // to Equatable, so compare by encoded JSON. `.sortedKeys` is\n        // essential here; without it, dictionary key ordering varies\n        // per encode call and the dedupe set never matches.\n        let encoder = JSONEncoder()\n        encoder.outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys]\n        let existingEncodings = Set(state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters\n            .compactMap { try? encoder.encode($0) })\n        for filter in imported.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters {\n            if let encoded = try? encoder.encode(filter),\n               !existingEncodings.contains(encoded) {\n                state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters.append(filter)\n            }\n        }"
}
```

> AGENT

Shipped as `624e8d0`. Summary:

**What changed**

- **`Shared/flux/state/AppDataImport.swift`** — pure-logic enum mirroring `AppDataExport`. Three responsibilities:
  - `decodeEnvelope(from:)` validates JSON shape and rejects envelopes whose `formatVersion` is outside `supportedFormatVersions`. Wraps decode errors in `ImportError.decodeFailed` with localized descriptions.
  - `previewCounts(for:against:)` returns how many wishlist / seenlist / fan-club / custom-list adds the user is about to commit to — drives the confirmation alert without touching state.
  - `merge(envelope:into:)` unions user collections, upserts custom lists by id with imported winning on conflict (the user intentionally exported that version), preserves current `movies`/`peoples`/`moviesUserMeta` cache entries on conflict (current is likely fresher), and dedupes `savedDiscoverFilters` via `.sortedKeys` JSON encoding.
- **`Shared/flux/reducers/AppReducer.swift`** — new `AppActions.ImportAppData(envelope:)` with reducer hook calling `AppDataImport.merge(envelope:into:)`.
- **`SettingsForm.swift`** — added Import-state, `handleImportSelection(_:)` (opens a security-scoped resource so the sandbox lets us read the picked file), `confirmImport(props:)`, and a new `importDataRow` mirroring the Export row's visual style. The body now hosts `.fileImporter`, a "Will add: …" confirmation alert, an error alert, and a post-import success alert. iOS `Form` gets a matching `Label("Import my data", …)` button.
- **`AppDataImportTests.swift`** — 11 new tests covering decode round-trip, unsupported-version rejection, decode-failure wrapping, preview counts (adds/upserts/subset), merge unioning of user collections, imported-wins custom-list upserts, current-wins cache/meta preservation, filter dedupe, and `AppActions.ImportAppData` reducer integration.

All 3 targets build clean; **282/282 unit tests** pass (271 → 282). The macOS sandbox already has `com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-write`, which covers `.fileImporter` reads as well as `.fileExporter` writes — so no additional entitlement work needed.

Try it: Export a copy of your data, hand-edit a wishlist id to 12345 in the JSON, then Import. You should see "Will add: • 1 movie to your wishlist" in the alert, and after confirming the row count goes up by one in My Lists.

```json
  "content": "//\n//  AppDataICloudBackup.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Reads and writes a single rolling backup of the user's data to\n//  iCloud Drive. Reuses AppDataExport's envelope format so a backup\n//  is just an export saved to a known iCloud path; restore reuses\n//  AppDataImport's merge semantics. The file lives at\n//\n//      <iCloudContainer>/Documents/Backups/MovieSwift-Latest.json\n//\n//  so it shows up under the user's iCloud Drive in Files.app and is\n//  automatically synced across devices that share the iCloud account.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum AppDataICloudBackup {\n\n    /// Errors surfaced by Backup/Restore operations.\n    enum BackupError: LocalizedError {\n        case iCloudUnavailable\n        case noBackupExists\n        case writeFailed(underlying: Error)\n        case readFailed(underlying: Error)\n\n        var errorDescription: String? {\n            switch self {\n            case .iCloudUnavailable:\n                return \"iCloud Drive is not available. Sign in to iCloud in System Settings and enable iCloud Drive for MovieSwift.\"\n            case .noBackupExists:\n                return \"No iCloud backup exists yet. Tap Back up to iCloud first.\"\n            case .writeFailed(let error):\n                return \"Couldn't write the backup: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n            case .readFailed(let error):\n                return \"Couldn't read the backup: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Filename of the rolling backup. A single file is overwritten\n    /// on each Back up — the goal is \"latest known good\", not a\n    /// versioned history.\n    static let backupFilename = \"MovieSwift-Latest.json\"\n\n    // MARK: - URL helpers (testable; take an explicit container)\n\n    /// Directory inside the given iCloud container where backups live.\n    /// `Documents/` is the conventional public-facing slot — files\n    /// there appear in the user's iCloud Drive in Files.app.\n    static func backupDirectory(in container: URL) -> URL {\n        container\n            .appendingPathComponent(\"Documents\", isDirectory: true)\n            .appendingPathComponent(\"Backups\", isDirectory: true)\n    }\n\n    /// Path of the rolling backup file inside the given container.\n    static func backupFileURL(in container: URL) -> URL {\n        backupDirectory(in: container).appendingPathComponent(backupFilename)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - URL helpers (production; resolve real iCloud)\n\n    /// Resolved iCloud container URL, or nil when iCloud Drive isn't\n    /// available (no signed-in iCloud account, the user disabled\n    /// iCloud Drive for the app, or the container isn't provisioned).\n    static func resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {\n        fileManager.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier: nil)\n    }\n\n    /// Production helper that resolves the iCloud container then\n    /// returns the rolling backup URL inside it. Returns nil when\n    /// iCloud is unavailable.\n    static func resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {\n        resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: fileManager).map(backupFileURL(in:))\n    }\n\n    /// Whether iCloud Drive can be used for backup right now.\n    static func isICloudAvailable(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Bool {\n        resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: fileManager) != nil\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Reading the last-backup date\n\n    /// Modification date of the backup file at `fileURL`, or nil when\n    /// the file isn't present.\n    static func lastBackupDate(at fileURL: URL,\n                               fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Date? {\n        guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path),\n              let attrs = try? fileManager.attributesOfItem(atPath: fileURL.path),\n              let modDate = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        return modDate\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: returns the iCloud backup's last-modified\n    /// date, or nil when iCloud is unavailable or no backup exists.\n    static func resolvedLastBackupDate(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Date? {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        return lastBackupDate(at: url, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Write\n\n    /// Writes the export envelope of `state` to `fileURL`. Creates\n    /// any missing intermediate directories. Re-throws decode/IO\n    /// failures wrapped in `BackupError.writeFailed`.\n    static func writeBackup(state: AppState,\n                            to fileURL: URL,\n                            date: Date = Date(),\n                            fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws {\n        do {\n            let directory = fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent()\n            try fileManager.createDirectory(at: directory,\n                                            withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n            let envelope = AppDataExport.envelope(from: state, exportDate: date)\n            let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: envelope)\n            try data.write(to: fileURL, options: [.atomic])\n        } catch {\n            throw BackupError.writeFailed(underlying: error)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and\n    /// writes there. Throws `iCloudUnavailable` if there's no\n    /// container.\n    static func writeBackupToICloud(state: AppState,\n                                    date: Date = Date(),\n                                    fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            throw BackupError.iCloudUnavailable\n        }\n        try writeBackup(state: state, to: url, date: date, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Read\n\n    /// Reads and decodes the backup envelope at `fileURL`. Throws\n    /// `noBackupExists` if the file isn't present, or a wrapped\n    /// `readFailed` for any other failure.\n    static func readBackup(from fileURL: URL,\n                           fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else {\n            throw BackupError.noBackupExists\n        }\n        // If the file is in iCloud and not yet downloaded, ask iCloud\n        // to start downloading it. `Data(contentsOf:)` then waits on\n        // the materialized file. On a non-iCloud URL this is a no-op.\n        try? fileManager.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at: fileURL)\n        do {\n            let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)\n            return try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: data)\n        } catch let error as AppDataImport.ImportError {\n            // Decode-side errors carry their own user-facing message;\n            // forward them as readFailed so the caller surfaces a\n            // single error type.\n            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)\n        } catch {\n            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and\n    /// reads from there. Throws `iCloudUnavailable` if there's no\n    /// container.\n    static func readBackupFromICloud(fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            throw BackupError.iCloudUnavailable\n        }\n        return try readBackup(from: url, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

```json
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/AppDataICloudBackupTests.swift",
  "content": "import XCTest\n#if os(tvOS)\n@testable import MovieSwiftTV\n#elseif os(macOS)\n@testable import Film_O_Matic\n#else\n@testable import MovieSwift\n#endif\n\nfinal class AppDataICloudBackupTests: XCTestCase {\n\n    private var tempContainer: URL!\n\n    override func setUpWithError() throws {\n        try super.setUpWithError()\n        // Stand up a temp directory that mimics an iCloud container —\n        // pure-logic helpers don't care that it's not iCloud-backed.\n        tempContainer = FileManager.default\n            .temporaryDirectory\n            .appendingPathComponent(\"AppDataICloudBackupTests-\\(UUID().uuidString)\",\n                                    isDirectory: true)\n        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: tempContainer,\n                                                withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n    }\n\n    override func tearDownWithError() throws {\n        if let tempContainer {\n            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: tempContainer)\n        }\n        tempContainer = nil\n        try super.tearDownWithError()\n    }\n\n    private func makeMovie(id: Int) -> Movie {\n        Movie(id: id,\n              original_title: \"Movie \\(id)\",\n              title: \"Movie \\(id)\",\n              overview: \"Overview\",\n              poster_path: nil,\n              backdrop_path: nil,\n              popularity: 0,\n              vote_average: 0,\n              vote_count: 0,\n              release_date: nil,\n              genres: nil,\n              runtime: nil,\n              status: nil,\n              video: false,\n              keywords: nil,\n              images: nil,\n              production_countries: nil,\n              character: nil,\n              department: nil)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - URL composition\n\n    func testBackupDirectoryAndFileURLLayout() {\n        let dir = AppDataICloudBackup.backupDirectory(in: tempContainer)\n        let file = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(dir.lastPathComponent, \"Backups\")\n        XCTAssertEqual(dir.deletingLastPathComponent().lastPathComponent, \"Documents\")\n        XCTAssertEqual(file.lastPathComponent, AppDataICloudBackup.backupFilename)\n        XCTAssertEqual(file.deletingLastPathComponent(), dir)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Write\n\n    func testWriteBackupCreatesIntermediateDirectoriesAndWritesEnvelope() throws {\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.movies[1] = makeMovie(id: 1)\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.insert(1)\n\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: state, to: fileURL)\n\n        XCTAssertTrue(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path),\n                      \"Backup file should exist after write\")\n\n        let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)\n        let decoded = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: data)\n        XCTAssertEqual(decoded.formatVersion, AppDataExportEnvelope.currentFormatVersion)\n        XCTAssertTrue(decoded.snapshot.moviesState.wishlist.contains(1))\n    }\n\n    func testWriteBackupOverwritesPreviousBackup() throws {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n\n        var firstState = AppState()\n        firstState.moviesState.wishlist.insert(11)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: firstState, to: fileURL)\n\n        var secondState = AppState()\n        secondState.moviesState.wishlist.insert(22)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: secondState, to: fileURL)\n\n        let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(from: fileURL)\n        XCTAssertFalse(envelope.snapshot.moviesState.wishlist.contains(11),\n                       \"Old backup data should not survive overwrite\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(envelope.snapshot.moviesState.wishlist.contains(22))\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Read\n\n    func testReadBackupRoundTripsTheWrittenEnvelope() throws {\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.movies[5] = makeMovie(id: 5)\n        state.moviesState.seenlist.insert(5)\n        state.peoplesState.fanClub.insert(7)\n\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: state, to: fileURL)\n\n        let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(from: fileURL)\n        XCTAssertTrue(envelope.snapshot.moviesState.seenlist.contains(5))\n        XCTAssertTrue(envelope.snapshot.peoplesState.fanClub.contains(7))\n    }\n\n    func testReadBackupThrowsNoBackupExistsWhenFileMissing() {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertFalse(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path))\n\n        XCTAssertThrowsError(try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(from: fileURL)) { error in\n            guard case AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError.noBackupExists = error else {\n                XCTFail(\"Expected noBackupExists, got \\(error)\")\n                return\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    func testReadBackupWrapsCorruptDataInReadFailedError() throws {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent(),\n                                                withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n        try Data(\"not actually json\".utf8).write(to: fileURL)\n\n        XCTAssertThrowsError(try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(from: fileURL)) { error in\n            guard case AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError.readFailed = error else {\n                XCTFail(\"Expected readFailed, got \\(error)\")\n                return\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - lastBackupDate\n\n    func testLastBackupDateReturnsNilWhenFileMissing() {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertNil(AppDataICloudBackup.lastBackupDate(at: fileURL))\n    }\n\n    func testLastBackupDateReturnsModificationDate() throws {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: AppState(), to: fileURL)\n\n        let modDate = AppDataICloudBackup.lastBackupDate(at: fileURL)\n        XCTAssertNotNil(modDate)\n        if let modDate {\n            XCTAssertLessThan(abs(modDate.timeIntervalSinceNow), 5,\n                              \"Mod date should be within 5 seconds of now\")\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

Shipped as `28e80a7`. Summary:

**What changed**

- **`Shared/flux/state/AppDataICloudBackup.swift`** — pure-logic enum mirroring Export/Import for the iCloud side. Separates URL composition (`backupDirectory(in:)`, `backupFileURL(in:)` take an explicit container so tests can use a temp directory) from the production helpers that resolve the real iCloud container via `FileManager.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier:)`. `writeBackup(state:to:)` reuses `AppDataExport.envelope`/`data` so the on-disk format is identical to local Export. `readBackup(from:)` pings `startDownloadingUbiquitousItem` before `Data(contentsOf:)` so non-local iCloud files get pulled down before reading. `lastBackupDate(at:)` reads file `modificationDate` to power the trailing label and disabled state.

- **`SettingsForm.swift`** — replaced the two `comingSoonRow` placeholders with active `backupToICloudRow` and `restoreFromICloudRow`. The Back-up row shows the last-backup timestamp on the trailing edge; the Restore row is disabled with a "No backup" hint when no file exists. Restore reuses the existing Import preview/confirmation/success alerts — same merge semantics, same UX. Added a "Backed up to iCloud" success alert and a generic "iCloud backup" error alert. iOS Form gets a matching pair of buttons.

- **`AppDataICloudBackupTests.swift`** — 8 new tests using a temp directory as a fake container: URL layout, write + intermediate-directory creation, overwrite semantics, round-trip read, missing-file error, corrupt-data error, last-backup-date nil/non-nil paths.

The on-disk path is `<iCloudContainer>/Documents/Backups/MovieSwift-Latest.json`, so the file shows up under the user's iCloud Drive in Files.app and is automatically synced across devices that share the iCloud account. The existing `CloudDocuments` + ubiquity-container entitlements on both `MovieSwift` and `MovieSwiftMac` cover this path — no new entitlement needed.

All 3 targets build clean; **290/290 unit tests** pass (282 → 290, +8 new).

Try it: tap Back up to iCloud, then look in Files.app under iCloud Drive → Film-O-Matic → Backups; you'll see `MovieSwift-Latest.json`. Add a movie to your wishlist after that, then tap Restore from iCloud — the alert will say "Will add: 0 movies" because the backup is already a subset, and you'll see "Import complete. Nothing new was added".
