\"exclamationmark.triangle\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    private var iconColor: Color {\n        switch failure.kind {\n        case .offline, .rateLimited, .server, .decode, .other:\n            return .steam_rust\n        case .missingAPIKey, .unauthorized, .forbidden:\n            return .steam_gold\n        }\n    }\n}"

XCTAssertEqual(failure.retryActionTitle, \"Try again\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(failure.message.lowercased().contains(\"offline\"))\n    }\n\n    func XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: 8))\n        XCTAssertTrue(failure.message.contains(\"8 seconds\"),\n                      \"Expected message to surface the retry-after seconds, got \\(failure.message)\")\n    }\n\n    func testPresenterMapsRateLimitedWithSingleSecondToSingularText() {\n        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: 1))\n        XCTAssertTrue(failure.message.contains(\"1 second\"))\n        XCTAssertFalse(failure.message.contains(\"1 seconds\"),\n                       \"Singular grammar matters in user-facing copy\")\n    }\n\n    func testPresenterMapsRateLimitedWithUnknownRetryAfterToVagueText() {\n        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: nil))\n        XCTAssertTrue(failure.message.lowercased().contains(\"moment\"),\n                      \"Without a known retry-after, fall back to a vague 'try again in XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .unauthorized)\n        XCTAssertEqual(failure.retryActionTitle, \"Open Settings\")\n    }\n\n    func testPresenterMapsHTTP403ToForbidden() {\n        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .httpStatus(code: 403))\n        XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .forbidden)\n    }\n\n    func testPresenterMapsHTTP500RangeToServer() {\n        for code in }\n    }\n\n    func testPresenterMapsOtherHTTPCodesToOther() {\n        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .httpStatus(code: 418))\n        XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, ```json
{
  "command": "git add MovieSwift.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift Packages/Backend/Sources/Backend/services/APIService.swift Packages/Backend/Tests/BackendTests/APIServiceTests.swift Shared/flux/actions/MoviesActions.swift Shared/flux/reducers/MoviesReducer.swift Shared/flux/state/MoviesState.swift MovieSwiftTests/MoviesListLoadingStateTests.swift Shared/flux/state/MoviesListLoadingState.swift && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nfeat(network): surface TMDB errors with inline retry on home menu lists\n\n`case .failure(_): break` swallowed every TMDB error. A 401 from a\nbad API key, a 429 rate limit, an offline device, and a 500 from\nTMDB all looked the same: an empty list, a spinner that never\nresolved, no signal to the user that anything was wrong. This\nestablishes a pattern for surfacing those failures and retries it\non the most-visited lists (Popular / Top Rated / Upcoming / Now\nPlaying / Trending). The other fetchers (FetchDetail, FetchSearch,\netc.) follow in subsequent commits.\n\nAPIService.APIError gains three richer cases:\n- `offline` for URLError.notConnectedToInternet (and the related\n  networkConnectionLost / dataNotAllowed / internationalRoamingOff\n  codes), so the UI can show \"you're offline\" instead of a generic\n  network message.\n- `rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds:)` for HTTP 429, parsing the\n  Retry-After header into seconds when present so the message can\n  be specific (\"Try again in 12 seconds\").\n- `httpStatus(code:)` for any other non-2xx response. Without this\n  a 401 from a bad API key was masquerading as jsonDecodingError —\n  TMDB's error body shape doesn't decode into the requested\n  success type.\n\nThe GET path now checks transport errors (and matches against\noffline-class URLError codes) before checking HTTPURLResponse\nstatus codes. 7 new APIServiceTests cover 401, 500, 429 with and\nwithout Retry-After, offline mapping, non-offline URLError\npreservation, the 200 happy path, and Retry-After parsing edge\ncases.\n\nShared/flux/state/MoviesListLoadingState.swift holds the\npure-logic types and translator. MoviesListLoadingState is\n.loading or .failed(MoviesListLoadFailure), with the failure\ncarrying a kind enum, user-facing message, and retry button title.\nMoviesListLoadFailurePresenter is the APIError → MoviesListLoadFailure\ntranslator, scoped per failure mode: missingAPIKey/unauthorized/\nforbidden flip the CTA to \"Open Settings\", server / decode / other\nall retry, rateLimited message includes singular/plural seconds.\n\nMoviesState gets a transient `moviesListLoadingState: [MoviesMenu:\nMoviesListLoadingState]` dict. Excluded from CodingKeys so it\ndoesn't persist — error states should die with the app session.\nThe reducer:\n- SetMoviesMenuListLoading sets .loading (used by the dispatch\n  prelude in FetchMoviesMenuList so the banner clears across a\n  retry).\n- SetMoviesMenuListFailure sets .failed.\n- SetMovieMenuList (success) clears the entry on the way through,\n  so a successful retry banishes the banner without an extra\n  round-trip.\n\nMoviesHomeList renders a steam_rust-tinted banner above the list\nwhen the menu's loading state is .failed, with an icon that\nadapts to the failure kind (wifi.slash for offline, hourglass for\nrate-limited, key.slash for auth/missing-key, etc.) and a one-tap\nretry that re-dispatches FetchMoviesMenuList. Shipped as `4ef53de`. Summary:

**What changed**

- **`Packages/Backend/Sources/Backend/services/APIService.swift`** — `APIError` gains three richer cases:
  - `offline` for `URLError.notConnectedToInternet` (and the related `networkConnectionLost` / `dataNotAllowed` / `internationalRoamingOff` codes).
  - `rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds:)` for HTTP 429, parsing `Retry-After` into seconds when present.
  - `httpStatus(code:)` for any other non-2xx — without this a 401 from a bad API key was masquerading as `jsonDecodingError`.
  
  `GET()` now checks transport errors first (with offline-class detection), then HTTPURLResponse status, before attempting to decode.

- **`Shared/flux/state/MoviesListLoadingState.swift`** — pure-logic types. `MoviesListLoadingState` is `.loading` or `.failed(MoviesListLoadFailure)`; the failure carries a `kind` enum (offline / rateLimited / missingAPIKey / server / unauthorized / forbidden / decode / other), user-facing `message`, and `retryActionTitle`. `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter` translates `APIError` to that — `missingAPIKey`/`unauthorized`/`forbidden` flip the CTA to "Open Settings", `rateLimited` produces "Try again in 12 seconds" / "in a moment" / "in 1 second" with proper grammar.

- **`Shared/flux/state/MoviesState.swift`** — added transient `moviesListLoadingState: [MoviesMenu: MoviesListLoadingState]` dict. Excluded from `CodingKeys` so error states don't persist across launches.

- **`Shared/flux/actions/MoviesActions.swift`** — `FetchMoviesMenuList.execute` now dispatches `SetMoviesMenuListLoading` first, then on completion either `SetMovieMenuList` (success) or `SetMoviesMenuListFailure(failure: presenter.failure(from: error))`. Two new action types added.

- **`Shared/flux/reducers/MoviesReducer.swift`** — handles the two new actions and clears the loading-state entry on successful `SetMovieMenuList` so the banner disappears on retry success without another round-trip.

- **`MoviesHomeList.swift`** — adds an inline `MoviesListErrorBanner` shown above the list when the menu's loading state is `.failed`. Steam-rust tinted card with a kind-adaptive icon (`wifi.slash` / `hourglass` / `key.slash` / `exclamationmark.icloud` / etc.), the failure message, and a one-tap retry button that re-dispatches the fetch.

- **Tests** — 7 new in `APIServiceTests` (HTTP 401/500/429 with and without Retry-After, offline mapping, non-offline URLError preservation, 200 happy path, retry-after parsing edge cases) + 15 new in `MoviesListLoadingStateTests` (every APIError branch in the presenter, reducer transitions, success-clears-failure, per-menu independence).

All 3 targets build clean. **Suite is now 330/330 in the app + 17/17 in Backend (was 315/315 + 10/10).** 

Out of scope for this commit (still on the legacy `case .failure(_): break` path): `FetchDetail`, `FetchSearch`, `FetchSimilar`, `FetchRecommended`, `FetchVideos`, `FetchMovieReviews`, `FetchGenres`, `FetchRandomDiscover`. The pattern is established now — extending it to those is mechanical.

Last item from the original priority list is **MetricKit crash reporting** — 1 hour, Apple-native, no SDK. Want me to do that next, or extend the error-handling pattern to one of the other fetchers (Discover is the next-most-visible)?

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/actions/MoviesActions.swift",
  "old_string": "    /// Marks `list`'s home menu as loading. Reducer should clear any\n    /// existing failure for that menu so the UI doesn't show a stale\n    /// error banner across a retry.\n    struct SetMoviesMenuListLoading: Action {\n        let list: MoviesMenu\n    }\n\n    /// Records a failed home-menu fetch so the UI can show an inline\n    /// error + retry banner. Reducer stores under\n    /// `moviesListLoadingState[list]`; success clears the entry.\n    struct SetMoviesMenuListFailure: Action {\n        let list: MoviesMenu\n        let failure: MoviesListLoadFailure\n    }",
  "new_string": "    /// Generic per-fetcher loading-state transition. `state == nil`\n    /// clears the entry — used on success to remove a stale\n    /// `.loading` or `.failed` from the dict so any error banner the\n    /// UI was showing disappears. Passing `.loading` marks the start\n    /// of a request; `.failed(...)` records a translated APIError.\n    ///\n    /// Replaces the earlier per-fetcher `Set<X>Loading` /\n    /// `Set<X>Failure` action pairs that were starting to multiply\n    /// once the home-menu pattern was extended to every async\n    /// fetcher in the app.\n    struct SetLoadingState: Action {\n        let key: LoadingKey\n        let state: MoviesListLoadingState?\n    }\n\n    /// Wraps an APIService completion handler with the loading-state\n    /// dispatches: marks `key` as `.loading` synchronously when\n    /// called, then on the result either dispatches\n    /// `.failed(translatedFailure)` or invokes `onSuccess` and clears\n    /// the entry. Caller passes the returned closure as the\n    /// completion handler to `APIService.shared.GET(...)`.\n    static func makeTrackedHandler<T>(\n        key: LoadingKey,\n        dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction,\n        onSuccess: @escaping (T) -> Void\n    ) -> (Result<T, APIService.APIError>) -> Void {\n        dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .loading))\n        return { result in\n            switch result {\n            case let .success(value):\n                onSuccess(value)\n                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: nil))\n            case let .failure(error):\n                let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: error)\n                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .failed(failure)))\n            }\n        }\n    }"
}

> AGENT

The pre-existing PeopleActions tests overwrite their captured action on every dispatch, so an extra trailing `SetLoadingState(nil)` clobbers the captured `SetDetail`. Reorder `makeTrackedHandler` to clear the loading state *before* invoking `onSuccess` — UX-equivalent and lets existing tests pass without modification:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01SGGfuVyemAR4CyMXEHNDpQ
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/actions/MoviesActions.swift",
  "old_string": "    /// Wraps an APIService completion handler with the loading-state\n    /// dispatches: marks `key` as `.loading` synchronously when\n    /// called, then on the result either dispatches\n    /// `.failed(translatedFailure)` or invokes `onSuccess` and clears\n    /// the entry. Caller passes the returned closure as the\n    /// completion handler to `APIService.shared.GET(...)`.\n    static func makeTrackedHandler<T>(\n        key: LoadingKey,\n        dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction,\n        onSuccess: @escaping (T) -> Void\n    ) -> (Result<T, APIService.APIError>) -> Void {\n        dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .loading))\n        return { result in\n            switch result {\n            case let .success(value):\n                onSuccess(value)\n                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: nil))\n            case let .failure(error):\n                let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: error)\n                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .failed(failure)))\n            }\n        }\n    }",
  "new_string": "    /// Wraps an APIService completion handler with the loading-state\n    /// dispatches: marks `key` as `.loading` synchronously when\n    /// called, then on the result either dispatches\n    /// `.failed(translatedFailure)` or invokes `onSuccess`. Caller\n    /// passes the returned closure as the completion handler to\n    /// `APIService.shared.GET(...)`.\n    ///\n    /// On success the loading-state entry is cleared *before*\n    /// `onSuccess` runs. Order is UX-equivalent (both dispatches run\n    /// in the same callback tick) but matters for tests that capture\n    /// the most-recently-dispatched action — those tests are about\n    /// the data action, not the loading bookkeeping.\n    static func makeTrackedHandler<T>(\n        key: LoadingKey,\n        dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction,\n        onSuccess: @escaping (T) -> Void\n    ) -> (Result<T, APIService.APIError>) -> Void {\n        dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .loading))\n        return { result in\n            switch result {\n            case let .success(value):\n                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: nil))\n                onSuccess(value)\n            case let .failure(error):\n                let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: error)\n                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .failed(failure)))\n            }\n        }\n    }"
}

> AGENT

Shipped as `fddbd29`. Summary:

**The pattern**

- **`SetLoadingState(key: LoadingKey, state: MoviesListLoadingState?)`** — single generic action. Nil-state clears the entry, used on success to remove the loading/failed banner.
- **`LoadingKey`** — Hashable enum unifying all 19 fetcher contexts (13 Movies + 6 People). Movies side: `homeMenu / movieDetail / recommended / similar / videos / search / searchKeyword / moviesGenre / movieReviews / moviesWithCrew / moviesWithKeyword / randomDiscover / genres`. People side: `personDetail / personImages / personMovieCredits / movieCasts / peopleSearch / popularPeople`.
- **`MoviesState.loadingStates: [LoadingKey: MoviesListLoadingState]`** — single transient dict, kept in MoviesState because `moviesStateReducer` is the natural single owner.
- **`MoviesActions.makeTrackedHandler(key:dispatch:onSuccess:)`** — wraps an APIService completion handler with `.loading` → `.failed` or `.cleared + onSuccess` dispatches. Each fetcher becomes ~5 lines instead of a switch with a silent failure branch.

**Coverage**

All 19 fetchers in `MoviesActions` and `PeopleActions` now dispatch `SetLoadingState` transitions. `FetchPopular` keeps its existing `PopularRequestStarted` / `PopularRequestFailed` actions (Fan Club's existing per-page retry depends on those) and layers the generic tracking on top.

**UI integration**

The `MoviesListErrorBanner` moved into `Shared/views/` so multiple views can render the same component. Banners now appear in:

- **MoviesHomeList** — already had it; migrated to `.homeMenu(menu)`.
- **MovieDetail** — replaces the generic "Movie not available" fallback when `FetchDetail` fails.
- **PeopleDetail** — at the top of both the iOS List and macOS ScrollView.
- **DiscoverView** — both iOS ZStack and the macOS card-deck layout, plus the empty/loading state.
- **GenresList** — at the top of both iOS and macOS bodies.

Lower-priority views (per-genre / per-keyword / per-crew lists, search, reviews) still get their loading-state tracked at the action layer — adding banner UI to those is mechanical follow-up work.

**Test impact**

- `MoviesListLoadingStateTests` migrated to the generic action shape; added a test verifying Movies and People keys coexist in the same dict without colliding.
- `PeopleActionsTests`' five `DoesNotDispatchOnFailure` tests updated to ignore `SetLoadingState` dispatches and assert specifically against the data action (`SetDetail`, `SetImages`, etc.). The `testFetchPopularDispatchesPopularRequestFailedOnFailure` test switches to `.contains` / `.compactMap` so additional dispatched actions don't break the assertions.
- `makeTrackedHandler` dispatches the nil-clear *before* invoking `onSuccess` — UX-equivalent (same callback tick) but lets existing capture-last-action tests pass without modification.

**Final**: 331/331 app tests + 30/30 Backend tests pass across iOS / macOS / tvOS. All 3 targets build clean.

  "content": "//\n//  CrashReportStore.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  On-device persistence for MetricKit crash + metric payloads.\n//\n//  Pure logic so the directory composition, write behaviour, and\n//  filename format can be unit-tested with a temp directory. The\n//  MetricKit subscriber (`MetricKitCrashReporter`) wires to the\n//  production helpers; tests pass an explicit directory.\n//\n//  Files land at <Documents>/CrashReports/<kind>-<UTC-date>-<short-uuid>.json\n//  so:\n//   - Sorting alphabetically also sorts chronologically.\n//   - The user can find them by their app container in Files.app\n//     (iOS) or via Xcode > Devices and Simulators > Download\n//     Container (iOS device) / ~/Library/Containers/<bundle>/...\n//     (macOS sandbox).\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum CrashReportKind: String {\n    case diagnostic\n    case metric\n}\n\nenum CrashReportStore {\n\n    enum WriteError: LocalizedError {\n        case directoryUnavailable\n        case writeFailed(underlying: Error)\n\n        var errorDescription: String? {\n            switch self {\n            case .directoryUnavailable:\n                return \"Couldn't resolve the Documents directory for crash reports.\"\n            case .writeFailed(let underlying):\n                return \"Couldn't write crash report: \\(underlying.localizedDescription)\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the on-device directory used to store crash reports.\n    /// Returns nil only when the user-domain Documents directory\n    /// can't be resolved at all (very rare in practice).\n    static func resolvedDirectory(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {\n        guard let docs = try? fileManager.url(for: .documentDirectory,\n                                              in: .userDomainMask,\n                                              appropriateFor: nil,\n                                              create: false) else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        return docs.appendingPathComponent(\"CrashReports\", isDirectory: true)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Filename composition\n\n    /// Composes a filename for a payload. Combines kind, ISO-style\n    /// UTC timestamp, and a short suffix for uniqueness so two\n    /// payloads delivered in the same second don't collide. Sorts\n    /// alphabetically === chronologically because the timestamp is\n    /// fixed-width.\n    static func filename(for kind: CrashReportKind,\n                         date: Date,\n                         suffix: String,\n                         calendar: Calendar = .init(identifier: .gregorian),\n                         timeZone: TimeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0) ?? .current) -> String {\n        let formatter = DateFormatter()\n        formatter.calendar = calendar\n        formatter.timeZone = timeZone\n        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: \"en_US_POSIX\")\n        formatter.dateFormat = \"yyyy-MM-dd-HHmmss\"\n        let stamp = formatter.string(from: date)\n        return \"\\(kind.rawValue)-\\(stamp)-\\(suffix).json\"\n    }\n\n    /// Default short suffix: 8 hex characters from a UUID. Stable in\n    /// length so filenames sort cleanly.\n    static func defaultSuffix() -> String {\n        String(UUID().uuidString.replacingOccurrences(of: \"-\", with: \"\").prefix(8))\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Write\n\n    /// Writes a payload into `directory`. Creates intermediate\n    /// directories. Returns the URL the payload was written to.\n    @discardableResult\n    static func write(payload: Data,\n                      kind: CrashReportKind,\n                      to directory: URL,\n                      date: Date = Date(),\n                      suffix: String = defaultSuffix(),\n                      fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> URL {\n        do {\n            try fileManager.createDirectory(at: directory,\n                                            withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n            let url = directory.appendingPathComponent(\n                filename(for: kind, date: date, suffix: suffix)\n            )\n            try payload.write(to: url, options: [.atomic])\n            return url\n        } catch {\n            throw WriteError.writeFailed(underlying: error)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: writes to the resolved Documents\n    /// directory. Throws `directoryUnavailable` when there's no\n    /// Documents directory.\n    @discardableResult\n    static func writeToDefaultDirectory(payload: Data,\n                                        kind: CrashReportKind,\n                                        date: Date = Date(),\n                                        fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> URL {\n        guard let directory = resolvedDirectory(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            throw WriteError.directoryUnavailable\n        }\n        return try write(payload: payload,\n                         kind: kind,\n                         to: directory,\n                         date: date,\n                         fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - List\n\n    /// Lists URLs of stored reports in `directory`, sorted by\n    /// filename (chronologically given the fixed timestamp prefix).\n    /// Returns empty when the directory doesn't exist yet — that's\n    /// the normal \"no reports captured yet\" case.\n    static func listReports(in directory: URL,\n                            fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [URL] {\n        guard let contents = try? fileManager.contentsOfDirectory(\n            at: directory,\n            includingPropertiesForKeys: nil\n        ) else {\n            return []\n        }\n        return contents\n            .filter { $0.pathExtension == \"json\" }\n            .sorted { $0.lastPathComponent < $1.lastPathComponent }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: lists from the resolved directory.\n    static func listReportsInDefaultDirectory(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [URL] {\n        guard let directory = resolvedDirectory(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            return []\n        }\n        return listReports(in: directory, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the count of stored reports. Convenience for\n    /// surfacing in the Settings UI.\n    static func countOfStoredReports(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Int {\n        listReportsInDefaultDirectory(fileManager: fileManager).count\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MetricKitCrashReporter.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  MetricKitCrashReporter.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Apple-native crash reporting via MetricKit. No third-party SDK,\n//  no transmission — payloads are written to <Documents>/CrashReports/\n//  for local inspection.\n//\n//  Hook in once at app launch by calling\n//  `MetricKitCrashReporter.shared.startObserving()`. The reporter\n//  retains itself as a long-lived singleton because MetricKit\n//  doesn't retain its subscribers, and we want delivery whenever it\n//  happens (typically up to once per ~24 hours, often when the app\n//  is re-opened after a crash).\n//\n//  MetricKit isn't available on tvOS. The code paths here compile\n//  to a no-op there so the app entry point doesn't need a platform\n//  branch.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n#if canImport(MetricKit) && !os(tvOS)\nimport MetricKit\n#endif\n\n#if canImport(MetricKit) && !os(tvOS)\n\nfinal class MetricKitCrashReporter: NSObject, MXMetricManagerSubscriber {\n    static let shared = MetricKitCrashReporter()\n\n    private var isObserving = false\n\n    /// Subscribes to MetricKit. Idempotent — calling twice doesn't\n    /// re-register.\n    func startObserving() {\n        guard !isObserving else { return }\n        MXMetricManager.shared.add(self)\n        isObserving = true\n    }\n\n    /// Unsubscribes. Useful for tests; production typically never\n    /// stops observing.\n    func stopObserving() {\n        guard isObserving else { return }\n        MXMetricManager.shared.remove(self)\n        isObserving = false\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - MXMetricManagerSubscriber\n\n    /// Daily aggregated metric payloads. Delivered roughly once per\n    /// day per the framework contract.\n    func didReceive(_ payloads: [MXMetricPayload]) {\n        for payload in payloads {\n            let data = payload.jsonRepresentation()\n            guard !data.isEmpty else { continue }\n            try? CrashReportStore.writeToDefaultDirectory(payload: data, kind: .metric)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Diagnostic payloads (crashes, hangs, CPU exceptions, disk\n    /// write exceptions). Available since iOS 14 / macOS 12.\n    @available(iOS 14.0, macOS 12.0, *)\n    func didReceive(_ payloads: [MXDiagnosticPayload]) {\n        for payload in payloads {\n            let data = payload.jsonRepresentation()\n            guard !data.isEmpty else { continue }\n            try? CrashReportStore.writeToDefaultDirectory(payload: data, kind: .diagnostic)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#else\n\n/// tvOS doesn't ship MetricKit. Provide an API-compatible stub so\n/// the app entry point can call `startObserving()` unconditionally\n/// without a platform branch at the call site.\nfinal class MetricKitCrashReporter {\n    static let shared = MetricKitCrashReporter()\n    func startObserving() {}\n    func stopObserving() {}\n}\n\n#endif\n"
}

  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CrashReportStoreTests.swift",
  "content": "import XCTest\n#if os(tvOS)\n@testable import MovieSwiftTV\n#elseif os(macOS)\n@testable import Film_O_Matic\n#else\n@testable import MovieSwift\n#endif\n\nfinal class CrashReportStoreTests: XCTestCase {\n\n    private var tempContainer: URL!\n\n    override func setUpWithError() throws {\n        try super.setUpWithError()\n        tempContainer = FileManager.default\n            .temporaryDirectory\n            .appendingPathComponent(\"CrashReportStoreTests-\\(UUID().uuidString)\",\n                                    isDirectory: true)\n        // Don't pre-create — `write` should create on demand.\n    }\n\n    override func tearDownWithError() throws {\n        if let tempContainer {\n            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: tempContainer)\n        }\n        tempContainer = nil\n        try super.tearDownWithError()\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Filename composition\n\n    func testFilenameUsesUTCISODateAndKnownSuffix() {\n        var components = DateComponents()\n        components.year = 2026\n        components.month = 5\n        components.day = 3\n        components.hour = 14\n        components.minute = 30\n        components.second = 7\n\n        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)\n        let utc = TimeZone(identifier: \"UTC\")!\n        calendar.timeZone = utc\n        let date = calendar.date(from: components)!\n\n        let name = CrashReportStore.filename(for: .diagnostic,\n                                             date: date,\n                                             suffix: \"abc12345\",\n                                             calendar: calendar,\n                                             timeZone: utc)\n        XCTAssertEqual(name, \"diagnostic-2026-05-03-143007-abc12345.json\")\n    }\n\n    func testFilenameDifferentiatesKinds() {\n        let date = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_000_000)\n        let metric = CrashReportStore.filename(for: .metric, date: date, suffix: \"x\")\n        let diagnostic = CrashReportStore.filename(for: .diagnostic, date: date, suffix: \"x\")\n\n        XCTAssertTrue(metric.hasPrefix(\"metric-\"))\n        XCTAssertTrue(diagnostic.hasPrefix(\"diagnostic-\"))\n    }\n\n    func testFilenamesWithSequentialDatesSortChronologically() {\n        // Filenames are designed so alphabetical sort produces\n        // chronological order. Verify with two dates a minute apart.\n        let earlier = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_000_000)\n        let later = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_000_060)\n\n        let a = CrashReportStore.filename(for: .diagnostic, date: earlier, suffix: \"00000000\")\n        let b = CrashReportStore.filename(for: .diagnostic, date: later, suffix: \"00000000\")\n\n        XCTAssertLessThan(a, b)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Default suffix\n\n    func testDefaultSuffixIsEightCharacters() {\n        // Stable length keeps filenames sorting cleanly even when\n        // multiple payloads land in the same second.\n        let suffix = CrashReportStore.defaultSuffix()\n        XCTAssertEqual(suffix.count, 8)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Write\n\n    func testWriteCreatesIntermediateDirectoriesAndStoresPayload() throws {\n        let payload = Data(\"{\\\"hello\\\":\\\"world\\\"}\".utf8)\n        let url = try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload,\n                                              kind: .diagnostic,\n                                              to: tempContainer,\n                                              suffix: \"deadbeef\")\n\n        XCTAssertTrue(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: tempContainer.path),\n                      \"Write should have created the directory\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path),\n                      \"Write should have created the payload file\")\n\n        let readBack = try Data(contentsOf: url)\n        XCTAssertEqual(readBack, payload)\n    }\n\n    func testWriteWrapsUnderlyingErrorsInWriteFailed() {\n        // Pointing the directory at a non-creatable location forces\n        // a failure. /dev/null/foo isn't a valid URL we can create\n        // a directory under, so write() should throw.\n        let invalid = URL(fileURLWithPath: \"/dev/null/CrashReportStoreTests/should-fail\")\n\n        XCTAssertThrowsError(\n            try CrashReportStore.write(payload: Data(),\n                                        kind: .diagnostic,\n                                        to: invalid)\n        ) { error in\n            guard case CrashReportStore.WriteError.writeFailed = error else {\n                XCTFail(\"Expected writeFailed, got \\(error)\")\n                return\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - List\n\n    func testListReportsReturnsOnlyJSONFilesSortedAlphabetically() throws {\n        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: tempContainer,\n                                                withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n        // Three valid reports + one stray non-JSON file that should\n        // be filtered out.\n        try Data().write(to: tempContainer.appendingPathComponent(\"metric-2026-05-03-100000-aaaaaaaa.json\"))\n        try Data().write(to: tempContainer.appendingPathComponent(\"diagnostic-2026-05-03-090000-bbbbbbbb.json\"))\n        try Data().write(to: tempContainer.appendingPathComponent(\"metric-2026-05-03-110000-cccccccc.json\"))\n        try Data().write(to: tempContainer.appendingPathComponent(\"README.txt\"))\n\n        let urls = CrashReportStore.listReports(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertEqual(urls.count, 3, \"Non-JSON files should be filtered out\")\n        XCTAssertEqual(urls.map(\\.lastPathComponent), [\n            \"diagnostic-2026-05-03-090000-bbbbbbbb.json\",\n            \"metric-2026-05-03-100000-aaaaaaaa.json\",\n            \"metric-2026-05-03-110000-cccccccc.json\",\n        ], \"Listed reports must sort by filename, which sorts chronologically\")\n    }\n\n    func testListReportsReturnsEmptyWhenDirectoryDoesNotExist() {\n        // Brand-new install case: directory hasn't been created yet,\n        // no payloads have been received. Should return [] cleanly\n        // rather than throwing.\n        let urls = CrashReportStore.listReports(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertEqual(urls, [])\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - End-to-end: write multiple, list back\n\n    func testWriteThenListReturnsAllPayloadsInOrder() throws {\n        let payload = Data(\"{}\".utf8)\n\n        let earlierDate = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_000_000)\n        let laterDate = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_001_000)\n\n        try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload, kind: .metric,\n                                    to: tempContainer,\n                                    date: laterDate,\n                                    suffix: \"cccccccc\")\n        try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload, kind: .metric,\n                                    to: tempContainer,\n                                    date: earlierDate,\n                                    suffix: \"aaaaaaaa\")\n        try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload, kind: .diagnostic,\n                                    to: tempContainer,\n                                    date: earlierDate,\n                                    suffix: \"bbbbbbbb\")\n\n        let urls = CrashReportStore.listReports(in: tempContainer)\n        let names = urls.map(\\.lastPathComponent)\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(names.count, 3)\n        // diagnostic-...-1700000000... < metric-...-1700000000... < metric-...-1700001000...\n        XCTAssertTrue(names[0].hasPrefix(\"diagnostic-\"))\n        XCTAssertTrue(names[1].hasPrefix(\"metric-\"))\n        XCTAssertLessThan(names[1], names[2])\n    }\n}\n"
}

Shipped as `c032669`. Summary:

**What changed**

- **`Shared/flux/state/CrashReportStore.swift`** — pure-logic enum with directory resolution, filename composition, atomic write, and JSON-only list. Filenames are `<kind>-<UTC-iso-date>-<short-uuid>.json` so alphabetical sort equals chronological sort. Production helpers wrap the resolved Documents directory; testable helpers take an explicit URL for temp-dir test isolation.

- **`Shared/flux/state/MetricKitCrashReporter.swift`** — `MXMetricManagerSubscriber` singleton. `startObserving()` is idempotent. Both `didReceive([MXMetricPayload])` (daily aggregates) and `didReceive([MXDiagnosticPayload])` (crashes / hangs / CPU exceptions / disk-write exceptions, iOS 14+ / macOS 12+) are implemented. tvOS doesn't ship MetricKit, so the file compiles to a no-op stub there — call sites stay branch-free.

- **App entry points** (`HomeView`, `MovieSwiftMacApp`, `MovieSwiftTVApp`) — each calls `MetricKitCrashReporter.shared.startObserving()` after `startArchiving`, gated on `!isRunningUISmokeTests` so the XCUITest rig doesn't collect payloads during the suite.

- **`SettingsForm.swift`** — Debug info section adds a "Crash reports stored: N" row (both macOS card and iOS Form) reading from `CrashReportStore.countOfStoredReports()`.

- **`CrashReportStoreTests.swift`** — 9 tests: UTC-date filename composition, kind differentiation, chronological-sort invariant, default suffix length, intermediate-directory creation, error wrapping, JSON-only filtering, missing-directory empty case, and end-to-end write-then-list ordering.

All 3 targets build clean. **Suite is 340/340 (331 → 340, +9 new) plus 30/30 in Backend.**

**How to retrieve crash reports**
- **iOS device**: Xcode → Devices and Simulators → select device → click MovieSwift → ⚙ → Download Container → Show Package Contents → `AppData/Documents/CrashReports/`.
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Containers/com.scottdensmore.film-o-matic-mac/Data/Documents/CrashReports/`

Perfect. Now I have enough data. Let me compile my findings into a concise report.

## Audit Findings: String Catalog Migration Plan

### 1. Existing Localization Assets
**Status:** ✓ Clean slate. No `.xcstrings`, `.strings`, or `Localizable` files exist in the source tree.

**Info.plist Configuration:**
- **MovieSwift/Info.plist**: `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion = $(DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE)` (no `CFBundleLocalizations`)
- **MovieSwiftMac/Info.plist**: `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion = $(DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE)` (no `CFBundleLocalizations`)
- **MovieSwiftTV/Info.plist**: `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion = $(DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE)` (no `CFBundleLocalizations`)

All three app targets are ready to receive a String Catalog—no cleanup required.

### 2. Raw String Patterns (Non-Auto-Extracting)
- `Text(verbatim:)`: **0 instances**
- `LocalizedStringKey()`: **0 instances**
- `NSLocalizedString()`: **0 instances**
- `String(localized:)`: **0 instances**
- `accessibilityLabel()` with string literals: **27 instances**
- `accessibilityHint()`: **0 instances**
- `print()` calls with strings: **9 instances**
- `.alert()` definitions: **6 instances**
- `ToolbarItem` / `ToolbarItemGroup`: **11 instances**

Minimal friction. The 27 accessibility labels will require manual wrapping with `String(localized:)` post-migration, and error messages in state files (AppDataICloudBackup, AppDataImport, AppPersistence) need localization review.

### 3. Text(...) Literal Count
- **Shared/views/**: ~13 Text() calls (2 view files with Text)
- **MovieSwift/views/**: 59 view files, ~113 Text() calls (estimated)
- **MovieSwiftTV/views/**: 4 view files, sparse usage (estimated ~10 calls)
- **MovieSwiftMac**: No dedicated views (reuses Shared/views)

**Rough order of magnitude: 126+ `Text("...")` call sites** identified via grep. These will auto-extract for free once `.xcstrings` is added to each target.

### 4. Resources Phase Pattern (Shared Assets)
**Confirmed:** Fonts (FjallaOne-Regular.ttf, FHACondFrenchNC.otf, American Captain.otf) are currently wired via:
1. Single `PBXFileReference` in the project
2. Multiple `PBXBuildFile` entries linking that reference to each target's Resources phase

Example: `69FC640822C3A72F0043AB37` (FjallaOne-Regular.ttf) appears in at least 5 PBXBuildFile entries across iOS, Mac, and TV targets. We'll replicate this pattern: create one `.xcstrings` PBXFileReference, add PBXBuildFile entries for each of the three app targets' Resources phases.

### 5. String Constants Files
**Status:** None. No centralized `Strings.swift` or `Constants.swift` found. All display text is currently inline in views or computed properties in models.

### 6. Non-View Display Strings (State/Models)
**Found in Shared/flux/state/:**
- `AppDataICloudBackup.swift`: 2 error messages ("Couldn't write/read the backup: ...")
- `AppDataImport.swift`: 1 error message ("Couldn't read the export file: ...")
- `AppPersistence.swift`: 2 print statements with error context
- `CrashReportStore.swift`, `MoviesListLoadingState.swift`: Comments only (not display strings)

These 5 error strings will need explicit `String(localized:)` wrapping since they're not in view literals—they're returned/logged from state logic.

---

## Recommendation

**Scope for initial localization-scaffolding commit:**

Create the `.xcstrings` file targeting **all three app targets** (MovieSwift, MovieSwiftMac, MovieSwiftTV) and wire it into the project via PBXBuildFile entries for each target's Resources phase. This single commit should:
1. Add `Localizable.xcstrings` as a new, empty String Catalog
2. Add 3 PBXBuildFile entries pointing to it (one per target)
3. Update each target's Resources phase to include the catalog

This enables auto-extraction of the 126+ `Text("...")` literals immediately—the highest-value localization work with zero manual code changes. **Follow-up commit:** wrap the 27 accessibility labels and 5 state error messages with `String(localized:)` to include them in the catalog. This two-stage approach minimizes risk and delivers immediate value.

85	/// Translates the network-layer `APIError` into a UI-friendly
86	/// `MoviesListLoadFailure`. Pure logic so it can be unit-tested
87	/// without spinning up a SwiftUI view tree.
88	enum MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter {
89	
90	    static func failure(from error: APIService.APIError) -> MoviesListLoadFailure {
91	        switch error {
92	        case .missingAPIKey:
93	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
94	                kind: .missingAPIKey,
95	                message: "No TMDB API key is configured. Add one in Settings to load movies.",
96	                retryActionTitle: "Open Settings"
97	            )
98	        case .offline:
99	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
100	                kind: .offline,
101	                message: "You're offline. Check your connection and try again.",
102	                retryActionTitle: "Try again"
103	            )
104	        case .rateLimited(let retryAfter):
105	            let suffix: String
106	            if let retryAfter, retryAfter > 0 {
107	                let seconds = Int(retryAfter.rounded(.up))
108	                suffix = " Try again in \(seconds) second\(seconds == 1 ? "" : "s")."
109	            } else {
110	                suffix = " Try again in a moment."
111	            }
112	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(

This commit lands the scaffolding so SwiftUI's\nauto-extraction machinery starts populating Localizable.xcstrings\non every build, gives translators a place to work, and migrates\nthe user-facing error strings that don't go through Text() (and\ntherefore wouldn't auto-extract).\n\nShared/Localizable.xcstrings is the empty source-of-truth catalog,\nreferenced from the iOS, macOS, and tvOS app targets the same way\nfonts and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy are: one PBXFileReference, three\nPBXBuildFile entries, one Resources phase entry per target.\n\nMovieSwiftConfig.xcconfig flips two build settings on for every\nconfig that inherits from it:\n- SWIFT_EMIT_LOC_STRINGS = YES so the Swift compiler writes a\n  per-source-file .stringsdata sidecar with each Text(\"...\") /\n  Button(\"...\") / etc. that takes a LocalizedStringKey.\n- LOCALIZATION_PREFERS_STRING_CATALOGS = YES so the build system\n  merges those .stringsdata into Localizable.xcstrings instead of\n  generating legacy .strings files.\n\nVerified post-build: extraction is running. e.g.\nOnboardingView.stringsdata captures \"Welcome to MovieSwift\",\n\"Step %lld of %lld\", and the rest of the wizard's literals.\nxcstringstool compile --dry-run executes against the catalog on\nevery build. Opening the project in Xcode IDE will populate the\ncatalog with the harvested keys; from the command line the\n.stringsdata sidecars are already enough for runtime lookup.\n\nMigrated the four error-description surfaces that don't go\nthrough SwiftUI Text() (and therefore wouldn't auto-extract):\nAppDataICloudBackup.BackupError, AppDataImport.ImportError,\nAppStatePersistedFormat.LoadError, and the MoviesListLoadFailure\npresenter — eight messages plus the \"Try again\" / \"Open Settings\"\ndefault retry titles. Each gets a comment explaining the context\nfor translators and what interpolated values represent.\n\nExisting MoviesListLoadingState tests continue to pass (340/340)\nbecause String(localized:) returns the source text when no\ntranslation exists, so the .lowercased().contains(\"offline\")-style\nassertions still match.\n\nOut of scope: wrapping the 27 accessibilityLabel string literals\n(those auto-extract since they take StringProtocol that wraps\nLocalizedStringKey when given a literal). Followups can extend\nthe catalog with rate-limit pluralization (move to Apple's\nstringsdict-style %#@seconds@ format) once the catalog is being\nedited in Xcode IDE.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
  "description": "Commit localization scaffolding"
}

153	        // If the file is in iCloud and not yet downloaded, ask iCloud

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataICloudBackup.swift",
  "old_string": "    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and\n    /// reads from there. Throws `iCloudUnavailable` if there's no\n    /// container.\n    static func readBackupFromICloud(fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            throw BackupError.iCloudUnavailable\n        }\n        return try readBackup(from: url, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and\n    /// reads from there. Throws `iCloudUnavailable` if there's no\n    /// container.\n    static func readBackupFromICloud(fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            throw BackupError.iCloudUnavailable\n        }\n        return try readBackup(from: url, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Previous-version handling\n    //\n    // iCloud Drive automatically retains version history for every\n    // file in a CloudKit-backed container. NSFileVersion wraps that\n    // history so the user can restore a backup from before today's\n    // overwrite — e.g. they accidentally Cleared all their data,\n    // then Backed up the empty state, and want to recover yesterday's\n    // backup. Conflict versions (created when two devices back up\n    // simultaneously) live in the same list and need explicit\n    // resolution after the user picks a winner.\n\n    /// User-facing description of one available backup version.\n    /// Wraps the underlying `NSFileVersion` so the caller can\n    /// invoke `readBackup(at:)` / `restoreVersion(_:to:)` without\n    /// re-querying the version list.\n    struct BackupVersionInfo: Identifiable {\n        /// Stable id for SwiftUI ForEach. The version's URL path is\n        /// unique across the version list and stays valid for the\n        /// version's lifetime.\n        let id: String\n        let modificationDate: Date\n        /// Name of the device that wrote this version, when iCloud\n        /// has it. Used to disambiguate conflict versions (\"Backup\n        /// from Scott's MacBook\" vs \"Backup from Scott's iPhone\").\n        let computerName: String?\n        /// True for the current \"winning\" version that\n        /// `readBackupFromICloud` would otherwise return.\n        let isCurrent: Bool\n        /// True when this version is part of an unresolved conflict\n        /// (two devices wrote at the same time). Picking it for\n        /// restore should also mark all other unresolved versions\n        /// as resolved so iCloud stops surfacing the conflict.\n        let isUnresolvedConflict: Bool\n        /// The underlying NSFileVersion. Held strongly so the URL\n        /// stays valid until the caller is done with it.\n        let version: NSFileVersion\n    }\n\n    /// Lists every version of the backup file at `fileURL` — the\n    /// current one plus historical and conflict versions — sorted\n    /// newest-first. Returns `[]` if the file doesn't exist yet.\n    static func availableVersions(at fileURL: URL,\n                                  fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [BackupVersionInfo] {\n        guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else {\n            return []\n        }\n        var infos: [BackupVersionInfo] = []\n        if let current = NSFileVersion.currentVersionOfItem(at: fileURL) {\n            infos.append(makeInfo(from: current,\n                                  isCurrent: true,\n                                  isUnresolvedConflict: false))\n        }\n        let unresolved = Set((NSFileVersion.unresolvedConflictVersionsOfItem(at: fileURL) ?? [])\n            .compactMap { $0.url.path })\n        for version in NSFileVersion.otherVersionsOfItem(at: fileURL) ?? [] {\n            infos.append(makeInfo(from: version,\n                                  isCurrent: false,\n                                  isUnresolvedConflict: unresolved.contains(version.url.path)))\n        }\n        return infos.sorted { ($0.modificationDate ?? .distantPast) > ($1.modificationDate ?? .distantPast) }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and\n    /// lists versions there. Returns `[]` if iCloud is unavailable\n    /// or no backup exists yet.\n    static func resolvedAvailableVersions(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [BackupVersionInfo] {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            return []\n        }\n        return availableVersions(at: url, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n\n    /// Reads and decodes the backup envelope from a specific version\n    /// (rather than always reading the current one). Useful when the\n    /// user picks a previous backup from `availableVersions(at:)`.\n    static func readBackup(at version: NSFileVersion,\n                           fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {\n        // Same iCloud-download nudge as readBackup(from:).\n        try? fileManager.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at: version.url)\n        do {\n            let data = try Data(contentsOf: version.url)\n            return try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: data)\n        } catch let error as AppDataImport.ImportError {\n            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)\n        } catch {\n            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Marks any unresolved conflict versions at `fileURL` as\n    /// resolved. Call after the user has picked which version to\n    /// restore from — without this iCloud keeps surfacing the\n    /// conflict on every subsequent read.\n    static func markAllConflictsResolved(at fileURL: URL) {\n        guard let unresolved = NSFileVersion.unresolvedConflictVersionsOfItem(at: fileURL) else {\n            return\n        }\n        for version in unresolved {\n            version.isResolved = true\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: marks conflicts on the resolved\n    /// iCloud backup file.\n    static func resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved(fileManager: FileManager = .default) {\n        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            return\n        }\n        markAllConflictsResolved(at: url)\n    }\n\n    /// Builds a `BackupVersionInfo` from an `NSFileVersion`.\n    private static func makeInfo(from version: NSFileVersion,\n                                 isCurrent: Bool,\n                                 isUnresolvedConflict: Bool) -> BackupVersionInfo {\n        BackupVersionInfo(\n            id: version.url.absoluteString,\n            modificationDate: version.modificationDate ?? .distantPast,\n            computerName: version.localizedNameOfSavingComputer,\n            isCurrent: isCurrent,\n            isUnresolvedConflict: isUnresolvedConflict,\n            version: version\n        )\n    }\n}"
}

  "new_string": "    private func performICloudRestore() {\n        do {\n            let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackupFromICloud()\n            let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: store.state)\n            pendingImportEnvelope = envelope\n            pendingImportCounts = counts\n        } catch let error as AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError {\n            backupErrorMessage = error.errorDescription\n        } catch {\n            backupErrorMessage = \"Restore failed: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reload the version list from iCloud and present the sheet.\n    /// Called when the user taps \"Show previous backups…\" — we\n    /// re-query NSFileVersion each time rather than caching, so a\n    /// freshly-uploaded backup from another device shows up.\n    private func showPreviousICloudVersions() {\n        availableICloudVersions = AppDataICloudBackup.resolvedAvailableVersions()\n        isPreviousVersionsSheetPresented = true\n    }\n\n    /// Restore from a specific version (rather than the current one).\n    /// After reading, marks any unresolved conflicts as resolved so\n    /// iCloud stops surfacing them — the user has now picked a\n    /// winner.\n    private func restoreFromICloudVersion(_ info: AppDataICloudBackup.BackupVersionInfo) {\n        do {\n            let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(at: info.version)\n            let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: store.state)\n            pendingImportEnvelope = envelope\n            pendingImportCounts = counts\n            AppDataICloudBackup.resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved()\n            isPreviousVersionsSheetPresented = false\n        } catch let error as AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError {\n            backupErrorMessage = error.errorDescription\n        } catch {\n            backupErrorMessage = \"Restore failed: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n        }\n    }"

  "new_string": "    func testLastBackupDateReturnsModificationDate() throws {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: AppState(), to: fileURL)\n\n        let modDate = AppDataICloudBackup.lastBackupDate(at: fileURL)\n        XCTAssertNotNil(modDate)\n        if let modDate {\n            XCTAssertLessThan(abs(modDate.timeIntervalSinceNow), 5,\n                              \"Mod date should be within 5 seconds of now\")\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - availableVersions\n    //\n    // NSFileVersion-backed iCloud version history can't be set up in\n    // a unit test (it requires the iCloud file coordination\n    // machinery). These tests cover what we can: the empty-file and\n    // missing-file paths, and the shape of BackupVersionInfo for\n    // freshly written non-iCloud files.\n\n    func testAvailableVersionsReturnsEmptyWhenFileMissing() {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertFalse(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path))\n        XCTAssertTrue(AppDataICloudBackup.availableVersions(at: fileURL).isEmpty,\n                      \"Missing file should produce no versions, not crash\")\n    }\n\n    func testAvailableVersionsExposesCurrentVersionForLocalFile() throws {\n        // For a local (non-iCloud) file NSFileVersion still returns\n        // a \"current\" version with the file's modification date —\n        // verify our wrapper surfaces it as isCurrent = true and\n        // doesn't fabricate any conflict state.\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: AppState(), to: fileURL)\n\n        let versions = AppDataICloudBackup.availableVersions(at: fileURL)\n        XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(versions.count, 1,\n                                     \"A written file should yield at least one version\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(versions.contains { $0.isCurrent },\n                      \"One version should be marked current\")\n        XCTAssertFalse(versions.contains { $0.isUnresolvedConflict },\n                       \"A freshly written local file shouldn't have unresolved conflicts\")\n    }\n\n    func testReadBackupAtVersionRoundTripsLocalFile() throws {\n        let fileURL = AppDataICloudBackup.backupFileURL(in: tempContainer)\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.insert(42)\n        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackup(state: state, to: fileURL)\n\n        // Pick the \"current\" version and read through the\n        // version-aware path. Should match what readBackup(from:)\n        // would have returned.\n        let versions = AppDataICloudBackup.availableVersions(at: fileURL)\n        let current = try XCTUnwrap(versions.first(where: \\.isCurrent),\n                                     \"Expected a current version for the freshly written file\")\n\n        let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(at: current.version)\n        XCTAssertTrue(envelope.snapshot.moviesState.wishlist.contains(42),\n                      \"Reading at a specific version should return the same data as reading the file directly\")\n    }\n}"

This wires up\nNSFileVersion so users can pick a previous backup to restore from\nand so unresolved conflict versions can be cleared after the\nuser picks a winner.\n\nAppDataICloudBackup gains:\n\n- BackupVersionInfo value-type wrapping NSFileVersion with the\n  fields the UI needs: id (URL.absoluteString for stable\n  Identifiable), modificationDate, computerName from\n  localizedNameOfSavingComputer, isCurrent, and isUnresolvedConflict.\n  Holds a strong reference to the underlying NSFileVersion so its\n  URL stays valid until the caller is done.\n- availableVersions(at:) — composes\n  NSFileVersion.currentVersionOfItem + .otherVersionsOfItem +\n  .unresolvedConflictVersionsOfItem into a single newest-first\n  list. Returns [] for missing files (the brand-new install case).\n- resolvedAvailableVersions() / readBackup(at:) /\n  resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved() — production wrappers that\n  resolve the iCloud container path.\n- markAllConflictsResolved(at:) — flips\n  NSFileVersion.isResolved on every conflict so iCloud stops\n  surfacing them after the user has chosen.\n\nSettings adds a \"Show previous backups…\" row in the App data\nsection (only visible when an iCloud backup exists). It opens a\nnew PreviousICloudBackupsSheet that lists every version with\ndate + originating-device label. The current version gets a\ngold \"Latest\" pill; unresolved conflicts get a rust-coloured\n\"Conflict\" pill so the user knows why two backups exist for the\nsame minute. {

  "old_string": "    /// Returns the count of stored reports. Convenience for\n    /// surfacing in the Settings UI.\n    static func countOfStoredReports(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Int {\n        listReportsInDefaultDirectory(fileManager: fileManager).count\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "    /// Returns the count of stored reports. Convenience for\n    /// surfacing in the Settings UI.\n    static func countOfStoredReports(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Int {\n        listReportsInDefaultDirectory(fileManager: fileManager).count\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Report metadata for the in-app viewer\n\n    /// User-facing description of one stored crash report file.\n    /// Surfaces the kind, the captured date (parsed from the\n    /// filename so we don't depend on filesystem mtime), the file\n    /// size for \"is this big enough to bother sharing?\" UX hints,\n    /// and the URL for ShareLink / Data(contentsOf:).\n    struct CrashReportFile: Identifiable, Hashable {\n        /// Stable id for SwiftUI ForEach. Filename is unique within\n        /// the directory and doesn't change once written.\n        let id: String\n        let url: URL\n        let kind: CrashReportKind\n        /// Capture date encoded in the filename. Falls back to file\n        /// modification date if the filename doesn't parse for any\n        /// reason (e.g. a hand-named legacy file).\n        let date: Date\n        let sizeBytes: Int\n    }\n\n    /// Parses a filename produced by `filename(for:date:suffix:)`\n    /// back into its kind + date components. Returns nil for\n    /// unrecognised names so the caller can fall back to filesystem\n    /// metadata.\n    static func parseKindAndDate(fromFilename filename: String,\n                                 calendar: Calendar = .init(identifier: .gregorian),\n                                 timeZone: TimeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0) ?? .current)\n    -> (kind: CrashReportKind, date: Date)? {\n        // Filename shape: \"<kind>-<yyyy>-<MM>-<dd>-<HHmmss>-<suffix>.json\"\n        let stem = (filename as NSString).deletingPathExtension\n        let parts = stem.split(separator: \"-\")\n        guard parts.count >= 5,\n              let kind = CrashReportKind(rawValue: String(parts[0])) else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        let dateString = \"\\(parts[1])-\\(parts[2])-\\(parts[3])-\\(parts[4])\"\n        let formatter = DateFormatter()\n        formatter.calendar = calendar\n        formatter.timeZone = timeZone\n        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: \"en_US_POSIX\")\n        formatter.dateFormat = \"yyyy-MM-dd-HHmmss\"\n        guard let date = formatter.date(from: dateString) else { return nil }\n        return (kind, date)\n    }\n\n    /// Builds a `CrashReportFile` from a URL, reading filesystem\n    /// metadata to fill in the size and (if needed) date fields.\n    /// Returns nil if the URL doesn't point at a recognisable\n    /// crash report.\n    static func metadata(forReportAt url: URL,\n                         fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> CrashReportFile? {\n        guard let parsed = parseKindAndDate(fromFilename: url.lastPathComponent) else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        let attributes = (try? fileManager.attributesOfItem(atPath: url.path)) ?? [:]\n        let size = (attributes[.size] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0\n        return CrashReportFile(id: url.lastPathComponent,\n                               url: url,\n                               kind: parsed.kind,\n                               date: parsed.date,\n                               sizeBytes: size)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns metadata for every parseable report in `directory`,\n    /// newest-first.\n    static func listReportFiles(in directory: URL,\n                                fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [CrashReportFile] {\n        listReports(in: directory, fileManager: fileManager)\n            .compactMap { metadata(forReportAt: $0, fileManager: fileManager) }\n            .sorted { $0.date > $1.date }\n    }\n\n    /// Production convenience: lists report files from the resolved\n    /// Documents directory.\n    static func listReportFilesInDefaultDirectory(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [CrashReportFile] {\n        guard let directory = resolvedDirectory(fileManager: fileManager) else {\n            return []\n        }\n        return listReportFiles(in: directory, fileManager: fileManager)\n    }\n}"
}

  "new_string": "        let urls = CrashReportStore.listReports(in: tempContainer)\n        let names = urls.map(\\.lastPathComponent)\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(names.count, 3)\n        // diagnostic-...-1700000000... < metric-...-1700000000... < metric-...-1700001000...\n        XCTAssertTrue(names[0].hasPrefix(\"diagnostic-\"))\n        XCTAssertTrue(names[1].hasPrefix(\"metric-\"))\n        XCTAssertLessThan(names[1], names[2])\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Filename round-trip parsing\n\n    func testParseKindAndDateRoundTripsFilenamesProducedByFilename() {\n        var components = DateComponents()\n        components.year = 2026\n        components.month = 5\n        components.day = 3\n        components.hour = 9\n        components.minute = 41\n        components.second = 27\n\n        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)\n        let utc = TimeZone(identifier: \"UTC\")!\n        calendar.timeZone = utc\n        let date = calendar.date(from: components)!\n\n        for kind: CrashReportKind in [.metric, .diagnostic] {\n            let name = CrashReportStore.filename(for: kind,\n                                                  date: date,\n                                                  suffix: \"deadbeef\",\n                                                  calendar: calendar,\n                                                  timeZone: utc)\n            let parsed = CrashReportStore.parseKindAndDate(fromFilename: name,\n                                                            calendar: calendar,\n                                                            timeZone: utc)\n            XCTAssertNotNil(parsed)\n            XCTAssertEqual(parsed?.kind, kind)\n            XCTAssertEqual(parsed?.date, date,\n                           \"Round-trip date for \\(kind) should match the input\")\n        }\n    }\n\n    func testParseKindAndDateReturnsNilForUnknownFilename() {\n        XCTAssertNil(CrashReportStore.parseKindAndDate(fromFilename: \"README.txt\"))\n        XCTAssertNil(CrashReportStore.parseKindAndDate(fromFilename: \"metric.json\"),\n                     \"Filenames missing the date components should not parse\")\n        XCTAssertNil(CrashReportStore.parseKindAndDate(fromFilename: \"telemetry-2026-05-03-090000-deadbeef.json\"),\n                     \"Unknown kinds should not parse\")\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - listReportFiles\n\n    func testListReportFilesReturnsMetadataNewestFirst() throws {\n        // Three reports written at known different dates. The\n        // listing helper should return them newest-first (the\n        // filename-sorted order is reversed for date-desc).\n        let payload = Data(\"{}\".utf8)\n        let earliest = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_000_000)\n        let middle = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_000_500)\n        let latest = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_700_001_000)\n\n        try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload, kind: .diagnostic,\n                                    to: tempContainer,\n                                    date: middle,\n                                    suffix: \"bbbbbbbb\")\n        try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload, kind: .metric,\n                                    to: tempContainer,\n                                    date: latest,\n                                    suffix: \"cccccccc\")\n        try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload, kind: .metric,\n                                    to: tempContainer,\n                                    date: earliest,\n                                    suffix: \"aaaaaaaa\")\n\n        let files = CrashReportStore.listReportFiles(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertEqual(files.count, 3)\n        XCTAssertEqual(files[0].date, latest)\n        XCTAssertEqual(files[1].date, middle)\n        XCTAssertEqual(files[2].date, earliest)\n    }\n\n    func testListReportFilesReturnsEmptyWhenDirectoryMissing() {\n        // Brand-new install: directory hasn't been created yet,\n        // viewer should render the empty state, not crash.\n        let files = CrashReportStore.listReportFiles(in: tempContainer)\n        XCTAssertEqual(files, [])\n    }\n\n    func testMetadataIncludesFileSize() throws {\n        // The viewer shows \"X KB\" per row so the user has a rough\n        // idea of how big a payload is before sharing. Verify\n        // metadata reports the actual on-disk byte count.\n        let payload = Data(repeating: 0x41, count: 1234)\n        let url = try CrashReportStore.write(payload: payload,\n                                              kind: .diagnostic,\n                                              to: tempContainer,\n                                              suffix: \"deadbeef\")\n\n        let info = try XCTUnwrap(CrashReportStore.metadata(forReportAt: url))\n        XCTAssertEqual(info.sizeBytes, 1234)\n    }\n\n    func testMetadataReturnsNilForUnparseableFilename() throws {\n        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: tempContainer,\n                                                withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n        let bogus = tempContainer.appendingPathComponent(\"README.txt\")\n        try Data(\"hi\".utf8).write(to: bogus)\n\n        XCTAssertNil(CrashReportStore.metadata(forReportAt: bogus),\n                     \"Files that don't match the kind-date-suffix shape shouldn't appear in the viewer list\")\n    }\n}"
}

.contentShape(Rectangle())\n        }\n        .buttonStyle(.plain)\n        .accessibilityIdentifier(\"crashReportsSheet.row.\\(report.id)\")\n        .sheet(isPresented: $isDetailPresented) {\n JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: raw),\n               let prettyData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: parsed,\n                                                             options: [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]),\n               let pretty = String(data: prettyData, encoding: .utf8) {\n                prettyJSON = pretty\n            } else {\n                prettyJSON = String(data: raw, encoding: .utf8) ?? \"\"\n            }\n        } catch {\n            loadError = \"Couldn't read this report: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n        }\n    }\n}\n"

This\nadds a Settings sheet that lists every stored report and a detail\nview that pretty-prints the JSON, with ShareLink to send a\nreport off the device.\n\nCrashReportStore gains a CrashReportFile metadata struct (id,\nurl, kind, parsed-from-filename date, on-disk size) plus three\nnew helpers:\n\n- parseKindAndDate(fromFilename:) — round-trips a filename\n  produced by filename(for:date:suffix:) back into its kind and\n  capture date. **What changed**

- **`CrashReportStore.swift`** — added `CrashReportFile` (Identifiable, Hashable) carrying id / url / kind / parsed-from-filename date / on-disk size; `parseKindAndDate(fromFilename:)` for filename→metadata round-trip; `metadata(forReportAt:)` and `listReportFiles(in:)` / `listReportFilesInDefaultDirectory()` newest-first list helpers.

- **`Shared/views/CrashReportsView.swift`** (new) — two surfaces:
  - **`CrashReportsSheet`** — list with steam_blue (metric) / steam_rust (diagnostic) glyphs, date + kind + size per row, per-row `ShareLink`, empty-state explaining MetricKit's ~24h cadence.
  - **`CrashReportDetailView`** — pretty-printed JSON via `JSONSerialization(.sortedKeys, .prettyPrinted)`, falls back to UTF-8 raw if not valid JSON, selectable text on iOS/macOS, top-right `ShareLink`.

## Highest-Value Fixes for One Commit

1. **Add `.dynamicTypeSize() ` to all 15 custom-font sites** – Allows users with accessibility needs (large text) to have readable UI without app crashing. Impact: CRITICAL for accessibility compliance.

2. **Wrap 2 unguarded `print()` in AppPersistence.swift with `#if DEBUG`** – Prevents user-facing error logs leaking in Release builds. Impact: HIGH for app quality/professionalism.

3. **Add `.accessibilityLabel()` to 3–4 icon-only buttons (ListImage, DiscoverView, PeopleDetail toolbar)** – VoiceOver users currently hear nothing; ~5-minute fix. Impact: HIGH for accessibility baseline.

4. **Hoist 8 hardcoded RGB colors in GenresList.swift to Color.swift assets with dark variants** – Enables theme switching and future dark-mode support without refactor. Impact: MEDIUM-HIGH for maintainability.

---

**Summary:** The codebase has solid accessibility foundations (many buttons already labeled, identifiers present) but three critical gaps block shipping: missing Dynamic Type scaling, unguarded print statements, and a few unlabeled icon buttons. A targeted 1–2 hour fix addressing items 1–3 above would unlock a professional accessibility posture.

  "content": "//\n//  Font.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Created by Thomas Ricouard on 23/06/2019.\n//  Copyright © 2019 Thomas Ricouard. All rights reserved.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftUI\n\nextension Font {\n    /// Custom-font factories accept an optional `relativeTo:` so the\n    /// resulting font scales with the user's Dynamic Type setting.\n    /// Default to `.body` so existing call sites pick up scaling for\n    /// free without an audit pass — section headers and large titles\n    /// can still pass `.title` / `.largeTitle` for a more dramatic\n    /// scaling curve.\n\n    public static func FHACondFrenchNC(size: CGFloat,\n                                       relativeTo style: Font.TextStyle = .body) -> Font {\n        return Font.custom(\"FHA Condensed French NC\", size: size, relativeTo: style)\n    }\n\n    public static func AmericanCaptain(size: CGFloat,\n                                       relativeTo style: Font.TextStyle = .body) -> Font {\n        return Font.custom(\"American Captain\", size: size, relativeTo: style)\n    }\n\n    public static func FjallaOne(size: CGFloat,\n                                 relativeTo style: Font.TextStyle = .body) -> Font {\n        return Font.custom(\"FjallaOne-Regular\", size: size, relativeTo: style)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct TitleFont: ViewModifier {\n    let size: CGFloat\n\n    func body(content: Content) -> some View {\n        // .titleStyle() is used for section headings (\"Popular\n        // people\", \"Known for\", \"Fan level\", etc.) — apply the\n        // `.isHeader` accessibility trait so VoiceOver navigates\n        // the page by heading. This pairs with the FjallaOne font\n        // and 16pt title size that compose the visual heading look.\n        return content\n            .font(.FjallaOne(size: size, relativeTo: .title3))\n            .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)\n    }\n}\n\nextension View {\n    func titleFont(size: CGFloat) -> some View {\n        return ModifiedContent(content: self, modifier: TitleFont(size: size))\n    }\n\n    func titleStyle() -> some View {\n        return ModifiedContent(content: self, modifier: TitleFont(size: 16))\n    }\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Shipped as `db0c909`. Summary:

**What changed**

- **`Font.swift`** — `FjallaOne`/`AmericanCaptain`/`FHACondFrenchNC` factories each gain an optional `relativeTo: Font.TextStyle = .body` parameter and route through `Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:)`. Single-line change unlocks Dynamic Type scaling at ~15 existing call sites without touching any of them. The audit's largest accessibility gap is closed.

- **`titleStyle()`** — now applies `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)` so the 18 section headings ("Popular people", "Known for", "Cast", "Crew", "Fan level", etc.) navigate via VoiceOver's heading rotor. Also bumped its scaling anchor from `.body` to `.title3` since these are visual headings.

- **`AppPersistence.swift`** — wrapped the two error-path `print()` statements in `#if DEBUG`. The last unguarded production prints in the codebase.

- **PeopleDetail star button** — reads "Add to fan club" / "Remove from fan club" to VoiceOver depending on state. Was bare to assistive tech before.

- **CrashReportsView ShareLink** — reads "Share crash report" to VoiceOver. Was just `square.and.arrow.up` icon before.

All 3 targets build clean; suite stays at 349/349.

**Audit items deferred for follow-ups** (the commit message lists them):
- 6 hit targets smaller than 44pt (mostly star/heart toggles where the surrounding row is tappable)
- 17 force-unwraps in production code (safer fixed one-by-one)
- 8 hardcoded RGB values in `GenresList` genre cards
- `ScaledMetric` for fixed `.frame(width: N, height: N)` icon sizes (Dynamic Type now scales labels but not surrounding frames)

The original priority list is fully done. The codebase is in a good place — a `git log --oneline -20` would show 60+ commits of substantive shipped work since we started, and `git status` is clean.

The first\n        // item is the front-of-stack draggable card; everything else\n        // gets a depth-based scale + offset so the deck reads as\n        // layered. X! }` → `if let` everywhere this pattern\n  appeared. ListImage's icon binding, PeopleDetailHeaderRow's\n  known_for_department text, PeopleDetailBiographyRow's three\n  optional date/location blocks. Cosmetic on its own but\n  removes the audit's noisiest finding.\n\n- DiscoverView's `props.movies.reversed().firstIndex(of: id)!`\n  appeared twice in a row, computed on every body redraw, and\n  could realistically crash on a Pop action: the `!` ran AFTER\n  an `if firstIndex == 0` check on a different invocation, so\n  if the array mutated between the two lookups (it can —\n  PopRandomDiscover is a redux action) the second lookup would\n  return nil. []` makes\n  the contract explicit and removes a crash class for free.\n\n- MovieDetail's `availableTargets.contains(focusedDetailItem!)`\n  was guarded by a preceding `focusedDetailItem == nil` check,\n  but the check + use were on the same line behind boolean ||\n  short-circuiting, which was hard to read. Restructured into\n  three explicit branches keyed on `force` and `if let focused`.\n\n- MovieDetail's two `props.reviewsCount!` interpolations were\n  inside `if props.reviewsCount ?? 0 > 0`. Bound the unwrapped\n  value once with `if let reviewsCount = props.reviewsCount,\n  reviewsCount > 0` and used the local variable.\n\n- MoviesHome's `MoviesMenu.allCases.first!` is non-nil at compile\n  time (the enum has cases) but the canonical default is\n  `.popular` — clearer to hard-code that than to force-unwrap.\n\n- APIService's `components.url!` runs after building the URL from\n  a known-good base + path.
