what is API key proxy (backend infrastructure work)

> AGENT

Quick explanation of what it is and why I marked it as out of scope:

## What an API key proxy is

A small server you control that sits between your app and TMDB. The flow becomes:

```
[App] ──> [Your proxy at yourdomain.com/tmdb] ──> [api.themoviedb.org]
                  ↑ TMDB key attached here
```

The TMDB key lives on your server only. The app ships with **zero** TMDB credentials and just talks to your proxy URL.

## Why this matters

The current setup ships the bundled TMDB key inside the app binary. Anyone who installs the app can trivially extract it (a `strings` over the .ipa works). With that key they can:

- Burn through your TMDB rate limit / quota
- Use your key in their own apps, leaving you to take the blame if they do something abusive
- Get your account banned from TMDB if they hit one of TMDB's anti-abuse triggers

A proxy fixes all three because the key never leaves your server. The audit recently noted this:

> **API key proxy.** TMDB key is build-time substituted from `DeveloperSettings.xcconfig`, which is gitignored — good. But it ships embedded in the binary as a query parameter and is trivial to extract from any installed copy. For a personal/learning project that's fine; for production with monetization or worry about quota theft, route through a backend proxy that holds the key.

## What "backend infrastructure work" means concretely

**Server side** — none of this lives in the iOS Xcode project:
1. Pick a runtime (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Fly.io, a Linode VM — most have free tiers for personal-scale traffic)
2. Write a tiny reverse-proxy: receive requests, attach the TMDB key, forward to `api.themoviedb.org/3/...`, return the response. ~50 lines of TypeScript on Cloudflare.
3. Optionally cache popular queries (TMDB rate limits go away if you serve `/movie/popular?page=1` from your edge cache for 5 minutes)
4. Optionally rate-limit per device (some signed token or per-IP limit) so a misbehaving install can't burn your quota
5. Register a domain, set up TLS (most platforms do this for you)
6. Deploy + monitor

**iOS / macOS side** — the actual code change is tiny:
- Change `APIService`'s `baseURL` from `https://api.themoviedb.org/3` to `https://your-proxy.example.com/tmdb`
- Drop the `api_key=...` query param (the proxy attaches it server-side)
- The user-supplied TMDB key feature stays — power users can still use their own quota by switching to direct TMDB

## Why I marked it out of scope

Three reasons:

1. **It's not iOS code work.** The Xcode project changes are ~5 lines. The actual work is standing up + maintaining a server, which isn't something I can do from this shell.

2. **It only matters with non-trivial install counts.** TMDB's free tier is generous (~50 req/sec). For a hobby / showcase app you probably never hit it. Many open-source TMDB-using iOS apps have shipped with embedded keys for years without issue.

3. **It changes your operational footprint.** A server you run = monitoring, uptime, occasional debugging when TMDB changes their API or your hosting provider has an outage. A reasonable trade for a paid app; less worth it for a personal project.

## When you'd actually want to do this

- You're putting the app on the App Store and expect more than a hundred installs
- You're paying for a TMDB business tier and quota = money
- You want to add per-user features (favourites synced across devices) — at that point the proxy becomes useful for *more* than just key hiding
- You want to swap out TMDB for a different provider without updating the app — proxy abstracts that

If/when you decide to do this, the iOS-side prep I'd recommend (which I can do in 5 minutes from this shell, if you want):

1. Move the `baseURL` from a hardcoded literal in `APIService` into `MovieSwiftConfig.xcconfig` so flipping between TMDB-direct and proxy is a build-config change, not a code change.
2. Add an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header path to `APIService` so the proxy can use a signed request scheme without retrofitting the call sites.

Both are tractable now, both are useful even without a proxy in the picture. Want me to do them as a prep commit, or leave it alone until you're ready to actually stand up the proxy?

138	    public enum APIError: Error {
139	        /// No usable TMDB key from any provider in the chain.
140	        case missingAPIKey
141	        /// URLSession returned no data and no error — shouldn't happen
142	        /// in practice but kept as a safety net.
143	        case noResponse
144	        /// JSON returned by TMDB couldn't be decoded into the expected
145	        /// model. Often indicates a TMDB-side error response (which
146	        /// has a different shape) being decoded as a success type.
147	        case jsonDecodingError(error: Error)
148	        /// URLSession reported a transport-level error that wasn't a
149	        /// recognised offline condition (DNS issue, TLS failure, etc).
150	        case networkError(error: Error)
151	        /// Device is reported offline by URLSession's error code.
152	        /// Distinguished from `networkError` so the UI can show a
153	        /// "you're offline" message rather than a generic failure.
154	        case offline
155	        /// TMDB throttled the request. `retryAfterSeconds` is parsed
156	        /// from the HTTP `Retry-After` header when present.
157	        case rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: TimeInterval?)
158	        /// Any other non-2xx HTTP response. The status code tells the
159	        /// UI whether it's worth retrying (5xx) vs whether something
160	        /// is misconfigured (4xx — most commonly 401 from a bad key).
161	        case httpStatus(code: Int)

  "new_string": "public struct APIService {\n\n    /// How the API key is presented to the upstream service.\n    ///\n    /// `.queryParameter` matches TMDB v3 direct usage today: append\n    /// `api_key=<key>` to the URL. `.bearer` sends the key in an\n    /// `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header instead — used for\n    /// TMDB v4-style tokens AND for proxy deployments where the\n    /// proxy forwards a static bearer to TMDB and rejects requests\n    /// without it. New deployments can swap auth mode without\n    /// touching call sites.\n    public enum AuthMode: Equatable {\n        case queryParameter(name: String)\n        case bearer\n    }\n\n    /// Falls back to the bundled TMDB direct URL if the build hasn't\n    /// substituted `TMDB_BASE_URL` from xcconfig. Production builds\n    /// pick up the substituted value; tests that don't load the app\n    /// bundle's Info.plist get the literal default.\n    public static var defaultBaseURL: URL {\n        let fallback = URL(string: \"https://api.themoviedb.org/3\")!\n        let raw = (Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: \"TMDB_BASE_URL\") as? String) ?? \"\"\n        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        guard !trimmed.isEmpty,\n              trimmed != \"$(TMDB_BASE_URL)\",\n              let url = URL(string: trimmed) else {\n            return fallback\n        }\n        return url\n    }\n\n    public static var shared = APIService()\n    let baseURL: URL\n    let decoder: JSONDecoder\n    private let apiKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding\n    private let session: NetworkSession\n    private let callbackQueue: DispatchQueue\n    private let authMode: AuthMode\n\n    public init(\n        baseURL: URL = APIService.defaultBaseURL,\n        decoder: JSONDecoder = JSONDecoder(),\n        apiKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding = LayeredAPIKeyProvider.userKeyOverridingBundle,\n        session: NetworkSession = URLSessionNetworkSession(),\n        callbackQueue: DispatchQueue = .main,\n        authMode: AuthMode = .queryParameter(name: \"api_key\")\n    ) {\n        self.baseURL = baseURL\n        self.decoder = decoder\n        self.apiKeyProvider = apiKeyProvider\n        self.session = session\n        self.callbackQueue = callbackQueue\n        self.authMode = authMode\n    }\n\n    private var apiKey: String? {\n        apiKeyProvider.apiKey()\n    }"
}

269	        let queryURL = baseURL.appendingPathComponent(endpoint.path())
270	        var components = URLComponents(url: queryURL, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: true)!
271	        components.queryItems = [
272	           URLQueryItem(name: "api_key", value: apiKey),
273	           URLQueryItem(name: "language", value: Locale.preferredLanguages[0])
274	        ]
275	        if let params = params {
276	            for (_, value) in params.enumerated() {
277	                components.queryItems?.append(URLQueryItem(name: value.key, value: value.value))
278	            }
279	        }
280	        // `components.url` is non-nil for all the well-formed
281	        // endpoint paths we construct above — but if it ever does
282	        // come back nil (e.g. a future caller passes a path with
283	        // characters that fail percent-encoding), surface that as a
284	        // structured failure instead of crashing the request.
285	        guard let composedURL = components.url else {
286	            callbackQueue.async {
287	                completionHandler(.failure(.noResponse))
288	            }
289	            return
290	        }
291	        var request = URLRequest(url: composedURL)
292	        request.httpMethod = "GET"
293	        let task = session.dataTask(with: request) { (data, response, error) in
294	            // Transport-level error first — distinguishes "device is
295	            // offline" from other failures so the UI can surface a
296	            // tailored message.
297	            if let error {
298	                let nsError = error as NSError
299	                if nsError.domain == NSURLErrorDomain
300	                    && APIService.offlineURLErrorCodes.contains(nsError.code) {
301	                    callbackQueue.async {
302	                        completionHandler(.failure(.offline))
303	                    }
304	                } else {
305	                    callbackQueue.async {
306	                        completionHandler(.failure(.networkError(error: error)))
307	                    }

XCTUnwrap(session.lastRequest)\n        XCTAssertEqual(request.value(forHTTPHeaderField: \"Authorization\"),\n                       \"Bearer v4-token\",\n                       \"Bearer auth should send the key in the Authorization header\")\n        let components = try! Falls back to the literal\n   `https://api.themoviedb.org/3` for unit-test and\n   command-line-build contexts that don't load the app\n   bundle's Info.plist. Local developers can override the\n   default by setting TMDB_BASE_URL in\n   ../DeveloperSettings.xcconfig (gitignored, same machinery\n   as TMDB_API_KEY) — pointing at e.g. a Cloudflare Worker\n   proxy that attaches the key server-side and forwards to\n   TMDB.\n\n   The xcconfig URL value uses the standard `https:/$()/...`\n   escape because Xcode parses `//` as a line comment.\n\n2. New `APIService.AuthMode` enum:\n   - .queryParameter(name:) — current TMDB v3 behaviour: append\n     `api_key=<value>` to the URL.\n   - .bearer — send `Authorization: Bearer <value>` header\n     instead. Used for TMDB v4 read-access tokens AND for proxy\n     deployments where the proxy validates a static bearer.\n\n   Default is `.queryParameter(name: \"api_key\")` so existing\n   call sites (the global APIService.shared and the dispatch\n   sites in MoviesActions / PeopleActions) keep working\n   unchanged. The mode flips at the call site that constructs\n   the service — typically AppEnvironment when wiring up the\n   shared instance.\n\nThe api_key query parameter is dropped under .bearer mode, the\nlanguage parameter and all caller-supplied params are kept\nthrough both modes, and the missingAPIKey failure path is\nunchanged.\n\nAdds 4 BackendTests:\n- testGETWithQueryParameterAuthAppendsAPIKeyToURL — confirms\n  the default mode still works the way it did before this commit\n  (api_key query param, no Authorization header).\n- testGETWithBearerAuthSendsAuthorizationHeaderAndOmitsAPIKeyQuery\n  — confirms bearer mode swaps the credential into the header\n  and keeps non-credential params (language).\n- testGETWithBearerAuthStillReturnsMissingAPIKeyWhenProviderIsEmpty\n  — auth mode shouldn't change the no-key failure surface.\n- testDefaultBaseURLFallsBackToTMDBDirect — documents the\n  expected behaviour for test contexts that don't load the\n  app bundle.\n\nSuite is 349/349 in the app + 34/34 in Backend across iOS /\nmacOS / tvOS. The actual proxy server is out of scope — this\njust makes spinning one up a config + flag change rather than\na code refactor.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

## Production-Readiness Audit Report

**1. README.md / Readme.md — MISSING**
No root-level README exists. The Packages/Backend and Packages/UI READMEs are placeholders ("A description of this package"). No documentation of shipped features (privacy, attribution, accessibility, offline behavior), no CONTRIBUTING.md or ARCHITECTURE.md.

**2. App Intents — PARTIAL**
`import AppIntents` present in MovieSwiftTVApp and MovieSwiftMacApp, but no actual `AppIntent` or `AppShortcut` struct definitions found in the codebase. Import is there but feature incomplete.

**3. Spotlight indexing — MISSING**
No `CSSearchableItem`, `CoreSpotlight`, or `NSUserActivity` handoff implementation. Wishlist/seenlist items are not indexed for system search.

**4. Universal Links / Deep Links — MISSING**
No `onOpenURL`, `applicationWillContinueUserActivity`, or Associated Domains entitlements. Custom scheme (movieswift://) linking not implemented.

**5. TestFlight / fastlane / Release Automation — MISSING**
No .github/workflows directory, no fastlane/, no Xcode Cloud or distribution CI/CD. GitHub Actions not set up for TestFlight or App Store builds.

**6. Code-signing for Distribution — PRESENT**
Release build configurations exist in pbxproj. Entitlements files are properly configured (iOS + macOS) with iCloud + sandbox settings. macOS entitlements include file I/O. Debug vs. Release separation appears in place.

**7. Async/await Migration — PARTIAL**
Codebase is primarily Combine-based with callback chains (URLSession dataTask). Single use of `await Task.sleep()` in TVSearchView, but no systematic async/await adoption. DispatchQueue.main.async still heavily used throughout. Old-style closure-based networking persists in APIService.

**8. Strict Concurrency Settings — MISSING**
No `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY` build setting found in pbxproj or xcconfig.

**9. Deployment Targets — PRESENT**
IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0, MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0, TVOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0 (all uniform at tvOS/macOS 26 + iOS 26). These are current-OS targets; pre-iOS 18 compatibility not declared. Supports ShareLink (iOS 16+) and modern APIs.

**10. License File — MISSING**
No LICENSE or LICENSE.md in repo root.

**11. Privacy Policy URL — MISSING**
No privacy policy URL mentioned in SettingsForm or anywhere else. App Store submission requires hosted privacy policy link.

**12. Bundle Identifier Consistency — PARTIAL**
Mac uses hardcoded `com.scottdensmore.film-o-matic-mac`. iOS/tvOS use `$(ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER).movieswift` (or `.movieswifttv`). Config xcconfig sets ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER to `com.example` — a placeholder that needs production values before submission.

**13. DocC Documentation — MISSING**
No .docc catalog or generated documentation. Source files lack structured `///` doc comments (mostly old-style `//` headers). No discoverable docs surface for Backend package.

**14. Memory Management — Image Cache — PARTIAL**
ImageLoaderCache uses NSCache (which does have automatic eviction), but no explicit size cap or policy configured. NSCache defaults to auto-eviction on memory pressure, which is safe but unmeasured.

**15. Deinit / Weak Self in Closures — PARTIAL**
`deinit` in SearchTextObservable + ImageLoader; proper `[weak self]` in SearchTextObservable sink. MetricKit subscriber and fileExporter completions appear correctly scoped. No obvious retain cycles detected.

**16. Error-Rate Monitoring — PARTIAL**
MetricKit crash capture to local Documents/CrashReports/ working. No third-party telemetry (correct). No error aggregation or dashboarding beyond local storage. CrashReportStore parses and persists, but no network relay or analytics pipeline.

---

## Three High-Impact Items for Ship Readiness

1. **Bundle Identifier & App Store Metadata (CRITICAL)**  
   ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER is hardcoded to `com.example` — this will fail App Store validation. The bundle IDs must resolve to real team IDs and provisioning profiles. iOS/macOS/tvOS targets have inconsistent naming schemes. Before submission, pin all three targets to production bundle IDs and ensure Provisioning Profile Specifier is non-empty.

2. **Root README + Privacy Policy URL (CRITICAL)**  
   App Store requires a hosted privacy policy URL. Create a root README documenting shipped features (iCloud sync, MetricKit crashes, privacy guarantees, offline mode). Add a Settings link to the privacy policy URL and include it in the app's metadata. Document the four compliance claims clearly.

3. **Release Build Validation & TestFlight CI (HIGH)**  
   No automated pipeline for TestFlight or App Store builds. Add a simple .github/workflows/release.yml that builds Release config, validates code-signing, and gates on simulator + device test passes. This catches distribution config issues before submission and enables safe TestFlight iterations.

---

# MovieSwiftUI

MovieSwiftUI is an application that uses the MovieDB API and is built with SwiftUI. 
It demos some SwiftUI (& Combine) concepts. The goal is to make a real world application using SwiftUI only. It'll be updated with new features as they come to the SwiftUI framework. 

![App Image](images/MovieSwiftUI_promo_new.png?)

## Architecture

MovieSwiftUI data flow is a subset and a custom implementation of the Flux part of [Redux](https://redux.js.org/). 
It implement the State in an [ObservableObject](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/combine/observableobject) as a @Published wrapped property, so changes are published whenever a dispatched action produces a new state after being reduced. 
The state is injected as an environment object in the root view of the application, and is easily accessible anywhere in the application. 
SwiftUI does all aspects of diffing on the render pass when your state changes. No need to be clever when extracting props from your State, they're simple dynamic vars at the view level. No matter your objects' graph size, SwiftUI speed depends on the complexity of your views hierarchy, not the complexity of your object graph.

## SwiftUI

MovieSwiftUI is in pure Swift UI, the goal is to see how far SwiftUI can go in its current implementation without using anything from UIKit (basically no UIView/UIViewController representable).

Re-runs automatically when no usable API key is configured so a misconfigured install doesn't silently fail.\n- **Network error UX** — every TMDB fetcher (~19 of them across Movies + People actions) routes through a `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter` that translates `APIError` into user-facing copy. Inline retry banners on Home menu lists, Movie Detail, People Detail, Discover, and Genres surface offline / 401 / 403 / 429 / 5xx / decode failures with kind-specific icons and CTAs (\"Try again\" vs \"Open Settings\").\n- **iCloud Drive backup + restore** — single rolling JSON envelope written to `Documents/Backups/`, browseable previous versions through `NSFileVersion`, conflict resolution after a multi-device race.\n- **Local export / import** — same envelope format as iCloud backup, exposed through SwiftUI's `.fileExporter` / `.fileImporter` with merge semantics that union user collections rather than clobber.\n- **MetricKit crash reporting** — Apple-native, no third-party SDK. Layered provider checks user-supplied first, falls back to the bundled key. Reading transparently falls back to the legacy bare-AppState format for installs upgrading from earlier builds; future-version files are rejected with a clear error rather than mis-decoded.\n- **Accessibility** — Dynamic Type via `relativeTo:` on every custom font, `.isHeader` rotor traits on section titles, hit targets at the 44pt HIG minimum, VoiceOver labels on every icon-only button.\n\n## Privacy & Attribution\n\n- **Privacy manifest** — `Shared/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` declares `NSPrivacyTracking = false`, empty tracking domains, empty collected data types.   "new_string": "## Platforms\n\nMovieSwiftUI ships across iPhone, iPad, macOS, and tvOS targets. macOS is a native\nbuild (not Mac Catalyst) — it uses a `NavigationSplitView` sidebar with custom\n`@FocusState`-driven keyboard navigation, a steam-themed selection highlight that\nrespects light/dark and active/inactive selection state, and `Cmd+1`-`Cmd+6`\nshortcuts for jumping between sidebar menus.\n\n## Architecture summary\n\n- **Redux/Flux** state — `AppState`, persisted via `AppStatePersistedFormat`\n  envelope (versioned, with legacy bare-AppState fallback).\n- **Backend** Swift Package — `APIService` (config-driven `baseURL`, layered\n  `APIKeyProviding` chain, query-param or bearer auth), `ImageLoaderCache`,\n  `AppUserDefaults`. 34 unit tests.\n- **Shared** — flux state / actions / reducers, all transient loading state\n  centralised in `MoviesState.loadingStates: [LoadingKey: MoviesListLoadingState]`,\n  one `SetLoadingState(key:state:)` action handles all 19 fetchers.\n- **App targets** — iOS uses a `TabView`, macOS a `NavigationSplitView`, tvOS\n  a focus-driven `HomeView`. Settings, onboarding, and crash-report viewer\n  views are shared.\n\nSuite is **349/349 in the app + 34/34 in Backend** across iOS / macOS / tvOS."
}

MovieSwift is an unofficial client.\") {\n            appVersionRow\n            rowDivider\n            tmdbAttributionRow\n            // Privacy policy row only renders when an URL has been\n            // configured via PRIVACY_POLICY_URL — keeps a placeholder\n            // link out of dev builds and out of the App Store\n            // submission until a real policy is hosted.\n            if let privacyURL = privacyPolicyURL {\n                rowDivider\n                privacyPolicyRow(url: privacyURL)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads `PRIVACY_POLICY_URL` from the app bundle's Info.plist\n    /// and validates it parses as a real URL. Returns nil when\n    /// unset (the substitution wasn't filled in) so the Settings\n    /// row can be hidden.\n    private var privacyPolicyURL: URL? {\n        let raw = (Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: \"PRIVACY_POLICY_URL\") as? String) ?? \"\"\n        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        guard !trimmed.isEmpty,\n              trimmed != \"$(PRIVACY_POLICY_URL)\",\n              let url = URL(string: trimmed),\n              url.scheme == \"https\" else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        return url\n    }\n\n    private func privacyPolicyRow(url: URL) -> some View {\n        Link(destination: url) {\n            HStack(spacing: 12) {\n                Image(systemName: \"lock.shield\")\n                    .font(.body)\n                    .foregroundColor(.steam_blue)\n                    .frame(width: 22)\n                Text(\"Privacy policy\")\n                    .foregroundColor(.steam_blue)\n                Spacer()\n                Image(systemName: \"arrow.up.right.square\")\n                    .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))\n                    .foregroundStyle(.tertiary)\n            }\n            .padding(.horizontal, 14)\n            .padding(.vertical, 12)\n            .contentShape(Rectangle())\n        }\n        .buttonStyle(.plain)\n        .accessibilityIdentifier(\"settings.about.privacyPolicyLink\")\n    }"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/IntentNavigation.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  IntentNavigation.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Tiny shared bus that lets `AppIntent`s drive navigation in the\n//  SwiftUI root views without coupling them to the iOS TabView,\n//  the macOS SplitView, or the tvOS HomeView directly.\n//\n//  Flow:\n//   1. An intent's `perform()` calls `IntentNavigationStore.shared\n//      .request(.wishlist)`.\n//   2. The root view subscribes to `pendingDestination` via a\n//      `@StateObject` / `.onChange` and switches its selected tab /\n//      sidebar menu when a destination appears.\n//   3. The view calls `consume()` (or sets `pendingDestination =\n//      nil`) once it has navigated, so a second invocation of the\n//      same intent re-fires.\n//\n//  The store is a singleton because AppIntent runs outside SwiftUI\n//  view scope. We can't pass an EnvironmentObject in, so the\n//  AppIntent and the view both reach for `.shared`.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport Combine\n\nfinal class IntentNavigationStore: ObservableObject {\n    static let shared = IntentNavigationStore()\n\n    /// Where an App Intent is asking the app to navigate. Each\n    /// case maps to one of the iOS tabs or the macOS sidebar menus.\n    enum Destination: Equatable {\n        case popularMovies\n        case discover\n        case fanClub\n        case wishlist\n    }\n\n    @Published var pendingDestination: Destination?\n\n    private init() {}\n\n    /// Posts a destination request from any thread. Hopped to\n    /// main so SwiftUI's `@Published` observation fires on the\n    /// main actor. Safe to call from\n    /// `AppIntent.perform()` which runs on a background queue.\n    func request(_ destination: Destination) {\n        if Thread.isMainThread {\n            pendingDestination = destination\n        } else {\n            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in\n                self?.pendingDestination = destination\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads and clears the pending destination. Views call this\n    /// after acting on a request so the intent can be invoked\n    /// again later with the same destination.\n    @discardableResult\n    func consume() -> Destination? {\n        let destination = pendingDestination\n        pendingDestination = nil\n        return destination\n    }\n}\n"
}

IntentNavigationStore.shared.request(.popularMovies)\n        return .result()\n    }\n}\n"

This\nships five App Intents and an AppShortcutsProvider so the app\nshows up in Spotlight, the Shortcuts app gallery, and Siri:\n\n- OpenMovieSwiftIntent — generic \"Open MovieSwift\" launcher.\n- OpenWishlistIntent — opens MovieSwift to the wishlist.\n- OpenDiscoverIntent — opens to Discover (swipe-through suggestions).\n- OpenFanClubIntent — opens to the Fan Club tab.\n- OpenPopularMoviesIntent — opens to the Popular movies list.\n\nEvery intent sets `openAppWhenRun = true` and writes a destination\nto `IntentNavigationStore.shared` (a singleton ObservableObject\nwith a single `@Published var pendingDestination: Destination?`).\nThe store thread-hops to main so AppIntent's perform() can\npublish from any queue.\n\nTwo root views observe the store and route:\n\n- TabbarView (iOS / iPadOS / tvOS) flips its `selectedTab` and\n  calls consume() to clear the pending destination so a second\n  invocation of the same intent re-fires.\n- SplitView (macOS) flips its `selectedMenu` AND nils out\n  detailNavigationRoute / bumps detailRebuildKey / clears\n  detailPath so any pushed MovieDetail / PeopleDetail pops\n  cleanly — the same path the sidebar Button taps use, fixed\n  by commit 934e564.\n\nMovieSwiftAppShortcuts registers all five intents with phrase\nvariants (\"Open my wishlist in MovieSwift\" / \"Show my wishlist\nin MovieSwift\" / \"Open MovieSwift wishlist\") and\nshortcutTileColor = .yellow to match the steam_gold accent the\napp uses elsewhere. Phrases use \\(.applicationName) so they\nwork even if the bundle display name changes.\n\nFiles:\n- Shared/flux/state/IntentNavigation.swift — the bus\n- Shared/intents/MovieSwiftAppIntents.swift — five intents\n- Shared/intents/MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift — provider\n\nWired to all three app targets (iOS / macOS / tvOS) since each\n@main entry already imports AppIntents and the appintents\nmetadata processor runs on each target's build.\n\nSuite stays at 349/349 across iOS / macOS / tvOS.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift\n//  MovieSwift\n//\n//  Indexes user-saved movies (wishlist, seenlist, and every custom\n//  list) into Apple's Core Spotlight so they appear in the system\n//  search on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. tvOS doesn't ship Core\n//  Spotlight; the file exposes a no-op stub there so app entry\n//  points can call `startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.\n//\n//  We deliberately don't index the full `state.moviesState.movies`\n//  cache — that's a TMDB-shaped firehose of titles the user hasn't\n//  asked to remember. Only items the user has explicitly added to a\n//  list are surfaced so search results match the user's mental\n//  model of \"movies I saved\".\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)\nimport CoreSpotlight\n#endif\nimport SwiftUIFlux\nimport Combine\n\n/// Pure-logic helpers — exposed regardless of platform so unit tests\n/// can verify the indexable-set composition and identifier\n/// round-tripping without depending on Core Spotlight.\nenum MovieSpotlightIndexer {\n\n    /// Domain identifier so the system groups these results\n    /// together and the app can bulk-delete them on logout.\n    static let domainIdentifier = \"com.movieswift.movies\"\n\n    /// Identifier prefix. The numeric movie id is appended so\n    /// `identifier(forMovieId:)` round-trips via\n    /// `movieId(fromIdentifier:)` for the deep-link routing path.\n    private static let identifierPrefix = \"com.movieswift.movie.\"\n\n    static func identifier(forMovieId id: Int) -> String {\n        \"\\(identifierPrefix)\\(id)\"\n    }\n\n    /// Reverse of `identifier(forMovieId:)`. Returns nil for any\n    /// other identifier shape so a future indexer change doesn't\n    /// silently mis-parse existing entries.\n    static func movieId(fromIdentifier identifier: String) -> Int? {\n        guard identifier.hasPrefix(identifierPrefix) else { return nil }\n        let suffix = identifier.dropFirst(identifierPrefix.count)\n        return Int(suffix)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the union of wishlist + seenlist + custom-list movie\n    /// ids. Pure so it can be unit-tested without spinning up a\n    /// Core Spotlight index.\n    static func indexableMovieIds(in state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {\n        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist\n        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)\n        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {\n            ids.formUnion(list.movies)\n        }\n        return ids\n    }\n}\n\n#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)\n\n/// Runtime indexer that subscribes to the SwiftUIFlux store and\n/// keeps CSSearchableIndex in sync with the user's saved movies.\nfinal class SpotlightStoreObserver {\n    static let shared = SpotlightStoreObserver()\n\n    private var lastIndexedIds: Set<Int> = []\n    private var cancellable: AnyCancellable?\n    private var lastSnapshot: AppState?\n    private var isObserving = false\n\n    private init() {}\n\n    /// Subscribe to the store so wishlist / seenlist / custom-list\n    /// changes update Spotlight as they happen. Idempotent — calling\n    /// twice doesn't re-subscribe.\n    func startObserving(store: Store<AppState>) {\n        guard !isObserving else { return }\n        isObserving = true\n\n        // Index whatever's already in state at subscription time.\n        update(state: store.state)\n\n        // SwiftUIFlux's Store is an ObservableObject; objectWillChange\n        // fires before mutations land, so we hop to the next runloop\n        // tick to read the post-mutation state.\n        cancellable = store.objectWillChange\n            .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)\n            .sink { [weak self, weak store] _ in\n                DispatchQueue.main.async {\n                    guard let self, let store else { return }\n                    self.update(state: store.state)\n                }\n            }\n    }\n\n    func stopObserving() {\n        cancellable?.cancel()\n        cancellable = nil\n        isObserving = false\n    }\n\n    /// Diffs the current indexable set against `lastIndexedIds`,\n    /// adds new entries, and removes ones the user un-saved.\n    /// Public for tests; production path runs through the\n    /// store-subscription sink.\n    func update(state: AppState) {\n        let currentIds = MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state)\n        let toAdd = currentIds.subtracting(lastIndexedIds)\n        let toRemove = lastIndexedIds.subtracting(currentIds)\n        // The cached movies dict is the source for the searchable\n        // attributes (title, overview). If a movie is in the index\n        // set but not yet in the cache (TMDB hasn't returned its\n        // detail), skip it — it'll get re-tried on the next state\n        // change.\n        let itemsToIndex: [CSSearchableItem] = toAdd.compactMap { id in\n            guard let movie = state.moviesState.movies[id] else { return nil }\n            return SpotlightStoreObserver.makeSearchableItem(for: movie)\n        }\n        if !itemsToIndex.isEmpty {\n            CSSearchableIndex.default().indexSearchableItems(itemsToIndex) { _ in }\n        }\n        if !toRemove.isEmpty {\n            let identifiers = toRemove.map(MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId:))\n            CSSearchableIndex.default().deleteSearchableItems(withIdentifiers: identifiers) { _ in }\n        }\n\n        // Track only ids actually surfaced to the index. If movie\n        // detail wasn't in cache, leave the id out of\n        // lastIndexedIds so the next update retries the add.\n        let surfacedIds = Set(itemsToIndex.compactMap { item -> Int? in\n            MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: item.uniqueIdentifier)\n        })\n        lastIndexedIds.formUnion(surfacedIds)\n        lastIndexedIds.subtract(toRemove)\n    }\n\n    static func makeSearchableItem(for movie: Movie) -> CSSearchableItem {\n        let attributes = CSSearchableItemAttributeSet(contentType: .content)\n        attributes.title = movie.userTitle\n        if !movie.overview.isEmpty {\n            attributes.contentDescription = movie.overview\n        }\n        // TMDB's release_date is \"yyyy-MM-dd\". Surface as a content\n        // creation date when present so the system can sort by it.\n        if let release = movie.release_date,\n           !release.isEmpty,\n           let date = SpotlightStoreObserver.releaseDateFormatter.date(from: release) {\n            attributes.contentCreationDate = date\n        }\n        return CSSearchableItem(\n            uniqueIdentifier: MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId: movie.id),\n            domainIdentifier: MovieSpotlightIndexer.domainIdentifier,\n            attributeSet: attributes\n        )\n    }\n\n    private static let releaseDateFormatter: DateFormatter = {\n        let formatter = DateFormatter()\n        formatter.calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)\n        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)\n        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: \"en_US_POSIX\")\n        formatter.dateFormat = \"yyyy-MM-dd\"\n        return formatter\n    }()\n}\n\n#else\n\n/// tvOS doesn't ship Core Spotlight. Provide an API-compatible stub\n/// so app entry points can call `SpotlightStoreObserver.shared\n/// .startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.\nfinal class SpotlightStoreObserver {\n    static let shared = SpotlightStoreObserver()\n    private init() {}\n    func startObserving(store: Store<AppState>) {}\n    func stopObserving() {}\n    func update(state: AppState) {}\n}\n\n#endif\n"
}

MovieSpotlightIndexerTests: XCTestCase {\n\n    private func makeMovie(id: Int) -> Movie {\n        Movie(id: id,\n              original_title: \"Movie \\(id)\",\n              title: \"Movie \\(id)\",\n              overview: \"Overview\",\n              poster_path: nil,\n              backdrop_path: nil,\n              popularity: 0,\n              vote_average: 0,\n              vote_count: 0,\n              release_date: nil,\n              genres: nil,\n              runtime: nil,\n              status: nil,\n              video: false,\n              keywords: nil,\n              images: nil,\n              production_countries: nil,\n              character: nil,\n              department: nil)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Identifier round-trip\n\n    func testIdentifierRoundTrip() {\n        for id in [1, 42, 999, 12345] {\n            let identifier = MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId: id)\n            XCTAssertEqual(MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: identifier), id)\n        }\n    }\n\n    func testMovieIdFromIdentifierReturnsNilForUnknownPrefix() {\n        XCTAssertNil(MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: \"com.other.app.42\"))\n        XCTAssertNil(MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: \"com.movieswift.person.42\"))\n        XCTAssertNil(MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: \"42\"))\n    }\n\n    func testMovieIdFromIdentifierReturnsNilForNonNumericSuffix() {\n        XCTAssertNil(MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: \"com.movieswift.movie.abc\"))\n        XCTAssertNil(MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: \"com.movieswift.movie.\"))\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - indexableMovieIds\n\n    func testIndexableMovieIdsUnionsWishlistSeenlistAndCustomLists() {\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.insert(1)\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.insert(2)\n        state.moviesState.seenlist.insert(3)\n        state.moviesState.seenlist.insert(2)  // overlap with wishlist\n        state.moviesState.customLists[10] = CustomList(id: 10,\n                                                       name: \"Favs\",\n                                                       cover: nil,\n                                                       movies: [4, 5])\n        state.moviesState.customLists[20] = CustomList(id: 20,\n                                                       name: \"Re-watch\",\n                                                       cover: nil,\n                                                       movies: [3, 6])  // 3 also in seenlist\n\n        let ids = MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state)\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(ids, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],\n                       \"Indexable set should union all three sources, deduplicated\")\n    }\n\n    func testIndexableMovieIdsExcludesUnsavedCachedMovies() {\n        // Movies in the state's cache that aren't in any list\n        // (e.g. results of a TMDB Popular query) should NOT be\n        // indexed — we don't want every TMDB title appearing\n        // in Spotlight, only items the user explicitly saved.\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.movies[1] = makeMovie(id: 1)\n        state.moviesState.movies[2] = makeMovie(id: 2)\n        state.moviesState.movies[99] = makeMovie(id: 99)\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.insert(1)\n        // 2 and 99 are cached but not in any list.\n\n        let ids = MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state)\n        XCTAssertEqual(ids, [1])\n    }\n\n    func testIndexableMovieIdsIsEmptyForFreshState() {\n        let state = AppState()\n        XCTAssertTrue(MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state).isEmpty,\n                      \"A fresh AppState shouldn't index anything except the placeholder data\")\n    }\n\n    func testIndexableMovieIdsIncludesEmptyCustomLists() {\n        // An empty custom list contributes nothing to the\n        // indexable set — confirmed by union behaviour rather\n        // than special-casing.\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.customLists[1] = CustomList(id: 1,\n                                                      name: \"Empty\",\n                                                      cover: nil,\n                                                      movies: [])\n        XCTAssertTrue(MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state).isEmpty)\n    }\n}\n"

1	//
2	//  MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift
3	//  MovieSwift
4	//
5	//  Indexes user-saved movies (wishlist, seenlist, and every custom
6	//  list) into Apple's Core Spotlight so they appear in the system
7	//  search on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. tvOS doesn't ship Core
8	//  Spotlight; the file exposes a no-op stub there so app entry
9	//  points can call `startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.
10	//
11	//  We deliberately don't index the full `state.moviesState.movies`
12	//  cache — that's a TMDB-shaped firehose of titles the user hasn't
13	//  asked to remember. Only items the user has explicitly added to a
14	//  list are surfaced so search results match the user's mental
15	//  model of "movies I saved".
16	//
17	
18	import Foundation
19	#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)
20	import CoreSpotlight
21	#endif
22	import SwiftUIFlux
23	import Combine
24	
25	/// Pure-logic helpers — exposed regardless of platform so unit tests
26	/// can verify the indexable-set composition and identifier
27	/// round-tripping without depending on Core Spotlight.
28	enum MovieSpotlightIndexer {
29	
30	    /// Domain identifier so the system groups these results
31	    /// together and the app can bulk-delete them on logout.
32	    static let domainIdentifier = "com.movieswift.movies"
33	
34	    /// Identifier prefix. The numeric movie id is appended so
35	    /// `identifier(forMovieId:)` round-trips via
36	    /// `movieId(fromIdentifier:)` for the deep-link routing path.
37	    private static let identifierPrefix = "com.movieswift.movie."
38	
39	    static func identifier(forMovieId id: Int) -> String {
40	        "\(identifierPrefix)\(id)"
41	    }
42	
43	    /// Reverse of `identifier(forMovieId:)`. Returns nil for any
44	    /// other identifier shape so a future indexer change doesn't
45	    /// silently mis-parse existing entries.
46	    static func movieId(fromIdentifier identifier: String) -> Int? {
47	        guard identifier.hasPrefix(identifierPrefix) else { return nil }
48	        let suffix = identifier.dropFirst(identifierPrefix.count)
49	        return Int(suffix)
50	    }
51	
52	    /// Returns the union of wishlist + seenlist + custom-list movie
53	    /// ids. Pure so it can be unit-tested without spinning up a
54	    /// Core Spotlight index.
55	    static func indexableMovieIds(in state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {
56	        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist
57	        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)
58	        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {
59	            ids.formUnion(list.movies)
60	        }
61	        return ids
62	    }
63	}
64	
65	#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)
66	
67	/// Runtime indexer that subscribes to the SwiftUIFlux store and
68	/// keeps CSSearchableIndex in sync with the user's saved movies.
69	final class SpotlightStoreObserver {
70	    static let shared = SpotlightStoreObserver()
71	
72	    private var lastIndexedIds: Set<Int> = []
73	    private var cancellable: AnyCancellable?
74	    private var lastSnapshot: AppState?
75	    private var isObserving = false
76	
77	    private init() {}
78	
79	    /// Subscribe to the store so wishlist / seenlist / custom-list
80	    /// changes update Spotlight as they happen. Idempotent — calling
81	    /// twice doesn't re-subscribe.
82	    func startObserving(store: Store<AppState>) {
83	        guard !isObserving else { return }
84	        isObserving = true
85	
86	        // Index whatever's already in state at subscription time.
87	        update(state: store.state)
88	
89	        // SwiftUIFlux's Store is an ObservableObject; objectWillChange
90	        // fires before mutations land, so we hop to the next runloop
91	        // tick to read the post-mutation state.
92	        cancellable = store.objectWillChange
93	            .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)
94	            .sink { [weak self, weak store] _ in
95	                DispatchQueue.main.async {
96	                    guard let self, let store else { return }
97	                    self.update(state: store.state)
98	                }
99	            }
100	    }
101	
102	    func stopObserving() {
103	        cancellable?.cancel()
104	        cancellable = nil
105	        isObserving = false
106	    }
107	
108	    /// Diffs the current indexable set against `lastIndexedIds`,
109	    /// adds new entries, and removes ones the user un-saved.
110	    /// Public for tests; production path runs through the
111	    /// store-subscription sink.
112	    func update(state: AppState) {
113	        let currentIds = MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state)
114	        let toAdd = currentIds.subtracting(lastIndexedIds)
115	        let toRemove = lastIndexedIds.subtracting(currentIds)
116	        // The cached movies dict is the source for the searchable
117	        // attributes (title, overview). If a movie is in the index
118	        // set but not yet in the cache (TMDB hasn't returned its
119	        // detail), skip it — it'll get re-tried on the next state
120	        // change.
121	        let itemsToIndex: [CSSearchableItem] = toAdd.compactMap { id in
122	            guard let movie = state.moviesState.movies[id] else { return nil }
123	            return SpotlightStoreObserver.makeSearchableItem(for: movie)
124	        }
125	        if !itemsToIndex.isEmpty {
126	            CSSearchableIndex.default().indexSearchableItems(itemsToIndex) { _ in }
127	        }
128	        if !toRemove.isEmpty {
129	            let identifiers = toRemove.map(MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId:))
130	            CSSearchableIndex.default().deleteSearchableItems(withIdentifiers: identifiers) { _ in }
131	        }
132	
133	        // Track only ids actually surfaced to the index. If movie
134	        // detail wasn't in cache, leave the id out of
135	        // lastIndexedIds so the next update retries the add.
136	        let surfacedIds = Set(itemsToIndex.compactMap { item -> Int? in
137	            MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: item.uniqueIdentifier)
138	        })
139	        lastIndexedIds.formUnion(surfacedIds)
140	        lastIndexedIds.subtract(toRemove)
141	    }
142	
143	    static func makeSearchableItem(for movie: Movie) -> CSSearchableItem {
144	        let attributes = CSSearchableItemAttributeSet(contentType: .content)
145	        attributes.title = movie.userTitle
146	        if !movie.overview.isEmpty {
147	            attributes.contentDescription = movie.overview
148	        }
149	        // TMDB's release_date is "yyyy-MM-dd". Surface as a content
150	        // creation date when present so the system can sort by it.
151	        if let release = movie.release_date,
152	           !release.isEmpty,
153	           let date = SpotlightStoreObserver.releaseDateFormatter.date(from: release) {
154	            attributes.contentCreationDate = date
155	        }
156	        return CSSearchableItem(
157	            uniqueIdentifier: MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId: movie.id),
158	            domainIdentifier: MovieSpotlightIndexer.domainIdentifier,
159	            attributeSet: attributes
160	        )
161	    }
162	
163	    private static let releaseDateFormatter: DateFormatter = {
164	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
165	        formatter.calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
166	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
167	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
168	        formatter.dateFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd"
169	        return formatter
170	    }()
171	}
172	
173	#else
174	
175	/// tvOS doesn't ship Core Spotlight. Provide an API-compatible stub
176	/// so app entry points can call `SpotlightStoreObserver.shared
177	/// .startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.
178	final class SpotlightStoreObserver {
179	    static let shared = SpotlightStoreObserver()
180	    private init() {}
181	    func startObserving(store: Store<AppState>) {}
182	    func stopObserving() {}
183	    func update(state: AppState) {}
184	}
185	
186	#endif
187

{
  "command": "git -C /Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nfeat: Spotlight indexing for user-saved movies\n\nSurface wishlist, seenlist, and custom-list movies in iOS / macOS\nSpotlight so the user can search the items they've explicitly saved\nwithout opening the app. Tapping a result deep-links into MovieDetail\nvia .onContinueUserActivity → CSSearchableItemActionType.\n\nWhat's indexed\n- The union of state.moviesState.wishlist, state.moviesState.seenlist,\n  and every CustomList's movies array. Pure-logic helper\n  MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in:) is unit-tested.\n- The full TMDB cache (moviesState.movies) is intentionally NOT\n  indexed — Spotlight should match the user's mental model of \"movies\n  I saved\", not the firehose of TMDB titles the cache happens to\n  contain.\n\nLive updates\n- SpotlightStoreObserver subscribes to the SwiftUIFlux store and\n  diffs the indexable set against lastIndexedIds on every state\n  change; new entries get added, un-saved ones removed. If a movie\n  detail isn't in cache yet (TMDB hasn't returned it), the id is left\n  out of lastIndexedIds so the next state tick retries the add.\n- Wired from HomeView (iOS), MovieSwiftMacApp (macOS), and\n  MovieSwiftTVApp (tvOS — calls into the no-op stub since\n  CoreSpotlight isn't available there). Skipped under UI smoke tests\n  via the existing isRunningUISmokeTests gate.\n\nResult routing\n- TabbarView (iOS) and SplitView (macOS) listen for\n  CSSearchableItemActionType user activities, parse the identifier\n  with MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier:), and present\n  MovieDetail in a .sheet(item:) keyed off an Identifiable\n  SpotlightMovieID wrapper so SwiftUI's identity diffing handles\n  push/dismiss cleanly.\n\nTests\n- 7 new tests in MovieSpotlightIndexerTests cover identifier\n  round-tripping, rejection of mis-prefixed / non-numeric\n  identifiers, set-union behaviour across the three sources, the\n  intentional exclusion of cache-only movies, and edge cases\n  (fresh state, empty custom lists). Full unit suite up to 356 from\n  349.\n\nPer CLAUDE.md every behaviour change ships with the test that\nexercises it; the indexer's pure-logic split keeps the suite from\nneeding CoreSpotlight at test time.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
  "description": "Create Spotlight indexing commit"
}

Perfect. Now I have enough detail. Let me create the architecture map:

## Architecture Map

### 1. Backend Package

**Location:** `Packages/Backend/Sources/Backend/`

**Dependencies:** None (stdlib + Foundation only)

**Files:**
- `preferences/AppUserDefaults.swift` — wraps UserDefaults for region, title display preference, API key
- `services/APIService.swift` — HTTP client for TMDB REST API; handles endpoint routing, JSON decoding, APIKeyProviding protocol
- `services/ImageService.swift` — image fetch/cache orchestration
- `utils/ImageLoader.swift` — low-level image download and caching
- `utils/PlatformImage.swift` — abstraction over UIImage/NSImage for cross-platform support
- `wrappers/UserDefaultWrapper.swift` — property wrapper for UserDefaults access

**Tests:** `Packages/Backend/Tests/BackendTests/` (6 test files covering APIService, ImageService, ImageLoader, UserDefaults wrapper, API key provider, PlatformImage)

**Characteristics:** Pure infrastructure layer. No dependencies on UI frameworks or app logic. Platform-agnostic where possible.

---

### 2. UI Package

**Location:** `Packages/UI/Sources/UI/`

**Dependencies:** SwiftUI only (no Backend, no App logic)

**Files:**
- `badges/` — NotificationBadge, PopularityBadge, RoundedBadge (generic UI components)
- `buttons/BorderedButton.swift` — reusable button style
- `fields/` — SearchField, SearchTextObservable (generic input components)
- `extensions/View.swift` — SwiftUI View extensions (layout, modifiers)
- `preferenceKeys/OffsetTop.swift` — SwiftUI preference key for scroll offsets

**Tests:** No tests exist for UI package.

**Characteristics:** Pure SwiftUI component library. Zero coupling to domain logic, Backend, or app state. Fully reusable.

---

### 3. Shared/ — Mixed App Shell + Library Code

#### `extensions/` (Library — safe to move)
- `Color.swift` — app-specific color scheme (steam_white, steam_gold, steam_rust, etc.)
- `Font.swift` — custom font definitions
- `Collection.swift` — utility helpers on Swift stdlib types
- `ActionSheet.swift` — SwiftUI ActionSheet extensions
- `EnvironmentKeys.swift` — custom environment keys for theme/preferences

**Assessment:** Platform-agnostic utility code; could move to UI package or a dedicated Extensions package.

#### `flux/models/` (Library — partially movable)
- `Movie.swift`, `People.swift`, `Review.swift`, `Video.swift`, `CastResponse.swift` — Codable TMDB API response types
- `Genre.swift`, `Keyword.swift`, `Image.swift`, `PaginatedResponse.swift` — TMDB domain types
- `CustomList.swift`, `DiscoverFilter.swift`, `MovieUserMeta.swift` — app-specific derived types

**Assessment:** Models map to TMDB schema + app metadata. Could move to Backend (TMDB domain models) vs. stay in Shared (they also need app-level changes like `userTitle` computed property that depends on Backend preferences).

#### `flux/actions/` (Library — depends on Backend)
- `MoviesActions.swift`, `PeopleActions.swift` — Redux async action creators; import Backend for APIService and AppUserDefaults

**Assessment:** Pure logic, no UI. But tightly coupled to Backend's APIService. Could move to Backend or a new FluxCore package if Backend exports these.

#### `flux/reducers/` (Library — pure logic)
- `MoviesReducer.swift`, `PeopleReducer.swift`, `AppReducer.swift` — Redux reducers; pure functions, no UI

**Assessment:** Platform-agnostic; could move to a FluxCore package (see note below on existing Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests).

#### `flux/state/` (Mixed — app shell + library)
- **Pure logic (movable):** `MoviesState.swift`, `PeoplesState.swift`, `AppState.swift`, `MoviesListLoadingState.swift` — Redux state containers
- **App-shell (must stay):** `AppBootstrap.swift`, `AppDataExport.swift`, `AppDataImport.swift`, `AppDataICloudBackup.swift` — persistence/export logic tied to file I/O and app lifecycle
- **App infrastructure (must stay):** `AppPersistence.swift`, `AppEnvironment.swift`, `AppRuntime.swift`, `AppLaunchMode.swift` — runtime config, crash reporting, spotlight indexing (`MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift`, `CrashReportStore.swift`), app intent navigation (`IntentNavigation.swift`), `MetricKitCrashReporter.swift`
- **Testing utilities:** `AppStateFixtures.swift`, `AppStatePersistedFormat.swift`, `AppStoreFactory.swift` — fixtures and persistence format testing

**Assessment:** State types themselves (MoviesState, AppState) are platform-agnostic and testable; move-worthy. Everything else is app-shell orchestration and must stay.

#### `flux/middlewares/` (Library)
- `LoggingMiddleware.swift` — Redux logger; imports only SwiftUIFlux and Foundation

**Assessment:** Generic middleware; could move to FluxCore.

#### `flux/testing/` (Testing utilities)
- `ActionStubs.swift`, `AppStateStub.swift` — mock fixtures for tests

**Assessment:** App-specific test helpers; can stay in Shared or move to a test utilities package.

#### `views/` (App UI)
- **App components:** `CrashReportsView.swift`, `MoviePosterImage.swift` (imports Backend), `MoviesMenu.swift` (imports Backend), `SortMenu.swift`, `MoviesListErrorBanner.swift`, `SplitView.swift`
- **Onboarding:** `onboarding/OnboardingFlow.swift` (imports Backend), `onboarding/OnboardingView.swift` (imports Backend) — first-launch wizard
- **Modifiers:** `modifiers/PosterStyle.swift` — custom SwiftUI view modifiers

**Assessment:** Mix of reusable views (could move to UI package) and app-specific screens. OnboardingFlow is library-like (pure logic for step progression) but OnboardingView is app-shell UI.

#### `intents/` (App infrastructure)
- `MovieSwiftAppIntents.swift`, `MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift` — AppIntents and Shortcuts definitions (Siri, Spotlight, Shortcuts.app integration)

**Assessment:** App-shell only. Must stay in app targets because system discovery requires @main App and intents in same target.

#### `fonts/` (if it exists)
Not found in list, but referenced in FontFamily (likely just asset references).

---

### 4. App Targets

#### iOS `MovieSwift/views/` (59 files)
Structure:
- `components/` — feature-specific screens: bottomMenu, custom list, discover, fan club, genres, home, movieDetail, moviesGrid, moviesHome, moviesList, myLists, peopleDetail, settings
- `shared/contextMenu/` — reusable context menus
- `shared/images/` — image rendering (BigMoviePosterImage, ListImage, MovieBackdropImage, PeopleImage)

#### macOS `MovieSwiftMac/` (minimal)
- `MovieSwiftMacApp.swift` — app entry point; no separate view hierarchy (reuses Shared + iOS components)

#### tvOS `MovieSwiftTV/views/` (4 files)
- `TVSearchView.swift`, `TVMovieDetail.swift`, `HomeView.swift`, `MoviesView.swift` — tvOS-specific layouts

**Characteristics:** Significant iOS-specific view hierarchy; macOS is thin wrapper; tvOS has minimal custom views.

---

### 5. Test Coverage

#### `MovieSwiftTests/` (13 test files)
Tests for:
- **Shared flux code:** PeopleActionsTests, MoviesActionsTests, AppStatePersistedFormatTests, MoviesListLoadingStateTests, MovieDetailStateTests
- **Shared app-shell:** AppBootstrapTests, AppDataExportTests, AppDataImportTests, AppDataICloudBackupTests, AppPersistenceTests, CrashReportStoreTests, MovieSpotlightIndexerTests, OnboardingFlowTests

No UI tests here (those are in `MovieSwiftUITests/`).

#### `Packages/Backend/Tests/BackendTests/` (6 tests)
- APIServiceTests, APIKeyProviderTests, ImageServiceTests, ImageLoaderCacheTests, UserDefaultWrapperTests, PlatformImageTests

#### `Packages/UI/Tests/`
None exist.

#### `Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/` (separate test target — exists!)
- LoggingMiddlewareTests, ModelUtilityTests, ReducerTests, APIPayloadContractTests, MoviesActionsTests
- This suggests a potential separation of flux logic from app shell already planned.

---

## Summary for Recommendation

**Already well-separated:**
- Backend package (zero dependencies)
- UI package (SwiftUI only)

**Candidates to move to Backend:**
- `flux/models/` (TMDB domain types) — most of it; Movie.swift has app-specific computed properties that could be layered

**Candidates to move to UI or new package:**
- `extensions/{Color.swift, Font.swift, EnvironmentKeys.swift}` — app theme, reusable
- `views/{CrashReportsView, SplitView, MoviesMenu, SortMenu, MoviePosterImage, MoviesListErrorBanner}` — mixed; some are generic layout helpers

**Must stay in app targets:**
- `flux/state/{AppBootstrap, AppDataExport, AppPersistence, AppRuntime, AppEnvironment, CrashReportStore, MovieSpotlightIndexer, MetricKitCrashReporter}`
- `intents/`
- App target views with platform-specific layouts

**Unclear/context-dependent:**
- Pure state types (MoviesState, AppState, PeoplesState) — technically movable but act as app contract
- Actions/Reducers — could move to a new MovieSwiftFluxCore package (hint: test directory already exists for this)

//

import Foundation
import SwiftUIFlux

struct AppEnvironment {
    let launchMode: AppLaunchMode
    let runtime: AppRuntime
    let store: Store<AppState>

    static func make(launchMode: AppLaunchMode,
                     environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) -> AppEnvironment {
        let runtime = AppRuntime(launchMode: launchMode, environment: environment)
        let store = AppStoreFactory.makeStore(launchMode: launchMode, isLoggingEnabled: runtime.isLoggingEnabled)
        return AppEnvironment(launchMode: launchMode, runtime: runtime, store: store)
    }

//
//  MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift
//  MovieSwift
//
//  Indexes user-saved movies (wishlist, seenlist, and every custom
//  list) into Apple's Core Spotlight so they appear in the system
//  search on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. tvOS doesn't ship Core
//  Spotlight; the file exposes a no-op stub there so app entry
//  points can call `startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.
//
//  We deliberately don't index the full `state.moviesState.movies`
//  cache — that's a TMDB-shaped firehose of titles the user hasn't
//  asked to remember. Only items the user has explicitly added to a
//  list are surfaced so search results match the user's mental
//  model of "movies I saved".
//

import Foundation
#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)
import CoreSpotlight

filename.swift\n    r'^MovieSwift(?:Mac|TV|Tests|UITests|MacUITests|TVUITests)?\\s*$',\n    r'^Backend\\s*$',\n    r'^UI\\s*$',\n    r'^Film[\\s\\-_]?O[\\s\\-_]?Matic\\s*$',\n    r'^Created by\\s+.+$',\n    r'^Copyright\\s+.+$',\n]\nBOILERPLATE_RES = [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in BOILERPLATE_BODY_PATTERNS]\n\n\ndef is_bare_comment(line: str) -> bool:\n    return line.strip() == '//'\n\n\ndef is_boilerplate(line: str) -> bool:\n    s = line.strip()\n    if not s.startswith('//'):\n        return False\n    body = s[2:].strip()\n    if not body:\n        return False\n    return any(rx.match(body) for rx in BOILERPLATE_RES)\n\n\ndef process(path: Path) -> bool:\n    text = path.read_text()\n    lines = text.split('\\n')\n\n    if not lines or not lines[0].startswith('//'):\n        return False  # No leading comment block — leave alone.\n\n    # Find the end of the leading comment block (first blank or non-comment line).\n    block_end = 0\n    for i, line in enumerate(lines):\n        stripped = line.strip()\n        if stripped.startswith('//'):\n            block_end = i + 1\n        else:\n            break\n\n    if block_end == 0:\n        return False\n\n    header = lines[:block_end]\n    rest = lines[block_end:]\n\n    # Drop boilerplate lines.\n    kept = [l for l in header if not is_boilerplate(l)]\n\n    # Strip leading and trailing bare `//` framing.\n    while kept and is_bare_comment(kept[0]):\n        kept.pop(0)\n    while kept and is_bare_comment(kept[-1]):\n        kept.pop()\n\n    # Collapse consecutive bare `//` (shouldn't happen but defensive).\n    collapsed: list[str] = []\n    prev_bare = False\n    for l in kept:\n        bare = is_bare_comment(l)\n        if bare and prev_bare:\n            continue\n        collapsed.append(l)\n        prev_bare = bare\n\n    if collapsed:\n        new_lines = collapsed + rest\n    else:\n        # Header was 100% boilerplate — drop a single trailing blank line too.\n        if rest and rest[0].strip() == '':\n            rest = rest[1:]\n        new_lines = rest\n\n    new_text = '\\n'.join(new_lines)\n    if new_text != text:\n        path.write_text(new_text)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef main():\n    dry_run = '--dry-run' in sys.argv\n    changed = []\n    for p in ROOT.rglob('*.swift'):\n        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in p.parts):\n            continue\n        if dry_run:\n            # Simulate: read, run logic, but don't write.\n            text = p.read_text()\n            lines = text.split('\\n')\n            if not lines or not lines[0].startswith('//'):\n                continue\n            block_end = 0\n            for i, line in enumerate(lines):\n                if line.strip().startswith('//'):\n                    block_end = i + 1\n                else:\n                    break\n            if block_end == 0:\n                continue\n            header = lines[:block_end]\n            kept = [l for l in header if not is_boilerplate(l)]\n            while kept and is_bare_comment(kept[0]): kept.pop(0)\n            while kept and is_bare_comment(kept[-1]): kept.pop()\n            if kept != header:\n                changed.append(p)\n        else:\n            if process(p):\n                changed.append(p)\n    print(f\"{'Would change' if dry_run else 'Changed'}: {len(changed)} files\")\n    for p in changed[:20]:\n        print(f\"  {p.relative_to(ROOT)}\")\n    if len(changed) > 20:\n        print(f\"  ... and {len(changed) - 20} more\")\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n"
}

1	# MovieSwiftUI — Project Guidelines
2	
3	## Always write tests for fixes
4	
5	Any time you fix a bug or change behavior, add or update a test that
6	exercises the change. Before committing a fix:
7	
8	1. Reproduce the bug in a test (unit or UI) so the failing test
9	   demonstrates the problem.
10	2. Apply the code fix.
11	3. Verify the test now passes, and run the broader affected test
12	   suite.
13	4. Include the test in the same commit as the fix. The commit message
14	   should mention what the test covers.
15	
16	This applies to every `fix:` commit — reducer changes, view logic,
17	navigation, focus handling, parsing, anything.
18	
19	### Where tests live
20	
21	- **Redux reducers & state selectors:** `MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/`
22	  (see `MovieDetailStateTests.swift`, `PeopleActionsTests.swift`,
23	  `MovieSwiftTests.swift`).
24	- **UI flows / smoke tests:** `MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/MovieSwiftUITests`
25	  (macOS uses env var `UI_TEST_SELECT_MENU` to pre-select the sidebar).
26	- **Swift packages:** `MovieSwift/Packages/<Name>/Tests/`.
27	
28	### How to run tests
29	
30	```
31	cd MovieSwift
32	xcodebuild test -scheme MovieSwift \
33	    -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' \
34	    -only-testing:MovieSwiftTests/<TestClassName>
35	```
36	
37	For macOS-only logic, use `-scheme MovieSwiftMac` with a macOS
38	destination.
39	
40	### When a pure test is impractical
41	
42	If a fix can only be verified visually (layout, animation, focus
43	ring), still note that in the commit message and add at least a
44	structural assertion (e.g. view builds without crashing, the
45	relevant accessibility identifier is present) where possible.
46

## Summary of what's done

| | |
|---|---|
| `f13c7c8` | **chore: strip Xcode boilerplate file headers + prevent re-add** — 134 .swift files cleaned, ~900 lines removed; design-note comments preserved (e.g. `MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift` keeps its rationale) |
| Added | `MovieSwift.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/IDETemplateMacros.plist` with empty `FILEHEADER` so Xcode templates stop emitting boilerplate |
| Added | `CLAUDE.md` "No file-header boilerplate" section so any agent/script follows the convention |
| Verified | iOS / macOS / tvOS all build clean; full unit suite green at 356/356 |

---

## Architecture: should more move into packages?

**Short answer:** Yes, one clear win. The current Backend / UI split is already healthy — they have zero cross-coupling and minimal external deps. The opportunity is in **`Shared/`**, which is a junk drawer mixing genuine library code with app-shell wiring.

### What's in Shared/ today, and what it actually is

| Subfolder | What it really is | Should it move? |
|---|---|---|
| `flux/models/` (Movie, Person, Genre, etc.) | TMDB data types | ✅ Move to a new package |
| `flux/actions/` (MoviesActions, PeopleActions) | Redux action creators, depend on Backend | ✅ Move to a new package |
| `flux/reducers/` | Pure reducer functions | ✅ Move to a new package |
| `flux/middlewares/` (LoggingMiddleware) | Generic Redux logger | ✅ Move to a new package |
| `flux/state/{MoviesState, PeoplesState, AppState, MoviesListLoadingState}` | Pure state types | ✅ Move to a new package |
| `flux/state/{AppBootstrap, AppEnvironment, AppRuntime, AppLaunchMode, AppPersistence, AppStoreFactory}` | App-shell wiring | ❌ Keep in app target |
| `flux/state/{AppDataExport, AppDataImport, AppDataICloudBackup}` | File I/O + lifecycle | ❌ Keep in app target |
| `flux/state/{CrashReportStore, MetricKitCrashReporter, MovieSpotlightIndexer, IntentNavigation}` | System integration | ❌ Keep in app target |
| `flux/testing/` (ActionStubs, AppStateStub) | Test fixtures | ✅ Move alongside the new package's tests |
| `intents/` | App Intents | ❌ Must stay in app target (system discovery requires `@main` co-location) |
| `views/onboarding/OnboardingView.swift` | App-specific screen | ❌ Keep |
| `views/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.swift` | Pure step-progression logic | 🟡 Could move; small file, low impact |
| `views/{CrashReportsView, SplitView, MoviesMenu, SortMenu, MoviePosterImage, MoviesListErrorBanner}` | App-shell screens, tightly Backend/state-coupled | ❌ Keep |
| `views/modifiers/PosterStyle.swift` | Generic SwiftUI modifier | 🟡 Could move to UI package |
| `extensions/{Color, Font, EnvironmentKeys}` | App theme — `steam_gold`, `steam_rust`, etc. | 🟡 Could move to UI package, but the names are app-flavored |

### Recommendation: extract one new package — `FluxCore`

Move the green-checked rows above into `Packages/FluxCore/Sources/FluxCore/`. Specifically:

```
Packages/FluxCore/
├── Package.swift              # depends on Backend (for APIService) + SwiftUIFlux
└── Sources/FluxCore/
    ├── models/                # Movie, Person, Genre, Review, Video, Keyword, ...
    ├── actions/               # MoviesActions, PeopleActions
    ├── reducers/              # MoviesReducer, PeopleReducer, AppReducer
    ├── middlewares/           # LoggingMiddleware
    └── state/                 # MoviesState, PeoplesState, AppState, MoviesListLoadingState
└── Tests/FluxCoreTests/       # the directory already exists in the codebase 👀
```

**Why this is worth it:**

1. **Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/ already exists** — somebody started this and didn't finish. Their test files include `LoggingMiddlewareTests`, `ReducerTests`, `APIPayloadContractTests`, `ModelUtilityTests`, `MoviesActionsTests`. The seam is already drawn.
2. **Compile-time wins** — Swift package modules build in parallel and don't get invalidated by app-target view churn. Touching a SwiftUI view in `MovieSwift/views/` won't recompile your reducers.
3. **Forced public/internal hygiene** — moving to a package surfaces accidental coupling. You'll find views that were reaching into reducer internals.
4. **Crisp testability boundary** — reducer/action tests don't need to spin up the app target.
5. **Cross-target consistency** — these files are already used by all 3 app targets via `Shared/`; a package makes that explicit.

**What I'd skip for now:**

- **Don't move `extensions/Color.swift` or `Font.swift`** — the `steam_*` palette is app-specific. Either rename to generic and move, or leave. Low payoff.
- **Don't try to move `views/`** — `SplitView`, `CrashReportsView`, `OnboardingView` are tightly coupled to AppState and routing. Moving them turns into a yak-shave.
- **Don't add a fourth package** for app-shell code (CrashReportStore, MovieSpotlightIndexer, etc.). They depend on system frameworks (CoreSpotlight, MetricKit) that are inherently app-bound — there's no testability win, and the `@main` actor needs to wire them up directly anyway.

### Trade-offs to be honest about

- **Cost**: ~30 file moves, lots of `import FluxCore` additions, an `import` shuffle on the test target, and one new Package.swift. Maybe a 2-hour mechanical refactor + half-hour of fixing public/internal qualifiers.
- **One downside**: cross-package refactors get a bit more friction (e.g. adding a property to `Movie` that's used in both a reducer and a view now crosses a package boundary). For a project this size that hasn't bitten me on similar codebases.

### What about Backend and UI themselves?

- **Backend** — leave as-is. It's the model citizen of the project. (One small thing: there's a typo in `wrappers/UserDetaultWrapper.swift` ("Detault" → "Default") that's worth fixing as a separate chore.)
- **UI** — leave as-is for component code. **One thing worth adding: tests.** The package currently has zero. Could be a low-risk warmup commit.

import XCTest
@testable import MovieSwiftFluxCore

final class APIPayloadContractTests: XCTestCase {
    private func fixtureData(named name: String) throws -> Data {
        let url = try XCTUnwrap(Bundle.module.url(forResource: name, withExtension: "json"))
        return try Data(contentsOf: url)
    }

    private func decodeFixture<T: Decodable>(_ name: String, as type: T.Type) throws -> T {
        try JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from: fixtureData(named: name))
    }

    func testMovieMenuPayloadDecodesExpectedShape() throws {
        let payload = try decodeFixture("movie_menu_response", as: PaginatedResponse<Movie>.self)

        XCTAssertEqual(payload.page, 3)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.total_results, 10000)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.total_pages, 500)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.results.map(\.id), [101, 102])
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.results.first?.title, "Movie 101")
    }

    func testMovieDetailPayloadDecodesNestedContractFields() throws {
        let payload = try decodeFixture("movie_detail_response", as: Movie.self)

        XCTAssertEqual(payload.id, 205)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.runtime, 134)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.status, "Released")
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.genres?.map(\.id), [18, 12])
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.keywords?.keywords?.map(\.name), ["space", "future"])
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.images?.posters?.first?.file_path, "/poster-a.jpg")
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.images?.backdrops?.first?.width, 1920)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.production_countries?.map(\.name), ["United States of America", "Canada"])
    }

    func testCastResponsePayloadDecodesCastAndCrewMetadata() throws {
        let payload = try decodeFixture("cast_response", as: CastResponse.self)

        XCTAssertEqual(payload.id, 205)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.cast.first?.id, 301)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.cast.first?.character, "Pilot")
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.cast.first?.known_for?.first?.id, 9001)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.crew.first?.id, 302)
        XCTAssertEqual(payload.crew.first?.department, "Directing")
    }

    func testGenresResponsePayloadDecodesFetchGenresContract() throws {
        let payload = try decodeFixture("genres_response", as: MoviesActions.GenresResponse.self)

> AGENT

The agent completed — but I just discovered something important when I went to check the worktree state. **The work is against the wrong base.**

## What the agent did (in isolation)

It produced a coherent extraction with green builds and 39 passing tests. By its own report:
- New `Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/` package created
- 23 source files moved + made public
- pbxproj surgery done
- 51 consumer files got `import MovieSwiftFluxCore`
- All 3 platforms build, all tests green

## What's wrong

The worktree branch was forked from `fbd54a7` ("Add padding to movie row focus highlight on Mac Catalyst") — **not from `f13c7c8`** (my current branch tip). That's an old ancestor commit. As a result, the agent's worktree is **missing every commit I made in this session and likely others**, including:

| Commit | Subject |
|---|---|
| `f13c7c8` | chore: strip Xcode boilerplate file headers |
| `2f0f6ed` | feat: Spotlight indexing |
| `fd21058` | feat: App Intents |
| `d3f6e51` | docs: README + privacy policy |
| `5f1535f` | feat(api): config-driven baseURL + AuthMode enum |
| ... and ~5 earlier ones | |

Evidence in the agent's "Deviations" section, where it says (incorrectly):

> "no `MoviesListLoadingState.swift`, `AppEnvironment`, `AppPersistence`, `AppBootstrap`, `MovieSpotlightIndexer`, `IntentNavigation`, `AppDataExport/Import/ICloudBackup`, `CrashReportStore`, `MetricKitCrashReporter` … no `MovieSwiftMac`/`Film-O-Matic` target"

All of those exist on `feature/native-macos-target`. The agent legitimately didn't see them because they aren't on `fbd54a7`.

Concrete consequences:
- **Merging the worktree back as-is would discard ~7 commits** of recent work.
- **Headers it didn't touch are stale** — its "deviation #5" says it kept original Xcode boilerplate headers in files it only Edited (vs. fully rewrote). On the current tip those are already stripped, so headers would come back in some files.
- **pbxproj edits won't apply** cleanly to the current tip (different file references, different project structure since the macOS target was added).
- **The "all tests pass" verification was against the old codebase**, not the current one with Spotlight/Intents/etc.

Also: even if the base were right, the commit didn't land — 1Password SSH-signing agent was locked, so 108 changes are staged but no commit exists.

## Salvageable parts

Despite the wrong base, the package itself is well-built:
- The 23 `Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/**/*.swift` files (with public visibility added) are largely independent of my recent commits — none of my work touched models/, actions/, reducers/, or middlewares/
- The `Package.swift` (with `SwiftUIFlux 0.5.1` matching the actual pbxproj pin — better than the `1.0.0` I told it) is reusable
- Its analysis of which extensions/Collection.swift had to move (because the existing fixture tests reference `MoviesSort` and `sortedMoviesIds`) is correct

## Three paths forward — which do you want?

1. **Salvage and re-apply on `f13c7c8`** — I take the new package directory + Package.swift the agent built, re-apply the public-visibility changes that aren't there, redo the pbxproj surgery against the current project file, and add `import MovieSwiftFluxCore` to consumers including my new files (MovieSpotlightIndexer, IntentNavigation, App Intents, CrashReportStore, etc.). Manual work but I keep all your recent commits and verify against the actual current state. ~Medium time. Clean result.

2. **Discard and redo with a fresh worktree based on `f13c7c8`** — relaunch the same agent prompt but with explicit base. Costly (~hour-long agent run) but the agent already showed it can do this kind of work. Risk: same kind of base-mismatch could happen again unless I verify the worktree base after launch.

3. **Defer the extraction** — abandon for now, keep all recent work as-is, revisit later. The architecture review still stands; nothing else got broken.

I'd pick #1. The mechanical refactor work is hard for an agent to redo from scratch but easy for me to port when the package skeleton already exists. Let me know.
