8	public struct AppState: FluxState, Codable {
9	    public var moviesState: MoviesState
10	    public var peoplesState: PeoplesState
11	
12	
13	    public init() {
14	        do {
15	            let icloudDirectory = FileManager.default.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier: nil)
16	            let documentDirectory = try FileManager.default.url(for: .documentDirectory,
17	                                                                in: .userDomainMask,
18	                                                                appropriateFor: nil,
19	                                                                create: false)
20	            if let icloudDirectory = icloudDirectory {
21	                try FileManager.default.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at: icloudDirectory)
22	            }
23	
24	            savePath = (icloudDirectory ?? documentDirectory).appendingPathComponent("userData")
25	        } catch let error {
26	            fatalError("Couldn't create save state data with error: \(error)")
27	        }
28	
29	        if let data = try? Data(contentsOf: savePath),
30	            let savedState = try? decoder.decode(AppState.self, from: data) {
31	            self.moviesState = savedState.moviesState
32	            self.peoplesState = savedState.peoplesState
33	        } else {
34	            self.moviesState = MoviesState()
35	            self.peoplesState = PeoplesState()

43	    public func archiveState() {
44	        let moviesState = self.moviesState
45	        let peoplesState = self.peoplesState
46	        DispatchQueue.global().async {
47	            let movies = moviesState.movies.filter { (arg) -> Bool in
48	                let (key, _) = arg
49	                return moviesState.seenlist.contains(key) ||
50	                    moviesState.wishlist.contains(key) ||
51	                    moviesState.customLists.contains(where: { (_, value) -> Bool in
52	                        value.movies.contains(key) ||
53	                            value.cover == key
54	                    })
55	            }
56	            let people = peoplesState.peoples.filter{ peoplesState.fanClub.contains($0.key) }
57	            var savingState = self
58	            savingState.moviesState.movies = movies
59	            savingState.peoplesState.peoples = people
60	            guard let data = try? encoder.encode(savingState) else {
61	                return
62	            }
63	            do {
64	                try data.write(to: savePath)
65	            } catch let error {
66	                print("Error while saving app state :\(error)")
67	            }
68	        }
69	
70	    }

75	            let formatter = ByteCountFormatter()
76	            formatter.allowedUnits = .useKB
77	            formatter.countStyle = .file
78	            return formatter.string(fromByteCount: Int64(resources.fileSize ?? 0))
79	        } catch {

{
  "file_path": "/tmp/add_public.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Add `public` modifier to type declarations and members in Swift source files,\nwithin type-body and extension-body scopes only (not function bodies).\n\nApproach: scope-aware brace tracking with simple string/comment skipping.\n\nUsage: add_public.py <file>...\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nACCESS_RE = re.compile(r'\\b(?:public|private|fileprivate|internal|open|package)\\b')\n\n# A \"top-level\" declaration on a line. We DON'T match `case` (enum case is\n# implicitly the same access as its enum), `import`, or `if/for/while/return`.\nDECL_RE = re.compile(\n    r'^(?P<indent>\\s*)'\n    r'(?P<attrs>(?:@\\w+(?:\\([^)]*\\))?\\s+)*)'\n    r'(?P<modifiers>(?:(?:final|static|class|override|mutating|nonmutating|weak|unowned|lazy|dynamic|convenience|required|indirect)\\s+)*)'\n    r'(?P<keyword>struct|enum|class|protocol|extension|typealias|func|init|let|var|subscript)\\b'\n)\n\n# Match {} with naive string/comment stripping.\ndef strip_strings_and_comments(line: str) -> str:\n    # Remove line comments\n    if '//' in line:\n        # naive: only strip if not inside a string\n        idx = line.find('//')\n        # check if inside string\n        in_str = False\n        for i, c in enumerate(line[:idx]):\n            if c == '\"' and (i == 0 or line[i-1] != '\\\\'):\n                in_str = not in_str\n        if not in_str:\n            line = line[:idx]\n    # Remove block-comment regions on this line (simplistic)\n    while '/*' in line and '*/' in line:\n        a = line.find('/*'); b = line.find('*/', a+2)\n        if b < 0: break\n        line = line[:a] + line[b+2:]\n    # Replace string literals with placeholder\n    out = []\n    in_str = False\n    i = 0\n    while i < len(line):\n        c = line[i]\n        if c == '\"' and (i == 0 or line[i-1] != '\\\\'):\n            in_str = not in_str\n            out.append('\"')\n        elif in_str:\n            out.append('X')\n        else:\n            out.append(c)\n        i += 1\n    return ''.join(out)\n\n\ndef count_braces(line: str) -> tuple[int, int]:\n    s = strip_strings_and_comments(line)\n    return s.count('{'), s.count('}')\n\n\ndef process(path: Path) -> bool:\n    text = path.read_text()\n    lines = text.split('\\n')\n    out_lines: list[str] = []\n\n    # scope_stack holds tags for each open `{`. Tags:\n    #   'type'      → struct/class/enum/protocol body — members get public\n    #   'extension' → extension body — members get public\n    #   'func'      → function body — members do NOT get public\n    #   'closure'   → block-bound braces in expressions — do NOT get public\n    #   'other'     → fallback (e.g. control flow if/for/while/do/switch)\n    scope_stack: list[str] = []\n\n    in_block_comment = False\n\n    for raw in lines:\n        line = raw\n\n        # Crude block-comment continuation skip (we won't transform comment lines).\n        if in_block_comment:\n            if '*/' in line:\n                in_block_comment = False\n            out_lines.append(line)\n            continue\n\n        stripped = line.lstrip()\n\n        if stripped.startswith('//') or stripped == '' or stripped.startswith('#'):\n            out_lines.append(line)\n            # still count braces in case (rare in comments)\n            continue\n\n        # Detect block comment start without end on same line.\n        if '/*' in line and '*/' not in line[line.find('/*')+2:]:\n            in_block_comment = True\n            out_lines.append(line)\n            continue\n\n        # Determine if THIS line has a decl that needs public-ization.\n        m = DECL_RE.match(line)\n        in_member_scope = (len(scope_stack) == 0\n                           or scope_stack[-1] in ('type', 'extension', 'top'))\n        # 'top' means we're at file top-level — also publicize.\n\n        # Effective scope: if stack empty, treat as 'top'.\n        effective_scope = scope_stack[-1] if scope_stack else 'top'\n        publicize = effective_scope in ('top', 'type', 'extension')\n\n        new_line = line\n        if m and publicize:\n            # Skip if access modifier already present somewhere in modifiers/attrs/keyword head\n            head = line[:m.end()]\n            if not ACCESS_RE.search(head):\n                # Insert 'public ' before the keyword (after attrs+modifiers)\n                indent = m.group('indent')\n                attrs = m.group('attrs') or ''\n                modifiers = m.group('modifiers') or ''\n                rest = line[m.start('keyword'):]\n                new_line = f\"{indent}{attrs}{modifiers}public {rest}\"\n        out_lines.append(new_line)\n\n        # Update scope stack based on braces opened/closed on THIS line.\n        # Determine what kind of scope the OPENED braces represent.\n        opens, closes = count_braces(new_line)\n\n        # Heuristic: if THIS line's stripped-decl indicates a type/extension/func, then\n        # the next opening { belongs to that scope. If the same line has both `{` and\n        # the decl, the FIRST `{` is the type/extension/func body. Subsequent `{` on the\n        # same line (rare) we tag 'other'.\n        scope_for_opens: list[str] = []\n        if m:\n            kw = m.group('keyword')\n            if kw in ('struct', 'enum', 'class', 'protocol'):\n                scope_for_opens.append('type')\n            elif kw == 'extension':\n                scope_for_opens.append('extension')\n            elif kw in ('func', 'init', 'subscript'):\n                scope_for_opens.append('func')\n            elif kw in ('var', 'let'):\n                # `var foo: Int { get { ... } set { ... } }` — opens are accessor blocks.\n                # `var foo = { ... }()` — closure literal. Either way: not type members.\n                scope_for_opens.append('closure')\n            else:\n                scope_for_opens.append('other')\n        # Pad remaining `{` on the line with 'other'.\n        while len(scope_for_opens) < opens:\n            scope_for_opens.append('other')\n\n        # Apply braces: pop closes first if they appear before opens? In practice, on the\n        # same line you can have `} else {` etc. We process closes then opens for simplicity.\n        for _ in range(closes):\n            if scope_stack:\n                scope_stack.pop()\n        for tag in scope_for_opens:\n            scope_stack.append(tag)\n\n    new_text = '\\n'.join(out_lines)\n    if new_text != text:\n        path.write_text(new_text)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef main():\n    changed = []\n    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:\n        p = Path(arg)\n        if process(p):\n            changed.append(p)\n    print(f\"Changed {len(changed)} files\")\n    for p in changed:\n        print(f\"  {p}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n"
}

import Foundation
import SwiftUIFlux

public func moviesStateReducer(state: MoviesState, action: Action) -> MoviesState {
    var state = state
    switch action {
    case let action as MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList:
        if action.page == 1 {
            state.moviesList[action.list] = action.response.results.map{ $0.id }
        } else {
            if var list = state.moviesList[action.list] {
                list.append(contentsOf: action.response.results.map{ $0.id })
                state.moviesList[action.list] = list
            } else {
                state.moviesList[action.list] = action.response.results.map{ $0.id }
            }
        }
        state.movies += action.response.results

    case let action as MoviesActions.SetLoadingState:
        // Generic loading-state transition: nil-state clears the
        // entry. Success paths in AsyncAction completion handlers
        // dispatch SetLoadingState(state: nil), so a successful
        // response banishes any prior error banner without an
        // additional reducer hook here.

  "file_path": "/tmp/pbxproj_remove_files.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Remove all references to a list of moved Swift files from a project.pbxproj.\n\nFor each filename, find:\n  - Its PBXFileReference UUID\n  - All PBXBuildFile UUIDs that reference that fileRef\n  - Then strip all lines that contain ANY of those UUIDs\n\nSide-effect-free style: it just removes lines whose entire content references\none of the doomed UUIDs. Empty groups are left empty (Xcode tolerates that).\n\"\"\"\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nPBXPROJ = Path(sys.argv[1])\nNAMES = sys.argv[2:]\ntext = PBXPROJ.read_text()\n\n# Find each file's PBXFileReference UUID (path = Foo.swift; pattern).\nfile_ref_uuids: set[str] = set()\nbuild_file_uuids: set[str] = set()\n\nfor name in NAMES:\n    # Match: <UUID> /* Foo.swift */ = {isa = PBXFileReference; ... path = Foo.swift; ...\n    pat = re.compile(\n        r'^\\s*([0-9A-F]{24})\\s*/\\*\\s*' + re.escape(name) + r'\\s*\\*/\\s*=\\s*\\{isa = PBXFileReference;[^}]*?path = ' + re.escape(name) + r'\\s*;',\n        re.MULTILINE,\n    )\n    for m in pat.finditer(text):\n        file_ref_uuids.add(m.group(1))\n\n# Find all PBXBuildFile entries that reference any of those file refs.\nfor fref in file_ref_uuids:\n    pat = re.compile(\n        r'^\\s*([0-9A-F]{24})\\s*/\\*\\s*\\S+\\.swift\\s+in\\s+Sources\\s*\\*/\\s*=\\s*\\{isa = PBXBuildFile;\\s*fileRef = '\n        + re.escape(fref),\n        re.MULTILINE,\n    )\n    for m in pat.finditer(text):\n        build_file_uuids.add(m.group(1))\n\ndoomed = file_ref_uuids | build_file_uuids\nprint(f\"Found {len(file_ref_uuids)} file refs, {len(build_file_uuids)} build files = {len(doomed)} UUIDs to scrub\")\n\n# Now remove every line that mentions any doomed UUID.\nremoved = 0\nnew_lines = []\nfor line in text.split('\\n'):\n    if any(uuid in line for uuid in doomed):\n        removed += 1\n        continue\n    new_lines.append(line)\n\nnew_text = '\\n'.join(new_lines)\nPBXPROJ.write_text(new_text)\nprint(f\"Removed {removed} lines from pbxproj\")\n"
}

15	    static public func persistentSnapshot(from state: AppState) -> AppState {
16	        var snapshot = AppState()
17	        let preservedMovieIds = preservedMovieIds(from: state)
18	
19	        snapshot.moviesState.movies = state.moviesState.movies.filter { preservedMovieIds.contains($0.key) }

21	        snapshot.moviesState.seenlist = state.moviesState.seenlist
22	        snapshot.moviesState.moviesUserMeta = state.moviesState.moviesUserMeta.filter {

30	            state.peoplesState.fanClub.contains($0.key)
31	        }
32	        snapshot.peoplesState.fanClub = state.peoplesState.fanClub
33	
34	        return snapshot
35	    }

37	    private static func preservedMovieIds(from state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {
38	        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist
39	        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)
40	
41	        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {
42	            ids.formUnion(list.movies)
43	            if let cover = list.cover {
44	                ids.insert(cover)
45	            }
46	        }
47	
48	        return ids
49	    }
50	}

52	public func appStateReducer(state: AppState, action: Action) -> AppState {
53	    if action is AppActions.ClearCachedData {
54	        return AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state)
55	    }
56	    if let importAction = action as? AppActions.ImportAppData {
57	        return AppDataImport.merge(envelope: importAction.envelope, into: state)
58	    }
59	
60	    var state = state
61	    state.moviesState = moviesStateReducer(state: state.moviesState, action: action)
62	    state.peoplesState = peoplesStateReducer(state: state.peoplesState, action: action)
63	    return state
64	}

Any file that mentions any of these\n# (as a whole-word token) needs the import.\nTYPES_AND_SYMBOLS = [\n    # State types\n    \"AppState\", \"MoviesState\", \"PeoplesState\", \"MoviesListLoadingState\",\n    # Models\n    \"Movie\", \"People\", \"Genre\", \"Keyword\", \"Keywords\", \"ImageData\", \"MovieImages\",\n    \"Review\", \"Video\", \"CustomList\", \"DiscoverFilter\", \"MovieUserMeta\",\n    \"PaginatedResponse\", \"CastResponse\", \"productionCountry\",\n    # Actions\n    \"MoviesActions\", \"PeopleActions\",\n    # Reducers (top-level functions)\n    \"moviesStateReducer\", \"peoplesStateReducer\",\n    # Middleware\n    \"AppLoggingPolicy\", \"loggingMiddleware\",\n    # Misc\n    \"MoviesMenu\", \"MoviesSort\", \"sortedMoviesIds\",\n    \"sampleMovie\", \"sampleCasts\",\n    \"makePreviewSampleState\", \"makeUISmokeTestState\",\n    \"LoadingKey\", \"MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter\", \"MoviesListLoadingPhase\",\n]\n\n# Word-boundary regex to avoid false positives like 'sampleMovieX'.\nTYPE_RE = re.compile(r'\\b(?:' + '|'.join(re.escape(t) for t in TYPES_AND_SYMBOLS) + r')\\b')\n\n\ndef insert_import(text: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Insert `import MovieSwiftFluxCore` after the last existing `import` line.\n    Returns new text, or None if nothing to insert (already imported).\"\"\"\n    if re.search(r'^import\\s+MovieSwiftFluxCore\\b', text, re.MULTILINE):\n        return None\n    # Find last `import X` line index\n    lines = text.split('\\n')\n    last_import = -1\n    for i, l in enumerate(lines):\n        if re.match(r'^\\s*import\\s+\\w', l):\n            last_import = i\n    if last_import < 0:\n        # No import lines? Insert at top, before the first non-comment non-blank.\n        # This is unusual — most Swift files have at least `import Foundation`.\n        # We'll punt and not insert.\n        return None\n    lines.insert(last_import + 1, 'import MovieSwiftFluxCore')\n    return '\\n'.join(lines)\n\n\ndef needs_import(text: str) -> bool:\n    # Strip strings/comments? For speed and simplicity, just regex over whole body.\n    # Only test the body AFTER the import block ends to avoid matching in comments above imports.\n    return bool(TYPE_RE.search(text))\n\n\ndef main():\n    changed = []\n    skipped_already = []\n    skipped_no_match = 0\n\n    for d in SCAN_DIRS:\n        if not d.exists():\n            continue\n        for p in d.rglob('*.swift'):\n            if any(part in SKIP_DIR_NAMES for part in p.parts):\n                continue\n            text = p.read_text()\n            if not needs_import(text):\n                skipped_no_match += 1\n                continue\n            new_text = insert_import(text)\n            if new_text is None:\n                skipped_already.append(p)\n                continue\n            p.write_text(new_text)\n            changed.append(p)\n\n    print(f\"Changed: {len(changed)}\")\n    for p in changed[:30]:\n        print(f\"  {p.relative_to(ROOT)}\")\n    if len(changed) > 30:\n        print(f\"  ... and {len(changed) - 30} more\")\n    print(f\"Already imported: {len(skipped_already)}\")\n    print(f\"No package types referenced: {skipped_no_match}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n"
}

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Auto-generate `public init(...)` for every public struct in a Swift file\nthat has stored properties and no explicit init.\n\nApproach: for each `public struct X` block, walk the body, collect lines that\nlook like stored property declarations (`public let name: Type` or `public var name: Type [= default]`),\nthen insert a `public init(...)` after the last stored property.\n\nSkips structs that already have any `init`.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nPROP_RE = re.compile(\n    r'^(?P<indent>\\s+)public\\s+(?P<kind>let|var)\\s+(?P<name>\\w+)\\s*:\\s*(?P<type>[^=]+?)(?P<default>\\s*=\\s*.+)?$'\n)\nCOMPUTED_HINT_RE = re.compile(r'\\{\\s*$|\\{\\s*get|\\{\\s*didSet|\\{\\s*willSet')\n# Lines that should END the property collection — control flow / function / nested type / closing brace.\nEND_PROP_RE = re.compile(r'^\\s+(?:public\\s+)?(?:func|init|subscript|struct|enum|class|protocol|@|//\\s*MARK|//\\s*-)|^\\s*\\}')\n\n\ndef find_struct_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Yield (start_line, end_line, indent) for each `public struct` block.\n    end_line is the line number of the closing brace at the struct's indent level.\n    \"\"\"\n    blocks: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []\n    i = 0\n    while i < len(lines):\n        m = re.match(r'^(?P<indent>\\s*)public\\s+(?:final\\s+)?struct\\s+\\w', lines[i])\n        if not m:\n            i += 1\n            continue\n        indent = m.group('indent')\n        # find the closing `}` at exactly this indent level\n        depth = 0\n        seen_open = False\n        for j in range(i, len(lines)):\n            stripped = lines[j].strip()\n            for c in lines[j]:\n                if c == '{':\n                    depth += 1\n                    seen_open = True\n                elif c == '}':\n                    depth -= 1\n                    if seen_open and depth == 0:\n                        blocks.append((i, j, indent))\n                        i = j + 1\n                        break\n            else:\n                continue\n            break\n        else:\n            i += 1\n    return blocks\n\n\ndef has_explicit_init(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int) -> bool:\n    for j in range(start, end + 1):\n        if re.match(r'^\\s+(?:public\\s+|private\\s+|fileprivate\\s+|internal\\s+)?init\\b', lines[j]):\n            return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef collect_props(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return list of (name, type) for stored properties in the struct body.\n    Skips computed properties (those with `{` after the type).\n    \"\"\"\n    props: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    j = start + 1\n    while j < end:\n        line = lines[j]\n        # Multi-line computed property detection: if we see `public let x: T {` or\n        # the next line is `{ ... }`-style, skip.\n        m = PROP_RE.match(line)\n        if m:\n            name = m.group('name')\n            tp = m.group('type').strip()\n            # Skip computed property — `{` at end of type line\n            if line.rstrip().endswith('{') or '{' in tp:\n                j += 1\n                continue\n            # Skip if next non-empty line opens a `{` (computed property body)\n            k = j + 1\n            while k < end and lines[k].strip() == '':\n                k += 1\n            if k < end and lines[k].strip().startswith('{'):\n                j += 1\n                continue\n            # Skip if there's an immediate default — we still keep it as a param though\n            props.append((name, tp))\n        j += 1\n    return props\n\n\ndef gen_init(props: list[tuple[str, str]], indent: str) -> list[str]:\n    if not props:\n        return []\n    inner = indent + '    '\n    out: list[str] = []\n    out.append('')  # blank line above\n    out.append(f\"{inner}public init(\")\n    for k, (name, tp) in enumerate(props):\n        comma = ',' if k < len(props) - 1 else ''\n        out.append(f\"{inner}    {name}: {tp}{comma}\")\n    out.append(f\"{inner}) {{\")\n    for name, _tp in props:\n        out.append(f\"{inner}    self.{name} = {name}\")\n    out.append(f\"{inner}}}\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef find_insertion_point(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Insert AFTER the last consecutive stored-property line, or right after the\n    opening brace if none.\"\"\"\n    # Find the opening { line\n    open_line = start\n    for j in range(start, end + 1):\n        if '{' in lines[j]:\n            open_line = j\n            break\n    # Walk down, tracking the last property line.\n    last_prop_line = open_line\n    j = open_line + 1\n    while j < end:\n        if PROP_RE.match(lines[j]):\n            # ensure not computed\n            if lines[j].rstrip().endswith('{'):\n                break\n            last_prop_line = j\n            j += 1\n            continue\n        if lines[j].strip() == '':\n            j += 1\n            continue\n        break\n    return last_prop_line + 1\n\n\ndef process_file(path: Path) -> bool:\n    text = path.read_text()\n    lines = text.split('\\n')\n    blocks = find_struct_blocks(lines)\n\n    # Process from bottom up so insertions don't shift later block boundaries.\n    edits: list[tuple[int, list[str]]] = []\n    for start, end, indent in blocks:\n        if has_explicit_init(lines, start, end):\n            continue\n        props = collect_props(lines, start, end)\n        if not props:\n            continue\n        ins = find_insertion_point(lines, start, end)\n        new_lines = gen_init(props, indent)\n        edits.append((ins, new_lines))\n\n    if not edits:\n        return False\n\n    edits.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])\n    for ins, new_lines in edits:\n        lines[ins:ins] = new_lines\n\n    new_text = '\\n'.join(lines)\n    if new_text != text:\n        path.write_text(new_text)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef main():\n    changed = []\n    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:\n        p = Path(arg)\n        if process_file(p):\n            changed.append(p)\n    print(f\"Changed {len(changed)} files\")\n    for p in changed:\n        print(f\"  {p}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n"
}

  "new_string": "def collect_props(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int, struct_indent: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return list of (name, type) for stored properties in the struct body.\n    Skips computed properties (those with `{` after the type).\n    Only collects properties at the IMMEDIATE indent level inside the struct\n    (struct_indent + one level), not deeper-nested types.\n    \"\"\"\n    props: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    target_indent = struct_indent + '    '\n\n    # Track brace depth WITHIN the struct so we skip nested type bodies.\n    depth = 0  # 0 = directly in struct body, >0 = inside a nested type/function\n    j = start\n    # Find the opening brace of the struct\n    while j < end and '{' not in lines[j]:\n        j += 1\n    j += 1\n    while j < end:\n        line = lines[j]\n        # Update depth based on braces on this line BEFORE collecting from it.\n        # If depth is 0 and the line is at target_indent and matches PROP_RE, collect.\n        if depth == 0:\n            m = PROP_RE.match(line)\n            if m and m.group('indent') == target_indent:\n                tp = m.group('type').strip()\n                # Skip computed property — `{` at end of type line\n                if line.rstrip().endswith('{') or '{' in tp:\n                    pass\n                else:\n                    # Skip if next non-empty line opens a `{` (computed property body)\n                    k = j + 1\n                    while k < end and lines[k].strip() == '':\n                        k += 1\n                    if k < end and lines[k].strip().startswith('{'):\n                        pass\n                    else:\n                        props.append((m.group('name'), tp))\n        # Update depth from braces on this line.\n        for c in line:\n            if c == '{':\n                depth += 1\n            elif c == '}':\n                depth -= 1\n        j += 1\n    return props"
}

  "new_string": "def find_struct_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Yield (start_line, end_line, indent) for EVERY `public struct` block,\n    including nested ones. end_line is the closing brace at the struct's indent.\n    \"\"\"\n    blocks: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []\n    for i, line in enumerate(lines):\n        m = re.match(r'^(?P<indent>\\s*)public\\s+(?:final\\s+)?struct\\s+\\w', line)\n        if not m:\n            continue\n        indent = m.group('indent')\n        # find the closing `}` at exactly this indent level via brace counting\n        depth = 0\n        seen_open = False\n        end = -1\n        for j in range(i, len(lines)):\n            for c in lines[j]:\n                if c == '{':\n                    depth += 1\n                    seen_open = True\n                elif c == '}':\n                    depth -= 1\n                    if seen_open and depth == 0:\n                        end = j\n                        break\n            if end >= 0:\n                break\n        if end >= 0:\n            blocks.append((i, end, indent))\n    return blocks"
}

  "new_string": "        if has_explicit_init(lines, start, end):\n            continue\n        props = collect_props(lines, start, end, indent)\n\n        # Special case: single-line struct definition `public struct X { }` or `public struct X: Action { }`.\n        # Replace it with a multi-line form including the new init.\n        if start == end:\n            line = lines[start]\n            single_line_re = re.compile(r'^(\\s*)public\\s+(?:final\\s+)?struct\\s+(\\w+(?:<[^>]+>)?)((?:\\s*:\\s*[^{]+?)?)\\s*\\{\\s*\\}\\s*$')\n            m2 = single_line_re.match(line)\n            if m2 and not props:\n                inner = indent + '    '\n                replacement = [\n                    f\"{m2.group(1)}public struct {m2.group(2)}{m2.group(3)} {{\",\n                    f\"{inner}public init() {{}}\",\n                    f\"{m2.group(1)}}}\",\n                ]\n                # Replace in-place by editing the line.\n                edits.append((start, replacement, True))\n                continue\n            # If single-line with a body but no closing brace handling — skip.\n            continue\n\n        ins = find_insertion_point(lines, start, end)\n        if props:\n            new_lines = gen_init(props, indent)\n        else:\n            # Empty public struct still needs a `public init()` so callers in\n            # other modules can construct it.\n            inner = indent + '    '\n            new_lines = ['', f'{inner}public init() {{}}']\n        edits.append((ins, new_lines, False))"
}

  "content": "import Foundation\nimport SwiftUIFlux\n\n/// Pure composition of the per-state reducers. App-shell concerns\n/// (cache-reset, on-disk import) live in a wrapper reducer in the\n/// app target, which delegates here for the routine action routing.\npublic func appStateReducer(state: AppState, action: Action) -> AppState {\n    var state = state\n    state.moviesState = moviesStateReducer(state: state.moviesState, action: action)\n    state.peoplesState = peoplesStateReducer(state: state.peoplesState, action: action)\n    return state\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/reducers/AppReducer.swift",
  "content": "import Foundation\nimport SwiftUIFlux\nimport MovieSwiftFluxCore\n\nenum AppActions {\n    struct ClearCachedData: Action { }\n\n    /// Merges the provided import envelope into the current state.\n    /// See `AppDataImport.merge(envelope:into:)` for the merge rules.\n    struct ImportAppData: Action {\n        let envelope: AppDataExportEnvelope\n    }\n}\n\nenum AppStateCacheReset {\n    static func persistentSnapshot(from state: AppState) -> AppState {\n        var snapshot = AppState()\n        let preservedMovieIds = preservedMovieIds(from: state)\n\n        snapshot.moviesState.movies = state.moviesState.movies.filter { preservedMovieIds.contains($0.key) }\n        snapshot.moviesState.wishlist = state.moviesState.wishlist\n        snapshot.moviesState.seenlist = state.moviesState.seenlist\n        snapshot.moviesState.moviesUserMeta = state.moviesState.moviesUserMeta.filter {\n            preservedMovieIds.contains($0.key)\n        }\n        snapshot.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters = state.moviesState.savedDiscoverFilters\n        snapshot.moviesState.discoverFilter = state.moviesState.discoverFilter\n        snapshot.moviesState.customLists = state.moviesState.customLists\n\n        snapshot.peoplesState.peoples = state.peoplesState.peoples.filter {\n            state.peoplesState.fanClub.contains($0.key)\n        }\n        snapshot.peoplesState.fanClub = state.peoplesState.fanClub\n\n        return snapshot\n    }\n\n    private static func preservedMovieIds(from state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {\n        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist\n        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)\n\n        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {\n            ids.formUnion(list.movies)\n            if let cover = list.cover {\n                ids.insert(cover)\n            }\n        }\n\n        return ids\n    }\n}\n\n/// App-shell wrapper around `MovieSwiftFluxCore.appStateReducer` that adds two\n/// app-only actions:\n///   - `AppActions.ClearCachedData`: drops every cached TMDB movie/person except\n///     ones the user has saved (wishlist, seenlist, custom lists, fan club).\n///   - `AppActions.ImportAppData`: merges a previously-exported state envelope.\n/// Both depend on app-target types (`AppDataImport`, `AppDataExportEnvelope`)\n/// that aren't available inside the package.\nfunc appReducerWithImports(state: AppState, action: Action) -> AppState {\n    if action is AppActions.ClearCachedData {\n        return AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state)\n    }\n    if let importAction = action as? AppActions.ImportAppData {\n        return AppDataImport.merge(envelope: importAction.envelope, into: state)\n    }\n    return appStateReducer(state: state, action: action)\n}\n"
}

- **67 / 86** package tests pass + **19 skipped** with inline TODO

## Important deviations from plan

1. **AppReducer split.** The original `appStateReducer` referenced app-shell types (`AppDataExportEnvelope`, `AppDataImport.merge`) that can't be in the package — that's a circular dependency. So I split it: the package gets a pure two-line `appStateReducer` (just the Movies + Peoples composition), and the app target keeps `appReducerWithImports` which handles the `ClearCachedData` and `ImportAppData` actions and delegates routine routing back to the package's reducer. `AppStoreFactory` and the three sample-store globals now wire up `appReducerWithImports`. Two existing tests had to switch from `appStateReducer(...)` to `appReducerWithImports(...)`.

2. **MoviesActionsTests skipped (19 tests).** These came from the agent's salvage and were authored against the pre-`makeTrackedHandler` MoviesActions contract — they assumed the `dispatch` closure fired exactly once per request. The current code emits a `SetLoadingState(.loading)` up-front and a `SetLoadingState(.failed)` on errors, so single-dispatch and `isInverted` expectations no longer hold. Skipped via `XCTSkip` in `setUpWithError` with a TODO to rewrite for tracked-handler semantics in a separate commit. Worth picking off as a small follow-up.

3. **`swift test --package-path` doesn't work.** SwiftUIFlux 0.5.1 (the version pinned in pbxproj) declares `swiftLanguageVersions: [.version("5.1")]` and the modern Swift 6 SPM CLI rejects `"5.1"` as invalid. Xcode's build system handles it fine. Tests run via `xcodebuild test` per the scheme. Inherited upstream constraint — not fixable in this commit.

4. **Package dependency on all 3 targets.** Added MovieSwiftFluxCore as a `XCSwiftPackageProductDependency` to iOS (`MovieSwift`), macOS (`MovieSwiftMac` / Film-O-Matic), and tvOS (`MovieSwiftTV`). The agent had only wired iOS + tvOS — I added macOS too.

The agent worktree has been removed.

## What "fixing" this means

The 19 tests fall into three patterns. Each pattern needs a different rewrite:

### Pattern 1 — "dispatches X on success" (12 tests)

```swift
// CURRENT (stale) shape:
var dispatchedAction: MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList?
MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(list: .popular, page: 2).execute(state: nil) { action in
    dispatchedAction = action as? MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList   // ← gets nil because
    expectation.fulfill()                                          //   first dispatch is
}                                                                  //   SetLoadingState
XCTAssertEqual(dispatchedAction?.page, 2)
```

**Fix shape**: track all dispatches, find the one of interest:

```swift
var actions: [Action] = []
let exp = expectation(description: "SetMovieMenuList dispatched")

MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(list: .popular, page: 2).execute(state: nil) { action in
    actions.append(action)
    if action is MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList { exp.fulfill() }
}

waitForExpectations(timeout: 1)

let setMenu = actions.compactMap { $0 as? MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList }.first
XCTAssertEqual(setMenu?.page, 2)
// Optional: also assert SetLoadingState(.loading) was the first dispatch and
// SetLoadingState(state: nil) was the last (the success-path clear).
```

Affected tests: `testFetchMoviesMenuListDispatchesSetMovieMenuListOnSuccess`, `testFetchGenresDispatchesSetGenresOnSuccess`, `testFetchDetailDispatchesSetDetailOnSuccess`, `testFetchRecommendedDispatchesSetRecommendedOnSuccess`, `testFetchSimilarDispatchesSetSimilarOnSuccess`, `testFetchVideosDispatchesSetVideosOnSuccess`, `testFetchSearchDispatchesSetSearchOnSuccess`, `testFetchSearchKeywordDispatchesSetSearchKeywordOnSuccess`, `testFetchMoviesGenreDispatchesSetMovieForGenreOnSuccess`, `testFetchMovieReviewsDispatchesSetMovieReviewsOnSuccess`, `testFetchMovieWithCrewDispatchesSetMovieWithCrewOnSuccess`, `testFetchMovieWithKeywordsDispatchesSetMovieWithKeywordOnSuccess`, `testFetchRandomDiscoverDispatchesSetRandomDiscoverOnSuccess`, `testFetchRandomDiscoverUsesRandomFilterWhenNilProvided`.

### Pattern 2 — "does not dispatch on failure" (4 tests)

```swift
// CURRENT (stale) shape:
let exp = expectation(description: "No dispatch on network error")
exp.isInverted = true                                              // ← will fail because
MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(...).execute(state: nil) { _ in  //   SetLoadingState(.failed)
    exp.fulfill()                                                  //   IS dispatched on failure
}
waitForExpectations(timeout: 0.2)
```

**Fix shape**: invert the test — the new contract _does_ dispatch on failure (a `SetLoadingState(.failed(...))`). Assert that:

```swift
var actions: [Action] = []
let exp = expectation(description: "SetLoadingState(.failed) dispatched")

MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(list: .upcoming, page: 1).execute(state: nil) { action in
    actions.append(action)
    if let setLoading = action as? MoviesActions.SetLoadingState,
       case .failed = setLoading.state { exp.fulfill() }
}
waitForExpectations(timeout: 1)

XCTAssertNil(actions.compactMap { $0 as? MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList }.first,
             "Failure path should not dispatch a Set… data action")
```

Affected: `testFetchMoviesMenuListDoesNotDispatchWhenAPIKeyMissing`, `testFetchMoviesMenuListDoesNotDispatchOnNetworkError`, `testFetchMoviesMenuListDoesNotDispatchOnDecodingError`, `testFetchGenresDoesNotDispatchOnFailure`, `testFetchDetailDoesNotDispatchOnFailure`.

### Pattern 3 — already-passing assertions buried inside skipped suite

These are the URL/path/queryItems assertions in the success-path tests (e.g. `XCTAssertTrue(components.path.contains("/movie/popular"))`, `XCTAssertEqual(queryItems["api_key"], "test-key")`). They're correct — they just happen to live in test methods that fail on the action-shape assertions before reaching them. Once Pattern 1 is fixed, these assertions come along for free.

## Estimate

~20–30 lines of mechanical rewrite per test, two test patterns, around 19 tests. Plus probably one or two helper methods (`firstDispatched<T>(in: [Action]) -> T?`, etc.) to keep the rewrite from being ratty. **One focused commit, probably 60–90 minutes** since the fixture data and mock plumbing are all already correct — only the assertion shape needs updating.

Want me to do that as the next commit? It'd close out the "19 skipped" line in the test report so the package suite returns to a "0 skipped" baseline.

1	//  Per-menu loading state for the home movie lists (Popular, Top
2	//  Rated, Upcoming, Now Playing, Trending). Lets the UI show an
3	//  inline error + retry banner when a TMDB request fails instead of
4	//  silently leaving the list empty forever — the "case .failure(_):
5	//  break" path that used to swallow every error.
6	//
7	//  This file holds the pure-logic types and an APIError → presenter
8	//  translator. The reducer wires it into MoviesState.
9	
10	import Foundation
11	import Backend
12	
13	/// Where a per-menu list is in its load lifecycle. Only stored when
14	/// not idle/loaded — `nil` in the dict means "no in-flight request,
15	/// data (if any) is the latest known good".
16	public enum MoviesListLoadingState: Equatable {
17	    case loading
18	    case failed(MoviesListLoadFailure)
19	}
20	
21	/// Identifies a single in-flight (or recently-failed) request so the
22	/// UI can surface a per-context error banner. One enum covers both
23	/// Movies and People fetchers because they all funnel through a
24	/// single `loadingStates: [LoadingKey: MoviesListLoadingState]`
25	/// dictionary in `MoviesState` — keeping it unified avoids needing a
26	/// parallel state slot inside `PeoplesState`.
27	public enum LoadingKey: Hashable {
28	    // Movies
29	    case homeMenu(MoviesMenu)
30	    case movieDetail(Int)
31	    case recommended(movie: Int)
32	    case similar(movie: Int)
33	    case videos(movie: Int)
34	    case search(query: String)
35	    case searchKeyword(query: String)
36	    case moviesGenre(genre: Int)
37	    case movieReviews(movie: Int)
38	    case moviesWithCrew(crew: Int)
39	    case moviesWithKeyword(keyword: Int)
40	    case randomDiscover
41	    case genres
42	
43	    // People
44	    case personDetail(Int)
45	    case personImages(Int)
46	    case personMovieCredits(Int)
47	    case movieCasts(movie: Int)
48	    case peopleSearch(query: String)
49	    case popularPeople
50	}
51	
52	/// User-facing description of a failed list load.
53	public struct MoviesListLoadFailure: Equatable {
54	
55	    /// What kind of failure happened. Drives the UI's icon/CTA
56	    /// choice — e.g. missingAPIKey shows "Open Settings" instead of
57	    /// "Try again".
58	    public enum Kind: Equatable {
59	        case offline
60	        case rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: TimeInterval?)
61	        case missingAPIKey
62	        case server          // 5xx
63	        case unauthorized    // 401
64	        case forbidden       // 403
65	        case decode
66	        case other
67	    }
68	
69	    public let kind: Kind
70	    public let message: String
71	    public let retryActionTitle: String
72	
73	    public init(kind: Kind,
74	         message: String,
75	         retryActionTitle: String = String(localized: "Try again",
76	                                           comment: "Default retry button label on inline error banners.")) {
77	        self.kind = kind
78	        self.message = message
79	        self.retryActionTitle = retryActionTitle
80	    }
81	}
82	
83	/// Translates the network-layer `APIError` into a UI-friendly
84	/// `MoviesListLoadFailure`. Pure logic so it can be unit-tested
85	/// without spinning up a SwiftUI view tree.
86	public enum MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter {
87	
88	    static public func failure(from error: APIService.APIError) -> MoviesListLoadFailure {
89	        switch error {
90	        case .missingAPIKey:
91	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
92	                kind: .missingAPIKey,
93	                message: String(localized: "No TMDB API key is configured. Add one in Settings to load movies.",
94	                                comment: "Inline error banner shown when no TMDB API key is available."),
95	                retryActionTitle: openSettingsTitle()
96	            )
97	        case .offline:
98	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
99	                kind: .offline,
100	                message: String(localized: "You're offline. Check your connection and try again.",
101	                                comment: "Inline error banner shown when the device has no network connection."),
102	                retryActionTitle: tryAgainTitle()
103	            )
104	        case .rateLimited(let retryAfter):
105	            let suffix: String
106	            if let retryAfter, retryAfter > 0 {
107	                let seconds = Int(retryAfter.rounded(.up))
108	                if seconds == 1 {
109	                    suffix = String(localized: " Try again in 1 second.",
110	                                    comment: "Trailing fragment appended to the rate-limit message when TMDB tells us to retry in exactly one second.")
111	                } else {
112	                    suffix = String(localized: " Try again in \(seconds) seconds.",
113	                                    comment: "Trailing fragment appended to the rate-limit message. \\(seconds) is the number of seconds to wait, always greater than 1.")
114	                }
115	            } else {
116	                suffix = String(localized: " Try again in a moment.",
117	                                comment: "Trailing fragment appended to the rate-limit message when TMDB doesn't tell us how long to wait.")
118	            }
119	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
120	                kind: .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: retryAfter),
121	                message: String(localized: "Too many requests to TMDB right now.",
122	                                comment: "Leading sentence of the rate-limit error banner.") + suffix,
123	                retryActionTitle: tryAgainTitle()
124	            )
125	        case .httpStatus(let code):
126	            switch code {
127	            case 401:
128	                return MoviesListLoadFailure(
129	                    kind: .unauthorized,
130	                    message: String(localized: "TMDB rejected the request — your API key may be invalid. Check it in Settings.",
131	                                    comment: "Error banner when TMDB returns 401 Unauthorized."),
132	                    retryActionTitle: openSettingsTitle()
133	                )
134	            case 403:
135	                return MoviesListLoadFailure(
136	                    kind: .forbidden,
137	                    message: String(localized: "TMDB declined the request. Your API key may not have access to this resource.",
138	                                    comment: "Error banner when TMDB returns 403 Forbidden."),
139	                    retryActionTitle: openSettingsTitle()
140	                )
141	            case 500...599:
142	                return MoviesListLoadFailure(
143	                    kind: .server,
144	                    message: String(localized: "TMDB is having a problem (\(code)). Try again in a minute.",
145	                                    comment: "Error banner for HTTP 5xx responses. \\(code) is the integer HTTP status."),
146	                    retryActionTitle: tryAgainTitle()
147	                )
148	            default:
149	                return MoviesListLoadFailure(
150	                    kind: .other,
151	                    message: String(localized: "TMDB returned an unexpected response (\(code)).",
152	                                    comment: "Error banner for unrecognised non-2xx HTTP responses. \\(code) is the integer HTTP status."),
153	                    retryActionTitle: tryAgainTitle()
154	                )
155	            }
156	        case .jsonDecodingError:
157	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
158	                kind: .decode,
159	                message: String(localized: "Got an unexpected response from TMDB. Try again.",
160	                                comment: "Error banner when TMDB's JSON response can't be decoded into the expected shape."),
161	                retryActionTitle: tryAgainTitle()
162	            )
163	        case .networkError, .noResponse:
164	            return MoviesListLoadFailure(
165	                kind: .other,
166	                message: String(localized: "Couldn't reach TMDB. Check your connection and try again.",
167	                                comment: "Error banner for transport-level network failures other than offline."),
168	                retryActionTitle: tryAgainTitle()
169	            )
170	        }
171	    }
172	
173	    private static func tryAgainTitle() -> String {
174	        String(localized: "Try again",
175	               comment: "Default retry button label on inline error banners.")
176	    }
177	
178	    private static func openSettingsTitle() -> String {
179	        String(localized: "Open Settings",
180	               comment: "Retry button label that takes the user to Settings rather than retrying the request — used when the failure is a missing/invalid API key.")
181	    }
182	}
183

The current code funnels every\nasync fetcher through `MoviesActions.makeTrackedHandler`, which emits:\n\n  1. SetLoadingState(key:, .loading)               — synchronously\n  2a. on success:\n       SetLoadingState(key:, nil)                  — clear\n       <data action, e.g. SetMovieMenuList>        — onSuccess\n  2b. on failure:\n       SetLoadingState(key:, .failed(translated))  — translated failure\n\nSo single-dispatch assertions and `isInverted` expectations no longer\nmatch. Rewrote each test to track the full dispatch trace and assert\non the relevant action.\n\nWhat changed\n- Added two private helpers that pin the dispatch-trace pattern down to\n  a few readable lines per test:\n  - `captureDispatches(waitingFor:until:timeout:when:)` runs the\n    AsyncAction against a synchronous mock session, collects every\n    dispatched action, and returns them once `until` fires the\n    expectation. assertForOverFulfill is set to false so noisy success\n    paths (where multiple actions could match `until`) don't crash\n    before assertions.\n  - `unwrapDispatched<T>(_:in:)` and\n    `assertFailureDispatch(in:for:notDispatching:)` collapse the\n    \"compactMap, XCTUnwrap, switch on .failed\" boilerplate that would\n    otherwise repeat in every test.\n  - `isFailedSetLoading(_:for:)` is a free-function predicate so the\n    `until` closures stay readable.\n\n- Renamed the four \"DoesNotDispatch{When,On}…\" tests to\n  \"DispatchesFailure…\" — the new contract DOES dispatch, just a\n  failure SetLoadingState rather than the data action. Names now\n  match what the test asserts. Affected:\n  - testFetchMoviesMenuListDoesNotDispatchWhenAPIKeyMissing →\n    testFetchMoviesMenuListDispatchesFailureWhenAPIKeyMissing\n  - testFetchMoviesMenuListDoesNotDispatchOnNetworkError →\n    testFetchMoviesMenuListDispatchesFailureOnNetworkError\n  - testFetchMoviesMenuListDoesNotDispatchOnDecodingError →\n    testFetchMoviesMenuListDispatchesFailureOnDecodingError\n  - testFetchGenresDoesNotDispatchOnFailure →\n    testFetchGenresDispatchesFailureOnError\n\n- The API-key-missing test now also asserts `session.lastRequest == nil`\n  and `resumeCalls == 0`. The pre-makeTrackedHandler test asserted\n  `resumeCalls == 1` even when the api key was nil — that was incorrect\n  for the current APIService.GET, which short-circuits with\n  `.failure(.missingAPIKey)` before the GET.\n\n- The decoding-error test additionally asserts the translated\n  `MoviesListLoadFailure.kind == .decode`.\n\n- Added `import SwiftUIFlux` so the helpers can name `Action` and\n  `DispatchFunction` directly.\n\n- Removed the `XCTSkip`-in-`setUpWithError` and the surrounding TODO\n  comment.\n\nVerification\n- Package tests: 86 pass, 0 skipped, 0 failures (was 67 pass + 19\n  skipped).\n- App-target tests: 356 pass, 0 failures (unchanged).\n- iOS, macOS, tvOS schemes all build clean.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
  "description": "Commit the test rewrite"
}

## Result

|---|---|---|
| Package tests | 67 pass + **19 skipped** | **86 pass, 0 skipped** |
| App tests | 356 pass | 356 pass (unchanged) |
| **Total** | 423 (with 19 skipped) | **442, 0 skipped** ✅ |

iOS / macOS / tvOS all build clean.

## What the rewrite looks like

Three small helpers absorb the boilerplate so each test stays focused. Success-path tests look like:

```swift
let dispatched = captureDispatches(
    waitingFor: "SetMovieMenuList dispatched",
    until: { $0 is MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList }
) { dispatch in
    MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(list: .popular, page: 2)
        .execute(state: nil, dispatch: dispatch)
}

let action = try unwrapDispatched(MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList.self, in: dispatched)
XCTAssertEqual(action.page, 2)
XCTAssertEqual(action.response.results.map(\.id), [20])
```

Failure-path tests look like:

```swift
let dispatched = captureDispatches(
    waitingFor: "SetLoadingState(.failed) for .homeMenu(.upcoming)",
    until: { isFailedSetLoading($0, for: .homeMenu(.upcoming)) }
) { dispatch in
    MoviesActions.FetchMoviesMenuList(list: .upcoming, page: 1)
        .execute(state: nil, dispatch: dispatch)
}

_ = try assertFailureDispatch(
    in: dispatched,
    for: .homeMenu(.upcoming),
    notDispatching: MoviesActions.SetMovieMenuList.self
)
```

Renamed four tests from `DoesNotDispatchWhen…` → `DispatchesFailureWhen…` because the current contract _does_ dispatch on failure (a `SetLoadingState(.failed)`) — the old name no longer matched the assertion shape. Also caught a bug-of-omission: the API-key-missing test was asserting `resumeCalls == 1` for an APIService that short-circuits with `.failure(.missingAPIKey)` before ever calling `dataTask` — fixed to assert `resumeCalls == 0` and `lastRequest == nil`.

Branch is now 68 commits ahead of origin/feature/native-macos-target. Ready for the next thing.

189	    private func handleImportSelection(_ result: Result<[URL], Error>) {
190	        switch result {
191	        case .failure(let error):
192	            // User cancellation isn't an error worth showing.
193	            if (error as NSError).domain != NSCocoaErrorDomain || (error as NSError).code != NSUserCancelledError {
194	                importErrorMessage = "Import failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
195	            }
196	        case .success(let urls):
197	            guard let url = urls.first else { return }
198	            // .fileImporter returns a security-scoped URL on macOS sandbox.
199	            // We must explicitly start/stop access while reading the file.
200	            let didStart = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
201	            defer { if didStart { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }

210	            } catch {

570	    // MARK: - macOS styled layout
571	    //
572	    // The system Form / Section look fights the rest of the app's
573	    // steam-themed design. This rebuilds Settings as a ScrollView of
574	    // grouped cards with FjallaOne section headers, steam_gold accents,
575	    // and steam_rust for destructive actions — matching the language used
576	    // by My Lists, Fan Club, Discover, and the sidebar.

578	    private func macOSContent(props: Props) -> some View {
579	        ScrollView {
580	            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 22) {
581	                regionPreferencesSection

587	            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
588	            .padding(.top, 16)
589	            .padding(.bottom, 24)
590	            .frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading)
591	        }
592	        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
593	        .background(Color.steam_background)
594	        .tint(.steam_gold)
595	        .onAppear(perform: loadCurrentPreferences)
596	        .onChange(of: selectedRegionCode) { _, _ in
597	            if !isModalPresentation {
598	                savePreferences(dispatch: props.dispatch)
599	            }
600	        }
601	        .onChange(of: alwaysOriginalTitle) { _, _ in
602	            if !isModalPresentation {
603	                savePreferences(dispatch: props.dispatch)
604	            }
605	        }
606	    }

610	    @ViewBuilder
611	    private func sectionCard<Content: View>(
612	        title: String,
613	        footer: String? = nil,
614	        @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content
615	    ) -> some View {
616	        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
617	            Text(title.uppercased())
618	                .font(.FjallaOne(size: 14))
619	                .tracking(1.4)
620	                .foregroundColor(.steam_gold)
621	                .padding(.horizontal, 4)
622	
623	            VStack(spacing: 0) {
624	                content()
625	            }
626	            .background(
627	                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14, style: .continuous)
628	                    .fill(Color.primary.opacity(0.06))
629	            )
630	            .overlay(
631	                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14, style: .continuous)
632	                    .stroke(Color.primary.opacity(0.08), lineWidth: 1)
633	            )
634	
635	            if let footer {
636	                Text(footer)
637	                    .font(.footnote)
638	                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
639	                    .padding(.horizontal, 4)
640	                    .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
641	            }
642	        }
643	    }

740	    private var aboutSection: some View {
741	        sectionCard(title: "About",
742	                    footer: "Movie and people data, posters, and biographies are provided by The Movie Database (TMDB). MovieSwift is an unofficial client.") {
743	            appVersionRow
744	            rowDivider
745	            tmdbAttributionRow
746	            // Privacy policy row only renders when an URL has been
747	            // configured via PRIVACY_POLICY_URL — keeps a placeholder
748	            // link out of dev builds and out of the App Store
749	            // submission until a real policy is hosted.
750	            if let privacyURL = privacyPolicyURL {
751	                rowDivider
752	                privacyPolicyRow(url: privacyURL)
753	            }

756	
757	    /// Reads `PRIVACY_POLICY_URL` from the app bundle's Info.plist
758	    /// and validates it parses as a real URL. Returns nil when
759	    /// unset (the substitution wasn't filled in) so the Settings
760	    /// row can be hidden.
761	    private var privacyPolicyURL: URL? {
762	        let raw = (Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "PRIVACY_POLICY_URL") as? String) ?? ""
763	        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
764	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty,
765	              trimmed != "$(PRIVACY_POLICY_URL)",
766	              let url = URL(string: trimmed),
767	              url.scheme == "https" else {
768	            return nil
769	        }
770	        return url
771	    }

1334	/// Picker sheet for restoring an older iCloud backup. Each row
1335	/// shows the version's date, the originating device when iCloud has
1336	/// it, and a Restore action. Conflict versions are flagged so the
1337	/// user knows why two backups exist for the same minute.
1338	private struct PreviousICloudBackupsSheet: View {
1339	    let versions: [AppDataICloudBackup.BackupVersionInfo]
1340	    let onRestore: (AppDataICloudBackup.BackupVersionInfo) -> Void
1341	    let onDismiss: () -> Void
1342	
1343	    var body: some View {
1344	        VStack(spacing: 0) {
1345	            HStack {
1346	                Text("Previous iCloud backups")
1347	                    .font(.FjallaOne(size: 22))
1348	                Spacer()
1349	                Button("Close", action: onDismiss)
1350	                    .buttonStyle(.plain)
1351	                    .foregroundColor(.steam_blue)
1352	                    .accessibilityIdentifier("previousBackupsSheet.closeButton")
1353	            }
1354	            .padding(.horizontal, 18)
1355	            .padding(.top, 18)
1356	            .padding(.bottom, 10)
1357	
1358	            if versions.isEmpty {
1359	                VStack(spacing: 6) {
1360	                    Image(systemName: "clock.arrow.circlepath")
1361	                        .font(.title2)
1362	                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
1363	                    Text("No previous backups available")
1364	                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
1365	                }
1366	                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
1367	                .padding(.bottom, 18)
1368	            } else {
1369	                ScrollView {
1370	                    VStack(spacing: 0) {
1371	                        ForEach(versions) { info in
1372	                            row(info: info)
1373	                            if info.id != versions.last?.id {
1374	                                Divider().padding(.leading, 16)
1375	                            }
1376	                        }
1377	                    }
1378	                    .padding(.horizontal, 8)
1379	                }
1380	            }
1381	        }
1382	        .frame(minWidth: 460, idealWidth: 520, minHeight: 320, idealHeight: 380)
1383	        .background(Color.steam_background.ignoresSafeArea())
1384	    }

1388	            Image(systemName: info.isUnresolvedConflict ? "exclamationmark.icloud" : "icloud")
1389	                .font(.title3)
1390	                .foregroundColor(info.isUnresolvedConflict ? .steam_rust : .steam_blue)
1391	                .frame(width: 26)
1392	            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
1393	                HStack(spacing: 8) {
1394	                    Text(formattedDate(info.modificationDate))
1395	                        .font(.callout.weight(.semibold))
1396	                    if info.isCurrent {
1397	                        Text("Latest")
1398	                            .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
1399	                            .padding(.horizontal, 6)
1400	                            .padding(.vertical, 2)
1401	                            .background(Capsule().fill(Color.steam_gold.opacity(0.25)))
1402	                            .foregroundColor(.primary)
1403	                    }
1404	                    if info.isUnresolvedConflict {
1405	                        Text("Conflict")
1406	                            .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
1407	                            .padding(.horizontal, 6)
1408	                            .padding(.vertical, 2)
1409	                            .background(Capsule().fill(Color.steam_rust.opacity(0.25)))
1410	                            .foregroundColor(.steam_rust)
1411	                    }
1412	                }
1413	                if let device = info.computerName {
1414	                    Text(device)
1415	                        .font(.caption)
1416	                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
1417	                }
1418	            }
1419	            Spacer()
1420	            Button("Restore") {
1421	                onRestore(info)
1422	            }
1423	            .buttonStyle(.plain)
1424	            .font(.callout.weight(.semibold))
1425	            .padding(.horizontal, 12)
1426	            .padding(.vertical, 6)
1427	            .background(Capsule().fill(Color.steam_gold.opacity(0.25)))
1428	            .accessibilityIdentifier("previousBackupsSheet.restore.\(info.id)")
1429	        }
1430	        .padding(.horizontal, 12)
1431	        .padding(.vertical, 10)
1432	    }

50	    private func detailRoot<Content: View>(title: String,
51	                                           @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) -> some View {
52	        #if os(macOS)
53	        // On macOS, SplitView wraps the detail column in a single
54	        // NavigationStack with a path binding it can reset on menu
55	        // change, so the inner per-menu NavigationStack is omitted
56	        // here to avoid stranding pushed destinations across menu
57	        // switches.
58	        content()
59	            .navigationTitle(title)
60	        #else
61	        NavigationStack {
62	            content()
63	                .navigationTitle(title)
64	                .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
65	        }

67	    }

> AGENT

Done. Commit `107877f` on `feature/native-macos-target`.

## What was wrong

In `macOSContent`:

```swift
ScrollView {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 22) { … }
        …
        .frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading)   // ← only frame
}
.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
```

`.frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading)` gives the ScrollView a content area that's at most 720pt wide and anchored to the left. SwiftUI's `ScrollView` sizes its scroll-tracking area to the content's max width, so the vertical scroller pinned itself to **column 720 from the left edge** of the pane — looking like a scrollbar floating mid-screen on any window wider than ~750pt — and the rest of the detail pane was an empty gap to the right of the card.

## The fix

One extra frame:

```swift
.frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading)   // card stays 720pt
.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)                  // wrapper fills width
```

The inner frame keeps the readable column at 720pt (so line lengths don't get unreadable on a wide window). The outer frame's `.infinity` is what makes the ScrollView's content area span the full detail pane width; default `.center` alignment puts the 720pt card in the horizontal middle. Now the vertical scroller sits flush against the right edge of the detail pane — the System Settings / Xcode preferences look.

## Scope

- **macOS only** — change is inside `macOSContent`, called from `formContent` only on `#if os(macOS)`. iOS `iOSFormContent` and tvOS layouts are untouched.
- **Layout-only** — no behavioral change. Verified visually; per CLAUDE.md guidance, the existing structural assertions (`testSettingsShowsRegionPicker`, `testSettingsShowsDebugInfo` — both checking the accessibility identifiers are present and findable) still cover the contract this view exposes to tests.
- iOS / macOS / tvOS all build clean.

Branch is now 69 commits ahead of `origin/feature/native-macos-target`.

> AGENT

Done. Commit `ab69fa2` lands on `feature/native-macos-target`.

## What was failing

Running `xcodebuild test -scheme MovieSwiftMac -destination 'platform=macOS'` failed every test before any test method even ran, with:

```
The bundle "MovieSwiftMacTests" couldn't be loaded.
dlopen ... code signature ... not valid for use in process:
mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs
```

Same symptom on `MovieSwiftMacUITests` ("Test crashed with signal kill before establishing connection" — the bug I'd flagged as "environmental" earlier was actually this).

## Why

| Target | Code-signing |
|---|---|
| `Film-O-Matic.app` (host) | `ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME = YES`, `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic`, signs with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = 27ZDER873F` |
| `MovieSwiftMacTests.xctest` | `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED = NO`, `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = "-"` — unsigned |
| `MovieSwiftMacUITests.xctest` | same |

Hardened runtime + Library Validation refuses to `dlopen` an unsigned `.xctest` into a properly-signed host process. The runner died during bootstrap, never reaching any test method. iOS doesn't enforce this so iOS tests worked even with the same shape.

## Fix

Replaced the three signing-disabled flags on both Mac test targets (Debug + Release) with `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic`. They now inherit `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = 27ZDER873F` from the project and sign with the same automatic identity as the host app — bundle loads, tests run.

## After

| Scheme | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `MovieSwiftMac` (unit tests, `-skip-testing:MovieSwiftMacUITests`) | 0 tests run, bundle load failed | **349 tests pass** |
| `MovieSwiftMac` UI test (single sample, `testSettingsShowsRegionPicker`) | crash with signal kill | **passes** |
| `MovieSwift` (iOS) | 442 pass | 442 pass (unchanged) |
| `MovieSwiftTV` | 106 pass | 106 pass (unchanged — tvOS host has `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = ""` and the simulator doesn't enforce library validation, so the existing config stays consistent with its host) |

## Follow-up flagged

While diagnosing, I noticed `Shared/Localizable.xcstrings` auto-pruning ~6 string keys (`"You're offline. Check your connection and try again."`, `"Couldn't reach TMDB..."`, etc.) — those `String(localized:)` calls live in `MoviesListLoadingState.swift`, which moved into the `MovieSwiftFluxCore` package, so the app-target string-extractor no longer sees them. I spawned a chip ("Re-add localized strings pruned by package extraction") to give the package its own catalog with `Bundle.module` lookups. Reverted those auto-modifications from this commit so the test-signing fix lands clean.

Branch is now 70 commits ahead of `origin/feature/native-macos-target`.

```
fix(localization): give MovieSwiftFluxCore its own string catalog

Cause
The MovieSwiftFluxCore extraction in 5076893 moved the
`String(localized:)` call sites in `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter`
into the package without a `bundle:` argument and without a package
catalog. Two regressions followed:

1. Lookups defaulted to `Bundle.main` (the app bundle), so the
   package can't be reused outside this app and tests that don't host
   in the app bundle fall through to the development-language source
   string.
2. The app target's `Use Compiler to Extract Swift Strings` setting
   only scans the app target's Swift sources, so once the calls
   moved into the package the auto-extractor stopped seeing them and
   pruned the keys from `Shared/Localizable.xcstrings` on every
   macOS build — a permanent `git diff` against the catalog.

Fix
Option A: the package now owns the strings.

- New catalog at
  `Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`
  with the 14 keys the presenter references (the six the app catalog
  had been pruning, plus "Try again", "Open Settings", and the
  per-status TMDB messages).
- `Package.swift` declares `defaultLocalization: "en"` and
  `resources: [.process("Resources")]` on the `MovieSwiftFluxCore`
  target so SwiftPM bundles the catalog and synthesizes
  `Bundle.module`.
- Every `String(localized:)` call in `MoviesListLoadingState.swift`
  now passes `bundle: .module`. The default `retryActionTitle`
  argument routes through a new public
  `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.defaultRetryActionTitle` because
  `Bundle.module` is internal and can't appear directly in a public
  default-argument expression.

Verification
- Full unit suite via `xcodebuild test -scheme MovieSwift
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro'
  -skip-testing:MovieSwiftUITests`: 446 tests pass, 0 failures
  (was 442 — 4 new package-level tests added).
- iOS, macOS, and tvOS schemes all build clean.
- `git diff Shared/Localizable.xcstrings` is empty after a clean
  build — the auto-extractor no longer prunes these keys because
  they're now also referenced by the package's own catalog.
- New tests in
  `Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/MoviesListLoadingStateTests.swift`
  resolve `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from:)` messages
  through `Bundle.module` (offline, missingAPIKey, rate-limited
  singular) and a `Bundle.module` reference that fails to compile
  if anyone removes `resources:` from `Package.swift`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

1	import XCTest
2	import Backend
3	@testable import MovieSwiftFluxCore
4	
5	/// Regression tests for the package-owned `Localizable.xcstrings`.
6	///
7	/// `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter` lives in `MovieSwiftFluxCore` and
8	/// must look up its strings against `Bundle.module`, not `Bundle.main`.
9	/// Without `bundle: .module`, lookups fall back to `Bundle.main` (the
10	/// app target's bundle when hosted, or the test runner when unhosted)
11	/// and the package can't be reused outside the app.
12	///
13	/// These tests run against the package's own bundle, so if the
14	/// catalog is missing or the call sites drop `bundle: .module`, the
15	/// English source string still falls through — which is why the
16	/// assertions below intentionally check substrings of the development
17	/// language text. The real safety net is that the catalog file ships
18	/// with the package and the build doesn't strip it.
19	final class MoviesListLoadingStateTests: XCTestCase {
20	
21	    func testOfflineFailureResolvesEnglishMessageThroughPackageBundle() {
22	        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .offline)
23	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .offline)
24	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.message,
25	                       "You're offline. Check your connection and try again.")
26	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.retryActionTitle, "Try again")
27	    }
28	
29	    func testMissingAPIKeyFailureResolvesEnglishMessageThroughPackageBundle() {
30	        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .missingAPIKey)
31	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .missingAPIKey)
32	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.message,
33	                       "No TMDB API key is configured. Add one in Settings to load movies.")
34	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.retryActionTitle, "Open Settings")
35	    }
36	
37	    func testRateLimitedSingularSecondResolvesThroughPackageBundle() {
38	        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: 1))
39	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.message,
40	                       "Too many requests to TMDB right now. Try again in 1 second.")
41	    }
42	
43	    /// `Bundle.module` is only synthesized when the target declares
44	    /// resources. Reference it from the test so anyone deleting
45	    /// `resources: [.process("Resources")]` from `Package.swift`
46	    /// breaks the build instead of silently regressing the lookup
47	    /// path back to `Bundle.main`.
48	    func testPackageBundleIsAvailable() {
49	        XCTAssertFalse(Bundle.module.bundlePath.isEmpty)
50	    }
51	}
52	
```

The package now owns its strings:
- `defaultLocalization: "en"` + `resources: [.process("Resources")]` in `Package.swift`

- `MoviesListLoadFailure.init`'s default `retryActionTitle` argument routes through a new public `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.defaultRetryActionTitle` because `Bundle.module` is internal and can't appear in a public default-arg expression

## Recommendation: tier the gaps

**Tier 1 — these touch user data and absolutely should have tests:**

1. **Export → roundtrip → Import** (iOS + macOS). End-to-end: save a wishlist movie, hit Export, capture the JSON, open Import on a fresh install with that file, verify the wishlist movie is there. This is the only thing standing between users and data loss.
2. **iCloud backup → restore** (iOS + macOS). Same shape, with the sheet flow.
3. **TMDB API key** (iOS + macOS). Paste a string → tap Save → status row goes from "No key configured" to "Using your key". Then tap Clear → status reverts. Without coverage, regressions here mean the app silently loses its main backend connection.
4. **Onboarding wizard** (all three). First-launch flow is the user's first impression and currently has zero UI test coverage.
5. **Clear cached data + iCloud restore** confirmation flows. Destructive actions without test coverage are a recipe for regressions.

**Tier 2 — widely-used flows currently uncovered:**

6. **Search** end-to-end on all three platforms (type query → see results → tap a result → land in detail).
7. **Custom list CRUD on iOS**: actual create flow, add a movie via search, delete. Currently only "form exists" is asserted.
8. **Movies pagination** on at least iOS — confirm scrolling triggers the next-page request.
9. **Spotlight deep-link** on iOS + macOS — save a movie, build the SearchableItem identifier (`MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId:)`), inject a `NSUserActivity` via launch arguments, assert a `MovieDetail` sheet opens.
10. **App Intents** routing — same pattern (`UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION` env var or similar) so Siri / Shortcuts integration doesn't bit-rot.

**Tier 3 — nice to have, lower risk if missing:**

11. macOS-specific keyboard nav (sidebar arrows, Tab/Shift-Tab, Escape-back).
12. tvOS wishlist/seenlist + focus navigation.
13. Rich movie-detail interactions: keywords, videos, backdrops carousel.
14. Sort menu, context menu.
15. Region change → list refresh (currently the assertion is only "preference persists").

## Concrete proposal

Tier 1 is **5 commits, ~12-15 new tests**. They'd cover the journeys where regressions would actually hurt users (data loss, settings amnesia, can't get into the app on first run). I'd estimate ~2 hours of work given the existing helpers.

Tier 2 is another **5-6 commits, ~10-12 tests**. Closes the "every menu has a basic happy-path" gap.

Tier 3 is open-ended — could be done as a "bring macOS to iOS-parity coverage" effort, ~1 day.

Want me to start on Tier 1? I'd suggest beginning with the **TMDB API key flow** (smallest, self-contained, exercises both `AppUserDefaults.userTMDBAPIKey` and the status-row UI logic) and then **export → import roundtrip** (highest user-data-loss risk). Each can land as its own commit so you can stop the train at any time.

//  Shared UI test utilities used across iOS, macOS, and tvOS UI test targets.

import XCTest

// MARK: - Common Constants

enum UITestConstants {
    static let uiWaitTimeout: TimeInterval = 15
    static let smokeTestArguments = ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES", "--ui-smoke-tests"]
    static let smokeTestEnvironment = ["UI_SMOKE_TESTS": "1"]
}

// MARK: - App Launch

extension XCUIApplication {
    @discardableResult
    static func launchForTesting(environment: [String: String] = [:]) -> XCUIApplication {
        let app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launchArguments = UITestConstants.smokeTestArguments
        for (key, value) in UITestConstants.smokeTestEnvironment {
            app.launchEnvironment[key] = value
        }
        for (key, value) in environment {
            app.launchEnvironment[key] = value
        }
        app.launch()
        return app
    }
}

// MARK: - Element Finders

extension XCUIApplication {
    func identifiedElement(_ identifier: String) -> XCUIElement {
        descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: identifier).firstMatch
    }

    func labeledElement(_ label: String) -> XCUIElement {
        descendants(matching: .any)
            .matching(NSPredicate(format: "label == %@", label))
            .firstMatch
    }

    func identifiedButton(_ identifierOrLabel: String) -> XCUIElement {
        let identifiedButton = buttons[identifierOrLabel]
        if identifiedButton.waitForExistence(timeout: 0.5) {
            return identifiedButton
        }
        return buttons.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label == %@", identifierOrLabel)).firstMatch
    }

    func scrollUntilVisible(_ element: XCUIElement, maxSwipes: Int = 6) -> Bool {
        if element.waitForExistence(timeout: 1) {
            return true
        }
        for _ in 0..<maxSwipes {
            #if os(tvOS)
            XCUIRemote.shared.press(.down)
            #else
            swipeUp()
            #endif
            if element.waitForExistence(timeout: 1) {
                return true
            }
        }
        return false
    }
}

// MARK: - Debug Helpers

/// Logs the app hierarchy when an element is missing. Available as a free function
/// to avoid conflicts with per-class overrides.
func logHierarchyOnMissing(_ app: XCUIApplication, element: XCUIElement, named name: String) {
    let shouldLog = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["UI_TEST_LOG_HIERARCHY"] == "1"
    if shouldLog && !element.exists {
        print("Missing element: \(name)")
        print(app.debugDescription)
    }
}

import Foundation

@propertyWrapper
public struct UserDefault<T> {
    let key: String
    let defaultValue: T
    
    init(_ key: String, defaultValue: T) {
        self.key = key
        self.defaultValue = defaultValue
    }
    
    public var wrappedValue: T {
        get {
            return UserDefaults.standard.object(forKey: key) as? T ?? defaultValue
        }
        set {
            UserDefaults.standard.set(newValue, forKey: key)
        }
    }
}
```
