Self-cleaning:\n    /// if a previous run left a user-provided key behind, we tap Clear before\n    /// running the real assertion sequence so the test starts from a known\n    /// state without needing a launch hook.\n    ///\n    /// We assert against the Clear button's appearance/disappearance rather\n    /// than the status label's text, because:\n    ///   - the Clear button is only rendered when `hasUserAPIKey` is true,\n    ///     so it's a faithful proxy for \"AppUserDefaults reflects a saved\n    ///     user key\";\n    ///   - SwiftUI's accessibility for the status row sometimes folds the\n    ///     inner Text into the row's combined label, making queries by\n    ///     standalone static-text label brittle.\n    func testSettingsTMDBAPIKeyPasteSaveAndClearRoundTrip() throws {\n        let app = launchApp()\n        openTab(\"Movies\", in: app)\n\n        let settingsButton = button(\"moviesHome.settingsButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(settingsButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        settingsButton.tap()\n\n        let apiKeyField = identifiedElement(\"settings.tmdb.apiKeyField\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(scrollUntilElementExists(apiKeyField, in: app),\n                      \"Could not scroll the TMDB API key SecureField into view\")\n\n        // Self-clean residual state from a previous run.\n        let preExistingClear = button(\"settings.tmdb.clearButton\", in: app)\n        if preExistingClear.waitForExistence(timeout: 1) {\n            preExistingClear.tap()\n            XCTAssertFalse(preExistingClear.waitForExistence(timeout: 2),\n                           \"Clear button should have hidden after tapping it\")\n        }\n\n        // Type a key into the SecureField and Save.\n        apiKeyField.tap()\n        apiKeyField.typeText(\"UI-TEST-PASTED-KEY\")\n\n        let saveButton = button(\"settings.tmdb.saveButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(saveButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        XCTAssertTrue(saveButton.isEnabled,\n                      \"Save should be enabled once the draft differs from the persisted value\")\n        saveButton.tap()\n\n        // After saving the Clear button should appear (proves\n        // AppUserDefaults.userTMDBAPIKey is now non-empty).\n        let clearButton = button(\"settings.tmdb.clearButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(clearButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"After saving a user-provided key, the Clear button should appear\")\n\n        // And Save itself should disable again because the draft now matches\n        // the persisted value (canSaveUserAPIKey == false).\n        XCTAssertFalse(saveButton.isEnabled,\n                       \"Save should disable once the draft matches the persisted value\")\n\n        // Clear and assert the Clear button hides (proves the persisted value\n        // was wiped).\n        clearButton.tap()\n        XCTAssertFalse(clearButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                       \"Clear button should hide once the user key is removed\")\n    }"

The difference is that `@AppStorage` IS a\nSwiftUI dependency: writes through it invalidate the view, so the\nstatus / Save / Clear rows refresh on the same tick.\n\n`saveUserAPIKey()` and `clearUserAPIKey()` now write through\n`persistedUserTMDBAPIKey`, and the three derived computed properties\n(`currentAPIKeySource`, `hasUserAPIKey`, `canSaveUserAPIKey`) read\nthrough it. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged.\n\nTests\nAdded four new UI tests, two per platform, covering the journey end\nto end. They use the visibility of the Clear button as the \"key is\npersisted\" signal because:\n  - It's only rendered when `hasUserAPIKey` is true, so its presence\n    proves the persisted value is non-empty.\n  - SwiftUI's accessibility for the status row sometimes folds inner\n    Text into the row's combined label, which makes a query for a\n    standalone `app.staticTexts[\"Using your key\"]` flaky.\n\nTests are self-cleaning (tap Clear at start if a previous run left a\nuser key, tap Clear at end so we don't leak it forward) so no launch\nhook is needed:\n\n  - testSettingsTMDBAPIKeyPasteSaveAndClearRoundTrip (iOS + macOS)\n    paste → Save → Clear button appears + Save disables → Clear →\n    Clear button hides.\n  - testSettingsTMDBAPIKeySavePersistsAcrossModalReopen (iOS) /\n    testSettingsTMDBAPIKeySavePersistsAcrossSidebarSwitch (macOS)\n    paste → Save → close modal / switch sidebar → reopen → Clear is\n    still visible.     func testDiscoverFilterDeleteSavedFiltersRemovesThem() {
        let app = launchApp()
        let filterButton = openDiscover(in: app)

        // First save a filter
        filterButton.tap()
        let saveButton = button("discoverFilter.saveButton", in: app)
        XCTAssertTrue(saveButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))
        saveButton.tap()

        // Reopen and verify saved filter exists, then delete all
        XCTAssertTrue(filterButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))
        filterButton.tap()

        let savedFilter = button("discoverFilter.savedFilter.0", in: app)
        XCTAssertTrue(savedFilter.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))

        let deleteButton = button("discoverFilter.deleteSavedFiltersButton", in: app)
        XCTAssertTrue(scrollUntilElementExists(deleteButton, in: app))
        deleteButton.tap()

        // After deletion, saved filter should be gone
        XCTAssertFalse(button("discoverFilter.savedFilter.0", in: app).waitForExistence(timeout: 2))
    }
}

import Foundation

enum AppLaunchMode {
    case normal
    case uiSmokeTests
    case preview

    static func current(processInfo: ProcessInfo = .processInfo) -> AppLaunchMode {
        from(arguments: processInfo.arguments, environment: processInfo.environment)
    }

    static func from(arguments: [String], environment: [String: String]) -> AppLaunchMode {
        #if DEBUG
        if environment["XCODE_RUNNING_FOR_PREVIEWS"] == "1" {
            return .preview
        }

        if arguments.contains("--ui-smoke-tests")
            || environment["UI_SMOKE_TESTS"] == "1" {
            return .uiSmokeTests
        }
        #endif

        return .normal
    }
}

  "content": "import XCTest\nimport MovieSwiftFluxCore\n#if os(tvOS)\n@testable import MovieSwiftTV\n#elseif os(macOS)\n@testable import Film_O_Matic\n#else\n@testable import MovieSwift\n#endif\n\n/// End-to-end integration tests for the user-data Export → Import journey.\n///\n/// `AppDataExportTests` covers `AppDataExport.data(from:)` in isolation;\n/// `AppDataImportTests` covers `AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope`,\n/// `previewCounts`, and `merge` in isolation. Both sides have unit\n/// coverage. What's been missing is a test that ties them together to\n/// prove the contract end users actually rely on:\n///\n///   \"I exported my library on Phone A. I install MovieSwift on Phone B.\n///    I tap Import on Phone B and pick the file. My wishlist, seenlist,\n///    fan club, and custom lists are now on Phone B.\"\n///\n/// A regression that breaks the JSON contract on either side, the merge\n/// logic, or the snapshot-trim that runs before encoding, would still\n/// pass the per-side unit tests but break the journey. These tests fail\n/// loudly if any of those pieces drifts.\nfinal class AppDataRoundTripTests: XCTestCase {\n\n    private func makeMovie(id: Int) -> Movie {\n        Movie(id: id,\n              original_title: \"Movie \\(id)\",\n              title: \"Movie \\(id)\",\n              overview: \"Overview\",\n              poster_path: nil,\n              backdrop_path: nil,\n              popularity: 0,\n              vote_average: 0,\n              vote_count: 0,\n              release_date: nil,\n              genres: nil,\n              runtime: nil,\n              status: nil,\n              video: false,\n              keywords: nil,\n              images: nil,\n              production_countries: nil,\n              character: nil,\n              department: nil)\n    }\n\n    private func makePeople(id: Int) -> People {\n        People(id: id,\n               name: \"Person \\(id)\",\n               character: nil,\n               department: nil,\n               profile_path: nil,\n               known_for_department: nil,\n               known_for: nil,\n               also_known_as: nil,\n               birthDay: nil,\n               deathDay: nil,\n               place_of_birth: nil,\n               biography: nil,\n               popularity: nil,\n               images: nil)\n    }\n\n    /// Phone A builds a library, exports the JSON file, ships it (in\n    /// memory here) to Phone B which has empty user data. After import,\n    /// every user-facing list on Phone B contains exactly what Phone A\n    /// had, and the cached movie/person records that those lists reference\n    /// rode along too.\n    func testFullRoundTripFromPopulatedPhoneAToEmptyPhoneB() throws {\n        // Phone A: user has built up a library across all four list types.\n        var phoneA = AppState()\n        phoneA.moviesState.movies[100] = makeMovie(id: 100)\n        phoneA.moviesState.movies[200] = makeMovie(id: 200)\n        phoneA.moviesState.movies[300] = makeMovie(id: 300)\n        phoneA.moviesState.wishlist.insert(100)\n        phoneA.moviesState.seenlist.insert(200)\n        phoneA.moviesState.customLists[42] = CustomList(id: 42,\n                                                        name: \"Favorites\",\n                                                        cover: 100,\n                                                        movies: [300])\n        phoneA.peoplesState.peoples[7] = makePeople(id: 7)\n        phoneA.peoplesState.fanClub.insert(7)\n\n        // Phone A: user taps Export. The bytes are what would land in\n        // their iCloud Drive / AirDrop / Files share.\n        let bytes = try AppDataExport.data(from: phoneA)\n\n        // Phone B: fresh install, empty user data.\n        let phoneB = AppState()\n\n        // Phone B: user taps Import → file picker → decode → preview →\n        // confirm. Each line is exactly what `SettingsForm` runs in\n        // sequence in `handleImportSelection` + `confirmImport`.\n        let envelope = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: bytes)\n        let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: phoneB)\n        let merged = AppDataImport.merge(envelope: envelope, into: phoneB)\n\n        // Phone B's lists now match Phone A's.\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.wishlist, Set([100]))\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.seenlist, Set([200]))\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.peoplesState.fanClub, Set([7]))\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.customLists.count, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.customLists[42]?.name, \"Favorites\")\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.customLists[42]?.cover, 100)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.customLists[42]?.movies, Set([300]))\n\n        // The cached movie/people records the lists refer to rode along —\n        // otherwise Phone B would have wishlist[100] but no Movie 100 to\n        // render, and the row would be empty.\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.movies[100]?.id, 100)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.movies[200]?.id, 200)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.movies[300]?.id, 300)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.peoplesState.peoples[7]?.name, \"Person 7\")\n\n        // The preview-counts UI shows the same numbers the user is\n        // committing to.\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.wishlistAdded, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.seenlistAdded, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.fanClubAdded, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.customListsAdded, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.customListsUpdated, 0)\n        XCTAssertTrue(counts.hasAnyChanges)\n    }\n\n    /// Phone B already has its own data; importing Phone A's export\n    /// should UNION rather than overwrite. Catches regressions where the\n    /// merge implementation accidentally replaces local state with the\n    /// envelope's snapshot.\n    func testFullRoundTripUnionsWithExistingPhoneBData() throws {\n        var phoneA = AppState()\n        phoneA.moviesState.movies[100] = makeMovie(id: 100)\n        phoneA.moviesState.wishlist.insert(100)\n        phoneA.peoplesState.peoples[7] = makePeople(id: 7)\n        phoneA.peoplesState.fanClub.insert(7)\n\n        var phoneB = AppState()\n        phoneB.moviesState.movies[200] = makeMovie(id: 200)\n        phoneB.moviesState.wishlist.insert(200)\n        phoneB.peoplesState.peoples[8] = makePeople(id: 8)\n        phoneB.peoplesState.fanClub.insert(8)\n\n        let bytes = try AppDataExport.data(from: phoneA)\n        let envelope = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: bytes)\n        let merged = AppDataImport.merge(envelope: envelope, into: phoneB)\n\n        // Both Phone A's and Phone B's prior lists are present.\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.moviesState.wishlist.contains(100))\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.moviesState.wishlist.contains(200))\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.peoplesState.fanClub.contains(7))\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.peoplesState.fanClub.contains(8))\n        XCTAssertNotNil(merged.moviesState.movies[100])\n        XCTAssertNotNil(merged.moviesState.movies[200])\n    }\n\n    /// Re-importing the same export onto a Phone B that already has\n    /// the data is a no-op — preview counts say \"nothing new\" and the\n    /// merged state equals the input. Catches regressions where the\n    /// merge double-counts or duplicates entries.\n    func testReImportingSameExportIsAnIdempotentNoOp() throws {\n        var state = AppState()\n        state.moviesState.movies[100] = makeMovie(id: 100)\n        state.moviesState.wishlist.insert(100)\n        state.peoplesState.peoples[7] = makePeople(id: 7)\n        state.peoplesState.fanClub.insert(7)\n\n        let bytes = try AppDataExport.data(from: state)\n        let envelope = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: bytes)\n        let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: state)\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.wishlistAdded, 0)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.fanClubAdded, 0)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.customListsAdded, 0)\n        XCTAssertEqual(counts.customListsUpdated, 0)\n        XCTAssertFalse(counts.hasAnyChanges,\n                       \"Re-importing the same data should not be a 'has any changes' state\")\n\n        let merged = AppDataImport.merge(envelope: envelope, into: state)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.moviesState.wishlist, state.moviesState.wishlist)\n        XCTAssertEqual(merged.peoplesState.fanClub, state.peoplesState.fanClub)\n    }\n\n    /// The export envelope's snapshot strips transient fetch caches that\n    /// don't belong to the user — pagination keys, search-result\n    /// dictionaries, popular-people lists, etc. After roundtripping,\n    /// Phone B should NOT inherit Phone A's transient fetch state, only\n    /// the user-owned lists.\n    func testRoundTripDoesNotLeakTransientFetchCaches() throws {\n        var phoneA = AppState()\n        phoneA.moviesState.wishlist.insert(100)  // user-owned\n        phoneA.moviesState.movies[100] = makeMovie(id: 100)\n        // Transient caches that should NOT cross to Phone B:\n        phoneA.moviesState.search[\"godfather\"] = [1, 2, 3]\n        phoneA.moviesState.recentSearches = Set([\"godfather\", \"casablanca\"])\n        phoneA.peoplesState.popular = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]\n        phoneA.peoplesState.search[\"spielberg\"] = [10, 20]\n\n        let bytes = try AppDataExport.data(from: phoneA)\n        let envelope = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: bytes)\n        let merged = AppDataImport.merge(envelope: envelope, into: AppState())\n\n        // User data crosses.\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.moviesState.wishlist.contains(100))\n\n        // Transient caches DO NOT cross.\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.moviesState.search.isEmpty,\n                      \"Phone A's search results should not appear on Phone B\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.moviesState.recentSearches.isEmpty,\n                      \"Phone A's recent searches should not appear on Phone B\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.peoplesState.popular.isEmpty,\n                      \"Phone A's popular-people list should not appear on Phone B\")\n        XCTAssertTrue(merged.peoplesState.search.isEmpty,\n                      \"Phone A's people search cache should not appear on Phone B\")\n    }\n}\n"
}

## Tier 1 summary

Two commits across the four chunks:

| Commit | What landed | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `4bbd4e7` | **TMDB API key UI flow** (iOS + macOS) — uncovered + fixed a real refresh bug in `SettingsForm` where the status row didn't update after Save/Clear because `@UserDefault` doesn't notify SwiftUI; switched to `@AppStorage` mirror | 4 UI |
| `adc7a03` | **Settings destructive flows** (Clear cache full path, Reset onboarding both branches) + **Export→Import roundtrip integration** | 6 UI + 4 integration |

### Total impact

| | Before Tier 1 | After Tier 1 |
|---|---|---|
| **iOS unit + package** | 356 + 86 = 442 | **360 + 90 = 450** (+4 roundtrip, +4 from earlier package work this session) |
| **iOS UI tests** | 38 | **45** (+7 — 4 API key, 1 extended clear-cache, 2 reset-onboarding) |
| **macOS UI tests** | 20 | **25** (+5 — 2 API key, 1 extended clear-cache, 2 reset-onboarding) |
| **Real bugs found + fixed** | — | **1** — TMDB API key status row didn't refresh after save/clear |

### Tier 1.2 (onboarding wizard) deferred

XCUITest can't reliably query `.fullScreenCover` content when the cover is set on the @main App's WindowGroup root — verified via `NSLog` that the wizard IS being shown (`shouldShow` returns true, the binding flips, etc.) but the contents don't appear in XCUITest's accessibility tree. The pure-logic `OnboardingFlowTests` already covers all 17 branches of the wizard's state machine. The journey-level UI test would need either a structural restructuring of where the modal is hosted, or a different testing approach (e.g. snapshot-based). Worth revisiting when there's appetite for either.

1	//  Tiny shared bus that lets `AppIntent`s drive navigation in the
2	//  SwiftUI root views without coupling them to the iOS TabView,
3	//  the macOS SplitView, or the tvOS HomeView directly.
4	//
5	//  Flow:
6	//   1. An intent's `perform()` calls `IntentNavigationStore.shared
7	//      .request(.wishlist)`.
8	//   2. The root view subscribes to `pendingDestination` via a
9	//      `@StateObject` / `.onChange` and switches its selected tab /
10	//      sidebar menu when a destination appears.
11	//   3. The view calls `consume()` (or sets `pendingDestination =
12	//      nil`) once it has navigated, so a second invocation of the
13	//      same intent re-fires.
14	//
15	//  The store is a singleton because AppIntent runs outside SwiftUI
16	//  view scope. We can't pass an EnvironmentObject in, so the
17	//  AppIntent and the view both reach for `.shared`.
18	
19	import Foundation
20	import Combine
21	
22	final class IntentNavigationStore: ObservableObject {
23	    static let shared = IntentNavigationStore()
24	
25	    /// Where an App Intent is asking the app to navigate. Each
26	    /// case maps to one of the iOS tabs or the macOS sidebar menus.
27	    enum Destination: Equatable {
28	        case popularMovies
29	        case discover
30	        case fanClub
31	        case wishlist
32	    }
33	
34	    @Published var pendingDestination: Destination?
35	
36	    private init() {}
37	
38	    /// Posts a destination request from any thread. Hopped to
39	    /// main so SwiftUI's `@Published` observation fires on the
40	    /// main actor. Safe to call from
41	    /// `AppIntent.perform()` which runs on a background queue.
42	    func request(_ destination: Destination) {
43	        if Thread.isMainThread {
44	            pendingDestination = destination
45	        } else {
46	            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in
47	                self?.pendingDestination = destination
48	            }
49	        }
50	    }
51	
52	    /// Reads and clears the pending destination. Views call this
53	    /// after acting on a request so the intent can be invoked
54	    /// again later with the same destination.
55	    @discardableResult
56	    func consume() -> Destination? {
57	        let destination = pendingDestination
58	        pendingDestination = nil
59	        return destination
60	    }
61	}
62

  "old_string": "    /// Reads and clears the pending destination. Views call this\n    /// after acting on a request so the intent can be invoked\n    /// again later with the same destination.\n    @discardableResult\n    func consume() -> Destination? {\n        let destination = pendingDestination\n        pendingDestination = nil\n        return destination\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "    /// Reads and clears the pending destination. Views call this\n    /// after acting on a request so the intent can be invoked\n    /// again later with the same destination.\n    @discardableResult\n    func consume() -> Destination? {\n        let destination = pendingDestination\n        pendingDestination = nil\n        return destination\n    }\n\n    /// UI-test seam: when `UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION` is set in the\n    /// process environment, post the matching destination to the\n    /// navigation bus. Called from a `.task` modifier on the iOS\n    /// TabbarView and macOS SplitView so the value lands AFTER the\n    /// `.onChange` subscription is in place — otherwise the change\n    /// would happen before observation starts and the view wouldn't\n    /// react.\n    ///\n    /// This is how `MovieSwiftUITests` simulates an App Intent firing\n    /// at launch (`OpenWishlistIntent`, `OpenDiscoverIntent`, etc.)\n    /// without invoking the AppIntent runtime, which can't be driven\n    /// from XCUITest.\n    static func handleUITestEnvironment(_ environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) {\n        guard let raw = environment[\"UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION\"] else { return }\n        let destination: Destination?\n        switch raw {\n        case \"popularMovies\": destination = .popularMovies\n        case \"discover\":      destination = .discover\n        case \"fanClub\":       destination = .fanClub\n        case \"wishlist\":      destination = .wishlist\n        default:              destination = nil\n        }\n        guard let destination else { return }\n        shared.request(destination)\n    }\n}"
}

We assert against content unique to that tab\n    /// (the \"movies in\" header from `MyLists.swift`) rather than\n    /// trying to inspect tab-bar selection state, which XCUITest\n    /// surfaces inconsistently.\n    func testAppIntentRoutesToWishlist() {\n        let app = launchApp(environment: [\"UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION\": \"wishlist\"])\n\n        let myListsHeader = app.staticTexts.matching(\n            NSPredicate(format: \"label CONTAINS %@\", \"movies in wishlist\")\n        ).firstMatch\n        XCTAssertTrue(myListsHeader.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"OpenWishlistIntent should land the user on the My Lists tab\")\n    }\n\n    /// `OpenDiscoverIntent` analogue — should select the Discover tab,\n    /// which exposes the filter button.\n    func testAppIntentRoutesToDiscover() {\n        let app = launchApp(environment: [\"UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION\": \"discover\"])\n\n        let filterButton = button(\"discover.filterButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(filterButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"OpenDiscoverIntent should land the user on the Discover tab\")\n    }\n\n    /// `OpenFanClubIntent` analogue — should select the Fan Club tab,\n    /// recognized by its empty-state copy.\n    func testAppIntentRoutesToFanClub() {\n        let app = launchApp(environment: [\"UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION\": \"fanClub\"])\n\n        XCTAssertTrue(app.navigationBars[\"Fan Club\"].waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"OpenFanClubIntent should land the user on the Fan Club tab\")\n    }\n}"
}

The launch hook runs the SAME parser\n    /// (`MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier:)`) and presents\n    /// the MovieDetail sheet, so this test catches regressions in\n    /// either the parser or the sheet-presentation glue.\n    ///\n    /// We use movie id 0 because the smoke-test fixture has\n    /// `state.moviesState.movies[0] = sampleMovie` — the sheet has\n    /// data to render.\n    func testSpotlightDeepLinkOpensMovieDetailSheet() {\n        let app = launchApp(environment: [\"UI_TEST_SPOTLIGHT_IDENTIFIER\": \"com.movieswift.movie.0\"])\n\n        let addToListButton = identifiedElement(\"movieDetail.addToListButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(addToListButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"Spotlight deep-link should open MovieDetail for the linked movie\")\n    }\n\n    /// Identifiers with the wrong prefix (or otherwise unparseable) MUST\n    /// be ignored — the user shouldn't see a stray MovieDetail sheet\n    /// for an unrelated app's NSUserActivity.\n    func testSpotlightDeepLinkIgnoresUnknownIdentifier() {\n        let app = launchApp(environment: [\"UI_TEST_SPOTLIGHT_IDENTIFIER\": \"com.other.app.42\"])\n\n        // Main tab bar visible; no MovieDetail sheet covering it.\n        XCTAssertTrue(app.tabBars.firstMatch.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        let addToListButton = identifiedElement(\"movieDetail.addToListButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertFalse(addToListButton.waitForExistence(timeout: 2),\n                       \"Unknown identifier should not open MovieDetail\")\n    }\n}"

144	    // MARK: - Computed views
145	    private func moviesRows(props: Props) -> some View {
146	        let movieIds = isSearching ? props.searchedMovies ?? [] : movies
147	        // Use enumeration-based identity so duplicate movie ids (e.g. 0
148	        // placeholders) don't collide in the LazyVStack.
149	        return ForEach(Array(movieIds.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { offset, id in
150	            Button(action: { navigationRoute = .movie(id) }) {
151	                MovieRow(movieId: id)
152	                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
153	                    .padding(.horizontal, 8)
154	                    .padding(.vertical, 6)
155	                    .contentShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous))
156	            }
157	            .buttonStyle(.plain)
158	            .accessibilityIdentifier("moviesList.movie.\(id)")
159	            #if os(macOS)
160	            .id(offset)
161	            .macFocusHighlight(isFocused: selectedMovieId == id || highlightedMovieId == id)
162	            .onTapGesture {
163	                selectedMovieId = id
164	                isListFocused = true
165	            }
166	            .onTapGesture(count: 2) {
167	                navigationRoute = .movie(id)
168	            }
169	            #endif
170	        }
171	    }
172	    
173	    private func movieSection(props: Props) -> some View {
174	        Group {
175	            if isSearching {
176	                Section(header: Text("Results for \(searchTextWrapper.searchText)")) {
177	                    if isSearching && props.searchedMovies == nil {
178	                        MovieRow(movieId: 0)
179	                        MovieRow(movieId: 0)
180	                        MovieRow(movieId: 0)
181	                        MovieRow(movieId: 0)
182	                    } else if isSearching && props.searchedMovies?.isEmpty == true {
183	                        Text("No results")
184	                    } else {
185	                        moviesRows(props: props)
186	                    }
187	                }
188	            } else {
189	                Section {
190	                    moviesRows(props: props)
191	                }
192	            }
193	        }
194	    }

201	                PeopleRow(peopleId: 0)

205	            } else {

216	                }
217	            }

  "new_string": "    /// Identifiers with the wrong prefix (or otherwise unparseable) MUST\n    /// be ignored — the user shouldn't see a stray MovieDetail sheet\n    /// for an unrelated app's NSUserActivity.\n    func testSpotlightDeepLinkIgnoresUnknownIdentifier() {\n        let app = launchApp(environment: [\"UI_TEST_SPOTLIGHT_IDENTIFIER\": \"com.other.app.42\"])\n\n        // Main tab bar visible; no MovieDetail sheet covering it.\n        XCTAssertTrue(app.tabBars.firstMatch.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        let addToListButton = identifiedElement(\"movieDetail.addToListButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertFalse(addToListButton.waitForExistence(timeout: 2),\n                       \"Unknown identifier should not open MovieDetail\")\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Phase 2: Search journey tests\n\n    /// Full search journey: tap the search field, type a query that the\n    /// smoke-test fixture pre-seeds results for (`uitestsearch` → movie\n    /// id 0), wait for the matching row to render in the results\n    /// section, tap it, and verify MovieDetail opens.\n    ///\n    /// The FetchSearch action dispatched by typing fires a network\n    /// request that fails in smoke-test mode (no network). The UI\n    /// shows results because `MoviesListSearchState.searchedMovies`\n    /// reads from `state.moviesState.search[query]` which the fixture\n    /// pre-populated. So this exercises the full Redux + view binding\n    /// for the search result path without needing a network mock.\n    func testMoviesSearchShowsResultsAndOpensMovieDetail() {\n        let app = launchApp()\n        openTab(\"Movies\", in: app)\n\n        let searchField = app.textFields[\"Search any movies or person\"]\n        XCTAssertTrue(searchField.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        searchField.tap()\n        searchField.typeText(\"uitestsearch\")\n\n        // The smoke-test fixture seeds search[\"uitestsearch\"] = [0].\n        // The result row should appear once isSearching flips true via\n        // the SearchField's `.onChange(of: searchText)` (fires when the\n        // text becomes non-empty).\n        let movieRow = identifiedElement(\"moviesList.movie.0\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(movieRow.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"After typing the seeded query, a matching movie row should appear in the search results\")\n        movieRow.tap()\n\n        let addToListButton = identifiedElement(\"movieDetail.addToListButton\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(addToListButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout),\n                      \"Tapping a search result should open MovieDetail\")\n    }\n\n    /// Cancel returns to the non-searching state: typing a query\n    /// produces the Cancel button (existing tests cover that); tapping\n    /// it should clear the field and hide the results.\n    func testMoviesSearchCancelClearsSearchAndHidesResults() {\n        let app = launchApp()\n        openTab(\"Movies\", in: app)\n\n        let searchField = app.textFields[\"Search any movies or person\"]\n        XCTAssertTrue(searchField.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        searchField.tap()\n        searchField.typeText(\"uitestsearch\")\n\n        let movieRow = identifiedElement(\"moviesList.movie.0\", in: app)\n        XCTAssertTrue(movieRow.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n\n        let cancelButton = app.buttons[\"Cancel\"]\n        XCTAssertTrue(cancelButton.waitForExistence(timeout: uiWaitTimeout))\n        cancelButton.tap()\n\n        // Cancel hides the search results section (isSearching goes\n        // false). The Cancel button itself disappears (only visible\n        // when the field has text).\n        let absent = NSPredicate(format: \"exists == NO\")\n        expectation(for: absent, evaluatedWith: cancelButton)\n        waitForExpectations(timeout: uiWaitTimeout)\n    }\n}"
}

import Foundation
import SwiftUIFlux
import MovieSwiftFluxCore

enum AppStoreFactory {
    static func makeStore(launchMode: AppLaunchMode = AppLaunchMode.current(),
                          isLoggingEnabled: Bool = AppLoggingPolicy.shouldEnableLogging(
                            isRunningTests: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[AppRuntime.xctestConfigurationFilePathKey] != nil
                          )) -> Store<AppState> {
        Store<AppState>(reducer: appReducerWithImports,
                        middleware: isLoggingEnabled ? [loggingMiddleware] : [],
                        state: makeInitialState(for: launchMode))
    }

    static func makeInitialState(for launchMode: AppLaunchMode) -> AppState {
        switch launchMode {
        case .normal:
            return AppPersistence.loadState() ?? AppState()
        case .uiSmokeTests:
            #if DEBUG
            return makeUISmokeTestState()
            #else
            return AppState()
            #endif
        case .preview:
            #if DEBUG
            return makePreviewSampleState()
            #else
            return AppState()
            #endif
        }
    }
}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	public protocol APIKeyProviding {
4	    func apiKey() -> String?
5	}
6	
7	public struct BundleAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding {
8	    private let bundle: Bundle
9	
10	    public init(bundle: Bundle = .main) {
11	        self.bundle = bundle
12	    }
13	
14	    public func apiKey() -> String? {
15	        guard let rawAPIKey = bundle.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "TMDB_API_KEY") as? String else {
16	            return nil
17	        }
18	        let value = rawAPIKey.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
19	        guard !value.isEmpty && value != "$(TMDB_API_KEY)" else {
20	            return nil
21	        }
22	        return value
23	    }
24	}
25	
26	/// Resolves the user-supplied TMDB key from `AppUserDefaults`.
27	///
28	/// Returns nil when the stored value is empty or only whitespace so a
29	/// chained `LayeredAPIKeyProvider` cleanly falls through to the
30	/// bundled key. The provider re-reads UserDefaults on every
31	/// `apiKey()` call, so changes the user makes in Settings are picked
32	/// up by the next API request without needing to reinitialize
33	/// `APIService.shared`.
34	public struct UserDefaultsAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding {
35	    public init() {}
36	
37	    public func apiKey() -> String? {
38	        let value = AppUserDefaults.userTMDBAPIKey.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
39	        return value.isEmpty ? nil : value
40	    }
41	}
42	
43	/// Tries each child provider in order and returns the first non-nil
44	/// key. Used to layer "user-supplied" over "bundled-default" so a
45	/// user's own TMDB key takes precedence without removing the bundled
46	/// fallback when the user hasn't entered one.
47	public struct LayeredAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding {
48	    private let providers: [APIKeyProviding]
49	
50	    public init(providers: [APIKeyProviding]) {
51	        self.providers = providers
52	    }
53	
54	    public func apiKey() -> String? {
55	        for provider in providers {
56	            if let key = provider.apiKey() {
57	                return key
58	            }
59	        }
60	        return nil
61	    }
62	}
63	
64	extension APIKeyProviding where Self == LayeredAPIKeyProvider {
65	    /// Default production resolution: try the user's saved key from
66	    /// AppUserDefaults first, then fall back to the bundle-substituted
67	    /// `TMDB_API_KEY` Info.plist value.
68	    public static var userKeyOverridingBundle: LayeredAPIKeyProvider {
69	        LayeredAPIKeyProvider(providers: [
70	            UserDefaultsAPIKeyProvider(),
71	            BundleAPIKeyProvider()
72	        ])
73	    }
74	}
75

  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/MoviesMenuListPageListenerTests.swift",
  "content": "import XCTest\nimport MovieSwiftFluxCore\n#if os(tvOS)\n@testable import MovieSwiftTV\n#elseif os(macOS)\n@testable import Film_O_Matic\n#else\n@testable import MovieSwift\n#endif\n\n/// Unit tests for the pagination trigger that drives the home-list\n/// \"scroll to bottom → load next page\" journey. The UI journey itself\n/// is hard to drive deterministically without a network mock — but the\n/// listener that translates \"bottom of list became visible\" into\n/// \"dispatch FetchMoviesMenuList(list:, page: N+1)\" is pure logic and\n/// fully testable here.\n///\n/// The reducer that handles the dispatched `SetMovieMenuList(page:N)`\n/// is covered by `MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/ReducerTests`\n/// (`testMoviesReducerSetMovieMenuListPageOneReplacesList` and\n/// `testMoviesReducerSetMovieMenuListPageTwoAppendsList`) so the\n/// data layer for pagination is covered end-to-end across the two\n/// suites.\nfinal class MoviesMenuListPageListenerTests: XCTestCase {\n\n    /// Setting `currentPage` to a new value triggers `loadPage()` via\n    /// `didSet`, which calls `dispatchPage` with (menu, page) when\n    /// `shouldLoadPage` returns true. This is exactly the path the\n    /// invisible bottom-of-list Rectangle in `MoviesList.listContent`\n    /// fires when it appears.\n    func testSettingCurrentPageToTwoDispatchesPageLoad() {\n        var captured: (menu: MoviesMenu, page: Int)?\n        let listener = MoviesMenuListPageListener(\n            menu: .popular,\n            loadOnInit: false,\n            shouldLoadPage: { true },\n            dispatchPage: { menu, page in captured = (menu, page) }\n        )\n\n        listener.currentPage = 2\n\n        XCTAssertNotNil(captured)\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured?.menu, .popular)\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured?.page, 2)\n    }\n\n    /// Changing `menu` resets `currentPage` back to 1, which itself\n    /// re-triggers `didSet`. The journey is: the user switches from\n    /// Popular to Top Rated; the listener should fire a fresh page-1\n    /// load for the new menu (and any stale page-N+1 sequence from the\n    /// old menu is abandoned).\n    func testChangingMenuResetsCurrentPageToOneAndDispatchesPageOne() {\n        var captured: [(menu: MoviesMenu, page: Int)] = []\n        let listener = MoviesMenuListPageListener(\n            menu: .popular,\n            loadOnInit: false,\n            shouldLoadPage: { true },\n            dispatchPage: { menu, page in captured.append((menu, page)) }\n        )\n        // Advance to page 3 first so we can prove the reset really happens.\n        listener.currentPage = 3\n        captured.removeAll()\n\n        listener.menu = .topRated\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(listener.currentPage, 1, \"Changing menu should reset currentPage to 1\")\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured.count, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured.first?.menu, .topRated)\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured.first?.page, 1)\n    }\n\n    /// When `shouldLoadPage` returns false (e.g. in smoke-test mode), the\n    /// listener should NOT dispatch. This is the gate that keeps real\n    /// network calls from firing during the UI smoke-test suite.\n    func testLoadPageSkipsDispatchWhenShouldLoadPageReturnsFalse() {\n        var dispatched = false\n        let listener = MoviesMenuListPageListener(\n            menu: .popular,\n            loadOnInit: false,\n            shouldLoadPage: { false },\n            dispatchPage: { _, _ in dispatched = true }\n        )\n\n        listener.currentPage = 2\n\n        XCTAssertFalse(dispatched,\n                       \"Listener should not dispatch when shouldLoadPage returns false\")\n    }\n\n    /// `loadOnInit: true` fires a page-1 dispatch right after init so the\n    /// first load doesn't wait for the user to scroll. The init path is\n    /// the same one MoviesHome wires up — without this firing, the\n    /// home grid would never see a page-1 fetch on first launch.\n    func testLoadOnInitTrueFiresPageOneDispatch() {\n        var captured: (menu: MoviesMenu, page: Int)?\n        _ = MoviesMenuListPageListener(\n            menu: .nowPlaying,\n            loadOnInit: true,\n            shouldLoadPage: { true },\n            dispatchPage: { menu, page in captured = (menu, page) }\n        )\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured?.menu, .nowPlaying)\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured?.page, 1)\n    }\n\n    /// `loadOnInit: false` does NOT fire on init. The home view sometimes\n    /// constructs the listener before it's ready to dispatch (e.g. needs\n    /// to wire up the closures first), so deferring the first load is\n    /// the explicit, callable-by-the-view behaviour we want to keep.\n    func testLoadOnInitFalseSuppressesInitialDispatch() {\n        var dispatched = false\n        _ = MoviesMenuListPageListener(\n            menu: .upcoming,\n            loadOnInit: false,\n            shouldLoadPage: { true },\n            dispatchPage: { _, _ in dispatched = true }\n        )\n\n        XCTAssertFalse(dispatched,\n                       \"loadOnInit=false should not fire a dispatch at construction time\")\n    }\n\n    /// Setting `currentPage` to the SAME value still re-fires `didSet`\n    /// (Swift's contract). This makes \"menu unchanged but pageListener\n    /// re-triggered\" deterministic: the home view explicitly relies on\n    /// resetting currentPage = 1 to refresh, even when it was already 1.\n    func testSettingCurrentPageToCurrentValueStillDispatches() {\n        var captured: [(menu: MoviesMenu, page: Int)] = []\n        let listener = MoviesMenuListPageListener(\n            menu: .trending,\n            loadOnInit: false,\n            shouldLoadPage: { true },\n            dispatchPage: { menu, page in captured.append((menu, page)) }\n        )\n        listener.currentPage = 1\n        captured.removeAll()\n\n        listener.currentPage = 1\n\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured.count, 1)\n        XCTAssertEqual(captured.first?.page, 1)\n    }\n}\n"
}

{

Both needed a way to make the\nsmoke-test runtime deterministic; one design solves both.\n\nThe seam (single source change for both)\n- Added `DisabledAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding` in Backend that\n  always returns nil.\n- Under UI smoke-test mode, the iOS HomeView and macOS MovieSwiftMacApp\n  inits now swap `APIService.shared` for one constructed with\n  `DisabledAPIKeyProvider`. Every async action that hits\n  `APIService.shared.GET(...)` short-circuits with\n  `.failure(.missingAPIKey)` before the request leaves the app, so\n  the smoke-test fixture state survives across UI interactions.\n- Without this, e.g. typing into the search field fires\n  `FetchSearch` which previously hit real TMDB and overwrote the\n  pre-seeded `state.moviesState.search[query]` dict with whatever\n  TMDB happened to return (empty results, in our case).\n\n1. Search journey (iOS + macOS)\n- Pre-seeded `state.moviesState.search[\"uitestsearch\"] = [0]` in\n  `makeUISmokeTestState()` so the typed-search journey has a\n  deterministic result row to find.\n- iOS `testMoviesSearchShowsResultsAndOpensMovieDetail` — tap search\n  field → type seeded query → \"Results for uitestsearch\" section\n  header appears → tap the seeded row → MovieDetail opens.\n- iOS `testMoviesSearchCancelClearsSearchAndHidesResults` — same\n  setup → Cancel button → typing UI clears, results section goes away.\n- macOS `testMoviesSearchShowsResultsAndOpensMovieDetail` — same\n  journey through the Popular sidebar menu's search field, ending in\n  MovieDetail showing in the detail pane.\n\n2. Pagination via listener unit tests\n- The UI journey \"scroll to bottom → load next page\" is hard to drive\n  without a network mock; the reducer side is already covered by\n  `MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/ReducerTests` (page-1 replaces, page-2+\n  appends). The remaining gap is the listener that translates\n  \"bottom-of-list visible\" into \"dispatch FetchMoviesMenuList(page: N+1)\".\n- New `MoviesMenuListPageListenerTests` (6 tests) covers\n  - Setting `currentPage = 2` dispatches `(menu, 2)` to dispatchPage.\n  - Changing `menu` resets `currentPage = 1` and re-dispatches with\n    the new menu + page 1.\n  - `shouldLoadPage { false }` (the smoke-test gate) suppresses\n    dispatch.\n  - `loadOnInit: true` fires page-1 at construction; `false` does not.\n  - Re-setting `currentPage` to the SAME value still re-fires\n    `didSet` — explicit because the home view relies on\n    \"currentPage = 1\" as a deliberate refresh signal.\n\nVerification\n- iOS unit + package suite: 366 + 90 = 456 tests, 0 failures\n  (was 360 + 90 = 450).\n- New iOS UI search tests: ~13s each on iPhone 17 Pro.\n- New macOS UI search test: ~7s.\n- iOS + macOS + tvOS all build clean.\n\nTier 2 is now complete (search + custom-list + App Intents +\nSpotlight + pagination listener). The wider pagination journey\nremains in a deferred state with a clear reason — it needs a real\nAPIService mock, which is a bigger design than the dispatch seam this\ncommit adds.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" && git log --oneline -4",

Tier 2 finale lands as `37d9ceb`.

## The seam

Single source change solves both deferred journeys:

`DisabledAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding` in Backend always returns `nil`. iOS HomeView + macOS MovieSwiftMacApp inits now swap `APIService.shared` for one using it when smoke-test mode is active. Every async action that hits `APIService.shared.GET(...)` short-circuits with `.failure(.missingAPIKey)` before the request leaves the app — which means **smoke-test fixture state survives across UI interactions**. (Previously, typing into the search field fired a real TMDB call that overwrote my pre-seeded `state.moviesState.search[query]` with whatever TMDB happened to return.)

This also makes the existing smoke-test suite faster + less flaky — no network calls during UI tests at all.

## What landed

| Feature | Tests | Location |
|---|---|---|
| **Search journey** (iOS) | 2 — `testMoviesSearchShowsResultsAndOpensMovieDetail` (type → results → tap → MovieDetail), `testMoviesSearchCancelClearsSearchAndHidesResults` | `MovieSwiftUITests` |
| **Search journey** (macOS) | 1 — same shape through the Popular sidebar menu | `MovieSwiftMacUITests` |
| **Pagination listener** | 6 — `MoviesMenuListPageListenerTests` covering currentPage-triggers-dispatch, menu-change-resets-page, shouldLoadPage-gate, loadOnInit semantics, idempotent re-set | `MovieSwiftTests` |

## Pagination — what's covered now vs deferred

| Layer | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Reducer (page-1 replaces, page-N appends) | ✅ `MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/ReducerTests` (pre-existing) |
| Listener (scroll → dispatch) | ✅ **new** `MoviesMenuListPageListenerTests` (6 tests) |
| UI journey (real scroll → real network → state grows) | ⏸ Still deferred — needs a real `APIService` mock that returns canned `PaginatedResponse<Movie>` for page 2. The dispatch seam alone isn't enough; you need the response to flow through. |

    func testFetchDetailDoesNotDispatchOnFailure() {
        let session = MockNetworkSession()
        session.nextData = nil
        session.nextError = StubError.failed

        APIService.shared = APIService(
            apiKeyProvider: StubAPIKeyProvider("test-key"),
            session: session,

        )

        let expectation = expectation(description: "No SetDetail on detail failure")
        expectation.isInverted = true

        // This test specifically checks the data action — ignoring

            if action is PeopleActions.SetDetail {
                expectation.fulfill()
            }
        }

        waitForExpectations(timeout: 0.2)
        XCTAssertEqual(session.task.resumeCalls, 1)
    }

testSettingsShowsDebugInfo is failing because `app.staticTexts["Movies in state"]` doesn't match — text inside a Form row is folded into the row's combined-accessibility `value`, not exposed as a standalone StaticText `label`. This is the same root cause as the macOS MyLists failures. **Pre-existing test bug**, not a regression.

### 🐛 One transient flake (passes in isolation)

- iOS `PeopleActionsTests/testFetchDetailDoesNotDispatchOnFailure` — fails in full run, passes when run alone. Looks like a simulator state issue, not a logic bug. Same `isInverted` expectation pattern as my refactored MoviesActionsTests but for People — semantically correct, just sometimes flakes.

### 🐛 Pre-existing UI test bugs (revealed by macOS signing fix making the suite runnable)

These were either always broken on macOS — but the bundle wouldn't load before commit `ab69fa2`, so failures were hidden — or are tests that depend on hardware features the simulator doesn't have.

| Test | Platform | Diagnosis |
|---|---|---|
| `testSettingsShowsDebugInfo` | iOS | Queries `app.staticTexts["Movies in state"]`. iOS Form rows fold the inner Text into the row's combined accessibility `value`, so the standalone-label query misses. Same root cause as the macOS MyLists tests. |
| `testMovieDetailKeyboardCanOpenTopPerson` | iOS | iPad hardware-keyboard test running against iPhone 17 Pro simulator (no hardware keyboard). |
| `testMovieDetailKeyboardReturnOpensFocusedGenreList` | iOS | Same — iPad-keyboard test. |
| `testMyListsShowsContent` | macOS | `app.staticTexts["…movies in wishlist"]` doesn't match because the SwiftUI Text's content is in the element's `value`, not `label`. Hierarchy dump confirms the text exists as `value: "1 movies in wishli..."`. |
| `testMyListsCustomListExists` | macOS | Default segment is Wishlist; custom-list rows aren't rendered until the user taps the Custom Lists segment. Test never switches segments. |
| `testFanClubPersonOpensPeopleDetail` | macOS | macOS FanClubHome opens PeopleDetail on **double**-click (`.onTapGesture(count: 2)`); test uses single `tap()`. |
| `testDiscoverDismissCanBeUndone` | macOS | After tapping `discover.dismissButton`, the test waits for `discover.undoButton` which never appears. Need to look at the macOS Discover undo behavior — may be a real UI bug or a missing identifier. |

import SwiftUI
import SwiftUIFlux
import Combine
import UI
import MovieSwiftFluxCore

enum MovieDetailLoadSlice: Equatable {
    case detail
    case credits
    case recommended
    case similar
    case reviews
    case videos
}

enum MovieDetailFetchPolicy {
    static func slicesToFetch(hasMovieDetail: Bool,
                              hasMovieCredits: Bool,
                              hasRecommended: Bool,
                              hasSimilar: Bool,
                              hasReviews: Bool,
                              hasVideos: Bool,
                              isRunningUISmokeTests: Bool) -> [MovieDetailLoadSlice] {
        guard !isRunningUISmokeTests else {
            return []
        }

        var slices: [MovieDetailLoadSlice] = []
        if !hasMovieDetail {
            slices.append(.detail)
        }
        if !hasMovieCredits {
            slices.append(.credits)
        }
        if !hasRecommended {
            slices.append(.recommended)
        }
        if !hasSimilar {
            slices.append(.similar)
        }
        if !hasReviews {
            slices.append(.reviews)
        }
        if !hasVideos {
            slices.append(.videos)
        }
        return slices
    }
}

enum MovieDetailState {
    static func movie(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Movie? {
        state.moviesState.movies[movieId]
    }

    static func hasLoadedDetail(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        guard state.moviesState.detailed.contains(movieId),
              let movie = movie(movieId: movieId, from: state) else {
            return false
        }

        return movie.keywords != nil && movie.images != nil
    }

    static func hasLoadedRecommended(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        state.moviesState.recommendedLoaded.contains(movieId) &&
            state.moviesState.recommended[movieId] != nil
    }

    static func hasLoadedSimilar(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        state.moviesState.similarLoaded.contains(movieId) &&
            state.moviesState.similar[movieId] != nil
    }

    static func hasLoadedReviews(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        state.moviesState.reviewsLoaded.contains(movieId) &&
            state.moviesState.reviews[movieId] != nil
    }

    static func hasLoadedVideos(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        state.moviesState.videosLoaded.contains(movieId) &&
            state.moviesState.videos[movieId] != nil
    }
}

enum MovieDetailListState {
    static func isInWishlist(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        state.moviesState.wishlist.contains(movieId)
    }

    static func isInSeenlist(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        state.moviesState.seenlist.contains(movieId)
    }

    static func customLists(from state: AppState) -> [CustomList] {
        state.moviesState.customLists.compactMap { $0.value }
    }
}

enum MovieDetailPeopleState {
    static func characters(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> [People]? {
        contextualPeople(movieId: movieId,
                         from: state,
                         peopleIds: state.peoplesState.movieCastOrder[movieId],
                         metadata: state.peoplesState.casts) { people, role in
            var contextual = people
            contextual.character = role
            contextual.department = nil
            return contextual
        }
    }

    static func credits(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> [People]? {
        contextualPeople(movieId: movieId,
                         from: state,
                         peopleIds: state.peoplesState.movieCrewOrder[movieId],
                         metadata: state.peoplesState.crews) { people, department in
            var contextual = people
            contextual.character = nil
            contextual.department = department
            return contextual
        }
    }

    static func hasLoadedMovieCredits(movieId: Int, from state: AppState) -> Bool {
        guard state.peoplesState.movieCreditsLoaded.contains(movieId),
              state.peoplesState.movieCastOrder[movieId] != nil,
              state.peoplesState.movieCrewOrder[movieId] != nil else {
            return false
        }

        let hasResolvedPeople = characters(movieId: movieId, from: state)?.isEmpty == false ||
            credits(movieId: movieId, from: state)?.isEmpty == false
        let hasExplicitlyEmptyCredits = state.peoplesState.movieCastOrder[movieId]?.isEmpty == true &&
            state.peoplesState.movieCrewOrder[movieId]?.isEmpty == true

        return hasResolvedPeople || hasExplicitlyEmptyCredits
    }

    private static func contextualPeople(movieId: Int,
                                         from state: AppState,
                                         peopleIds: [Int]?,
                                         metadata: [Int: [Int: String]],
                                         transform: (People, String) -> People) -> [People]? {
        let resolvedPeopleIds = peopleIds ?? state.peoplesState.peoplesMovies[movieId]?.sorted()
        guard let resolvedPeopleIds = resolvedPeopleIds, !resolvedPeopleIds.isEmpty else {
            return nil
        }

        let contextual = resolvedPeopleIds.compactMap { peopleId -> People? in
            guard let people = state.peoplesState.peoples[peopleId],
                  let role = metadata[peopleId]?[movieId],
                  !role.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else {
                return nil
            }
            return transform(people, role)
        }

        return contextual.isEmpty ? nil : contextual
    }
}

enum MovieDetailFocusTarget: Hashable {
    case genre(Int)
    case wishlistButton
    case seenlistButton
    case customListButton
    case reviewLink
    case topPerson(Int)
    case readMoreButton
    case keyword(Int)
    case castPerson(Int)
    case castSeeAll
    case crewPerson(Int)
    case crewSeeAll
    case similarMovie(Int)
    case similarSeeAll
    case recommendedMovie(Int)
    case recommendedSeeAll
    case poster(String)
    case backdrop(String)
}

#if os(macOS)
/// Adds standard macOS keyboard shortcuts to pop a pushed NavigationStack
/// destination: Cmd+[ (native "back" shortcut that matches Safari/Finder)
/// and Escape.
private struct MacBackKeyboardShortcut: ViewModifier {
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onExitCommand { dismiss() }
            .background {
                Button(action: { dismiss() }) {
                    EmptyView()
                }
                .keyboardShortcut("[", modifiers: .command)
                .frame(width: 0, height: 0)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// On macOS, enables Cmd+[ and Escape to pop the current pushed
    /// NavigationStack destination. No-op on other platforms.
    func macBackKeyboardShortcut() -> some View {
        modifier(MacBackKeyboardShortcut())
    }
}
#else
extension View {
    func macBackKeyboardShortcut() -> some View { self }
}
#endif

private struct TrackedDetailRowModifier: ViewModifier {
    let id: String
    @Binding var visibleRowIds: Set<String>

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .id(id)
            .onScrollVisibilityChange(threshold: 0.5) { visible in
                if visible {
                    visibleRowIds.insert(id)
                } else {
                    visibleRowIds.remove(id)
                }
            }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Tags a detail-view row with a stable scroll-anchor id and tracks
    /// whether it's at least 50% on-screen, feeding visibility into
    /// `visibleRowIds` so Tab navigation can skip scrolling when the
    /// focused row is already visible.
    func trackedDetailRow(_ id: String, visibleRowIds: Binding<Set<String>>) -> some View {
        modifier(TrackedDetailRowModifier(id: id, visibleRowIds: visibleRowIds))
    }
}

/// Maps a focus target to the scroll-anchor id of the row it lives in.
/// Used by the outer ScrollViewReader to scroll the focused row into
/// view when Tab / Shift+Tab jumps to an off-screen section.
enum MovieDetailFocusRow {
    static func scrollId(for target: MovieDetailFocusTarget) -> String {
        switch target {
        case .genre:                                return "row.cover"
        case .wishlistButton,
             .seenlistButton,
             .customListButton:                     return "row.buttons"
        case .reviewLink:                           return "row.review"
        case .topPerson:                            return "row.director"
        case .readMoreButton:                       return "row.overview"
        case .keyword:                              return "row.keywords"
        case .castPerson, .castSeeAll:              return "row.cast"
        case .crewPerson, .crewSeeAll:              return "row.crew"
        case .similarMovie, .similarSeeAll:         return "row.similar"
        case .recommendedMovie, .recommendedSeeAll: return "row.recommended"
        case .poster:                               return "row.posters"
        case .backdrop:                             return "row.backdrops"
        }
    }
}

/// Pure navigation decisions for the detail view's Tab / arrow focus.
/// Groups are passed in so tests can exercise the logic without a view.
enum MovieDetailFocusNavigation {
    /// Tab / Shift+Tab — jump to the first item of the next/previous group.
    /// When current is nil, returns the first (or last) group's first item.
    /// Returns nil if at the edge.
    static func nextGroupStart(from current: MovieDetailFocusTarget?,
                               in groups: [[MovieDetailFocusTarget]],
                               forward: Bool) -> MovieDetailFocusTarget? {
        guard !groups.isEmpty else { return nil }
        guard let current else {
            return forward ? groups.first?.first : groups.last?.first
        }
        guard let currentGroup = groups.firstIndex(where: { $0.contains(current) }) else {
            return forward ? groups.first?.first : groups.last?.first
        }
        let nextGroup = currentGroup + (forward ? 1 : -1)
        guard groups.indices.contains(nextGroup) else { return nil }
        return groups[nextGroup].first
    }

    /// Left / Right arrow — move within the current group only. Returns nil
    /// at the edge so the caller can leave focus alone.
    static func adjacentInGroup(from current: MovieDetailFocusTarget,
                                in groups: [[MovieDetailFocusTarget]],
                                forward: Bool) -> MovieDetailFocusTarget? {
        guard let group = groups.first(where: { $0.contains(current) }),
              let idx = group.firstIndex(of: current) else {
            return nil
        }
        let nextIdx = idx + (forward ? 1 : -1)
        guard group.indices.contains(nextIdx) else { return nil }
        return group[nextIdx]
    }
}

struct MovieDetail: ConnectedView {
    struct Props {
        let movie: Movie?
        let characters: [People]?
        let credits: [People]?
        let recommended: [Movie]?
        let similar: [Movie]?
        let reviewsCount: Int?
        let videos: [Video]?
        let hasMovieDetail: Bool
        let hasMovieCredits: Bool
        let hasRecommended: Bool
        let hasSimilar: Bool
        let hasReviews: Bool
        let hasVideos: Bool
        let isInWishlist: Bool
        let isInSeenlist: Bool
        let customLists: [CustomList]
        /// Failure for the top-level FetchDetail. Sub-row failures
        /// (recommended / similar / videos / reviews) are ignored
        /// here — those rows degrade gracefully when their data
        /// isn't loaded, and showing five separate banners would be
        /// noisy. The detail-level failure matters most because
        /// without it the whole page is empty.
        let detailFailure: MoviesListLoadFailure?
        let dispatch: DispatchFunction
    }
    
    let movieId: Int
    @EnvironmentObject private var store: Store<AppState>
    @Environment(\.isRunningUISmokeTests) private var isRunningUISmokeTests
    
    // MARK: View States
    @State var isAddSheetPresented = false
    @State var isCreateListFormPresented = false
    @State var isAddedToListBadgePresented = false
    @State var selectedPoster: ImageData?
    @State var selectedBackdrop: ImageData?
    @State private var selectedPeopleId: Int?
    @State private var selectedReviewMovieId: Int?
    @State private var selectedCrosslineRoute: MoviesListNavigationRoute?
    @State private var selectedGenre: Genre?
    @State private var selectedKeyword: Keyword?
    @State private var crosslineMoviesPresentation: CrosslineMoviesPresentation?
    @State private var peopleListPresentation: PeopleListPresentation?

    struct PeopleListPresentation: Identifiable, Hashable {
        let id: String
        let title: String
        let peopleIds: [Int]

        static func == (lhs: PeopleListPresentation, rhs: PeopleListPresentation) -> Bool {
            lhs.id == rhs.id
        }

        func hash(into hasher: inout Hasher) {
            hasher.combine(id)
        }
    }

    struct CrosslineMoviesPresentation: Identifiable, Hashable {
        let id: String
        let title: String
        let movieIds: [Int]

        static func == (lhs: CrosslineMoviesPresentation, rhs: CrosslineMoviesPresentation) -> Bool {
            lhs.id == rhs.id
        }

        func hash(into hasher: inout Hasher) {
            hasher.combine(id)
        }
    }

    #if os(macOS)
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss
    @FocusState private var focusedDetailItem: MovieDetailFocusTarget?
    @State private var visibleRowIds: Set<String> = []
    #endif
        
    // MARK: Computed Props
    func map(state: AppState, dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction) -> Props {
        var recommended: [Movie]?
        var similar: [Movie]?
        
        if let recommendedIds = state.moviesState.recommended[movieId] {
            recommended = recommendedIds.compactMap{ state.moviesState.movies[$0] }
        }
        if let simillarIds = state.moviesState.similar[movieId] {
            similar = simillarIds.compactMap{ state.moviesState.movies[$0] }
        }
        let detailFailure: MoviesListLoadFailure?
        if case .failed(let f) = state.moviesState.loadingStates[.movieDetail(movieId)] {
            detailFailure = f
        } else {
            detailFailure = nil
        }
        return Props(movie: MovieDetailState.movie(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     characters: MovieDetailPeopleState.characters(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     credits: MovieDetailPeopleState.credits(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     recommended: recommended,
                     similar: similar,
                     reviewsCount: state.moviesState.reviews[movieId]?.count ?? nil,
                     videos: state.moviesState.videos[movieId],
                     hasMovieDetail: MovieDetailState.hasLoadedDetail(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     hasMovieCredits: MovieDetailPeopleState.hasLoadedMovieCredits(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     hasRecommended: MovieDetailState.hasLoadedRecommended(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     hasSimilar: MovieDetailState.hasLoadedSimilar(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     hasReviews: MovieDetailState.hasLoadedReviews(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     hasVideos: MovieDetailState.hasLoadedVideos(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     isInWishlist: MovieDetailListState.isInWishlist(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     isInSeenlist: MovieDetailListState.isInSeenlist(movieId: movieId, from: state),
                     customLists: MovieDetailListState.customLists(from: state),
                     detailFailure: detailFailure,
                     dispatch: dispatch)
    }
    
    // MARK: - Fetch
    func fetchMovieDetails(props: Props) {
        for slice in MovieDetailFetchPolicy.slicesToFetch(hasMovieDetail: props.hasMovieDetail,
                                                          hasMovieCredits: props.hasMovieCredits,
                                                          hasRecommended: props.hasRecommended,
                                                          hasSimilar: props.hasSimilar,
                                                          hasReviews: props.hasReviews,
                                                          hasVideos: props.hasVideos,
                                                          isRunningUISmokeTests: isRunningUISmokeTests) {
            switch slice {
            case .detail:
                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchDetail(movie: movieId))
            case .credits:
                props.dispatch(PeopleActions.FetchMovieCasts(movie: movieId))
            case .recommended:
                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchRecommended(movie: movieId))
            case .similar:
                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchSimilar(movie: movieId))
            case .reviews:
                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchMovieReviews(movie: movieId))
            case .videos:
                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchVideos(movie: movieId))
            }
        }
    }

    // MARK: - View actions
    func displaySavedBadge() {
        isAddedToListBadgePresented = true
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) {
            self.isAddedToListBadgePresented = false
        }
    }
    
    func onAddButton() {
        isAddSheetPresented.toggle()
    }

    private func selectPeople(_ id: Int) {
        selectedPeopleId = id
    }

    private func primaryPeopleCredit(props: Props) -> People? {
        props.credits?.first(where: {
            ($0.department ?? "").localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("direct")
        })
    }

    private func presentCrosslineMoviesList(title: String, movies: [Movie]) {
        crosslineMoviesPresentation = CrosslineMoviesPresentation(
            id: "crossline-\(title)-\(movieId)",
            title: title,
            movieIds: MovieCrosslineState.movieIds(from: movies)
        )
    }

    private func presentPeopleList(title: String, peoples: [People]) {
        // Use a stable id based on title so repeated taps don't churn navigation.
        peopleListPresentation = PeopleListPresentation(
            id: "peopleList-\(title)-\(movieId)",
            title: title,
            peopleIds: peoples.map { $0.id }
        )
    }

    #if os(macOS)
    private func genreTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        (props.movie?.genres ?? []).map { .genre($0.id) }
    }

    private var actionTargets: [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        [.wishlistButton, .seenlistButton, .customListButton]
    }

    private func reviewTarget(props: Props) -> MovieDetailFocusTarget? {
        guard props.reviewsCount ?? 0 > 0 else {
            return nil
        }
        return .reviewLink
    }

    private func topPersonTarget(props: Props) -> MovieDetailFocusTarget? {
        primaryPeopleCredit(props: props).map { .topPerson($0.id) }
    }

    private func supplementalTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        [reviewTarget(props: props), topPersonTarget(props: props)].compactMap { $0 }
    }

    private func readMoreTarget(props: Props) -> MovieDetailFocusTarget? {
        guard let movie = props.movie, !movie.overview.isEmpty else {
            return nil
        }
        return .readMoreButton
    }

    private func keywordTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        (props.movie?.keywords?.keywords ?? []).map { .keyword($0.id) }
    }

    private func castTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        guard let characters = props.characters, !characters.isEmpty else {
            return []
        }
        var targets: [MovieDetailFocusTarget] = characters.map { .castPerson($0.id) }
        targets.append(.castSeeAll)
        return targets
    }

    private func crewTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        guard let credits = props.credits, !credits.isEmpty else {
            return []
        }
        var targets: [MovieDetailFocusTarget] = credits.map { .crewPerson($0.id) }
        targets.append(.crewSeeAll)
        return targets
    }

    private func similarTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        guard let similar = props.similar, !similar.isEmpty else {
            return []
        }
        var targets: [MovieDetailFocusTarget] = similar.map { .similarMovie($0.id) }
        targets.append(.similarSeeAll)
        return targets
    }

    private func recommendedTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        guard let recommended = props.recommended, !recommended.isEmpty else {
            return []
        }
        var targets: [MovieDetailFocusTarget] = recommended.map { .recommendedMovie($0.id) }
        targets.append(.recommendedSeeAll)
        return targets
    }

    private func posterTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        let posters = props.movie?.images?.posters ?? []
        guard !posters.isEmpty else { return [] }
        return posters.map { .poster($0.file_path) }
    }

    private func backdropTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        let backdrops = props.movie?.images?.backdrops ?? []
        guard !backdrops.isEmpty else { return [] }
        return backdrops.map { .backdrop($0.file_path) }
    }


    /// Groups of focus targets, in Tab order. Each group is a horizontal row
    /// of related items (genres, action buttons, keywords, cast, crew etc).
    /// Tab / Shift+Tab moves between groups; Left/Right arrows move within.
    private func focusGroups(props: Props) -> [[MovieDetailFocusTarget]] {
        var groups: [[MovieDetailFocusTarget]] = []
        let genres = genreTargets(props: props)
        if !genres.isEmpty { groups.append(genres) }
        groups.append(actionTargets)
        if let review = reviewTarget(props: props) { groups.append([review]) }
        if let person = topPersonTarget(props: props) { groups.append([person]) }
        if let readMore = readMoreTarget(props: props) { groups.append([readMore]) }
        let keywords = keywordTargets(props: props)
        if !keywords.isEmpty { groups.append(keywords) }
        let cast = castTargets(props: props)
        if !cast.isEmpty { groups.append(cast) }
        let crew = crewTargets(props: props)
        if !crew.isEmpty { groups.append(crew) }
        let similar = similarTargets(props: props)
        if !similar.isEmpty { groups.append(similar) }
        let recommended = recommendedTargets(props: props)
        if !recommended.isEmpty { groups.append(recommended) }
        let posters = posterTargets(props: props)
        if !posters.isEmpty { groups.append(posters) }
        let backdrops = backdropTargets(props: props)
        if !backdrops.isEmpty { groups.append(backdrops) }
        return groups
    }

    private func availableTopTargets(props: Props) -> [MovieDetailFocusTarget] {
        focusGroups(props: props).flatMap { $0 }
    }

    private func preferredFocusTarget(props: Props) -> MovieDetailFocusTarget? {
        genreTargets(props: props).first ?? actionTargets.first
    }

    private func restoreDetailFocus(props: Props, force: Bool = false) {
        guard selectedPoster == nil else {
            return
        }

        let availableTargets = availableTopTargets(props: props)
        guard !availableTargets.isEmpty else {
            focusedDetailItem = nil
            return
        }

        // Re-pick the preferred target when:
        //   force == true (user nav action),
        //   nothing is focused yet,
        //   or the focused item is no longer in the available list.
        // The earlier `availableTargets.contains(focusedDetailItem!)`
        // forced an unwrap that was already guarded by the
        // immediately-preceding `focusedDetailItem == nil` check —
        // restructured to make the guard explicit.
        if force {
            focusedDetailItem = preferredFocusTarget(props: props)
        } else if let focused = focusedDetailItem {
            if !availableTargets.contains(focused) {
                focusedDetailItem = preferredFocusTarget(props: props)
            }
        } else {
            focusedDetailItem = preferredFocusTarget(props: props)
        }
    }
    #endif

    // Crossline movies list is presented as a sheet — see the See-all sheet
    // explanation on peopleListPresentation.

20	    /// Navigate to a tab by using the remote. Focus moves to the tab bar first,
21	    /// then right/left to the desired tab, then select.
22	    private func selectTab(_ title: String, in app: XCUIApplication) {
23	        let tabButton = app.tabBars.buttons[title]
24	        XCTAssertTrue(tabButton.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout),
25	                      "Expected tab '\(title)' to exist")
26	        // Focus the tab bar (move up repeatedly to ensure we're at the top)
27	        for _ in 0..<5 {
28	            XCUIRemote.shared.press(.up)
29	        }
30	        // Navigate horizontally to the desired tab
31	        // Try pressing right until we find the focused tab matching our title
32	        for _ in 0..<10 {
33	            if tabButton.hasFocus {
34	                break
35	            }
36	            XCUIRemote.shared.press(.right)
37	        }
38	        // If we overshot, try left
39	        for _ in 0..<10 {
40	            if tabButton.hasFocus {
41	                break
42	            }
43	            XCUIRemote.shared.press(.left)
44	        }
45	        XCUIRemote.shared.press(.select)
46	    }
47	
48	    @discardableResult
49	    private func openFirstMovieDetail(in app: XCUIApplication) -> XCUIElement {
50	        selectTab("Popular", in: app)
51	
52	        // Navigate down from tab bar to content
53	        XCUIRemote.shared.press(.down)
54	
55	        let firstMovie = app.identifiedElement("moviesList.movie.0")
56	        XCTAssertTrue(firstMovie.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout))
57	        XCUIRemote.shared.press(.select)
58	
59	        let movieDetail = app.identifiedElement("movieDetail")
60	        logHierarchyOnMissing(app, element: movieDetail, named: "movieDetail")
61	        XCTAssertTrue(movieDetail.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout))
62	        return movieDetail
63	    }

6	struct TVSearchView: ConnectedView {
7	    struct Props {
8	        let searchResults: [Int]
9	        let movies: [Int: Movie]
10	        let dispatch: DispatchFunction
11	    }
12	
13	    @State private var searchText = ""
14	    @State private var searchTask: Task<Void, Never>?
15	
16	    func map(state: AppState, dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction) -> Props {
17	        let results = searchText.isEmpty ? [] : (state.moviesState.search[searchText] ?? [])
18	        return Props(searchResults: results,
19	                     movies: state.moviesState.movies,
20	                     dispatch: dispatch)
21	    }
22	
23	    private static let gridColumns = Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 40), count: 5)
24	
25	    func body(props: Props) -> some View {
26	        ScrollView {
27	            if searchText.isEmpty {
28	                Text("Search for movies")
29	                    .font(.headline)
30	                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
31	                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
32	                    .padding(.top, 200)
33	                    .accessibilityIdentifier("search.emptyState")
34	            } else if props.searchResults.isEmpty {
35	                Text("No results for \"\(searchText)\"")
36	                    .font(.headline)
37	                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
38	                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
39	                    .padding(.top, 200)
40	                    .accessibilityIdentifier("search.noResults")
41	            } else {
42	                LazyVGrid(columns: Self.gridColumns, spacing: 40) {
43	                    ForEach(props.searchResults, id: \.self) { id in
44	                        if let movie = props.movies[id] {
45	                            NavigationLink(value: id) {
46	                                TVSearchCard(movie: movie)
47	                            }
48	                            .buttonStyle(.card)
49	                            .accessibilityIdentifier("search.result.\(id)")
50	                        }
51	                    }
52	                }
53	                .padding(.horizontal, 60)
54	                .padding(.vertical, 40)
55	            }
56	        }
57	        .navigationDestination(for: Int.self) { id in
58	            TVMovieDetail(movieId: id)
59	        }
60	        .searchable(text: $searchText, prompt: "Movie title")
61	        .onChange(of: searchText) { _, newValue in
62	            searchTask?.cancel()
63	            guard !newValue.isEmpty else { return }
64	            searchTask = Task {
65	                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(500))
66	                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
67	                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.FetchSearch(query: newValue, page: 1))
68	            }
69	        }
70	    }
71	}
72
