235	                return "discover/movie"
236	            }
237	        }
238	    }
239	    
240	    public func GET<T: Codable>(endpoint: Endpoint,
241	                         params: [String: String]?,
242	                         completionHandler: @escaping (Result<T, APIError>) -> Void) {
243	        guard let apiKey = apiKey else {
244	            #if DEBUG
245	            print("Missing TMDB_API_KEY. Set it in DeveloperSettings.xcconfig.")
246	            #endif
247	            callbackQueue.async {
248	                completionHandler(.failure(.missingAPIKey))
249	            }
250	            return
251	        }
252	        
253	        let queryURL = baseURL.appendingPathComponent(endpoint.path())
254	        var components = URLComponents(url: queryURL, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: true)!
255	        var queryItems: [URLQueryItem] = [
256	            URLQueryItem(name: "language", value: Locale.preferredLanguages[0])
257	        ]
258	        // Auth path: query parameter for direct TMDB v3 usage,
259	        // header for TMDB v4 / proxy deployments. Both modes
260	        // ignore the credential's exact form; the apiKeyProvider
261	        // is the single source of truth.
262	        if case .queryParameter(let name) = authMode {
263	            queryItems.append(URLQueryItem(name: name, value: apiKey))
264	        }
265	        if let params {
266	            for (_, value) in params.enumerated() {
267	                queryItems.append(URLQueryItem(name: value.key, value: value.value))
268	            }
269	        }
270	        components.queryItems = queryItems
271	        // `components.url` is non-nil for all the well-formed
272	        // endpoint paths we construct above — but if it ever does
273	        // come back nil (e.g. a future caller passes a path with
274	        // characters that fail percent-encoding), surface that as a
275	        // structured failure instead of crashing the request.
276	        guard let composedURL = components.url else {
277	            callbackQueue.async {
278	                completionHandler(.failure(.noResponse))
279	            }
280	            return
281	        }
282	        var request = URLRequest(url: composedURL)
283	        request.httpMethod = "GET"
284	        if case .bearer = authMode {
285	            request.setValue("Bearer \(apiKey)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Authorization")
286	        }
287	        // Fire the request on an unstructured Task so GET keeps its
288	        // synchronous, completion-handler signature (the AsyncAction /
289	        // dispatch facade and all callers are unchanged) while the
290	        // networking itself uses structured async/await internally.
291	        let session = self.session
292	        let decoder = self.decoder
293	        let callbackQueue = self.callbackQueue
294	        Task {
295	            do {
296	                let (data, response) = try await session.data(for: request)
297	
298	                // HTTP status first — without this, a 401 from a bad API
299	                // key gets mis-reported as `jsonDecodingError` because the
300	                // error body shape doesn't match the success type.
301	                if let http = response as? HTTPURLResponse, !(200...299).contains(http.statusCode) {
302	                    #if DEBUG
303	                    // Diagnostic for Discover-style 400s and other non-2xx
304	                    // responses: print the request URL (api_key stripped)
305	                    // and the response body so a user reporting "TMDB
306	                    // returned an unexpected response (400)" can tell which
307	                    // query parameter combination TMDB rejected. Visible in
308	                    // `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream` / Console.app.
309	                    let sanitizedURL = APIService.sanitizeURLForLogging(request.url)
310	                    let body = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) ?? ""
311	                    let bodyPreview = body.isEmpty
312	                        ? "<no body>"
313	                        : (body.count > 500 ? String(body.prefix(500)) + "…" : body)
314	                    print("APIService HTTP \(http.statusCode) for \(sanitizedURL ?? "<no url>")\n  body: \(bodyPreview)")
315	                    #endif
316	                    if http.statusCode == 429 {
317	                        let retryAfter = APIService.retryAfterSeconds(from: http)
318	                        callbackQueue.async {
319	                            completionHandler(.failure(.rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: retryAfter)))
320	                        }
321	                    } else {
322	                        callbackQueue.async {
323	                            completionHandler(.failure(.httpStatus(code: http.statusCode)))
324	                        }
325	                    }
326	                    return
327	                }
328	
329	                do {
330	                    let object = try decoder.decode(T.self, from: data)
331	                    callbackQueue.async {
332	                        completionHandler(.success(object))
333	                    }
334	                } catch let error {
335	                    callbackQueue.async {
336	                        #if DEBUG
337	                        print("JSON Decoding Error: \(error)")
338	                        #endif
339	                        completionHandler(.failure(.jsonDecodingError(error: error)))
340	                    }
341	                }
342	            } catch {
343	                // Transport-level error — distinguish "device is offline"
344	                // from other failures so the UI can tailor the message.
345	                let nsError = error as NSError
346	                if nsError.domain == NSURLErrorDomain
347	                    && APIService.offlineURLErrorCodes.contains(nsError.code) {
348	                    callbackQueue.async {
349	                        completionHandler(.failure(.offline))
350	                    }
351	                } else {
352	                    callbackQueue.async {
353	                        completionHandler(.failure(.networkError(error: error)))
354	                    }
355	                }
356	            }
357	        }
358	    }
359	
360	    /// URLError codes that indicate the device is offline rather than
361	    /// hitting a generic transport failure. Surfaced as
362	    /// `APIError.offline` so the UI can show "you're offline" instead
363	    /// of a generic networking message.
364	    static let offlineURLErrorCodes: Set<Int> = [
365	        URLError.notConnectedToInternet.rawValue,
366	        URLError.networkConnectionLost.rawValue,
367	        URLError.dataNotAllowed.rawValue,
368	        URLError.internationalRoamingOff.rawValue
369	    ]
370	
371	    /// Parses the `Retry-After` header from a 429 response. TMDB
372	    /// returns it as a number-of-seconds. Returns nil when the header
373	    /// is missing or unparseable.
374	    static func retryAfterSeconds(from response: HTTPURLResponse) -> TimeInterval? {
375	        guard let raw = response.value(forHTTPHeaderField: "Retry-After"),
376	              let seconds = TimeInterval(raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)) else {
377	            return nil
378	        }
379	        return seconds
380	    }
381	
382	    /// Strips `api_key` from a request URL so the URL can safely be
383	    /// printed to the device log without leaking the credential. Used
384	    /// by the DEBUG-only HTTP-error diagnostic in `GET`.
385	    static func sanitizeURLForLogging(_ url: URL?) -> String? {
386	        guard let url,
387	              var components = URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false) else {
388	            return url?.absoluteString
389	        }
390	        components.queryItems = (components.queryItems ?? []).filter { item in
391	            item.name != "api_key"
392	        }
393	        return components.url?.absoluteString
394	    }
395	}
396

A new error surfaced once the globals were fixed: at line 302 the `Task { }` closure is passed as a `sending` parameter but captures the non-Sendable `completionHandler` — `#SendingClosureRisksDataRace`. This is the same root cause as the warnings. The correct fix is the proper strict-concurrency design: constrain `T: Sendable` and make the handler `@Sendable`.

> AGENT

These completion closures don't capture `self` (they use global `XCTFail`/`XCTAssert` and a local `expectation`). The real error is that `waitForExpectations` is `@MainActor`-isolated in the Swift 6 XCTest overlay, so calling it from a nonisolated test method tries to send the non-Sendable `self` to the main actor. The standard fix is to mark the test class `@MainActor` (XCTest cases run on the main thread anyway). Let me apply that.

> TOOL

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/Backend/Tests/BackendTests/APIServiceTests.swift",
  "old_string": "final class APIServiceTests: XCTestCase {",
  "new_string": "// `@MainActor`: under the Swift 6 language mode `waitForExpectations`\n// is main-actor-isolated, so a nonisolated test method calling it would\n// have to send the non-Sendable `XCTestCase` across actors. Pinning the\n// case to the main actor (where XCTest already runs it) satisfies that\n// without weakening any assertions.\n@MainActor\nfinal class APIServiceTests: XCTestCase {"
}
```

> AGENT

101 errors in FluxCore, clustering into clear patterns:
1. **Model types not `Sendable`** → global `let sampleMovie`/fixtures flagged, and `PaginatedResponse<T>` fails GET's `T: Sendable`.
2. **Action completion handlers** → the closures passed to `GET` capture non-Sendable `dispatch` (`DispatchFunction` from the pinned SwiftUIFlux), `self` (Action), etc., now that GET's handler is `@Sendable`.

The handler-`@Sendable` requirement I added to Backend is what forces the painful `dispatch`-capture errors throughout the Redux layer. Let me read the action code to choose between (a) embracing `@Sendable` everywhere vs (b) confining the unsafety to Backend.

449	    /// On success the loading-state entry is cleared *before*
450	    /// `onSuccess` runs. Order is UX-equivalent (both dispatches run
451	    /// in the same callback tick) but matters for tests that capture
452	    /// the most-recently-dispatched action — those tests are about
453	    /// the data action, not the loading bookkeeping.
454	    static public func makeTrackedHandler<T>(
455	        key: LoadingKey,
456	        dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction,
457	        onSuccess: @escaping (T) -> Void
458	    ) -> (Result<T, APIService.APIError>) -> Void {
459	        dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .loading))
460	        return { result in
461	            switch result {
462	            case let .success(value):
463	                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: nil))
464	                onSuccess(value)
465	            case let .failure(error):
466	                let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: error)
467	                dispatch(SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .failed(failure)))
468	            }
469	        }
470	    }

> AGENT

I now see the full picture. Every action's completion handler captures `dispatch` (`DispatchFunction` from the **pinned, non-Sendable** SwiftUIFlux) — that's unavoidable without either touching SwiftUIFlux or boxing `dispatch` at ~30 sites. 

The cleaner architecture is to **confine the concurrency escape hatch to Backend**: make GET's completion handler ordinary (non-`@Sendable`) again and box the delivery internally, so FluxCore's Redux actions need zero changes. Models still become `Sendable` (required by the global fixtures regardless). Let me revise Backend's GET.

First, revert the GET signature and drop the `T: Sendable` constraint (the internal result-box handles delivery uniformly):

51	        return sortBy[Int.random(in: 0..<sortBy.count)]

59	        toParams(page: DiscoverFilter.randomPage())
60	    }
61	
62	    /// Build the TMDB `/discover/movie` query parameters with an explicit
63	    /// `page` value. `FetchRandomDiscover` uses this for its two-phase
64	    /// flow — phase 1 probes `page=1` to learn `total_pages`, then phase 2
65	    /// requests a random page in `[1, min(total_pages, randomPageCeiling)]`.
66	    ///
67	    /// Asking TMDB for a `page` greater than `total_pages` returns HTTP 400
68	    /// (not an empty result), so picking a random page WITHOUT knowing the
69	    /// real ceiling — which is what the old `toParams()` did — caused
70	    /// flaky Discover failures for obscure filters (e.g. `year=1952` +
71	    /// `sort_by=vote_average.asc` often has fewer than 19 pages).
72	    public func toParams(page: Int) -> [String: String] {
73	        var params: [String: String] = [:]
74	        if let startYear = startYear, let endYear = endYear {
75	            params["primary_release_date.gte"] = "\(startYear)-01-01"
76	            params["primary_release_date.lte"] = "\(endYear)-12-31"
77	        } else {
78	            params["year"] = "\(year)"
79	        }
80	        if let genre = genre {
81	            params["with_genres"] = "\(genre)"
82	        }
83	        if let region = region {
84	            params["region"] = region
85	            // Restrict to movies originating from the selected country.
86	            params["with_origin_country"] = region
87	        }
88	        params["page"] = "\(page)"
89	        params["sort_by"] = sort
90	        // NOTE: `language` is intentionally NOT set here. `APIService.GET`
91	        // already adds `language=<Locale.preferredLanguages[0]>` to every
92	        // request — duplicating the key produces a URL like
93	        // `?language=en-US&...&language=en-US` which has worked
94	        // historically but is a known suspect for TMDB returning HTTP 400
95	        // on `/discover/movie` under newer API behaviour. Removing the
96	        // dupe is the safer baseline.
97	        return params
98	    }
99	
100	    /// Upper bound used by `FetchRandomDiscover` when picking a random page
101	    /// after probing `total_pages`. TMDB allows up to 500 pages but the
102	    /// "random surprise" effect is already saturated well before that —
103	    /// and capping at a small number means we never wander into the tail
104	    /// where TMDB's index is sparse.
105	    public static let randomPageCeiling: Int = 19
106	    
107	    public func toText(genres: [Genre]) -> String {
108	        var parts: [String] = []
109	        if let startYear = startYear, let endYear = endYear {
110	            parts.append("\(startYear)-\(endYear)")
111	        } else {
112	            // `bundle: .module`: this type is in the MovieSwiftFluxCore package.
113	            parts.append(String(localized: "Random", bundle: .module,
114	                                comment: "Discover filter description shown when no specific year range is set"))
115	        }
116	        if let genre = genre,
117	            let stateGenre = genres.first(where: { (realGenre) -> Bool in
118	                realGenre.id == genre
119	            }) {
120	            parts.append(stateGenre.name)
121	        }
122	        if let region = region {
123	            parts.append(region)
124	        }
125	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
126	    }
127	}
128

import Foundation
import Backend

public enum MoviesMenu: Int, CaseIterable {
    case nowPlaying, upcoming, trending, popular, topRated, genres
    
    public func title() -> String {
        // `bundle: .module` is required: this type lives in the
        // MovieSwiftFluxCore package, whose localized strings are in the
        // package's own Localizable.xcstrings (not the app's main bundle).
        switch self {
        case .popular:
            return String(localized: "Popular", bundle: .module,
                          comment: "Movies menu / nav title: most popular movies")
        case .topRated:
            return String(localized: "Top Rated", bundle: .module,
                          comment: "Movies menu / nav title: highest rated movies")
        case .upcoming:
            return String(localized: "Upcoming", bundle: .module,
                          comment: "Movies menu / nav title: upcoming releases")
        case .nowPlaying:
            return String(localized: "Now Playing", bundle: .module,
                          comment: "Movies menu / nav title: movies in theaters now")
        case .trending:
            return String(localized: "Trending", bundle: .module,
                          comment: "Movies menu / nav title: trending movies")
        case .genres:
            return String(localized: "Genres", bundle: .module,
                          comment: "Movies menu / nav title: browse by genre")
        }
    }
    
    public func endpoint() -> APIService.Endpoint {
        switch self {
        case .popular: return APIService.Endpoint.popular
        case .topRated: return APIService.Endpoint.topRated
        case .upcoming: return APIService.Endpoint.upcoming
        case .nowPlaying: return APIService.Endpoint.nowPlaying
        case .trending: return APIService.Endpoint.trending
        case .genres: return APIService.Endpoint.genres
        }
    }
}

6	/// Tests for the `MoviesActions` AsyncAction execute paths.
7	///
8	/// **Dispatch contract.** Every action that hits the network funnels through
9	/// `MoviesActions.makeTrackedHandler(...)`, which dispatches:
10	///   1. `SetLoadingState(key:, state: .loading)` — synchronously, before
11	///      the GET fires.
12	///   2a. on success — `SetLoadingState(key:, state: nil)` (clears the
13	///       loading entry), then the data action (e.g. `SetMovieMenuList`).
14	///   2b. on failure — `SetLoadingState(key:, state: .failed(translated))`.
15	///       No data action is dispatched on failure.
16	///
17	/// So success-path tests have to look at three dispatches and pick out the
18	/// data action; failure-path tests have to look at two dispatches and assert
19	/// the second is a `.failed` SetLoadingState.
20	final class MoviesActionsTests: XCTestCase {

22	        private let value: String?
23	
24	        init(_ value: String?) {
25	            self.value = value
26	        }

29	            value
30	        }

33	    private final class MockNetworkSession: NetworkSession, @unchecked Sendable {
34	        var lastRequest: URLRequest?
35	
36	        /// All requests issued, in order. Used by multi-phase tests (e.g.
37	        /// `FetchRandomDiscover` probe → fetch) to inspect both URLs.
38	        var allRequests: [URLRequest] = []
39	
40	        var nextData: Data?
41	        var nextResponse: URLResponse?
42	        var nextError: Error?
43	
44	        /// FIFO queue of `(Data?, URLResponse?, Error?)` triples — when
45	        /// non-empty, each `data(for:)` call pops the front element and
46	        /// returns/throws it. Falls back to `(nextData, nextResponse,
47	        /// nextError)` once the queue drains, so existing tests that only
48	        /// set `nextData` keep working.
49	        var responseQueue: [(Data?, URLResponse?, Error?)] = []
50	
51	        func data(for request: URLRequest) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse) {
52	            lastRequest = request
53	            allRequests.append(request)
54	            // Pop the queued triple if present, else fall back to the
55	            // single `next*` values. Choosing the tuple first, then
56	            // destructuring, keeps this a single clear expression.
57	            let (data, response, error) = responseQueue.isEmpty
58	                ? (nextData, nextResponse, nextError)
59	                : responseQueue.removeFirst()
60	            if let error { throw error }
61	            // Default to 200 when a test only sets data (matches the prior

65	                                   httpVersion: "HTTP/1.1", headerFields: nil)!

67	        }

90	    /// `trigger` returns true for one of the dispatched actions; the wait then
91	    /// returns and the caller asserts on the captured array.
92	    ///
93	    /// `assertForOverFulfill` is set to false so a slightly noisy success path
94	    /// (e.g. SetLoadingState clear → data action where both qualify under
95	    /// `trigger`) doesn't crash the test before it can make its real
96	    /// assertions.
97	    private func captureDispatches(
98	        waitingFor description: String,
99	        until trigger: @escaping (Action) -> Bool,
100	        timeout: TimeInterval = 1.0,
101	        when execute: (@escaping DispatchFunction) -> Void
102	    ) -> [Action] {
103	        // `dispatched` is mutated from two threads:
104	        //   - the test thread, which receives the synchronous
105	        //     SetLoadingState(.loading) dispatch fired immediately by
106	        //     `makeTrackedHandler` before APIService.GET returns
107	        //   - the APIService's `callbackQueue` thread, which fires
108	        //     the subsequent .failed / .success+data dispatches
109	        //
110	        // `Array<any Action>` stores existential containers (5
111	        // machine-words per element). Concurrent writes corrupt the
112	        // storage and cause downcasts (`$0 as? SetMovieMenuList`) to
113	        // succeed on garbage that wasn't actually a SetMovieMenuList,
114	        // which surfaces as "Failure path unexpectedly dispatched a
115	        // SetMovieMenuList data action" with the value's description
116	        // rendered as "(Function)". The race is data-loss-prone on
117	        // any ARM machine; macos-26 CI runners hit it deterministically
118	        // while local M-series Macs tend to slip past it.
119	        //
120	        // Serialize all reads/writes through an NSLock so the array
121	        // stays consistent regardless of which thread dispatches.
122	        let lock = NSLock()
123	        var dispatched: [Action] = []
124	        let exp = expectation(description: description)
125	        exp.assertForOverFulfill = false
126	        execute { action in
127	            lock.lock()
128	            dispatched.append(action)
129	            let shouldFulfill = trigger(action)
130	            lock.unlock()
131	            if shouldFulfill { exp.fulfill() }
132	        }
133	        waitForExpectations(timeout: timeout)
134	        lock.lock()
135	        defer { lock.unlock() }
136	        return dispatched
137	    }
138	
139	    /// Find the first dispatched action of the given type, or fail the test if
140	    /// none was dispatched.
141	    private func unwrapDispatched<T>(
142	        _ type: T.Type,
143	        in dispatched: [Action],
144	        file: StaticString = #file,
145	        line: UInt = #line
146	    ) throws -> T {
147	        let matches = dispatched.compactMap { $0 as? T }
148	        return try XCTUnwrap(matches.first,
149	                             "Expected one \(T.self) in dispatched actions, got: \(dispatched)",
150	                             file: file, line: line)
151	    }
152	
153	    /// Assert that the dispatch trace ends in a `SetLoadingState(.failed)`
154	    /// for `key`, with no data action of `dataType` ever dispatched. Returns
155	    /// the failure for further assertion.
156	    ///
157	    /// Takes a `noDataActionMatching` closure rather than a generic `T.Type`.
158	    /// The generic-T form (`$0 as? T`) was triggering a Swift 6 compiler
159	    /// quirk on the macos-26 GitHub runner where the cast returned a value
160	    /// whose dynamic type rendered as `(Function)` — even though no Action
161	    /// passed to dispatch was a closure. Inlining the type check at the
162	    /// call site (via the closure) bypasses the generic-existential cast
163	    /// path and produces consistent results locally and on CI.
164	    private func assertFailureDispatch(
165	        in dispatched: [Action],
166	        for key: LoadingKey,
167	        noDataActionMatching matches: (Action) -> Bool,
168	        dataActionDescription: String,
169	        file: StaticString = #file,
170	        line: UInt = #line
171	    ) throws -> MoviesListLoadFailure {
172	        let unwantedDataAction = dispatched.first(where: matches)
173	        XCTAssertNil(unwantedDataAction,
174	                     "Failure path unexpectedly dispatched a \(dataActionDescription) data action.",
175	                     file: file, line: line)
176	        let loadingStates = dispatched.compactMap { $0 as? MoviesActions.SetLoadingState }
177	        let lastForKey = loadingStates.last { $0.key == key }
178	        let unwrapped = try XCTUnwrap(lastForKey,
179	                                      "No SetLoadingState dispatched for key \(key); got: \(loadingStates)",
180	                                      file: file, line: line)
181	        guard case let .failed(failure) = unwrapped.state else {
182	            XCTFail("Last SetLoadingState for \(key) was \(String(describing: unwrapped.state)), not .failed",
183	                    file: file, line: line)
184	            throw StubError.failed
185	        }
186	        return failure
187	    }

  "new_string": "    // The async setUp/tearDown variants are main-actor-isolated in this\n    // @MainActor case, so they can touch the main-actor `originalAPIService`\n    // (the sync overrides are nonisolated and would warn).\n    override func setUp() async throws {\n        originalAPIService = APIService.shared\n    }\n\n    override func tearDown() async throws {\n        APIService.shared = originalAPIService\n    }"

1	//  Tiny shared bus that lets `AppIntent`s drive navigation in the
2	//  SwiftUI root views without coupling them to the iOS TabView,
3	//  the macOS SplitView, or the tvOS HomeView directly.
4	//
5	//  Flow:
6	//   1. An intent's `perform()` calls `IntentNavigationStore.shared
7	//      .request(.wishlist)`.
8	//   2. The root view subscribes to `pendingDestination` via a
9	//      `@StateObject` / `.onChange` and switches its selected tab /
10	//      sidebar menu when a destination appears.
11	//   3. The view calls `consume()` (or sets `pendingDestination =
12	//      nil`) once it has navigated, so a second invocation of the
13	//      same intent re-fires.
14	//
15	//  The store is a singleton because AppIntent runs outside SwiftUI
16	//  view scope. We can't pass an EnvironmentObject in, so the
17	//  AppIntent and the view both reach for `.shared`.
18	
19	import Foundation
20	import Observation
21	
22	@Observable
23	final class IntentNavigationStore {
24	    static let shared = IntentNavigationStore()
25	
26	    /// Where an App Intent is asking the app to navigate. Each
27	    /// case maps to one of the iOS tabs or the macOS sidebar menus.
28	    enum Destination: Equatable {
29	        case popularMovies
30	        case discover
31	        case fanClub
32	        case wishlist
33	    }
34	
35	    var pendingDestination: Destination?
36	
37	    private init() {}
38	
39	    /// Posts a destination request from any thread. Hopped to
40	    /// main so SwiftUI's `@Published` observation fires on the
41	    /// main actor. Safe to call from
42	    /// `AppIntent.perform()` which runs on a background queue.
43	    func request(_ destination: Destination) {
44	        if Thread.isMainThread {
45	            pendingDestination = destination
46	        } else {
47	            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in
48	                self?.pendingDestination = destination
49	            }
50	        }
51	    }
52	
53	    /// Reads and clears the pending destination. Views call this
54	    /// after acting on a request so the intent can be invoked
55	    /// again later with the same destination.
56	    @discardableResult
57	    func consume() -> Destination? {
58	        let destination = pendingDestination
59	        pendingDestination = nil
60	        return destination
61	    }
62	
63	    /// UI-test seam: when `UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION` is set in the
64	    /// process environment, post the matching destination to the
65	    /// navigation bus. Called from a `.task` modifier on the iOS
66	    /// TabbarView and macOS SplitView so the value lands AFTER the
67	    /// `.onChange` subscription is in place — otherwise the change
68	    /// would happen before observation starts and the view wouldn't
69	    /// react.
70	    ///
71	    /// This is how `MovieSwiftUITests` simulates an App Intent firing
72	    /// at launch (`OpenWishlistIntent`, `OpenDiscoverIntent`, etc.)
73	    /// without invoking the AppIntent runtime, which can't be driven
74	    /// from XCUITest.
75	    static func handleUITestEnvironment(_ environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) {
76	        guard let raw = environment["UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION"] else { return }
77	        let destination: Destination?
78	        switch raw {
79	        case "popularMovies": destination = .popularMovies
80	        case "discover":      destination = .discover
81	        case "fanClub":       destination = .fanClub
82	        case "wishlist":      destination = .wishlist
83	        default:              destination = nil
84	        }
85	        guard let destination else { return }
86	        shared.request(destination)
87	    }
88	}
89

1	//  Indexes user-saved movies (wishlist, seenlist, and every custom
2	//  list) into Apple's Core Spotlight so they appear in the system
3	//  search on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. tvOS doesn't ship Core
4	//  Spotlight; the file exposes a no-op stub there so app entry
5	//  points can call `startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.
6	//
7	//  We deliberately don't index the full `state.moviesState.movies`
8	//  cache — that's a TMDB-shaped firehose of titles the user hasn't
9	//  asked to remember. Only items the user has explicitly added to a
10	//  list are surfaced so search results match the user's mental
11	//  model of "movies I saved".
12	
13	import Foundation
14	#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)
15	import CoreSpotlight
16	#endif
17	import SwiftUIFlux
18	import Combine
19	import MovieSwiftFluxCore
20	
21	/// Pure-logic helpers — exposed regardless of platform so unit tests
22	/// can verify the indexable-set composition and identifier
23	/// round-tripping without depending on Core Spotlight.
24	enum MovieSpotlightIndexer {
25	
26	    /// Domain identifier so the system groups these results
27	    /// together and the app can bulk-delete them on logout.
28	    static let domainIdentifier = "com.movieswift.movies"
29	
30	    /// Identifier prefix. The numeric movie id is appended so
31	    /// `identifier(forMovieId:)` round-trips via
32	    /// `movieId(fromIdentifier:)` for the deep-link routing path.
33	    private static let identifierPrefix = "com.movieswift.movie."
34	
35	    static func identifier(forMovieId id: Int) -> String {
36	        "\(identifierPrefix)\(id)"
37	    }
38	
39	    /// Reverse of `identifier(forMovieId:)`. Returns nil for any
40	    /// other identifier shape so a future indexer change doesn't
41	    /// silently mis-parse existing entries.
42	    static func movieId(fromIdentifier identifier: String) -> Int? {
43	        guard identifier.hasPrefix(identifierPrefix) else { return nil }
44	        let suffix = identifier.dropFirst(identifierPrefix.count)
45	        return Int(suffix)
46	    }
47	
48	    /// Returns the union of wishlist + seenlist + custom-list movie
49	    /// ids. Pure so it can be unit-tested without spinning up a
50	    /// Core Spotlight index.
51	    static func indexableMovieIds(in state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {
52	        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist
53	        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)
54	        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {
55	            ids.formUnion(list.movies)
56	        }
57	        return ids
58	    }
59	}
60	
61	#if canImport(CoreSpotlight) && !os(tvOS)
62	
63	/// Runtime indexer that subscribes to the SwiftUIFlux store and
64	/// keeps CSSearchableIndex in sync with the user's saved movies.
65	final class SpotlightStoreObserver {
66	    static let shared = SpotlightStoreObserver()
67	
68	    private var lastIndexedIds: Set<Int> = []
69	    private var cancellable: AnyCancellable?
70	    private var lastSnapshot: AppState?
71	    private var isObserving = false
72	
73	    private init() {}
74	
75	    /// Subscribe to the store so wishlist / seenlist / custom-list
76	    /// changes update Spotlight as they happen. Idempotent — calling
77	    /// twice doesn't re-subscribe.
78	    func startObserving(store: Store<AppState>) {
79	        guard !isObserving else { return }
80	        isObserving = true
81	
82	        // Index whatever's already in state at subscription time.
83	        update(state: store.state)
84	
85	        // SwiftUIFlux's Store is an ObservableObject; objectWillChange
86	        // fires before mutations land, so we hop to the next runloop
87	        // tick to read the post-mutation state.
88	        cancellable = store.objectWillChange
89	            .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)
90	            .sink { [weak self, weak store] _ in
91	                DispatchQueue.main.async {
92	                    guard let self, let store else { return }
93	                    self.update(state: store.state)
94	                }
95	            }
96	    }
97	
98	    func stopObserving() {
99	        cancellable?.cancel()
100	        cancellable = nil
101	        isObserving = false
102	    }
103	
104	    /// Diffs the current indexable set against `lastIndexedIds`,
105	    /// adds new entries, and removes ones the user un-saved.
106	    /// Public for tests; production path runs through the
107	    /// store-subscription sink.
108	    func update(state: AppState) {
109	        let currentIds = MovieSpotlightIndexer.indexableMovieIds(in: state)
110	        let toAdd = currentIds.subtracting(lastIndexedIds)
111	        let toRemove = lastIndexedIds.subtracting(currentIds)
112	        // The cached movies dict is the source for the searchable
113	        // attributes (title, overview). If a movie is in the index
114	        // set but not yet in the cache (TMDB hasn't returned its
115	        // detail), skip it — it'll get re-tried on the next state
116	        // change.
117	        let itemsToIndex: [CSSearchableItem] = toAdd.compactMap { id in
118	            guard let movie = state.moviesState.movies[id] else { return nil }
119	            return SpotlightStoreObserver.makeSearchableItem(for: movie)
120	        }
121	        if !itemsToIndex.isEmpty {
122	            CSSearchableIndex.default().indexSearchableItems(itemsToIndex) { _ in }
123	        }
124	        if !toRemove.isEmpty {
125	            let identifiers = toRemove.map(MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId:))
126	            CSSearchableIndex.default().deleteSearchableItems(withIdentifiers: identifiers) { _ in }
127	        }
128	
129	        // Track only ids actually surfaced to the index. If movie
130	        // detail wasn't in cache, leave the id out of
131	        // lastIndexedIds so the next update retries the add.
132	        let surfacedIds = Set(itemsToIndex.compactMap { item -> Int? in
133	            MovieSpotlightIndexer.movieId(fromIdentifier: item.uniqueIdentifier)
134	        })
135	        lastIndexedIds.formUnion(surfacedIds)
136	        lastIndexedIds.subtract(toRemove)
137	    }
138	
139	    static func makeSearchableItem(for movie: Movie) -> CSSearchableItem {
140	        let attributes = CSSearchableItemAttributeSet(contentType: .content)
141	        attributes.title = movie.userTitle
142	        if !movie.overview.isEmpty {
143	            attributes.contentDescription = movie.overview
144	        }
145	        // TMDB's release_date is "yyyy-MM-dd". Surface as a content
146	        // creation date when present so the system can sort by it.
147	        if let release = movie.release_date,
148	           !release.isEmpty,
149	           let date = SpotlightStoreObserver.releaseDateFormatter.date(from: release) {
150	            attributes.contentCreationDate = date
151	        }
152	        return CSSearchableItem(
153	            uniqueIdentifier: MovieSpotlightIndexer.identifier(forMovieId: movie.id),
154	            domainIdentifier: MovieSpotlightIndexer.domainIdentifier,
155	            attributeSet: attributes
156	        )
157	    }
158	
159	    private static let releaseDateFormatter: DateFormatter = {
160	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
161	        formatter.calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
162	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
163	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
164	        formatter.dateFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd"
165	        return formatter
166	    }()
167	}
168	
169	#else
170	
171	/// tvOS doesn't ship Core Spotlight. Provide an API-compatible stub
172	/// so app entry points can call `SpotlightStoreObserver.shared
173	/// .startObserving(store:)` unconditionally.
174	final class SpotlightStoreObserver {
175	    static let shared = SpotlightStoreObserver()
176	    private init() {}
177	    func startObserving(store: Store<AppState>) {}
178	    func stopObserving() {}
179	    func update(state: AppState) {}
180	}
181	
182	#endif
183	
```

> AGENT

`SpotlightStoreObserver` is main-thread-confined at runtime (it `.receive(on: .main)` and is started from app launch on main), but making it `@MainActor` would cascade into the legacy Combine sink. Since only `shared` is flagged, `nonisolated(unsafe)` is the consistent, honest fix — matching `APIService.shared` and `loggingMiddleware`. Let me apply it to both the real class and the tvOS stub:

> TOOL

`AppPersistence` has two issues: the mutable `static var savePath` cache and a `state: AppState` capture in the background-archive closure. For `savePath`, a lazy `static let` (atomic, computed once) replaces the mutable cache cleanly. For the capture, the cleanest fix is making `AppState` `Sendable` (it's an immutable Redux value of now-Sendable models). Let me check `AppState` and its sub-states.

=== MoviesListLoadingState.swift ===
//  Per-menu loading state for the home movie lists (Popular, Top
//  Rated, Upcoming, Now Playing, Trending). Lets the UI show an
//  inline error + retry banner when a TMDB request fails instead of
//  silently leaving the list empty forever — the "case .failure(_):
//  break" path that used to swallow every error.
//
//  This file holds the pure-logic types and an APIError → presenter
//  translator. The reducer wires it into MoviesState.

import Foundation
import Backend

/// Where a per-menu list is in its load lifecycle. Only stored when
/// not idle/loaded — `nil` in the dict means "no in-flight request,
/// data (if any) is the latest known good".
public enum MoviesListLoadingState: Equatable {
    case loading
    case failed(MoviesListLoadFailure)
}

/// Identifies a single in-flight (or recently-failed) request so the
/// UI can surface a per-context error banner. One enum covers both
/// Movies and People fetchers because they all funnel through a
/// single `loadingStates: [LoadingKey: MoviesListLoadingState]`
/// dictionary in `MoviesState` — keeping it unified avoids needing a
/// parallel state slot inside `PeoplesState`.
public enum LoadingKey: Hashable {
    // Movies
    case homeMenu(MoviesMenu)
    case movieDetail(Int)
    case recommended(movie: Int)
    case similar(movie: Int)
    case videos(movie: Int)
    case search(query: String)
    case searchKeyword(query: String)
    case moviesGenre(genre: Int)
    case movieReviews(movie: Int)
    case moviesWithCrew(crew: Int)
    case moviesWithKeyword(keyword: Int)
    case randomDiscover
    case genres

    // People
    case personDetail(Int)
    case personImages(Int)
    case personMovieCredits(Int)
    case movieCasts(movie: Int)
    case peopleSearch(query: String)
    case popularPeople
}

/// User-facing description of a failed list load.
public struct MoviesListLoadFailure: Equatable {

    /// What kind of failure happened. Drives the UI's icon/CTA
    /// choice — e.g. missingAPIKey shows "Open Settings" instead of
    /// "Try again".
    public enum Kind: Equatable {
        case offline
        case rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: TimeInterval?)
        case missingAPIKey
        case server          // 5xx
        case unauthorized    // 401
        case forbidden       // 403
        case decode
        case other
    }

    public let kind: Kind
    public let message: String
    public let retryActionTitle: String

    public init(kind: Kind,
         message: String,
         retryActionTitle: String = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.defaultRetryActionTitle) {
        self.kind = kind
        self.message = message
        self.retryActionTitle = retryActionTitle
    }
}
```

2	//  no transmission — payloads are written to <Documents>/CrashReports/
3	//  for local inspection.
4	//
5	//  Hook in once at app launch by calling

7	//  retains itself as a long-lived singleton because MetricKit
8	//  doesn't retain its subscribers, and we want delivery whenever it
9	//  happens (typically up to once per ~24 hours, often when the app
10	//  is re-opened after a crash).
11	//
12	//  MetricKit isn't available on tvOS. The code paths here compile
13	//  to a no-op there so the app entry point doesn't need a platform

19	#endif

24	    static let shared = MetricKitCrashReporter()
25	
26	    private var isObserving = false
27	
28	    /// Subscribes to MetricKit. Idempotent — calling twice doesn't
29	    /// re-register.
30	    func startObserving() {
31	        guard !isObserving else { return }
32	        MXMetricManager.shared.add(self)
33	        isObserving = true
34	    }
35	
36	    /// Unsubscribes. Useful for tests; production typically never
37	    /// stops observing.

39	        guard isObserving else { return }
40	        MXMetricManager.shared.remove(self)
41	        isObserving = false
42	    }

45	
46	    /// Daily aggregated metric payloads. Delivered roughly once per
47	    /// day per the framework contract.
48	    func didReceive(_ payloads: [MXMetricPayload]) {
49	        for payload in payloads {
50	            let data = payload.jsonRepresentation()
51	            guard !data.isEmpty else { continue }
52	            try? CrashReportStore.writeToDefaultDirectory(payload: data, kind: .metric)
53	        }
54	    }

Its only mutable\n// state, `isObserving`, is touched solely by start/stop at app launch on\n// the main thread; the `didReceive` callbacks just write files. 1	//  Builds a sanitized diagnostic blob describing an in-app failure so
2	//  users can paste it into a GitHub issue. Deliberately conservative
3	//  about what goes in:
4	//
5	//    INCLUDED:
6	//      - app version + build
7	//      - OS family + version
8	//      - device model
9	//      - failure kind (offline / rateLimited / missingAPIKey / etc.)
10	//      - failure message
11	//      - the user's locale identifier (useful because TMDB filters by it)
12	//      - timestamp the user copied it (ISO-8601, UTC, no millis)
13	//
14	//    NOT INCLUDED:
15	//      - TMDB API key (never; it's behind a separate provider chain)
16	//      - request URLs (could contain query params with PII like region/genre)
17	//      - the user's saved movies / lists / wishlist
18	//      - hostname, MAC, advertising id, push token
19	//
20	//  Output is a plain-text block with a small header line and key/value
21	//  rows so it pastes legibly into any issue tracker without markdown
22	//  rendering shenanigans.

41	        for failure: MoviesListLoadFailure,
42	        appVersion: String = AppDataExport.bundleVersion(),
43	        appBuild: String = AppDataExport.bundleBuild(),
44	        osDescription: String = ErrorDiagnostic.defaultOSDescription(),
45	        deviceModel: String = ErrorDiagnostic.defaultDeviceModel(),
46	        localeIdentifier: String = Locale.current.identifier,
47	        now: Date = Date()
48	    ) -> String {
49	        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
50	        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime]
51	        let timestamp = formatter.string(from: now)
52	
53	        return """
54	        MovieSwift diagnostic
55	        ─────────────────────
56	        app:      MovieSwift \(appVersion) (\(appBuild))
57	        os:       \(osDescription)
58	        device:   \(deviceModel)
59	        locale:   \(localeIdentifier)

`OutlineMenu` is an `enum` (a menu identifier) with 8 view-builder members — and this pattern (non-View types building views) will keep recurring. Rather than continue per-method whack-a-mole, the idiomatic Swift 6.2 solution for an app target is to flip the **default actor isolation to MainActor**. The packages keep their own (nonisolated) default, so this only affects app code — which is overwhelmingly UI/main-actor. Let me set it and observe the new landscape.

38	    private static func preservedMovieIds(from state: AppState) -> Set<Int> {
39	        var ids = state.moviesState.wishlist
40	        ids.formUnion(state.moviesState.seenlist)

42	        for list in state.moviesState.customLists.values {

46	            }
47	        }

49	        return ids

53	/// App-shell wrapper around `MovieSwiftFluxCore.appStateReducer` that adds two
54	/// app-only actions:
55	///   - `AppActions.ClearCachedData`: drops every cached TMDB movie/person except
56	///     ones the user has saved (wishlist, seenlist, custom lists, fan club).
57	///   - `AppActions.ImportAppData`: merges a previously-exported state envelope.
58	/// Both depend on app-target types (`AppDataImport`, `AppDataExportEnvelope`)
59	/// that aren't available inside the package.
60	func appReducerWithImports(state: AppState, action: Action) -> AppState {
61	    if action is AppActions.ClearCachedData {
62	        return AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state)
63	    }
64	    if let importAction = action as? AppActions.ImportAppData {
65	        return AppDataImport.merge(envelope: importAction.envelope, into: state)
66	    }
67	    return appStateReducer(state: state, action: action)
68	}

1	//  Builds a JSON-encoded export of the user's persistent app data —
2	//  wishlist, seenlist, custom lists, fan club, and the cached metadata
3	//  for those movies / people. Wraps the snapshot in an envelope with a
4	//  format version, export date, and app version so future imports can
5	//  detect format drift.
6	
7	import Foundation
8	import MovieSwiftFluxCore
9	
10	/// Versioned envelope around an `AppState` snapshot, written out as JSON.
11	///
12	/// The envelope is intentionally a separate type from `AppState` so the
13	/// import side can read the version field before attempting to decode
14	/// the snapshot body — letting older or newer formats fail with a clear
15	/// error instead of silently corrupting state.
16	struct AppDataExportEnvelope: Codable {
17	    /// Bumped when the on-disk export format changes in a way that
18	    /// would prevent older readers from understanding the file.
19	    static let currentFormatVersion: Int = 1
20	
21	    let formatVersion: Int
22	    let exportDate: Date
23	    let appVersion: String
24	    let appBuild: String
25	    let snapshot: AppState
26	}
27	
28	enum AppDataExport {
29	    /// Default JSON encoder used for exports. Pretty-printed and ISO 8601
30	    /// dates so the file is human-inspectable.
31	    static func makeEncoder() -> JSONEncoder {
32	        let encoder = JSONEncoder()
33	        encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]
34	        encoder.dateEncodingStrategy = .iso8601
35	        return encoder
36	    }
37	
38	    static func makeDecoder() -> JSONDecoder {
39	        let decoder = JSONDecoder()
40	        decoder.dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601
41	        return decoder
42	    }
43	
44	    /// Builds the export envelope from the live app state. Reuses
45	    /// `AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from:)` so transient
46	    /// caches (search results, popular lists, recommended sets, etc.)
47	    /// are stripped — only the user's actual data ships.
48	    static func envelope(from state: AppState,
49	                         exportDate: Date = Date(),
50	                         appVersion: String = bundleVersion(),
51	                         appBuild: String = bundleBuild()) -> AppDataExportEnvelope {
52	        AppDataExportEnvelope(
53	            formatVersion: AppDataExportEnvelope.currentFormatVersion,
54	            exportDate: exportDate,
55	            appVersion: appVersion,
56	            appBuild: appBuild,
57	            snapshot: AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from: state)
58	        )
59	    }
60	
61	    /// Encodes the envelope as pretty-printed JSON.
62	    static func data(from envelope: AppDataExportEnvelope,
63	                     encoder: JSONEncoder = makeEncoder()) throws -> Data {
64	        try encoder.encode(envelope)
65	    }
66	
67	    /// Convenience: build the envelope and encode in one step.
68	    static func data(from state: AppState,
69	                     exportDate: Date = Date()) throws -> Data {
70	        try data(from: envelope(from: state, exportDate: exportDate))
71	    }
72	
73	    /// "MovieSwift-Export-2026-05-02.json" style filename based on the
74	    /// export date, without spaces or path separators.
75	    static func suggestedFilename(for date: Date,
76	                                  calendar: Calendar = .init(identifier: .gregorian),
77	                                  timeZone: TimeZone = .current) -> String {
78	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
79	        formatter.calendar = calendar
80	        formatter.timeZone = timeZone
81	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
82	        formatter.dateFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd"
83	        return "MovieSwift-Export-\(formatter.string(from: date))"
84	    }
85	
86	    // MARK: - Bundle helpers
87	
88	    static func bundleVersion(bundle: Bundle = .main) -> String {
89	        bundle.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String ?? "0.0"
90	    }
91	
92	    static func bundleBuild(bundle: Bundle = .main) -> String {
93	        bundle.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleVersion") as? String ?? "0"
94	    }
95	}

1	//  Versioned envelope for the on-disk persisted state file.
2	//
3	//  Without a format version, the day someone adds a non-optional
4	//  field to AppState every existing user's userData file silently
5	//  fails to decode — they open the app, find their wishlist empty,
6	//  and conclude something corrupted them. This wraps AppState in an
7	//  envelope with a format version, validates that version on load,
8	//  and transparently falls back to the legacy bare-AppState format
9	//  so installs from pre-versioning builds upgrade cleanly.
10	//
11	//  The export envelope (AppDataExportEnvelope) and this persisted
12	//  envelope are deliberately separate types: exports go to a file
13	//  the user shares with themselves and may carry version metadata
14	//  (app version, export date) that doesn't make sense on the local
15	//  cache file, while the persisted envelope is internal-only and
16	//  optimised for fast load.
17	
18	import Foundation
19	import MovieSwiftFluxCore
20	
21	/// Wraps `AppState` with a format version so future schema changes
22	/// can be detected (and rejected, if they're newer than this build
23	/// understands) instead of silently producing junk data.
24	struct PersistedAppStateEnvelope: Codable {
25	    /// Bumped when the persisted on-disk schema changes in a way
26	    /// that older builds would mis-decode. New optional fields
27	    /// don't require a bump; renames, removals, and required-field
28	    /// additions do.
29	    static let currentFormatVersion: Int = 1
30	
31	    let formatVersion: Int
32	    let savedAt: Date
33	    let state: AppState
34	}
35	
36	nonisolated enum AppStatePersistedFormat {
37	
38	    /// Errors surfaced when a persisted file can't be loaded.
39	    enum LoadError: LocalizedError {
40	        case unsupportedFutureVersion(found: Int, supported: ClosedRange<Int>)
41	        case decodeFailed(underlying: Error)
42	
43	        var errorDescription: String? {
44	            switch self {
45	            case .unsupportedFutureVersion(let found, let supported):
46	                return String(localized: "Saved data uses format version \(found), which this build of MovieSwift can't read (supported: \(supported.lowerBound)–\(supported.upperBound)). Update the app and try again.",
47	                              comment: "Logged at app launch when the persisted userData file is from a newer build than the one running. The integers are format-version numbers.")

24	        case .region:  return String(localized: "Region", comment: "Onboarding step name: region selection")
25	        case .ready:   return String(localized: "Ready", comment: "Onboarding step name: finished")
26	        }
27	    }
28	}
29	
30	/// Stateless decisions about onboarding: should it appear, can the
31	/// user continue from a given step, can they finish? Lives separate
32	/// from the view so each branch is unit-testable.
33	public enum OnboardingFlow {
34	
35	    // MARK: - Visibility
36	
37	    /// Whether onboarding should be shown right now.
38	    ///
39	    /// Returns true when:
40	    /// - The user has never finished onboarding, OR
41	    /// - The app has no usable API key (forcing the user to pick one),
42	    /// AND the runtime isn't a UI smoke test (those bypass the flow).
43	    public static func shouldShow(
44	        hasCompletedOnboarding: Bool,
45	        hasUsableAPIKey: Bool,
46	        isRunningUISmokeTests: Bool
47	    ) -> Bool {
48	        if isRunningUISmokeTests { return false }
49	        return !hasCompletedOnboarding || !hasUsableAPIKey
50	    }
51	
52	    /// Production convenience that pulls the inputs from
53	    /// AppUserDefaults and the layered API key provider.
54	    public static func shouldShowFromCurrentState(isRunningUISmokeTests: Bool) -> Bool {
55	        shouldShow(
56	            hasCompletedOnboarding: AppUserDefaults.hasCompletedOnboarding,
57	            hasUsableAPIKey=[REDACTED].userKeyOverridingBundle.apiKey() != nil,
58	            isRunningUISmokeTests: isRunningUISmokeTests
59	        )
60	    }
61	
62	    // MARK: - Step navigation
63	
64	    /// Returns the next step after `current`, or nil if `current` is
65	    /// the last step.
66	    public static func nextStep(after current: OnboardingStep) -> OnboardingStep? {
67	        let all = OnboardingStep.allCases
68	        guard let idx = all.firstIndex(of: current),
69	              idx + 1 < all.count else { return nil }
70	        return all[idx + 1]
71	    }
72	
73	    /// Returns the step before `current`, or nil if `current` is the
74	    /// first step.
75	    public static func previousStep(before current: OnboardingStep) -> OnboardingStep? {
76	        let all = OnboardingStep.allCases
77	        guard let idx = all.firstIndex(of: current),
78	              idx - 1 >= 0 else { return nil }
79	        return all[idx - 1]
80	    }
81	
82	    /// Whether the Continue / Finish button on `step` should be
83	    /// enabled given the current state.
84	    ///
85	    /// Per-step rules:
86	    /// - `.welcome` and `.region` always advance.
87	    /// - `.apiKey` only advances when there's a usable key (user or
88	    ///   bundled). The user can paste one or fall back to the bundled
89	    ///   default.
90	    /// - `.ready` is the finish step — only available when there's
91	    ///   still a usable key by the time we get there.
92	    public static func canAdvance(from step: OnboardingStep, hasUsableAPIKey: Bool) -> Bool {
93	        switch step {
94	        case .welcome, .region:
95	            return true
96	        case .apiKey, .ready:
97	            return hasUsableAPIKey
98	        }
99	    }
100	}
101	
```

> AGENT

`logHierarchyOnMissing` is a nonisolated UI-test helper; the `&&` short-circuit makes `!element.exists` a nonisolated autoclosure, triggering the warning. Splitting it into nested `if`s avoids the autoclosure:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01KKqmRKsPYFBVwEHVwMndbr
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/UITestHelpers.swift",
  "old_string": "func logHierarchyOnMissing(_ app: XCUIApplication, element: XCUIElement, named name: String) {\n    let shouldLog = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[\"UI_TEST_LOG_HIERARCHY\"] == \"1\"\n    if shouldLog && !element.exists {\n        print(\"Missing element: \\(name)\")\n        print(app.debugDescription)\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "func logHierarchyOnMissing(_ app: XCUIApplication, element: XCUIElement, named name: String) {\n    let shouldLog = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[\"UI_TEST_LOG_HIERARCHY\"] == \"1\"\n    guard shouldLog else { return }\n    // Evaluate `exists` outside the `&&` short-circuit: the operator's\n    // right-hand side is a nonisolated @autoclosure, which flags the\n    // main-actor `exists` access under the Swift 6 mode.\n    let missing = !element.exists\n    if missing {\n        print(\"Missing element: \\(name)\")\n        print(app.debugDescription)\n    }\n}"
}

Modernization 5 is implemented and pushed as **PR #11**. Here's where it stands:

## Swift 6 language mode + strict concurrency — PR #11 open

This was by far the largest item. Summary of what landed across 7 commits:

- **All three packages** → `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]`:
  - **Backend**: `AppUserDefaults` → computed statics; `APIService.GET` confines its completion-handler hand-off to an internal `@unchecked Sendable` box (so the Redux callers stay unchanged); stateless services made `Sendable`.
  - **FluxCore**: every TMDB model + the entire `AppState` graph conform to `Sendable`.
  - **UI**: `PreferenceKey` default → `let`; `SearchTextObservable` → `@MainActor`.
- **App targets (iOS/macOS/tvOS)** → `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` **plus `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`** — the idiomatic choice for a UI app. This collapsed ~30 view-conformance errors that the targeted approach was whack-a-moling. Pure value/logic types (reducers, persistence, onboarding, spotlight, focus identity) are explicitly `nonisolated`; the pinned pre-concurrency SwiftUIFlux is bridged with `@preconcurrency import` + localized `nonisolated(unsafe)` on configure-once singletons.
- **Test targets** stay nonisolated-by-default; cases opt into `@MainActor` where they touch main-actor code.

**Local verification (all green, 0 warnings):** Backend (33 tests) + FluxCore (100 tests) pass; iOS/macOS/tvOS app *and* test targets build clean; iOS unit tests (370) pass.

> AGENT

Modernization 5 is done and merged. Here's the summary:

## ✅ Modernization 5 complete — PR #11 merged (the big one)

**Swift 6 language mode + strict concurrency** across the entire project — **94 files**, 8 commits.

- **All 3 packages** → `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]`: Backend (computed `AppUserDefaults`, internal `@unchecked Sendable` box in `GET` so the Redux layer stays untouched, `Sendable` services), FluxCore (every TMDB model + `AppState` graph `Sendable`), UI (`PreferenceKey` → `let`, `SearchTextObservable` → `@MainActor`).
- **App targets (iOS/macOS/tvOS)** → `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` **+ `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`**. This pivot was the key decision — it collapsed ~30 view-conformance errors the per-view approach was whack-a-moling. Pure value/logic types (reducers, persistence, onboarding, spotlight, focus identity) marked `nonisolated`; pinned SwiftUIFlux bridged with `@preconcurrency import` + `nonisolated(unsafe)` on configure-once singletons.
- **Test targets** stay nonisolated-by-default; cases opt into `@MainActor` where they touch main-actor code.
- **Copilot review:** 2 false positives (public-extension members stay public — CI proved it), 3 valid fixes applied (`Task { @MainActor in }` over `assumeIsolated`, restored `super` calls in async setup). All 5 threads resolved.
- **CI:** all 5 required jobs green (no flake), both runs.

---

## 📋 Final item — Modernization 6: finish the XCTest → Swift Testing migration

The last one. The codebase is mid-migration: most suites are still XCTest (`XCTestCase` + `XCTAssert`/`waitForExpectations`), while a handful already use Swift Testing (`@Test`/`@Suite`/`#expect` — e.g. Backend's `PlatformImageTests`, `ImageService.Size` tests). The goal is to convert the remaining XCTest suites to Swift Testing for consistency: `#expect`/`#require` instead of `XCTAssert`, `@Test` functions, `@Suite` types, and async confirmation (`confirmation`/`await`) in place of `XCTestExpectation`/`waitForExpectations`.

Note: the Swift 6 work I just merged left many test classes pinned `@MainActor` with `waitForExpectations` — those completion-handler-based suites (APIServiceTests, MoviesActionsTests, PeopleActionsTests) are the most involved to convert since they need `confirmation`/continuation-based async instead of expectations.

Want me to start on Modernization 6?

Now the complex one — `APIServiceTests` with its `waitForExpectations`-based async tests. The clean Swift Testing pattern: a `runGET` helper that bridges the completion handler to `async` via `withCheckedContinuation`, using an `@unchecked Sendable` box to carry the non-Sendable `Result` across, so assertions run in the test's async context. No `@MainActor` needed (no `waitForExpectations`), so it's a parallel-safe `struct`.

HTTPURLResponse(url: request.url!, statusCode: 200,\n                                   httpVersion: \"HTTP/1.1\", headerFields: nil)!\n            return (nextData, response)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private enum StubError: Error {\n        case failed\n    }\n\n    private struct Payload: Codable, Equatable, Sendable {\n        let value: String\n    }\n\n    /// Carries a (non-Sendable) `Result` across the continuation so the\n    /// completion-handler `GET` can be awaited and asserted on in the\n    /// test's async context. Safe: the handler fires exactly once.\n    private struct ResultBox<T>: @unchecked Sendable {\n        let result: Result<T, APIService.APIError>\n    }\n\n    private func makeService(\n        apiKey: String?,\n        session: MockNetworkSession,\n        callbackQueue: DispatchQueue = DispatchQueue(label: \"APIServiceTests.callbackQueue\"),\n        authMode: APIService.AuthMode = .queryParameter(name: \"api_key\")\n    ) -> APIService {\n        APIService(\n            apiKeyProvider: StubAPIKeyProvider(apiKey),\n            session: session,\n            callbackQueue: callbackQueue,\n            authMode: authMode\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Bridges `APIService.GET`'s completion handler to async/await.\n    private func get<T: Codable & Sendable>(\n        _ service: APIService,\n        endpoint: APIService.Endpoint,\n        params: [String: String]? = nil,\n        as type: T.Type = T.self\n    ) async -> Result<T, APIService.APIError> {\n        await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in\n            service.GET(endpoint: endpoint, params: params) { (result: Result<T, APIService.APIError>) in\n                continuation.resume(returning: ResultBox(result: result))\n            }\n        }.result\n    }\n\n    @Test func endpointPathBuildsExpectedValues() {\n        #expect(APIService.Endpoint.popular.path() == \"movie/popular\")\n        #expect(APIService.Endpoint.movieDetail(movie: 42).path() == \"movie/42\")\n        #expect(APIService.Endpoint.personImages(person: 99).path() == \"person/99/images\")\n        #expect(APIService.Endpoint.discover.path() == \"discover/movie\")\n    }\n\n    @Test func getReturnsMissingAPIKeyWhenProviderIsEmpty() async {\n        let session = MockNetworkSession()\n        let service = makeService(apiKey: nil, session: session)\n\n        let result: Result<Payload, APIService.APIError> = await get(service, endpoint: .popular)\n        guard case .failure(.missingAPIKey) = result else {\n            Issue.record(\"Expected missing API key error\")\n            return\n        }\n        // Missing key short-circuits before any network call.\n        #expect(session.lastRequest == nil)\n    }\n\n    @Test func getBuildsRequestAndDecodesOnSuccess() async {\n        let session = MockNetworkSession()\n        session.nextData = Data(#\"{\"value\":\"ok\"}\"#.utf8)\n        let service = makeService(apiKey: \"abc123\", session: session)\n\n        let result: Result<Payload, APIService.APIError> = await get(\n            service, endpoint: .searchMovie, params: [\"page\": \"2\", \"query\": \"batman\"])\n        guard case let .success(payload) = result else {\n            Issue.record(\"Expected success\")\n            return\n        }\n        #expect(payload == Payload(value: \"ok\"))\n\n        #expect(session.lastRequest?.httpMethod == \"GET\")\n\n        let requestURL = try? #require(session.lastRequest?.url)\n        let components = requestURL.flatMap { URLComponents(url: $0, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false) }\n        let queryItems = Dictionary(\n            uniqueKeysWithValues: (components?.queryItems ?? []).map { ($0.name, $0.value ?? \"\") }\n        )\n\n        #expect(requestURL?.absoluteString.contains(\"/search/movie\") == true)\n        #expect(queryItems[\"api_key\"] == \"abc123\")\n        #expect(queryItems[\"language\"] == Locale.preferredLanguages[0])\n        #expect(queryItems[\"page\"] == \"2\")\n        #expect(queryItems[\"query\"] == \"batman\")\n    }\n\n    // (The former testGETReturnsNoResponseWhenDataIsMissing was removed:\n    // URLSession.data(for:) always yields a non-nil Data, so the\n    // \"successful response with missing data\" path is structurally\n    // impossible under async/await. The `.noResponse` error remains for\n    // the URL-construction-failure guard in GET.)\n\n    @Test func getReturnsNetworkErrorWhenErrorExists() async {\n        let session = MockNetworkSession()\n APIService.APIError> = await get(service, endpoint: .popular)\n        guard case let .failure(.networkError(error)) = result else {\n            Issue.record(\"Expected network error\")\n            return\n        }\n        #expect(error is StubError)\n    }\n\n    @Test func getReturnsDecodingErrorForInvalidPayload() async {\n        let session = MockNetworkSession()\n        session.nextData = Data(\"not-json\".utf8)\n        session.nextError = nil\n        let service = makeService(apiKey: \"abc123\", session: session)\n\n        let result: Result<Payload, APIService.APIError> = await 1	import XCTest

3	@testable import MovieSwiftFluxCore
4	
5	/// Regression tests for the package-owned `Localizable.xcstrings`.
6	///
7	/// `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter` lives in `MovieSwiftFluxCore` and
8	/// must look up its strings against `Bundle.module`, not `Bundle.main`.
9	/// Without `bundle: .module`, lookups fall back to `Bundle.main` (the
10	/// app target's bundle when hosted, or the test runner when unhosted)
11	/// and the package can't be reused outside the app.
12	///
13	/// These tests run against the package's own bundle, so if the
14	/// catalog is missing or the call sites drop `bundle: .module`, the
15	/// English source string still falls through — which is why the
16	/// assertions below intentionally check substrings of the development
17	/// language text. The real safety net is that the catalog file ships
18	/// with the package and the build doesn't strip it.
19	final class MoviesListLoadingStateTests: XCTestCase {
20	
21	    func testOfflineFailureResolvesEnglishMessageThroughPackageBundle() {
22	        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .offline)
23	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .offline)
24	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.message,
25	                       "You're offline. Check your connection and try again.")
26	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.retryActionTitle, "Try again")
27	    }
28	
29	    func testMissingAPIKeyFailureResolvesEnglishMessageThroughPackageBundle() {
30	        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .missingAPIKey)
31	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.kind, .missingAPIKey)
32	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.message,
33	                       "No TMDB API key is configured. Add one in Settings to load movies.")
34	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.retryActionTitle, "Open Settings")
35	    }
36	
37	    func testRateLimitedSingularSecondResolvesThroughPackageBundle() {
38	        let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: 1))
39	        XCTAssertEqual(failure.message,
40	                       "Too many requests to TMDB right now. Try again in 1 second.")
41	    }
42	
43	    /// `Bundle.module` is only synthesized when the target declares
44	    /// resources. Reference it from the test so anyone deleting
45	    /// `resources: [.process("Resources")]` from `Package.swift`
46	    /// breaks the build instead of silently regressing the lookup
47	    /// path back to `Bundle.main`.
48	    func testPackageBundleIsAvailable() {
49	        XCTAssertFalse(Bundle.module.bundlePath.isEmpty)
50	    }
51	}
52

1	import XCTest
2	@testable import MovieSwiftFluxCore
3	
4	/// Guards the localizability of the display-name helpers in this package.
5	///
6	/// These helpers (`MoviesMenu.title()`, `MoviesSort.title()`) used to
7	/// return bare `String` literals, which bypassed the String Catalog and
8	/// could never be translated. They now route through
9	/// `String(localized:bundle:.module)`. This suite pins the resolved
10	/// English ("en" is the package's source language) so a regression that
11	/// (a) drops the localization, (b) points at the wrong bundle, or
12	/// (c) changes a case's text is caught.
13	///
14	/// Note: with the package's source language being English, a missing
15	/// catalog entry would still resolve to the key itself — which for these
16	/// equals the English text — so this suite primarily guards the case
17	/// mapping and the presence of every case. The `bundle: .module`
18	/// correctness is exercised at runtime by the app (wrong-bundle lookups
19	/// would fall back to the key, which here is identical, so it stays safe
20	/// either way).
21	final class LocalizationTests: XCTestCase {
22	
23	    func testMoviesMenuTitlesResolveForEveryCase() {
24	        let expected: [MoviesMenu: String] = [
25	            .popular: "Popular",
26	            .topRated: "Top Rated",
27	            .upcoming: "Upcoming",
28	            .nowPlaying: "Now Playing",
29	            .trending: "Trending",
30	            .genres: "Genres",
31	        ]
32	        // Every case must be covered, and each must produce a non-empty title.
33	        for menu in MoviesMenu.allCases {
34	            let title = menu.title()
35	            XCTAssertFalse(title.isEmpty, "MoviesMenu.\(menu) produced an empty title")
36	            XCTAssertEqual(title, expected[menu],
37	                           "MoviesMenu.\(menu).title() should resolve to its English source string")
38	        }
39	        XCTAssertEqual(Set(MoviesMenu.allCases.map { $0.title() }).count,
40	                       MoviesMenu.allCases.count,
41	                       "Every MoviesMenu title should be distinct")
42	    }
43	
44	    func testMoviesSortTitlesResolveForEveryCase() {
45	        let cases: [(MoviesSort, String)] = [
46	            (.byReleaseDate, "by release date"),
47	            (.byAddedDate, "by added date"),
48	            (.byScore, "by rating"),
49	            (.byPopularity, "by popularity"),
50	        ]
51	        for (sort, expected) in cases {
52	            let title = sort.title()
53	            XCTAssertFalse(title.isEmpty, "MoviesSort title was empty")
54	            XCTAssertEqual(title, expected,
55	                           "MoviesSort.\(sort).title() should resolve to its English source string")
56	        }
57	    }
58	
59	    func testDiscoverFilterToTextLocalizesRandomFallback() {
60	        // A filter with no explicit year range renders the localized
61	        // "Random" token (rather than a bare literal). English source
62	        // resolves to "Random".
63	        let filter = DiscoverFilter(year: 2000, startYear: nil, endYear: nil,
64	                                    sort: "popularity.desc")
65	        let text = filter.toText(genres: [])
66	        XCTAssertTrue(text.contains("Random"),
67	                      "DiscoverFilter.toText should include the localized Random token when no year range is set; got: \(text)")
68	    }
69	}
70

- CrashReportStore/AppDataICloudBackup each use a unique per-test temp dir, so they're arguably isolated enough for a plain struct. Per the task's explicit instruction to treat these as `.serialized` (and because they had setUp/tearDown), I used `@Suite(.serialized) final class`.

115	        //   - the APIService's `callbackQueue` thread, which fires
116	        //     the subsequent .failed / .success+data dispatches
117	        //
118	        // `Array<any Action>` stores existential containers (5
119	        // machine-words per element). Concurrent writes corrupt the
120	        // storage and cause downcasts (`$0 as? SetMovieMenuList`) to
121	        // succeed on garbage that wasn't actually a SetMovieMenuList,
122	        // which surfaces as "Failure path unexpectedly dispatched a
123	        // SetMovieMenuList data action" with the value's description
124	        // rendered as "(Function)". The race is data-loss-prone on
125	        // any ARM machine; macos-26 CI runners hit it deterministically
126	        // while local M-series Macs tend to slip past it.
127	        //
128	        // Serialize all reads/writes through an NSLock so the array
129	        // stays consistent regardless of which thread dispatches.
130	        let lock = NSLock()
131	        var dispatched: [Action] = []
132	        let exp = expectation(description: description)
133	        exp.assertForOverFulfill = false
134	        execute { action in
135	            lock.lock()
136	            dispatched.append(action)
137	            let shouldFulfill = trigger(action)
138	            lock.unlock()
139	            if shouldFulfill { exp.fulfill() }
140	        }
141	        waitForExpectations(timeout: timeout)
142	        lock.lock()
143	        defer { lock.unlock() }
144	        return dispatched
145	    }
146	
147	    /// Find the first dispatched action of the given type, or fail the test if
148	    /// none was dispatched.
149	    private func unwrapDispatched<T>(
150	        _ type: T.Type,
151	        in dispatched: [Action],
152	        file: StaticString = #filePath,
153	        line: UInt = #line
154	    ) throws -> T {
155	        let matches = dispatched.compactMap { $0 as? T }
156	        return try XCTUnwrap(matches.first,
157	                             "Expected one \(T.self) in dispatched actions, got: \(dispatched)",
158	                             file: file, line: line)
159	    }
160	
161	    /// Assert that the dispatch trace ends in a `SetLoadingState(.failed)`
162	    /// for `key`, with no data action of `dataType` ever dispatched. Returns
163	    /// the failure for further assertion.
164	    ///
165	    /// Takes a `noDataActionMatching` closure rather than a generic `T.Type`.
166	    /// The generic-T form (`$0 as? T`) was triggering a Swift 6 compiler
167	    /// quirk on the macos-26 GitHub runner where the cast returned a value
168	    /// whose dynamic type rendered as `(Function)` — even though no Action
169	    /// passed to dispatch was a closure. Inlining the type check at the
170	    /// call site (via the closure) bypasses the generic-existential cast
171	    /// path and produces consistent results locally and on CI.
172	    private func assertFailureDispatch(
173	        in dispatched: [Action],
174	        for key: LoadingKey,
175	        noDataActionMatching matches: (Action) -> Bool,
176	        dataActionDescription: String,
177	        file: StaticString = #filePath,
178	        line: UInt = #line
179	    ) throws -> MoviesListLoadFailure {
180	        let unwantedDataAction = dispatched.first(where: matches)
181	        XCTAssertNil(unwantedDataAction,
182	                     "Failure path unexpectedly dispatched a \(dataActionDescription) data action.",
183	                     file: file, line: line)
184	        let loadingStates = dispatched.compactMap { $0 as? MoviesActions.SetLoadingState }
185	        let lastForKey = loadingStates.last { $0.key == key }
186	        let unwrapped = try XCTUnwrap(lastForKey,
187	                                      "No SetLoadingState dispatched for key \(key); got: \(loadingStates)",
188	                                      file: file, line: line)
189	        guard case let .failed(failure) = unwrapped.state else {
190	            XCTFail("Last SetLoadingState for \(key) was \(String(describing: unwrapped.state)), not .failed",
191	                    file: file, line: line)
192	            throw StubError.failed
193	        }
194	        return failure
195	    }

Swift's CaseIterable\n    /// makes this exhaustive — if a new kind is added to the enum, this\n    /// test makes the author add it here too (or accept the default\n    /// CustomStringConvertible behaviour).\n    @Test func diagnosticIncludesAllFailureKindsDistinctly() {\n        let kinds: [MoviesListLoadFailure.Kind] = [\n            .offline, .rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds: 30), .missingAPIKey, .unauthorized,\n            .forbidden, .server, .decode, .other\n        ]\n        var rendered: Set<String> = []\n        for kind in kinds {\n            let blob = ErrorDiagnostic.text(\n                for: makeFailure(kind: kind),\n                appVersion: \"1.0\", appBuild: \"1\",\n                osDescription: \"iOS 26.5\", deviceModel: \"iPhone\",\n                localeIdentifier: \"en_US\", now: makeFixedDate()\n            )\n            // Extract just the failure line so we're not comparing entire blobs.\n            guard let line = blob.split(separator: \"\\n\").first(where: { $0.hasPrefix(\"failure:\") }) else {\n                Issue.record(\"Expected a 'failure:' line in the diagnostic blob\")\n                return\n            }\n            rendered.insert(String(line))\n        }\n        #expect(rendered.count == kinds.count,\n                \"Each failure kind should render a distinct 'failure:' line so triage can tell them apart; got duplicates: \\(rendered)\")\n    }\n\n    /// Sanity check that `Clipboard.copy(_:)` actually wrote what we\n    /// asked it to write. Doesn't assert anything about Clipboard's\n    /// platform impl beyond round-trip identity — sufficient for the\n    /// banner's \"Copied!\" feedback to be honest.\n    @Test func clipboardCopyRoundTripsTheStringOnHostPlatform() {\n        let payload = \"MovieSwift diagnostic test \\(UUID().uuidString)\"\n        let succeeded = Clipboard.copy(payload)\n        // tvOS has no pasteboard, so Clipboard.copy returns false there (as\n        // can a sandboxed test host); there's nothing to round-trip, so\n        // return without asserting — the Swift Testing equivalent of the\n        // old XCTSkipUnless.\n        guard succeeded else { return }\n\n        #if os(tvOS)\n        // unreachable — `succeeded` is always false on tvOS (no pasteboard)\n        #elseif canImport(UIKit)\n        #expect(UIPasteboard.general.string == payload)\n        #elseif canImport(AppKit)\n        #expect(NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string) == payload)\n        #endif\n    }\n}\n"
}
