## Code review — chore/add-verifier-subagent

Note: the pending work is entirely uncommitted (no commits ahead of main). The diff consists of modifications to `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/CLAUDE.md` and a new untracked file `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md`.

---

### Must fix (correctness, CI-blocking)

**1. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:42` — mac-tests invocation is wrong and will not reproduce what CI actually runs.**

The verifier table says:

```
cd MovieSwift && xcodebuild test -scheme MovieSwiftMac -destination "platform=macOS"
```

The actual CI invocation in `.github/workflows/xcodebuild.yml` (lines 137-145) is:

```
xcodebuild test \
  -project MovieSwift/MovieSwift.xcodeproj \
  -scheme MovieSwiftMac \
  -destination "platform=macOS" \
  -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  -retry-tests-on-failure \
  CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-" \
  CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
```

Three critical differences: (a) the `-project` flag is absent — `cd MovieSwift &&` plus no `-project` will either pick up the wrong scheme or fail to build; (b) `-parallel-testing-enabled NO` is missing — macOS UI tests are known to flake without it; (c) all three `CODE_SIGNING_*` overrides are absent — on a local developer machine these may not matter, but omitting them means the local run does not mirror CI, and on a CI-like sandboxed environment it will fail to sign. The purpose of the verifier is to be a faithful local mirror of CI; a divergent invocation defeats that.

Fix: replace the mac-tests row with the full `-project`-qualified, unsigned, non-parallel invocation, run from the repo root (not `cd MovieSwift`), matching the workflow exactly.

---

**2. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:42` — tvos-tests invocation is similarly incomplete.**

The verifier table says:

```
cd MovieSwift && xcodebuild test -scheme MovieSwiftTV -destination "platform=tvOS Simulator,name=Apple TV"
```

CI (`.github/workflows/xcodebuild.yml` lines 159-164) adds `-retry-tests-on-failure` and `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, and uses `-project MovieSwift/MovieSwift.xcodeproj` (run from the repo root). Both the code-signing flag and the retry flag are absent in the table.

Fix: same pattern as mac-tests — supply `-project`, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, and `-retry-tests-on-failure`, and drop the `cd MovieSwift &&` prefix.

---

**3. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:40` — ios-tests-ipad invocation omits `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING`, which changes what is actually run.**

CI sets `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING: MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftUITests/testLaunchShowsMainTabs,MovieSwiftTests` for the `ios-tests-ipad` job (xcodebuild.yml line 97), meaning it runs both a UI smoke test and the full unit suite. The verifier table gives only `IOS_SIMULATOR_FAMILY=iPad IOS_SIMULATOR_NAME="iPad (A16)" ./scripts/ci/run_ios_tests.sh`, with no `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING`. Without it `run_ios_tests.sh` will run everything (or whatever `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING` happens to be set to in the environment), not what CI actually enforces.

Fix: add `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING="MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftUITests/testLaunchShowsMainTabs,MovieSwiftTests"` to the environment prefix in the table row.

---

### Should fix (accuracy, readability, conventions)

**4. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:38` — `package-tests` row conflates two distinct scripts with different scopes.**

The table entry reads: `./scripts/ci/check_coverage.sh — or, faster, swift test from MovieSwift/Packages/<Name>`. But `check_coverage.sh` does more than run tests — it enforces coverage thresholds (currently 76.1% for Backend, 52.2% for MovieSwiftFluxCore) and will fail the gate if coverage drops even if all tests pass. A bare `swift test` run in a single package will not enforce the threshold for the other package and will not enforce any threshold at all. The "or, faster" framing implies they are equivalent; they are not.

Fix: separate the two: note that `./scripts/ci/check_coverage.sh` is the full gate (both packages + coverage thresholds), and that `swift test` in a single package is a quick sanity check only, not a substitute for the gate.

---

**5. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:26` — the verifier's "establish the change set" section uses `git diff main...HEAD` but the branch has uncommitted changes.**

The same issue exists in `code-reviewer.md`, but the verifier is the first gate and is meant to catch build failures before review. `git diff main...HEAD` shows only committed changes; it will silently ignore `git diff` (unstaged) and `git diff --staged`. The agent already lists all three commands in the bullet list below, but the prose "Determine what changed, the same way the reviewer does" implies parity with the code-reviewer, which itself has this gap. On this current branch, all changes are uncommitted, so `git diff main...HEAD` would show nothing and the verifier would exit with "no change, stopping" — never running any gate. The prose should make explicit that uncommitted (`git diff` + `git diff --staged`) changes are in scope too, and that the agent must run those gates even when the three-dot diff is empty.

Fix: add a sentence: "If `git diff main...HEAD` is empty but `git diff` or `git diff --staged` are non-empty, the pending uncommitted work is still in scope — run all gates against it."

---

**6. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/CLAUDE.md:4` (step 4) — the loop termination condition uses backtick-quoted `PASS` but verifier.md's output format uses plain `PASS`.**

CLAUDE.md step 4 says "re-run the verifier until it returns `PASS`". verifier.md's output format section (line 106) shows the verdict as `PASS — ready for code review.` — not a bare `PASS`. A literal string-match check by the main agent would fail. This is minor but could confuse an agent trying to automate the loop.

Fix: either align CLAUDE.md to say "returns a verdict of `PASS`" (describing the section), or align verifier.md's verdict line to be a bare `PASS` followed by prose on the next line.

---

**7. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:44-46` — the "always re-read the workflow files" instruction appears after the table but the table is the output of reading those files, creating a forward reference.**

The instruction says "Always re-read `.github/workflows/lint.yml` and `.github/workflows/xcodebuild.yml` to confirm the canonical invocations before relying on the table." This is correct guidance but it comes after the table, implying the agent should use the table first and check afterward. Given that the table already has diverged from the workflows (findings 1-3 above), the instruction should appear before the table to make clear the table is illustrative and the workflows are authoritative.

Fix: move the "always re-read" note to immediately before the table, or reframe the table header as "Example invocations — verify against the workflow files above before using."

---

### Nits

**8. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:3` — the `description:` field says "Use proactively right after finishing the work and before the code-reviewer subagent." The phrase "right after finishing the work" is ambiguous — it could mean before or after lint/format (step 3). CLAUDE.md step 4 says "After the work is done and before the review" which matches, but "the work" in the verifier description doesn't make clear whether step 3 (lint) must have run first.**

Fix: tighten to "Use after lint/format (step 3) and before the code-reviewer subagent (step 5)."

---

**9. `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.claude/agents/verifier.md:1` — `model: sonnet` is not pinned to a specific model version, unlike the description field of the code-reviewer which also says `sonnet`. This is consistent with the existing agent but worth noting if the platform supports pinning.**

No immediate fix needed if this mirrors the project's existing convention.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the mac-tests and tvos-tests invocations in verifier.md are missing `-project`, code-signing overrides, and retry flags that CI actually uses, the ios-tests-ipad row omits the `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING` scoping, and the uncommitted-work edge case means the verifier would exit early on this very branch; fix those four issues before shipping.

The workflow update is shipped to PR [#30](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/30) and CI is running in the background (I'll merge once the required suites are green).

## What I added

**`verifier` subagent** (`.claude/agents/verifier.md`) — a read-only agent that runs the exact gates CI enforces over a pending change (SwiftLint, the relevant builds, and the package/iOS/iPad/macOS/tvOS test suites that cover the change) and reports build failures, failing tests, and lint violations back with failing-command excerpts and probable cause. It scopes to the suites the change touches, treats uncommitted work as in scope, and stays out of the reviewer's lane (no style/design commentary).

**Workflow wiring** (`CLAUDE.md`) — new **step 4 "Verify with the verifier subagent,"** sitting exactly where you asked: after the work + lint/format, before the code-reviewer. The rule is explicit: *the main agent must fix everything the verifier reports and re-run it to a `PASS` verdict before the review* (and re-verify if review feedback changes code). Steps renumbered through merge.

## Two notes
- I ran the existing **code-reviewer** over this change and it earned its keep immediately — it caught that my first draft of the verifier's gate commands had drifted from CI (missing `-project`, code-signing overrides, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`, `-retry-tests-on-failure`, and the iPad `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING` scope). I verified the real invocations against `.github/workflows/` and corrected them, plus clarified that `package-tests` enforces coverage thresholds (not just `swift test`) and fixed an uncommitted-work edge case.
- I **couldn't dogfood the verifier via the Agent tool** this session — agent definitions load at session start, so the newly written one isn't selectable until a reload. It'll be available next session; I ran its checks manually here (lint clean; no Swift touched).

Once #30 merges, the next session will have the `verifier` available, and we can resume Phase 2 hardening (Settings export/import/iCloud-backup tests, FanClub follow/unfollow, tvOS/macOS parity, PeopleActions per-thunk failures) under the new verify-then-review flow.

# MovieSwiftUI — Roadmap

A phased plan derived from an expert audit (Apple-platform modernity, test
coverage, readability, and product/feature gaps). The app is in strong
shape — iOS/macOS/tvOS 26, Swift 6 strict concurrency, modern SwiftUI,
503 unit + 109 UI tests, good accessibility/localization. What follows is
high-leverage refinement and growth, sequenced so the codebase stays safe
to change at every step.

**Guiding principle: harden as you build.** Every feature ships with
unit + UI tests for its journey. Every change goes through the delivery
workflow in `CLAUDE.md` (branch → TDD → `code-reviewer` → green CI →
merge).

Effort key: **S** ≈ days · **M** ≈ 1–2 weeks · **L** ≈ multi-week.

---

## Phase 1 — Trailer playback (the headline gap) · S

Trailers are half-built: `MoviesActions.FetchVideos` fetches `[Video]`
(YouTube keys) into `moviesState.videos`, and `MovieDetailState` emits a
`.videos` load slice — **but nothing renders it.** No `VideoPlayer`,
play button, or link anywhere. Best impact-to-effort item in the app; the
data pipeline already exists.

- [ ] `MovieVideosRow` rendering `moviesState.videos` (trailer thumbnails).
- [ ] "Play Trailer" affordance on the hero/cover row.
- [ ] Inline YouTube/web-embed player (or deep-link to the YouTube app).
- [ ] Tests: a `MovieVideosState`/presentation unit test + a UI test that
      opens a movie and plays/launches the top trailer.

## Phase 2 — Harden critical journeys (tests) · S–M

Close the regression-risk holes so feature work is safe. (Logic layer is
already excellent; these are end-to-end + edge gaps.)

- [ ] **UI: Settings data management** — export creates a document;
      import shows preview counts + merges; iCloud backup + "restore older
      version". *No UI test exists on any platform today, and it's the most
      data-destructive surface in the app.*
- [ ] **UI: Fan Club** — people-search results + follow/unfollow toggle
      (full reducer coverage today, zero XCUITest).
- [ ] **Platform parity UI tests** — tvOS currently covers only
      browse/detail/search; macOS lags iOS on MyLists create/edit,
      Discover undo, search-cancel. Bring the critical journeys to parity.
- [ ] Strengthen existence-only assertions (189 `XCTAssertTrue` vs 18
      value-asserting on iOS) — verify state *changed*, not just that an
      element appeared.
- [ ] `PeopleActions` per-thunk failure tests (currently thinner than
      `MoviesActions`).
- [ ] Fix the two tracked macOS parity bugs and un-skip their tests:
      `CustomListRow` needs an accessibility identifier; macOS
      `DiscoverView` doesn't render `discover.undoButton`.

## Phase 3 — Readability & architecture foundation · S–M

Make the codebase easier for humans *and* agents before scaling it up.

- [ ] **Model `CodingKeys` boundary** — `Movie`/`People`/`Image`/etc.
      expose raw TMDB `snake_case` (`poster_path`, `vote_average`) as the
      public Swift API, while the `state/` layer already uses `CodingKeys`
      + camelCase. Confine snake_case to the decoding boundary (same move
      as the `productionCountry` rename, scaled up). This is the biggest
      "agent trap" in the code.
- [ ] **Centralize test seams** — env-var flags
      (`UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION`, etc.) and the 77 accessibility IDs are
      bare string literals re-typed across app + test targets. Hoist into
      `enum UITestEnv` / an `AccessibilityID` namespace shared by both.
- [ ] Document the 43 `MoviesActions` structs (the Redux flow's
      discoverability hinges on them).
- [ ] Extract a `MovieDetailFocusModel` — the ~16 near-identical
      `*Targets(props:)` focus helpers dominate `MovieDetail.swift`.

## Phase 4 — Modern platform plumbing · M

Adopt current iOS-26 patterns; unblock cleaner code.

- [ ] **Migrate the SwiftUIFlux `Store` to `@Observable`** — it's a
      Combine `ObservableObject`, the root cause of **33
      `@preconcurrency import SwiftUIFlux`** workarounds and the
      `nonisolated(unsafe)` sample-store globals. Vendorable dependency;
      highest-leverage concurrency cleanup.
- [ ] **App Intent entities + parameterized Shortcuts** — intents are
      launch-only today. Add a `MovieEntity: AppEntity` +
      `AddToWatchlistIntent(movie:)` / `MarkAsSeenIntent` that dispatch the
      existing `AddToWishlist`/`AddToSeenList` actions. Unlocks Siri +
      Spotlight actions and feeds Widgets/Controls.
- [ ] Liquid Glass (`.glassEffect`) on the Discover floating buttons +
      toolbars; `@Entry` macro for environment keys; `reduceMotion` gating
      on the swipe animations; SF Symbol animations on toggles/loading.
- [ ] Remove the dead `ActionSheet`/`Alert.Button` factory
      (`Shared/extensions/ActionSheet.swift`).
- [ ] `ShareLink` on movie + person detail (TMDB URL + poster preview).

## Phase 5 — Killer features · M

- [ ] **"Where to Watch" streaming providers** — the #1 table-stakes
      feature that's entirely missing. Add `Endpoint.watchProviders`, a
      `WatchProvider` model + action/reducer, and a region-aware provider
      row (region picker already exists).
- [ ] **Watchlist Widget + lock-screen Control** — reads persisted
      `AppState`; pairs with the Phase-4 App Intents.
- [ ] Personal star ratings (stored in `AppState`); release notifications
      (`UNUserNotification` keyed off `release_date`); `movieswift://` URL
      scheme + Handoff; Spotlight poster thumbnails (`thumbnailData`).

## Phase 6 — Strategic / marquee · L

- [ ] **TV-show support** — the app is movies-only (`/tv` endpoints
      absent). Add `/tv`, season/episode models, and a media-type enum
      threaded through state. The bet that removes the app's ceiling.
- [ ] watchOS companion (watchlist on the wrist); visionOS target; Apple
      TV "Top Shelf"; "Your Year in Movies" recap (seenlist + genres are
      already in state).

---

## Cross-cutting / housekeeping
```

> AGENT

We're inside **Phase 2 — Harden critical journeys**. The macOS parity bugs (the last checklist item) are now done and merged (#28/#29), and the workflow now has the verifier gate (#30). Five Phase 2 items remain:

- **Settings data management** UI tests — export/import/iCloud backup-restore. *Zero UI tests on any platform, and the roadmap flags it as the most data-destructive surface in the app.*
- **Fan Club** UI tests — people-search results + follow/unfollow (full reducer coverage, zero XCUITest).
- **Platform parity** UI tests — tvOS covers only browse/detail/search; macOS lags iOS on MyLists create/edit, search-cancel.
- **Strengthen existence-only assertions** — 189 `XCTAssertTrue`-element-exists vs 18 value-asserting on iOS; verify state actually *changed*.
- **`PeopleActions` per-thunk failure tests** — thinner than `MoviesActions`.

My recommendation is to take the Settings data-management tests next: it's the highest-risk gap (data loss surface) with literally no end-to-end coverage, so it's where a regression would hurt most and where tests buy the most safety. Which would you like to tackle?

### 3. UNDERLYING LOGIC

**AppDataExport.swift** (`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataExport.swift`, Lines 1–96):

Returns: `AppDataExportEnvelope` (contains formatVersion, exportDate, appVersion, appBuild, snapshot: AppState)

What it does:
- `envelope(from:exportDate:appVersion:appBuild)` — wraps app state in versioned envelope
- `data(from:encoder)` — encodes envelope to pretty-printed JSON with sorted keys
- `suggestedFilename(for:)` — generates "MovieSwift-Export-YYYY-MM-DD.json"
- Reuses `AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot(from:)` to strip transient caches
- Exports: wishlist, seenlist, customLists, fanClub, movies cache (only referenced items), peoples cache

**SettingsForm.swift** (Export logic, Lines 125–149):

```swift
private func startExport() {
    let now = Date()
    do {
        let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: store.state, exportDate: now)
        exportDocument = UserDataDocument(data: data)
        exportSuggestedFilename = AppDataExport.suggestedFilename(for: now)
        isExportPresented = true  // Triggers .fileExporter
    } catch {
        exportErrorMessage = "Couldn't build the export file: \(error.localizedDescription)"
    }
}

private func handleExportResult(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {
    exportDocument = nil
    if case .failure(let error) = result {
        if (error as NSError).domain != NSCocoaErrorDomain || (error as NSError).code != NSUserCancelledError {
            exportErrorMessage = "Export failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
        }
    }
}
```

**AppDataImport.swift** (`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataImport.swift`, Lines 1–167):

Returns: `Counts` struct with preview of additions

What it does:
- `decodeEnvelope(from:decoder)` — validates format version, decodes JSON
- `previewCounts(for:against:)` — counts wishlist/seenlist/fanClub/customLists additions/updates without mutation
  - wishlistAdded = difference set
  - seenlistAdded = difference set
  - fanClubAdded = difference set
  - customListsAdded = new list IDs
  - customListsUpdated = ID conflicts
- `merge(envelope:into:)` — non-destructive union:
  - User collections: set union (existing + imported)
  - Custom lists: upsert by ID (imported wins on conflict)
  - Movies/peoples caches: current wins (likely fresher)
  - Discover filters: append new ones (dedupe by JSON encoding)

**SettingsForm.swift** (Import logic, Lines 151–190):

```swift
private func handleImportSelection(_ result: Result<[URL], Error>) {
    switch result {
    case .failure(let error):
        if (error as NSError).domain != NSCocoaErrorDomain || (error as NSError).code != NSUserCancelledError {
            importErrorMessage = "Import failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
        }
    case .success(let urls):
        guard let url = urls.first else { return }
        let didStart = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
        defer { if didStart { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }
        do {
            let data = try Data(contentsOf: url)
            let envelope = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: data)
            let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: store.state)
            pendingImportEnvelope = envelope
            pendingImportCounts = counts
        } catch let error as AppDataImport.ImportError {
            importErrorMessage = error.errorDescription
        } catch {
            importErrorMessage = "Couldn't read the export file: \(error.localizedDescription)"
        }
    }
}

private func confirmImport(props: Props) {
    guard let envelope = pendingImportEnvelope else { return }
    let counts = pendingImportCounts
    pendingImportEnvelope = nil
    pendingImportCounts = nil
    props.dispatch(AppActions.ImportAppData(envelope: envelope))
    importSuccessCounts = counts
}
```

**AppDataICloudBackup.swift** (`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataICloudBackup.swift`, Lines 1–304):

Returns: `AppDataExportEnvelope` (reuses export format)

What it does:
- `writeBackupToICloud(state:date:)` — creates/overwrites rolling backup at `<iCloudContainer>/Documents/Backups/MovieSwift-Latest.json`
- `readBackupFromICloud()` — reads and decodes latest backup
- `resolvedAvailableVersions()` — lists all versions (current + historical + unresolved conflicts)
- `readBackup(at:)` — reads from specific `NSFileVersion`
- `resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved()` — marks conflict versions as resolved after user picks one
- Uses `NSFileVersion` API for version history
- iCloud availability check: `resolvedICloudContainer()` returns nil if iCloud Drive not available

**SettingsForm.swift** (iCloud logic, Lines 223–276):

```swift
private func performICloudBackup() {
    let now = Date()
    do {
        try AppDataICloudBackup.writeBackupToICloud(state: store.state, date: now)
        lastICloudBackupDate = now
        backupSuccessDate = now  // Shows success alert
    } catch let error as AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError {
        backupErrorMessage = error.errorDescription
    } catch {
        backupErrorMessage = "Backup failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
    }
}

private func performICloudRestore() {
    do {
        let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackupFromICloud()
        let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: store.state)
        pendingImportEnvelope = envelope
        pendingImportCounts = counts
    } catch let error as AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError {
        backupErrorMessage = error.errorDescription
    } catch {
        backupErrorMessage = "Restore failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
    }
}

private func showPreviousICloudVersions() {
    availableICloudVersions = AppDataICloudBackup.resolvedAvailableVersions()
    isPreviousVersionsSheetPresented = true
}

private func restoreFromICloudVersion(_ info: AppDataICloudBackup.BackupVersionInfo) {
    do {
        let envelope = try AppDataICloudBackup.readBackup(at: info.version)
        let counts = AppDataImport.previewCounts(for: envelope, against: store.state)
        pendingImportEnvelope = envelope
        pendingImportCounts = counts
        AppDataICloudBackup.resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved()
        isPreviousVersionsSheetPresented = false
    } catch let error as AppDataICloudBackup.BackupError {
        backupErrorMessage = error.errorDescription
    } catch {
        backupErrorMessage = "Restore failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
    }
}
```

**UserDataDocument.swift** (Lines 1–30):

Thin `FileDocument` wrapper for `.fileExporter`:
```swift
struct UserDataDocument: FileDocument {
    static var readableContentTypes: [UTType] { [.json] }
    static var writableContentTypes: [UTType] { [.json] }
    let data: Data
    
    init(configuration: ReadConfiguration) throws {
        guard let raw = configuration.file.regularFileContents else {
            throw CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile)
        }
        self.data = raw
    }
    
    func fileWrapper(configuration: WriteConfiguration) throws -> FileWrapper {
        FileWrapper(regularFileWithContents: data)
    }
}
```

**Real filesystem vs. injectable:**
- Export/Import/iCloud all read/write real filesystem (no mock points)
- SettingsForm dispatches via Flux store — testable via fixture state
- fileExporter/fileImporter are system UI — **NOT directly driveable from XCUITest** (see section 5 below)

        let app = XCUIApplication()

        for (key, value) in UITestConstants.smokeTestEnvironment {

---

### 6. THE HARDEST PART: FILE PICKER SYSTEM UI TESTABILITY

**The Core Problem:**

Both `.fileExporter` and `.fileImporter` present system-level file pickers:
- **macOS:** `NSSavePanel` (export) and `NSOpenPanel` (import)
- **iOS:** UIDocumentPickerViewController (via document browser)
- **tvOS:** Limited to local file access

These are **NOT part of your app's XCUITest window** — they're presented by the OS and run in a separate process. **XCUITest cannot directly click buttons in system dialogs.**

**Current Limitations:**

1. **fileExporter:** XCUITest can tap `settings.exportDataButton` to trigger the picker, but:
   - Cannot click "Save" in NSSavePanel
   - Cannot type a filename
   - Cannot navigate to a directory
   - The `onCompletion` callback won't fire from an XCUITest

2. **fileImporter:** Same issue in reverse:
   - Cannot browse files
   - Cannot select a file
   - The `onCompletion` callback won't fire from an XCUITest

**Why This Matters for Your Tests:**

The full export/import/backup/restore journeys involve:
1. User taps button → state sets `isExportPresented = true`
2. SwiftUI presents `.fileExporter` modifier
3. **System file picker opens** ← test can't drive this
4. User clicks Save/Open in system picker
5. System calls the `onCompletion` callback with result
6. SettingsForm updates state based on result (success/error alerts)

**Possible Workarounds:**

**Option A: Mock the FileExporter/FileImporter (Requires Code Changes)**

Add an env-var-gated test injection point in SettingsForm:

```swift
@State private var filePickerOverride: (() -> Void)?  // Injected in tests

private func startExport() {
    let now = Date()
    do {
        let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: store.state, exportDate: now)
        exportDocument = UserDataDocument(data: data)
        exportSuggestedFilename = AppDataExport.suggestedFilename(for: now)
        
        #if DEBUG
        if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["UI_TEST_EXPORT_FILE"] != nil {
            // Simulate fileExporter completion with a test file
            let testFile = URL(fileURLWithPath: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["UI_TEST_EXPORT_FILE"]!)
            do {
                try data.write(to: testFile)
                handleExportResult(.success(testFile))
            } catch {
                handleExportResult(.failure(error))
            }
        } else {
            isExportPresented = true
        }
        #else
        isExportPresented = true
        #endif
    } catch {
        exportErrorMessage = "Couldn't build the export file: \(error.localizedDescription)"
    }
}
```

Then in tests:
```swift
let testExportPath = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("export-test.json")
let app = launchApp(environment: ["UI_TEST_EXPORT_FILE": testExportPath.path])
app.buttons["settings.exportDataButton"].tap()
// App writes file and calls onCompletion callback internally
await fulfillment(of: [expectation(...)], timeout: 15)
XCTAssert(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: testExportPath.path))
```

**Option B: Test the Logic, Not the Full UI Flow**

Separate concerns:

1. **Unit tests** (already exist): Export/import/backup data transformations
2. **UI tests**: Only test the non-file-picker parts:
   - Button taps
   - State transitions (alerts, success messages)
   - Export button → "Export failed" alert (simulate failure in unit tests)
   - Import button → "Import data?" confirmation (unit tests verify counts)
   - iCloud backup button → "Backed up to iCloud" alert
   - iCloud restore button → Import confirmation sheet

Example:
```swift
func testExportButtonTriggersExport() {
    let app = launchApp(selectMenu: "Settings")
    app.buttons["settings.exportDataButton"].tap()
    
    // We can't verify the file was written (system picker blocks), but we can:
    // 1. Verify the app didn't crash
    // 2. In a separate unit test, verify AppDataExport.data() works correctly
}

// Can't test this in UI tests — test in AppDataExportTests instead
// func testExportFileRoundTrip() { ... }
```

**Option C: Scripted File Placement (For Import Testing)**

For import, you CAN write files into a known location before running the test, then if the file picker can be scripted via AppleScript or automation APIs (tricky and fragile).

A more robust approach: write the import file to a location the app can access, then:
1. Tap "Import my data"
2. File picker opens — **test halts here and cannot proceed without human interaction**

**Option D: Hybrid: Test via URL Scheme or Deep Linking** (Not Applicable Here)

Some apps accept file imports via URL schemes, but MovieSwift's SettingsForm uses standard SwiftUI `.fileImporter`, not a custom URL handler.

---

### **RECOMMENDATION FOR YOUR XCUITest STRATEGY:**

**Given the system file picker constraint, here's what's testable:**

✅ **Fully testable in XCUITest:**
- Export button tap → no crash (file picker launches)
- Import button tap → no crash
- Backup to iCloud button tap → success/error alert
- Restore from iCloud button tap → success/error alert (if backup exists)
- Show previous backups button tap → sheet presents
- Previous backups sheet: list rendering, restore button tap → import confirmation alert
- Import confirmation alert: tap "Import" button → success alert
- Import confirmation alert: tap "Cancel" button → alert dismisses
- All success/error alerts: tap "OK" button → alert dismisses
- Clear cached data: confirmation dialog → confirm → button re-tappable

❌ **NOT testable in XCUITest (system file picker):**
- Actually saving a file via fileExporter
- Actually selecting a file via fileImporter
- End-to-end export→import roundtrip via file picker

✅ **Testable in Unit Tests (already exist or should add):**
- Export data transformation and JSON encoding
- Import envelope decode and merge logic
- iCloud backup write/read
- iCloud version history (NSFileVersion API)
- Export→Import roundtrip (without UI)
- Conflict resolution logic

**File Picker Testing Options:**

1. **Mock injection (recommended):** Add UI_TEST mode that bypasses fileExporter/fileImporter and simulates file operations in-process
2. **Separate integration test suite:** Non-XCUITest file-based tests that don't rely on the file picker
3. **Manual test checklist:** Document the export/import/picker flows as manual test procedures (for human QA)

> AGENT

The macOS app **is sandboxed** (`com.apple.security.app-sandbox`), with only user-selected (picker-granted) file access — so a seam writing to an arbitrary temp path would be blocked, and the test process can't read the app's container anyway. That rules out cross-process file verification.

**Refined scope for this PR:** the **import journey**, driven fully in-process and sandbox-safe — the seam self-seeds a deterministic export file into the app's *own* container temp dir, then feeds it through the real decode→preview→confirm→merge path, and the test verifies the merge actually happened by finding the imported list in My Lists. This is the most valuable slice (it's the destructive merge path) and gives a strong value-asserting test. Export and iCloud become follow-ups (export needs an in-process round-trip signal; iCloud needs its own injectable store).

## Code review — test/settings-data-management-ui

All three files are uncommitted (no commits on this branch ahead of main). The diff is pure working-tree changes; the review scope is those changes.

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:168`** — `Data.write(to:)` is called without `.atomic` write option.

The seam writes the fixture JSON as `try data.write(to: url)`. `Data.write(to:)` without options is not atomic: if the host process crashes mid-write (e.g. watchdog kill during a slow CI run) the file is left in a partial state and the next test launch picks up garbage, decodes a `decodeFailed` error, shows the error alert, and the `confirmButton` never appears — making the test fail with a mysterious timeout rather than a useful message. `AppPersistence` has the same pattern (line 82), which the project already tolerates, but there the file is in the app's Documents container and gets regenerated on next save. Here the file is shared state across test retries.

Fix: `try data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)`. One extra flag; zero API churn.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:168`** — `NSTemporaryDirectory()` returns the process's own temp directory on a sandboxed macOS app, so it is inside the sandbox container, which is correct. However the synthesised URL is a plain file-system URL. When `handleImportSelection` receives it at line 193 it calls `url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()`, which returns `false` for a non-security-scoped URL and the `defer` correctly skips the matching stop. This is safe as-is, but leaves a subtle implicit dependency on that guard and is easy to misread as "the seam breaks sandbox access." A one-line comment in `seedAndImportUITestFixture` adjacent to the `handleImportSelection(.success([url]))` call would clarify: "// Plain temp URL — not security-scoped; startAccessingSecurityScopedResource returns false, which handleImportSelection already guards against." That prevents the next reader from adding a spurious `startAccessing` call thinking the existing one is unreachable.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/state/AppStateFixtures.swift:119-122`** — `cover: 0` passes an `Int` literal to `cover: Int?`. This compiles (Swift coerces `0` to `Optional(0)`), so movie id 0 is included in `AppStateCacheReset.preservedMovieIds`, meaning the movie is preserved through the export's `persistentSnapshot` pass and the resulting import file is structurally valid. There is no correctness bug, but other fixture construction sites (`sampleCustomList` at line 7 and `smokeTestList` at line 53) also use `cover: 0` for the same reason — this is an established pattern in the file. The only nit is that the convention makes it look like the cover is required, while the model documents `cover: Int? = nil` as "no cover selected." Since the test asserts on the list name and id rather than cover rendering, this is fine as written, but if a future reader changes the model to `cover: Int` it silently breaks the "no cover" semantics. Worth `cover: nil` for the newly-added fixture at line 121 to be explicit that the test list intentionally has no cover image — but given the existing pattern this is a very low-priority nit (see Nits tier below).

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:730`** — `customListsSegment.tap()` is not guarded by `waitForExistence` with a failure message.

The test already correctly calls `XCTAssertTrue(customListsSegment.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout))` at line 730, but then calls `.tap()` on `customListsSegment` (line 731) rather than on the element after the wait. This is fine — `customListsSegment` is the same element, the wait was the guard — but the pair `waitForExistence` + bare `tap()` on the same variable is the project's existing idiom and the test follows it correctly. No issue here; I called this out to verify it before dismissing.

Actually reviewing the lines again:

```swift
let customListsSegment = app.identifiedElement("myLists.section.Custom Lists")
XCTAssertTrue(customListsSegment.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout))
customListsSegment.tap()
```

This is correct: wait → tap is the right pattern and matches every other test in the file.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:708`** — Test is `func` (sync), but navigating My Lists after a successful import requires the sidebar tap to propagate a state change that might need a runloop beat. All other tests with cross-pane navigation either use `waitForExistence` (which this test does, correctly) or are `async`. The `waitForExistence(timeout: timeout)` at line 734 is a 15-second wait so any propagation lag is covered. No issue; noting for completeness.

---

**Missing unit test for `makeUITestImportFixtureState`** — The project guideline is "every behaviour change ships with a test." `makeUITestImportFixtureState` is a new exported public function in the package (`AppStateFixtures.swift`). The function is tested indirectly through the UI test, but no unit test exists that asserts: (a) the returned state differs from `makeUISmokeTestState()` by exactly one custom list, (b) that list has id 99 and name "Imported List", and (c) `AppDataExport.data(from:)` round-trips through `AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope` without error. A unit test in `AppDataImportTests.swift` or a new `AppStateFixturesTests.swift` satisfies the TDD requirement cheaply and would catch regressions to the fixture without needing to run the full UI-test suite.

This is the answer to "what's next" — and it's already in flight. PR [#31](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/31) is up and CI is running (I'll merge once the required suites are green).

## What I built
The first end-to-end UI test for the **Settings import journey** — the most data-destructive surface in the app, which had zero UI coverage on any platform.

The crux was that `.fileImporter` is a system panel XCUITest can't drive, and the macOS app is sandboxed (so no cross-process file verification). The solution: a DEBUG-only seam that self-seeds a deterministic export file into the app's own container and runs it through the **real** decode→preview→confirm→merge path. The test then asserts the merge *actually happened* by finding the imported list in My Lists — a value-asserting test, not existence-only (which also chips at another Phase 2 goal).

## The new workflow proved itself
This was the first run through the **verify-then-review** flow with the new `verifier` subagent:
- **Verifier (step 4)** ran lint + package-tests + iOS/tvOS builds + the unit suite + Settings macOS tests, returned PASS — catching nothing broken, exactly as intended for a clean change.
- **Code-reviewer (step 5)** returned FIX-FIRST with two legitimate catches: a non-atomic write that would cause silent CI flakes on retry, and a missing unit test for the new fixture (TDD policy). Fixed both, re-verified green.

So the verifier gate handled the mechanical correctness and freed the reviewer to focus on reliability/policy — the division of labor you designed.

## Scope I deliberately deferred
Export and iCloud backup/restore are follow-up PRs (one logical unit each): under the sandbox, **export** needs an in-process round-trip signal and **iCloud** needs its own injectable store to be CI-deterministic. Bundling them would've made this PR flaky and oversized.

Once #31 merges, the natural next steps are those two follow-ups to complete the data-management triad, then the remaining Phase 2 items (Fan Club, platform parity, PeopleActions failures). I'll merge #31 when CI comes back green.

  "new_string": "            let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: store.state, exportDate: now)\n            exportDocument = UserDataDocument(data: data)\n            exportSuggestedFilename = AppDataExport.suggestedFilename(for: now)\n            #if DEBUG\n            if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[\"UI_TEST_EXPORT_VERIFY\"] == \"1\" {\n                verifyExportRoundTripForUITest(data: data)\n                return\n            }\n            #endif\n            isExportPresented = true\n        } catch {\n            exportErrorMessage = \"Couldn't build the export file: \\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    #if DEBUG\n    // UI-test seam: `.fileExporter` presents a system save panel XCUITest\n    // can't operate, so instead write the produced file into the app's own\n    // sandbox container, read it back, and surface the round-tripped custom\n    // list names. The test asserts the export captured real user data (the\n    // seeded \"TestName\" list) rather than just that the button didn't crash.\n    private func verifyExportRoundTripForUITest(data: Data) {\n        exportDocument = nil\n        let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory())\n            .appendingPathComponent(\"uitest-export.json\")\n        do {\n            try data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)\n            let reread = try Data(contentsOf: url)\n            let envelope = try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: reread)\n            let names = envelope.snapshot.moviesState.customLists.values\n                .map(\\.name).sorted().joined(separator: \"|\")\n            uiTestExportVerification = \"lists=\\(envelope.snapshot.moviesState.customLists.count);names=\\(names)\"\n        } catch {\n            uiTestExportVerification = \"error=\\(error.localizedDescription)\"\n        }\n    }\n    #endif"
}

## Code review — test/settings-export-ui

### Correctness and production-safety assessment

The seam design is sound. Every new line touching production behaviour is behind `#if DEBUG`, and the three guarding conditions all nest correctly: the `@State` property, `verifyExportRoundTripForUITest`, and the `exportVerifyProbe` are each individually `#if DEBUG`-fenced. The `isExportPresented = true` call (which drives the `.fileExporter` sheet) is only reached when the env-var branch is not taken, so the system save panel is unaffected in release builds. The seam also correctly mirrors the established pattern from `seedAndImportUITestFixture` in the same file.

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, missing tests, CI-blocking lint)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:135-142` — `exportDocument` is set to a `UserDataDocument(data: data)` allocation at line 135, and then immediately cleared to `nil` inside `verifyExportRoundTripForUITest` at line 156 when the seam fires. The `.fileExporter` modifier at line 1308 is bound to `$isExportPresented`, not to `exportDocument` directly, so no sheet appears — but the short-lived `UserDataDocument` allocation is wasted work that is also slightly misleading: `exportDocument` carries a non-nil value at the moment the seam's function call begins, which implies a document is "ready" when in fact the seam path never consumes it. The fix is to move the `exportDocument` and `suggestedFilename` assignments below the seam check (or inside an `else` branch), exactly as the import seam skips its panel setup entirely:

```swift
private func startExport() {
    let now = Date()
    do {
        let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: store.state, exportDate: now)
        #if DEBUG
        if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["UI_TEST_EXPORT_VERIFY"] == "1" {
            verifyExportRoundTripForUITest(data: data)
            return
        }
        #endif
        exportDocument = UserDataDocument(data: data)
        exportSuggestedFilename = AppDataExport.suggestedFilename(for: now)
        isExportPresented = true
    } catch { ... }
}
```

This also makes `verifyExportRoundTripForUITest`'s first line (`exportDocument = nil`) unnecessary, removing a ghost-write.

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:762-764` — The test accepts the result string in either `label` or `value` without documenting which the platform actually uses. On macOS a static `Text` with `.accessibilityIdentifier` does surface its content as the element's `label`, not `value`. The `value` fallback looks defensive but will silently pass even if both are empty strings (they'd both be empty and neither would contain "TestName", so the assertion would actually fail — that's fine, but the comment says "accept either" as though it's an intentional hedge, which could mislead a future reader into thinking `value` is a real observed alternative). Consider asserting `label` directly and adding a one-line comment explaining why: `// macOS Text with .accessibilityIdentifier surfaces its content as label, not value`. This makes the intent precise and removes the dead fallback.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:732-733` — The `exportVerifyProbe` renders inside `appDataSection` (macOS-only path), but the `@State private var uiTestExportVerification` and the seam logic in `startExport()` are compiled into all platforms (iOS, tvOS) that share `SettingsForm.swift` under `#if DEBUG`. The env-var check in `startExport()` would trigger on those platforms too if someone passes `UI_TEST_EXPORT_VERIFY=1` to an iOS simulator test session, but the result would never appear (since `iOSFormContent` doesn't include `exportVerifyProbe`). This is a non-shipping concern, but it diverges from the import seam, which is also in a shared function and similarly would silently do nothing visible on iOS — so consistency is preserved. Still worth a brief inline comment acknowledging the probe is only wired into the macOS layout path.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:747` — `testSettingsExportCapturesUserData` is declared as a synchronous `func`, while several comparable tests in the same file (`testSettingsClearCachedDataConfirmsAndReturnsToSettings`, `testDiscoverDismissCanBeUndone`, etc.) that also wait on UI state are `async` and use `await fulfillment(of:)`. The export test uses `waitForExistence(timeout:)` which is fine for XCTest synchronous polling, but is inconsistent with the file's stated pattern and wouldn't catch a race where the probe appears and disappears before the assertion fires. Declaring the test `async` and using `await fulfillment(of:)` on a predicate checking `result.exists` would be more robust and consistent with the test file's conventions.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:10` — The `exportVerifyProbe` inserts a plain `Text` directly into the `sectionCard` inner `VStack(spacing: 0)` between `exportDataRow` and the `rowDivider`. When the probe becomes visible it will render flush against the export button's bottom edge with no horizontal padding, as it lacks the `.padding(.horizontal, 14).padding(.vertical, 12)` present on every other row. Since it's only visible in DEBUG under a specific env-var it won't affect real users, but if you ever run the app in DEBUG without the test env-var it can render (if `uiTestExportVerification` were ever set outside the test path). A `hiddenSeamRow` wrapper with matching padding, or an explicit `.hidden()` modifier in all non-test DEBUG runs, would prevent any accidental layout impact.

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:165` — The probe string format `"lists=\(count);names=\(names)"` is decoded in the test only via substring `contains("TestName")`. The `lists=` count field is produced but never asserted. Either assert `label.contains("lists=1")` in the test (making the count meaningful) or drop it from the probe string to keep the contract minimal and self-documenting.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/settings/SettingsForm.swift:157-158` — `URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory()).appendingPathComponent("uitest-export.json")` is the same construction pattern as the import seam's `"uitest-import.json"`. Neither cleans up after itself. These files persist in the simulator's temp directory across test runs, which is harmless since `.atomic` overwrite semantics cover subsequent runs — but worth noting they match the already-accepted pattern from the import seam, so no change is needed.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:740-742` — The doc comment says "companion to the import test" and describes the seam rationale clearly. The one missing statement: say explicitly that `AppDataExportTests` already covers export correctness at the unit level and that this test's scope is button→produces-valid-user-data wiring only. The context description says this, but it isn't in the in-source doc comment for future readers.

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the `exportDocument` ghost-allocation before the seam check is a correctness nit that also leaves `verifyExportRoundTripForUITest`'s first line (`exportDocument = nil`) as dead cleanup. Fix the ordering in `startExport()` before pushing; the rest can land with the commit or as follow-ups.

1	//  Reads and writes a single rolling backup of the user's data to
2	//  iCloud Drive. Reuses AppDataExport's envelope format so a backup
3	//  is just an export saved to a known iCloud path; restore reuses
4	//  AppDataImport's merge semantics. The file lives at
5	//
6	//      <iCloudContainer>/Documents/Backups/MovieSwift-Latest.json
7	//
8	//  so it shows up under the user's iCloud Drive in Files.app and is
9	//  automatically synced across devices that share the iCloud account.
10	
11	import Foundation
12	import MovieSwiftFluxCore
13	
14	// `nonisolated`: pure iCloud-backup file I/O (like AppPersistence),
15	// invoked from the main-actor Settings UI and from nonisolated unit tests.
16	// It must opt out of the app target's default-MainActor isolation.
17	nonisolated enum AppDataICloudBackup {
18	
19	    /// Errors surfaced by Backup/Restore operations.
20	    enum BackupError: LocalizedError {
21	        case iCloudUnavailable
22	        case noBackupExists
23	        case writeFailed(underlying: Error)
24	        case readFailed(underlying: Error)
25	
26	        var errorDescription: String? {
27	            switch self {
28	            case .iCloudUnavailable:
29	                return String(localized: "iCloud Drive is not available. Sign in to iCloud in System Settings and enable iCloud Drive for MovieSwift.",
30	                              comment: "Error shown when the user taps Back up to iCloud or Restore from iCloud but iCloud Drive isn't set up.")
31	            case .noBackupExists:
32	                return String(localized: "No iCloud backup exists yet. Tap Back up to iCloud first.",
33	                              comment: "Error shown when the user taps Restore from iCloud before any backup has been made.")
34	            case .writeFailed(let error):
35	                return String(localized: "Couldn't write the backup: \(error.localizedDescription)",
36	                              comment: "Error shown when the iCloud Drive write of a backup file fails. The interpolated value is the underlying system error.")
37	            case .readFailed(let error):
38	                return String(localized: "Couldn't read the backup: \(error.localizedDescription)",
39	                              comment: "Error shown when the iCloud Drive read of a backup file fails. The interpolated value is the underlying system error.")
40	            }
41	        }
42	    }
43	
44	    /// Filename of the rolling backup. A single file is overwritten
45	    /// on each Back up — the goal is "latest known good", not a
46	    /// versioned history.
47	    static let backupFilename = "MovieSwift-Latest.json"
48	
49	    // MARK: - URL helpers (testable; take an explicit container)
50	
51	    /// Directory inside the given iCloud container where backups live.
52	    /// `Documents/` is the conventional public-facing slot — files
53	    /// there appear in the user's iCloud Drive in Files.app.
54	    static func backupDirectory(in container: URL) -> URL {
55	        container
56	            .appendingPathComponent("Documents", isDirectory: true)
57	            .appendingPathComponent("Backups", isDirectory: true)
58	    }
59	
60	    /// Path of the rolling backup file inside the given container.
61	    static func backupFileURL(in container: URL) -> URL {
62	        backupDirectory(in: container).appendingPathComponent(backupFilename)
63	    }
64	
65	    // MARK: - URL helpers (production; resolve real iCloud)
66	
67	    /// Resolved iCloud container URL, or nil when iCloud Drive isn't
68	    /// available (no signed-in iCloud account, the user disabled
69	    /// iCloud Drive for the app, or the container isn't provisioned).
70	    static func resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {
71	        fileManager.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier: nil)
72	    }
73	
74	    /// Production helper that resolves the iCloud container then
75	    /// returns the rolling backup URL inside it. Returns nil when
76	    /// iCloud is unavailable.
77	    static func resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {
78	        resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: fileManager).map(backupFileURL(in:))
79	    }
80	
81	    /// Whether iCloud Drive can be used for backup right now.
82	    static func isICloudAvailable(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Bool {
83	        resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: fileManager) != nil
84	    }
85	
86	    // MARK: - Reading the last-backup date
87	
88	    /// Modification date of the backup file at `fileURL`, or nil when
89	    /// the file isn't present.
90	    static func lastBackupDate(at fileURL: URL,
91	                               fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Date? {
92	        guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path),
93	              let attrs = try? fileManager.attributesOfItem(atPath: fileURL.path),
94	              let modDate = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date else {
95	            return nil
96	        }
97	        return modDate
98	    }
99	
100	    /// Production convenience: returns the iCloud backup's last-modified
101	    /// date, or nil when iCloud is unavailable or no backup exists.
102	    static func resolvedLastBackupDate(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> Date? {
103	        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {
104	            return nil
105	        }
106	        return lastBackupDate(at: url, fileManager: fileManager)
107	    }
108	
109	    // MARK: - Write
110	
111	    /// Writes the export envelope of `state` to `fileURL`. Creates
112	    /// any missing intermediate directories. Re-throws decode/IO
113	    /// failures wrapped in `BackupError.writeFailed`.
114	    static func writeBackup(state: AppState,
115	                            to fileURL: URL,
116	                            date: Date = Date(),
117	                            fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws {
118	        do {
119	            let directory = fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent()
120	            try fileManager.createDirectory(at: directory,
121	                                            withIntermediateDirectories: true)
122	            let envelope = AppDataExport.envelope(from: state, exportDate: date)
123	            let data = try AppDataExport.data(from: envelope)
124	            try data.write(to: fileURL, options: [.atomic])
125	        } catch {
126	            throw BackupError.writeFailed(underlying: error)
127	        }
128	    }
129	
130	    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and
131	    /// writes there. Throws `iCloudUnavailable` if there's no
132	    /// container.
133	    static func writeBackupToICloud(state: AppState,
134	                                    date: Date = Date(),
135	                                    fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws {
136	        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {
137	            throw BackupError.iCloudUnavailable
138	        }
139	        try writeBackup(state: state, to: url, date: date, fileManager: fileManager)
140	    }
141	
142	    // MARK: - Read
143	
144	    /// Reads and decodes the backup envelope at `fileURL`. Throws
145	    /// `noBackupExists` if the file isn't present, or a wrapped
146	    /// `readFailed` for any other failure.
147	    static func readBackup(from fileURL: URL,
148	                           fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {
149	        guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else {
150	            throw BackupError.noBackupExists
151	        }
152	        // If the file is in iCloud and not yet downloaded, ask iCloud
153	        // to start downloading it. `Data(contentsOf:)` then waits on
154	        // the materialized file. On a non-iCloud URL this is a no-op.
155	        try? fileManager.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at: fileURL)
156	        do {
157	            let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)
158	            return try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: data)
159	        } catch let error as AppDataImport.ImportError {
160	            // Decode-side errors carry their own user-facing message;
161	            // forward them as readFailed so the caller surfaces a
162	            // single error type.
163	            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)
164	        } catch {
165	            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)
166	        }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and
170	    /// reads from there. Throws `iCloudUnavailable` if there's no
171	    /// container.
172	    static func readBackupFromICloud(fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {
173	        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {
174	            throw BackupError.iCloudUnavailable
175	        }
176	        return try readBackup(from: url, fileManager: fileManager)
177	    }

179	    // MARK: - Previous-version handling
180	    //
181	    // iCloud Drive automatically retains version history for every
182	    // file in a CloudKit-backed container. NSFileVersion wraps that
183	    // history so the user can restore a backup from before today's
184	    // overwrite — e.g. they accidentally Cleared all their data,
185	    // then Backed up the empty state, and want to recover yesterday's
186	    // backup. Conflict versions (created when two devices back up
187	    // simultaneously) live in the same list and need explicit
188	    // resolution after the user picks a winner.
189	
190	    /// User-facing description of one available backup version.
191	    /// Wraps the underlying `NSFileVersion` so the caller can
192	    /// invoke `readBackup(at:)` / `restoreVersion(_:to:)` without
193	    /// re-querying the version list.
194	    struct BackupVersionInfo: Identifiable {
195	        /// Stable id for SwiftUI ForEach. The version's URL path is
196	        /// unique across the version list and stays valid for the
197	        /// version's lifetime.
198	        let id: String
199	        let modificationDate: Date
200	        /// Name of the device that wrote this version, when iCloud
201	        /// has it. Used to disambiguate conflict versions ("Backup
202	        /// from Scott's MacBook" vs "Backup from Scott's iPhone").
203	        let computerName: String?
204	        /// True for the current "winning" version that
205	        /// `readBackupFromICloud` would otherwise return.
206	        let isCurrent: Bool
207	        /// True when this version is part of an unresolved conflict
208	        /// (two devices wrote at the same time). Picking it for
209	        /// restore should also mark all other unresolved versions
210	        /// as resolved so iCloud stops surfacing the conflict.
211	        let isUnresolvedConflict: Bool
212	        /// The underlying NSFileVersion. Held strongly so the URL
213	        /// stays valid until the caller is done with it.
214	        let version: NSFileVersion
215	    }
216	
217	    /// Lists every version of the backup file at `fileURL` — the
218	    /// current one plus historical and conflict versions — sorted
219	    /// newest-first. Returns `[]` if the file doesn't exist yet.
220	    static func availableVersions(at fileURL: URL,
221	                                  fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [BackupVersionInfo] {
222	        guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else {
223	            return []
224	        }
225	        var infos: [BackupVersionInfo] = []
226	        if let current = NSFileVersion.currentVersionOfItem(at: fileURL) {
227	            infos.append(makeInfo(from: current,
228	                                  isCurrent: true,
229	                                  isUnresolvedConflict: false))
230	        }
231	        let unresolved = Set((NSFileVersion.unresolvedConflictVersionsOfItem(at: fileURL) ?? [])
232	            .compactMap { $0.url.path })
233	        for version in NSFileVersion.otherVersionsOfItem(at: fileURL) ?? [] {
234	            infos.append(makeInfo(from: version,
235	                                  isCurrent: false,
236	                                  isUnresolvedConflict: unresolved.contains(version.url.path)))
237	        }
238	        return infos.sorted { $0.modificationDate > $1.modificationDate }
239	    }

241	    /// Production convenience: resolves the iCloud container and
242	    /// lists versions there. Returns `[]` if iCloud is unavailable
243	    /// or no backup exists yet.
244	    static func resolvedAvailableVersions(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> [BackupVersionInfo] {
245	        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {
246	            return []
247	        }
248	        return availableVersions(at: url, fileManager: fileManager)
249	    }

251	    /// Reads and decodes the backup envelope from a specific version
252	    /// (rather than always reading the current one). Useful when the
253	    /// user picks a previous backup from `availableVersions(at:)`.
254	    static func readBackup(at version: NSFileVersion,
255	                           fileManager: FileManager = .default) throws -> AppDataExportEnvelope {
256	        // Same iCloud-download nudge as readBackup(from:).
257	        try? fileManager.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at: version.url)
258	        do {
259	            let data = try Data(contentsOf: version.url)
260	            return try AppDataImport.decodeEnvelope(from: data)
261	        } catch let error as AppDataImport.ImportError {
262	            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)
263	        } catch {
264	            throw BackupError.readFailed(underlying: error)
265	        }
266	    }
267	
268	    /// Marks any unresolved conflict versions at `fileURL` as
269	    /// resolved. Call after the user has picked which version to
270	    /// restore from — without this iCloud keeps surfacing the
271	    /// conflict on every subsequent read.
272	    static func markAllConflictsResolved(at fileURL: URL) {
273	        guard let unresolved = NSFileVersion.unresolvedConflictVersionsOfItem(at: fileURL) else {
274	            return
275	        }
276	        for version in unresolved {
277	            version.isResolved = true
278	        }
279	    }
280	
281	    /// Production convenience: marks conflicts on the resolved
282	    /// iCloud backup file.
283	    static func resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved(fileManager: FileManager = .default) {
284	        guard let url = resolvedBackupFileURL(fileManager: fileManager) else {
285	            return
286	        }
287	        markAllConflictsResolved(at: url)
288	    }

290	    /// Builds a `BackupVersionInfo` from an `NSFileVersion`.
291	    private static func makeInfo(from version: NSFileVersion,
292	                                 isCurrent: Bool,
293	                                 isUnresolvedConflict: Bool) -> BackupVersionInfo {
294	        BackupVersionInfo(
295	            id: version.url.absoluteString,
296	            modificationDate: version.modificationDate ?? .distantPast,
297	            computerName: version.localizedNameOfSavingComputer,
298	            isCurrent: isCurrent,
299	            isUnresolvedConflict: isUnresolvedConflict,
300	            version: version
301	        )
302	    }

> AGENT

This is cleaner than I feared. The whole iCloud surface funnels through one chokepoint — `resolvedICloudContainer` — and the underlying read/write/version logic already takes an explicit container URL (that's how the unit tests exercise it). So I only need to override that one method in DEBUG to point at a real local directory in the app's sandbox container. That makes **every** iCloud journey (backup, restore-latest, previous-versions) run against real files — even `NSFileVersion` works on local files — with no protocol refactor and no faking.

Let me add the seam:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_019ZNuqCenFdfR3BUA3UUmtX
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppDataICloudBackup.swift",
  "old_string": "    static func resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {\n        fileManager.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier: nil)\n    }",
  "new_string": "    static func resolvedICloudContainer(fileManager: FileManager = .default) -> URL? {\n        #if DEBUG\n        // UI-test seam: real iCloud Drive isn't available in headless CI, so\n        // when the harness sets `UI_TEST_ICLOUD_FAKE` redirect the container to\n        // a real local directory inside the app's own sandbox container. The\n        // genuine write/read/version/last-date logic then runs end-to-end\n        // against real files (NSFileVersion works on local files too) without\n        // touching iCloud. No effect in production — the env var is never set.\n        if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[\"UI_TEST_ICLOUD_FAKE\"] == \"1\" {\n            let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory(), isDirectory: true)\n                .appendingPathComponent(\"uitest-icloud-container\", isDirectory: true)\n            try? fileManager.createDirectory(at: url, withIntermediateDirectories: true)\n            return url\n        }\n        #endif\n        return fileManager.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier: nil)\n    }"
}

## Code review — test/settings-icloud-ui

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, missing tests, CI-blocking lint)

**`AppDataICloudBackup.swift:39` (SettingsForm.swift) — `lastICloudBackupDate` initialised before the seam is active**

`@State private var lastICloudBackupDate: Date? = AppDataICloudBackup.resolvedLastBackupDate()` is evaluated at view-init time. In the test run the env var `UI_TEST_ICLOUD_FAKE=1` is set on the `XCUIApplication.launchEnvironment`, which means it is present in the *app process* from the moment the process starts. `resolvedLastBackupDate()` chains through `resolvedICloudContainer()`, so on a clean CI machine the seam fires correctly here too — the container URL is the fake local path, the file won't yet exist, and `lastICloudBackupDate` is correctly `nil`. This path is actually safe. No fix needed on correctness grounds — noted for clarity below as a should-fix documentation gap.

**`AppDataICloudBackup.swift:79-82` — `NSTemporaryDirectory()` shared between test *runs* without cleanup**

`NSTemporaryDirectory()` on macOS returns the same per-user temp directory every time. The fake container `uitest-icloud-container/Documents/Backups/MovieSwift-Latest.json` is never cleaned up between test runs (there is no `tearDown`, and the test target has no mechanism to wipe it). Concretely:

- `testSettingsRestoreFromICloudPreviewsAndCompletes` taps "Back up" first and then immediately taps "Restore". Because the fake container persists from a previous run, there may already be a stale backup file. The test reads that old file, not the one it just wrote. If the previously written state contained data that round-trips differently (e.g. a different app version or fixture), the restore succeeds but the `importSuccessCounts` step exercises a different code path from what the test intends.
- More concretely: if the test is run twice in succession in the same simulator session, the second run finds the backup from run 1 already present. The `restoreFromICloudButton` is therefore already enabled before "Back up" is even tapped, meaning the test exercises a pre-existing backup rather than the one it created. This violates determinism.
- `testSettingsShowPreviousICloudBackupsListsAVersion` has the same exposure.

`testSettingsBackupToICloudShowsSuccess` is the only test that is truly idempotent here (overwriting the backup is fine since only the success alert is asserted).

Suggested fix: add a per-test teardown step in each test that removes the fake container, or — better — use a unique subdirectory per run derived from a UUID, analogous to how `AppDataICloudBackupTests` uses `UUID()` to isolate unit-test containers. Since the fake path is baked into `AppDataICloudBackup.swift`, the cleanest approach is to have the env var carry the path itself (e.g. `UI_TEST_ICLOUD_FAKE=/path/to/per-run-dir`) rather than a hard-coded name, and generate a fresh UUID-suffixed path in `launchApp(...)`. That eliminates cross-run pollution without adding any teardown obligation to the test.

Alternatively, a `tearDown` in the test class that removes `NSTemporaryDirectory()/uitest-icloud-container` solves the immediate determinism problem at the cost of coupling the test to the seam's internal path — acceptable but fragile.

**`MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:807-810` — `restoreButton` not verified to be enabled before tapping**

```swift
let restoreButton = app.identifiedButton("settings.restoreFromICloudButton")
XCTAssertTrue(restoreButton.waitForExistence(timeout: timeout))
restoreButton.tap()
```

`restoreFromICloudRow` is `.disabled(!hasBackup)` when `lastICloudBackupDate == nil`. If the stale-state problem above means the button exists but is disabled, `tap()` on a disabled button on macOS silently does nothing — the test then waits `timeout` seconds for `confirmButton` and fails with a confusing timeout message rather than a clear "button was disabled" assertion. Add `XCTAssertTrue(restoreButton.isEnabled, "Restore button should be enabled after backup")` before the tap.

---

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:797-819` — restore test exercises a 0-change merge with no meaningful state assertion**

As acknowledged in the PR description, restoring a just-made backup of the current state is always a 0-change merge. The test confirms the UI path (confirm dialog → success alert) runs, which is valuable. However, it does not assert that the merge *actually applied* (e.g. a secondary query confirming the library is intact, or checking `importSuccessCounts`). Because the merge is always empty, even a broken restore that short-circuits after the confirm and never calls the dispatcher would produce the same success-alert outcome — the test cannot distinguish "restore completed" from "restore path went through but silently no-oped". Consider seeding a known backup (analogous to `UI_TEST_IMPORT_SEED`) and asserting a resulting state change, or at minimum note in the doc comment that this test intentionally covers only the UI path, not state correctness (which is already covered by unit tests).

**`AppDataICloudBackup.swift:73-83` — seam comment does not mention `NSTemporaryDirectory()` sharing risk**

The comment says "No effect in production — the env var is never set." It would be more complete to note that the directory is not cleaned between runs and callers should be aware of stale-state, or that cleanup is the test's responsibility. This helps the next author avoid the determinism trap.

**`MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:841-845` — `BEGINSWITH` predicate against a URL-derived identifier could be clarified**

```swift
let restoreRow = app.descendants(matching: .any)
    .matching(NSPredicate(format: "identifier BEGINSWITH %@", "previousBackupsSheet.restore."))
    .firstMatch
```

The suffix after `"previousBackupsSheet.restore."` is `version.url.absoluteString` — on local files this is a `file://` URL string containing slashes (`file:///private/var/folders/.../uitest-icloud-container/Documents/Backups/MovieSwift-Latest.json`). That is a perfectly legal accessibility identifier string, and `BEGINSWITH` finds it correctly. The concern is readability: anyone reading the predicate and the view code together will need to trace back through `makeInfo(from:) → id: version.url.absoluteString` to understand why the suffix is unpredictable. A one-line comment like `// suffix is version.url.absoluteString — unpredictable, so BEGINSWITH rather than exact match` next to the predicate would make this self-documenting.

**`SettingsForm.swift:1366-1370` — new `accessibilityIdentifier` placement is correct but previously the error-alert button lacked one**

The backup *error* alert at line 1373-1382 has no `accessibilityIdentifier` on its OK button. The success path now has `settings.backup.successOkButton`, but if a future test needs to assert the error path (e.g. to verify `iCloudUnavailable` is surfaced correctly), it has no stable tap target. Not a blocking issue for this diff, but worth adding `settings.backup.errorOkButton` while the pattern is fresh.

**TDD red-green concern — dev machine bypass is sound but should be documented at the test level**

The PR description explains correctly why RED can't be demonstrated locally: on a dev machine signed into iCloud, the backup test passes via real iCloud even without the seam. The reasoning is sound — CI headless runners have no iCloud account, so the seam is genuinely necessary for CI determinism. The missing piece is that this reasoning lives only in the PR description. A comment in the test class or its MARK section (e.g. "NOTE: on a dev machine signed into iCloud, these tests pass without the seam via the real iCloud container. The seam is required for CI determinism where no iCloud account is present.") would preserve this for reviewers who look at the test file months from now without the PR context.

---

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

- `AppDataICloudBackup.swift:81` — `try? fileManager.createDirectory(...)` silently swallows the error. A failure here would cause `resolvedICloudContainer` to return a URL that doesn't exist on disk, and every subsequent write to it would fail. The error is surfaced eventually by `writeBackup`'s `writeFailed` path, so production is safe, but in the test this would produce a confusing "Couldn't write the backup" error rather than a clear setup-failure message. This mirrors the existing pattern in `AppDataICloudBackupTests.init()` (which also uses `try?`), so it's consistent — just worth noting.

- `MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:840-850` — the `testSettingsShowPreviousICloudBackupsListsAVersion` test taps Close but does not assert that the sheet actually dismisses. Tap + timeout on `closeButton` passes trivially even if Close did nothing. A brief `XCTAssertFalse(restoreRow.waitForExistence(timeout: 2), "Previous backups sheet should have dismissed")` after the close tap would close that gap.

- `AppDataICloudBackup.swift:73` — the inline comment says `UI_TEST_ICLOUD_FAKE` but the guard checks `== "1"`. The comment could say `UI_TEST_ICLOUD_FAKE=1` (matching the value) to be consistent with how the other seam comments are written throughout `SettingsForm.swift`.

---

### On the seam design question (single-chokepoint vs env-var branches)

The choice to redirect `resolvedICloudContainer` rather than branch at the call-site in `SettingsForm` is the right call. The import/export seams branch at call-sites because those operations interact with system panels (`fileImporter`/`fileExporter`) that XCUITest can't drive — the seam's job is to replace the system UI. Here there is no system UI to replace; the issue is purely that `url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier:)` returns `nil` in CI. Intercepting at the single source of that URL means every callee (`writeBackupToICloud`, `readBackupFromICloud`, `resolvedAvailableVersions`, `resolvedLastBackupDate`, `resolvedMarkAllConflictsResolved`) is automatically covered with no per-call-site branching, and the genuine I/O logic runs unchanged. This is a cleaner and less error-prone design than the import/export approach applied here would be.

The unit tests in `AppDataICloudBackupTests` are correctly unaffected: they never call `resolvedICloudContainer` — they pass explicit `fileURL` arguments to the pure helpers (`writeBackup(state:to:)`, `readBackup(from:)`, etc.) — so the `#if DEBUG` branch is never reachable from the unit-test process regardless of env vars. The claim that "the seam is inert for explicit-URL unit tests" is accurate.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the stale fake-container across repeated runs is a real determinism defect (the restore and previous-backups tests can silently exercise a prior run's backup file), and the missing `isEnabled` assertion before the restore tap will produce confusing timeouts rather than actionable failures. Both are straightforward to fix before pushing.
