Memory recorded. Now I wait for the CI watcher on [PR #48](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/48) to report.

**Status:** The CI failure is fixed. I traced it to a genuinely subtle root cause and validated the fix on-device:

- **What failed:** 3 macOS Discover "undo" UI tests (iOS/iPad/tvOS were green).
- **Root cause:** Undo eligibility was tracked in view-local `@State` (`previousMovie`). Under the old SwiftUIFlux `@EnvironmentObject` store, a `ConnectedView` re-rendered on *every* store change just by holding the store; under the new `@Observable` store it only re-renders when it *reads* `store.state`. So when the deck emptied (store change), the body re-rendered but read a **stale local `@State`** — and the macOS undo button is *conditionally created* (iOS opacity-gates it, which had been masking the same latent issue).
- **Fix:** moved the "last discarded movie" into the store (`MoviesState.discoverLastDiscarded`, set by `PopRandromDiscover`, cleared by `Push`/`Reset`); `DiscoverView` reads it from props so undo re-renders reliably. Also restored `Store.dispatch` to `DispatchQueue.main.async` (matching the original's exact scheduling). Added reducer tests.
- **Validated locally:** both macOS *and* iOS undo tests pass, new + existing reducer tests pass, persistence/round-trip suites pass, all 3 platforms build-for-testing, lint clean, coverage gates green.

I also captured the `@Observable` re-render gotcha in memory so it doesn't bite again. I'll merge once the watcher confirms CI is green (and run a quick local app launch if you'd like the belt-and-suspenders manual check), then close out with PR 3 (docs/ROADMAP sweep).

## SwiftUIFlux dependency removed ✅

Your ask — *"write things so we get rid of the dependency on SwiftUIFlux"* — is complete and merged to `main`:

| PR | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#47](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/47) | New in-repo `Flux` package (`@Observable @MainActor Store`), inert + fully tested | ✅ merged |
| [#48](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/48) | Cut the app + MovieSwiftFluxCore over to `Flux`, **deleted SwiftUIFlux** | ✅ merged |
| [#49](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/49) | ROADMAP update | CI running |

**Outcome:** zero SwiftUIFlux references remain. The Combine `ObservableObject` store became an `@Observable @MainActor` one, which let me delete **all 33 `@preconcurrency import`s** and **both `nonisolated(unsafe)` store globals** — net concurrency-debt reduction. The Redux architecture (reducers, 40+ actions, 19 async actions, 32 `ConnectedView`s) is unchanged; the cutover was an import-swap plus a handful of concurrency annotations.

**The hard part:** CI caught a subtle `@Observable` regression — 3 macOS Discover-undo tests — that I traced to view-local `@State` going stale across a store-driven re-render (it no longer rides along the way `@EnvironmentObject` did). Fixed by moving undo state into the store, validated on both macOS and iOS, with reducer tests added. Captured the gotcha in memory so it won't recur.

This also completes the **first (and highest-leverage) item of Phase 4**, going beyond the roadmap's "migrate the store" by removing the dependency entirely. Once #49 merges I'll have closed out the SwiftUIFlux work; I'll report the result and can continue with the rest of Phase 4 (App Intent entities, Liquid Glass, `ShareLink`, dead-code removal) whenever you'd like.

| PR | What |

| [#49](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/49) | ROADMAP updated | 

**What changed and why it's better:**
- The third-party dependency is replaced by `MovieSwift/Packages/Flux` — same Redux contract, but the store is now `@Observable @MainActor` instead of a Combine `ObservableObject`.
- That cleared **all 33 `@preconcurrency import`s** and **both `nonisolated(unsafe)` store globals** — a net reduction in concurrency debt, not just a dependency swap.
- Reducers, 40+ actions, 19 async actions, and 32 `ConnectedView`s were untouched apart from their `import` line. `Action`/`FluxState` now refine `Sendable`.
- This also completes the **highest-leverage item of Phase 4**, exceeding the roadmap (which only asked to migrate the store).

**Engineering notes:** the cutover surfaced a genuinely subtle `@Observable` regression (macOS Discover-undo) — view-local `@State` going stale across a store-driven re-render, which `@EnvironmentObject` had masked. I root-caused it, moved that state into the store, added reducer tests, validated on both platforms, and recorded the gotcha to memory. Every PR went through the full verify → review → green-CI gate (the reviewer's false-positive "Swift 6 errors" were correctly dismissed via the project's `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` setting + green builds).

Remaining Phase 4 work, whenever you want it: App Intent entities + parameterized Shortcuts, Liquid Glass / `@Entry` / `reduceMotion` polish, `ShareLink` on detail screens, and removing the dead `ActionSheet` factory. Just say the word.

=== ActionSheet.swift contents ===
import Foundation
import SwiftUI
import MovieSwiftFluxCore

#if !os(macOS)
enum ActionSheetMovieListAction: Equatable {
    case addToWishlist(movie: Int)
    case removeFromWishlist(movie: Int)
    case addToSeenlist(movie: Int)
    case removeFromSeenlist(movie: Int)
    case addToCustomList(list: Int, movie: Int)
    case removeFromCustomList(list: Int, movie: Int)

    static func wishlist(movie: Int, isInWishlist: Bool) -> ActionSheetMovieListAction {
        isInWishlist ? .removeFromWishlist(movie: movie) : .addToWishlist(movie: movie)
    }

    static func seenlist(movie: Int, isInSeenlist: Bool) -> ActionSheetMovieListAction {
        isInSeenlist ? .removeFromSeenlist(movie: movie) : .addToSeenlist(movie: movie)
    }

    static func customList(list: CustomList, movie: Int) -> ActionSheetMovieListAction {
        list.movies.contains(movie) ? .removeFromCustomList(list: list.id, movie: movie) : .addToCustomList(list: list.id, movie: movie)
    }
}

extension ActionSheet {
    private static func dispatch(_ action: ActionSheetMovieListAction,
                                 with dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction,
                                 onTrigger: (() -> Void)?) {
        switch action {
        case let .addToWishlist(movie):
            dispatch(MoviesActions.AddToWishlist(movie: movie))
            #if !os(tvOS)
            UISelectionFeedbackGenerator().selectionChanged()
            #endif
        case let .removeFromWishlist(movie):
            dispatch(MoviesActions.RemoveFromWishlist(movie: movie))
        case let .addToSeenlist(movie):
            dispatch(MoviesActions.AddToSeenList(movie: movie))
            #if !os(tvOS)
            UISelectionFeedbackGenerator().selectionChanged()
            #endif
        case let .removeFromSeenlist(movie):
            dispatch(MoviesActions.RemoveFromSeenList(movie: movie))
        case let .addToCustomList(list, movie):
            dispatch(MoviesActions.AddMovieToCustomList(list: list, movie: movie))
            #if !os(tvOS)
            UISelectionFeedbackGenerator().selectionChanged()
            #endif
        case let .removeFromCustomList(list, movie):
            dispatch(MoviesActions.RemoveMovieFromCustomList(list: list, movie: movie))
        }

        onTrigger?()
    }

    static func wishlistButton(isInWishlist: Bool, movie: Int, dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction, onTrigger: (() -> Void)?) -> Alert.Button {
        let action = ActionSheetMovieListAction.wishlist(movie: movie, isInWishlist: isInWishlist)
        switch action {
        case .removeFromWishlist:
            return .destructive(Text("Remove from wishlist")) {
                self.dispatch(action, with: dispatch, onTrigger: onTrigger)
            }
        case .addToWishlist:
            return .default(Text("Add to wishlist")) {
                self.dispatch(action, with: dispatch, onTrigger: onTrigger)
            }
        default:
            return .cancel()
        }
    }

    static func seenListButton(isInSeenlist: Bool, movie: Int, dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction, onTrigger: (() -> Void)?) -> Alert.Button {
        let action = ActionSheetMovieListAction.seenlist(movie: movie, isInSeenlist: isInSeenlist)
        switch action {
        case .removeFromSeenlist:
            return .destructive(Text("Remove from seenlist")) {
                self.dispatch(action, with: dispatch, onTrigger: onTrigger)
            }
        case .addToSeenlist:
            return .default(Text("Add to seenlist")) {
                self.dispatch(action, with: dispatch, onTrigger: onTrigger)
            }
        default:
            return .cancel()
        }
    }

    static func customListsButttons(customLists: [CustomList], movie: Int, dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction, onTrigger: (() -> Void)?) -> [Alert.Button] {
        var buttons: [Alert.Button] = []
        for list in customLists {
            let action = ActionSheetMovieListAction.customList(list: list, movie: movie)
            switch action {
            case .removeFromCustomList:
                buttons.append(.destructive(Text("Remove from \(list.name)")) {
                    self.dispatch(action, with: dispatch, onTrigger: onTrigger)
                })
            case .addToCustomList:
                buttons.append(.default(Text("Add to \(list.name)")) {
                    self.dispatch(action, with: dispatch, onTrigger: onTrigger)
                })
            default:
                break
            }
        }
        return buttons
    }

    static func sortActionSheet(onAction: @escaping ((MoviesSort?) -> Void)) -> ActionSheet {
        let byAddedDate: Alert.Button = .default(Text("Sort by added date")) {
            onAction(.byAddedDate)
        }
        let byReleaseDate: Alert.Button = .default(Text("Sort by release date")) {
            onAction(.byReleaseDate)
        }
        let byScore: Alert.Button = .default(Text("Sort by ratings")) {
            onAction(.byScore)
        }
        let byPopularity: Alert.Button = .default(Text("Sort by popularity")) {
            onAction(.byPopularity)
        }

        return ActionSheet(title: Text("Sort movies by"),
                           message: nil,
                           buttons: [byAddedDate, byReleaseDate, byScore, byPopularity, Alert.Button.cancel({
                            onAction(nil)
                           }), ])
    }
}
#endif

import Foundation

// Stateless (no stored properties), so safe to share across threads —
// the `shared` singleton requires `Sendable` under the Swift 6 mode.
public final class ImageService: Sendable {
    public static let shared = ImageService()

    public enum Size: String, Sendable {
        case small = "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w154/"
        case medium = "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/"
        case cast = "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w185/"
        case original = "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/"

        public func path(poster: String) -> URL {
            // `rawValue` is a hardcoded valid https URL literal from the Size enum.
            // swiftlint:disable:next force_unwrapping
            return URL(string: rawValue)!.appendingPathComponent(poster)
        }
    }

    public enum ImageError: Error {
        case decodingError
    }

    /// Fetches the raw image data, returning `nil` on any transport error
    /// (matching the previous Combine pipeline's `.catch { Just(nil) }`).
    public func fetchImage(poster: String, size: Size) async -> Data? {
        do {
            let (data, _) = try await URLSession.shared.data(from: size.path(poster: poster))

## Code review — feat/sharelink-detail

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/movieDetail/MovieDetail.swift:713` — ShareLink has no `.accessibilityLabel`**

The `ShareLink` at line 709–713 carries `.accessibilityIdentifier` but no `.accessibilityLabel`. The existing `CrashReportsView` `ShareLink` at line 107 of `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/views/CrashReportsView.swift` sets `.accessibilityLabel("Share crash report")` as the project convention. Without an explicit label, VoiceOver reads the default system label ("Share"), which gives no context about what is being shared. Suggested fix:

```swift
.accessibilityLabel("Share \(movie.userTitle) on TMDB")
.accessibilityIdentifier(AccessibilityID.MovieDetail.shareButton)
```

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/peopleDetail/PeopleDetail.swift:329` — same issue on PeopleDetail ShareLink**

Same missing `.accessibilityLabel` for the person detail toolbar. Suggested fix:

```swift
.accessibilityLabel("Share \(props.people.name) on TMDB")
.accessibilityIdentifier(AccessibilityID.PeopleDetail.shareButton)
```

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftUITests/MovieSwiftUITests.swift:194` — no macOS coverage for share button tests**

`testMovieDetailShowsShareButton` and `testPeopleDetailShowsShareButton` live in `MovieSwiftUITests.swift`, which is shared between iOS and macOS. The macOS test file (`MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift`) has no share button test at all. Since `ShareLink` renders differently on macOS (as a toolbar button via `NSToolbar` rather than an icon button), even a structural existence check in `MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift` parallel to the iOS test would close the gap. This is low risk because the iOS test and macOS build both passing gives high confidence, but it is a coverage gap the TDD policy notices.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/state/AccessibilityID.swift:173` — `PeopleDetail.shareButton` inserted out of alphabetical order**

All other members inside `PeopleDetail` are sorted alphabetically (`fanClubButton`, `image`, `knownFor`, `movie`). `shareButton` comes after `movie` alphabetically, so the placement is correct — but the source block groups `image` and `movie` as functions (with trailing blank lines) while the new `shareButton` constant sits after a blank line that was also inserted. Compare the `MovieDetail` enum where `shareButton` is inserted between `recommendedHeader` and `title` without a preceding blank line. The extra blank line before `shareButton` in the `PeopleDetail` enum is inconsistent with the rest of the file's style; remove it so the constants read as a contiguous block.

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/models/TMDBWeb.swift:17–19` — `personURL` comment omitted relative to `movieURL`**

`movieURL` explains the force-unwrap rationale in a comment on line 12–13 before the disable directive. `personURL` has only the lint-disable line and no rationale comment. They are symmetric cases; either add the same "The base is a constant valid https URL and `id` is an Int" comment to `personURL`, or factor the explanation into a single doc comment on the enum itself so both functions are covered.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/movieDetail/MovieDetail.swift:706–715` — `#if !os(tvOS)` gate is correct but technically redundant**

The `#if !os(tvOS)` guard on the `ShareLink` in `MovieDetail` is good defensive practice and matches the project pattern (`CrashReportsView` uses the same guard). However, as confirmed by the project file, `MovieDetail.swift` is not in the tvOS target's build phase at all — the tvOS app uses `TVMovieDetail.swift` exclusively. The gate is not wrong (it documents intent and future-proofs against any target membership change), but a one-line comment — similar to the one in `CrashReportsView.swift` line 95 ("tvOS doesn't ship ShareLink") — would make the rationale explicit rather than leaving a reader to infer it.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the two missing `.accessibilityLabel` modifiers on the `ShareLink` buttons diverge from the project's own established pattern (see `CrashReportsView`) and will give VoiceOver users a context-free "Share" label; add them before opening the PR.

//  AppIntent definitions that surface MovieSwift in Siri,
//  Spotlight search, and the Shortcuts app. Each intent opens the
//  app and (where applicable) writes a destination to
//  `IntentNavigationStore.shared` for the root view to read on its
//  next layout pass.
//
//  AppShortcut registration lives in `MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift`
//  — the provider must be in the same target as the intents and
//  the @main App entry point so the system can discover the
//  shortcuts when it indexes the app.

import Foundation
import AppIntents

/// "Open MovieSwift" — generic launcher. Useful as the system
/// fallback shortcut and as a foundation for future parameterised
/// intents (e.g. "Open MovieSwift to Popular").
struct OpenMovieSwiftIntent: AppIntent {
    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Open MovieSwift"

    static let description = IntentDescription(
        "Opens MovieSwift to whatever section you were last viewing.",
        categoryName: "Navigation"
    )

    static let openAppWhenRun: Bool = true

    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {
        // No specific destination — opening the app is the action.
        // The system brings the app to the foreground because of
        // openAppWhenRun.
        return .result()
    }
}

struct OpenWishlistIntent: AppIntent {
    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Open Wishlist"

    static let description = IntentDescription(
        "Opens MovieSwift to your wishlist.",
        categoryName: "Navigation"
    )

    static let openAppWhenRun: Bool = true

    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {
        await IntentNavigationStore.shared.request(.wishlist)
        return .result()
    }
}

struct OpenDiscoverIntent: AppIntent {
    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Discover Movies"

    static let description = IntentDescription(
        "Opens MovieSwift to the Discover view for swipe-through movie suggestions.",
        categoryName: "Navigation"
    )

    static let openAppWhenRun: Bool = true

    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {
        await IntentNavigationStore.shared.request(.discover)
        return .result()
    }
}

struct OpenFanClubIntent: AppIntent {
    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Open Fan Club"

    static let description = IntentDescription(
        "Opens MovieSwift to your Fan Club — actors and people you've added.",
        categoryName: "Navigation"
    )

    static let openAppWhenRun: Bool = true

    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {
        await IntentNavigationStore.shared.request(.fanClub)
        return .result()
    }
}

struct OpenPopularMoviesIntent: AppIntent {
    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Browse Popular Movies"

    static let description = IntentDescription(
        "Opens MovieSwift to the Popular movies list.",
        categoryName: "Navigation"
    )

//  Registers the app's intents with the system so they appear in:
//   - Spotlight search ("wishlist" / "discover" / "movieswift")
//   - The Shortcuts app gallery
//   - Siri ("open my wishlist in MovieSwift")
//
//  The provider must compile into the app target alongside the
//  @main entry point. It's discovered automatically by Xcode's
//  appintentsmetadataprocessor build step (visible in the build
//  log around the app target's late phases).

import Foundation
import AppIntents

struct MovieSwiftAppShortcuts: AppShortcutsProvider {

    /// Tint applied to every shortcut row in the Shortcuts app.
    /// Matches the steam_gold accent used throughout the UI.
    static let shortcutTileColor: ShortcutTileColor = .yellow

    @AppShortcutsBuilder
    static var appShortcuts: [AppShortcut] {
        AppShortcut(
            intent: OpenMovieSwiftIntent(),
            phrases: [
                "Open \(.applicationName)",
                "Launch \(.applicationName)",
            ],
            shortTitle: "Open MovieSwift",
            systemImageName: "film.stack"
        )
        AppShortcut(
            intent: OpenWishlistIntent(),
            phrases: [
                "Open my wishlist in \(.applicationName)",
                "Show my wishlist in \(.applicationName)",
                "Open \(.applicationName) wishlist",
            ],
            shortTitle: "Wishlist",
            systemImageName: "heart.circle"
        )
        AppShortcut(
            intent: OpenDiscoverIntent(),
            phrases: [
                "Discover movies in \(.applicationName)",
                "Open Discover in \(.applicationName)",
                "Find movies in \(.applicationName)",
            ],
            shortTitle: "Discover",
            systemImageName: "square.stack"
        )

//  Tiny shared bus that lets `AppIntent`s drive navigation in the
//  SwiftUI root views without coupling them to the iOS TabView,
//  the macOS SplitView, or the tvOS HomeView directly.
//
//  Flow:
//   1. An intent's `perform()` calls `IntentNavigationStore.shared
//      .request(.wishlist)`.
//   2. The root view subscribes to `pendingDestination` via a
//      `@StateObject` / `.onChange` and switches its selected tab /
//      sidebar menu when a destination appears.
//   3. The view calls `consume()` (or sets `pendingDestination =
//      nil`) once it has navigated, so a second invocation of the
//      same intent re-fires.
//
//  The store is a singleton because AppIntent runs outside SwiftUI
//  view scope. We can't pass an EnvironmentObject in, so the
//  AppIntent and the view both reach for `.shared`.

import Foundation
import MovieSwiftFluxCore
import Observation

// `@MainActor`: this is an @Observable store whose `pendingDestination`
// drives SwiftUI, so every mutation has to land on the main actor. Under
// the Swift 6 language mode that makes the `shared` singleton — and the
// store's mutable state — concurrency-safe. App Intents call into it from
// their async `perform()` via `await`.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class IntentNavigationStore {
    static let shared = IntentNavigationStore()

    /// Where an App Intent is asking the app to navigate. Each
    /// case maps to one of the iOS tabs or the macOS sidebar menus.
    enum Destination: Equatable {
        case popularMovies
        case discover
        case fanClub
        case wishlist
    }

    var pendingDestination: Destination?

    private init() {}

    /// Posts a destination request. The store is `@MainActor`, so callers
    /// off the main actor (e.g. `AppIntent.perform()`) reach it with
    /// `await` and the assignment lands on the main actor where SwiftUI's
    /// observation expects it.
    func request(_ destination: Destination) {
        pendingDestination = destination
    }

    /// Reads and clears the pending destination. Views call this
    /// after acting on a request so the intent can be invoked
    /// again later with the same destination.
    @discardableResult
    func consume() -> Destination? {
        let destination = pendingDestination
        pendingDestination = nil
        return destination
    }

    /// UI-test seam: when `UI_TEST_INTENT_DESTINATION` is set in the
    /// process environment, post the matching destination to the
    /// navigation bus. Called from a `.task` modifier on the iOS
    /// TabbarView and macOS SplitView so the value lands AFTER the
    /// `.onChange` subscription is in place — otherwise the change
    /// would happen before observation starts and the view wouldn't
    /// react.
    ///
    /// This is how `MovieSwiftUITests` simulates an App Intent firing
    /// at launch (`OpenWishlistIntent`, `OpenDiscoverIntent`, etc.)
    /// without invoking the AppIntent runtime, which can't be driven
    /// from XCUITest.
    static func handleUITestEnvironment(_ environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) {
        guard let raw = environment[UITestEnv.Variable.intentDestination] else { return }
        let destination: Destination?
        switch raw {
        case "popularMovies": destination = .popularMovies
        case "discover":      destination = .discover
        case "fanClub":       destination = .fanClub
        case "wishlist":      destination = .wishlist
        default:              destination = nil
        }
        guard let destination else { return }
        shared.request(destination)
    }
}
```

  "content": "//  Shared bus that lets parameterised `AppIntent`s (Add to Watchlist /\n//  Mark as Seen) mutate user lists without reaching into the store from\n//  outside SwiftUI.\n//\n//  Why not mutate persisted state directly from the intent? The running\n//  app archives its in-memory `AppState` on a timer, so a behind-the-back\n//  write to disk would be clobbered. Instead the intent (with\n//  `openAppWhenRun`) posts a pending action here; the root view observes\n//  it and dispatches the real Flux action through the live store, which\n//  then persists normally — mirroring `IntentNavigationStore`.\n\nimport Foundation\nimport Observation\n\n@MainActor\n@Observable\nfinal class IntentActionStore {\n    static let shared = IntentActionStore()\n\n    /// A list mutation an App Intent is asking the app to perform, by movie id.\n    enum Action: Equatable {\n        case addToWishlist(movie: Int)\n        case markAsSeen(movie: Int)\n    }\n\n    var pendingAction: Action?\n\n    private init() {}\n\n    /// Posts a pending action. `@MainActor`, so `AppIntent.perform()`\n    /// reaches it with `await`.\n    func request(_ action: Action) {\n        pendingAction = action\n    }\n\n    /// Reads and clears the pending action so the same intent can fire again.\n    @discardableResult\n    func consume() -> Action? {\n        let action = pendingAction\n        pendingAction = nil\n        return action\n    }\n}\n"

  "content": "import Foundation\n\n/// Pure helpers that back the `MovieEntity` App Intent query: which movies\n/// to suggest when the user picks one in Shortcuts/Siri, and how to resolve\n/// a set of ids back to movies. Kept free of the AppIntents framework so it\n/// is unit-testable; the `AppEntity`/`EntityQuery` wrapper lives in the app\n/// target and reads state via `AppPersistence`.\npublic enum MovieEntitySource {\n    /// The user's saved movies (wishlist ∪ seenlist) resolved from the movie\n    /// cache, deduped and ordered by id for a stable suggestion list. Ids not\n    /// present in the cache are skipped (nothing to display for them).\n    public static func suggested(from state: AppState, limit: Int = 20) -> [Movie] {\n        let saved = state.moviesState.wishlist.union(state.moviesState.seenlist)\n        return saved\n            .sorted()\n            .compactMap { state.moviesState.movies[$0] }\n            .prefix(limit)\n            .map { $0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the given ids to cached movies, preserving the input order\n    /// and dropping any id that isn't cached.\n    public static func movies(for ids: [Int], from state: AppState) -> [Movie] {\n        ids.compactMap { state.moviesState.movies[$0] }\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/intents/MovieEntity.swift",
  "content": "//  `AppEntity` representation of a movie so parameterised App Intents\n//  (Add to Watchlist / Mark as Seen) can take a movie the user picks in\n//  Shortcuts/Siri. The query resolves and suggests movies from the\n//  persisted `AppState` (the intent runs outside the app, so it reads the\n//  last-archived state rather than the live store); the pure selection\n//  logic lives in `MovieEntitySource` for unit testing.\n\nimport AppIntents\nimport MovieSwiftFluxCore\n\nstruct MovieEntity: AppEntity, Identifiable {\n    let id: Int\n    let title: String\n\n    init(id: Int, title: String) {\n        self.id = id\n        self.title = title\n    }\n\n    init(movie: Movie) {\n        self.id = movie.id\n        self.title = movie.title\n    }\n\n    static let typeDisplayRepresentation = TypeDisplayRepresentation(name: \"Movie\")\n    static let defaultQuery = MovieEntityQuery()\n\n    var displayRepresentation: DisplayRepresentation {\n        DisplayRepresentation(title: \"\\(title)\")\n    }\n}\n\nstruct MovieEntityQuery: EntityQuery {\n    func entities(for identifiers: [MovieEntity.ID]) async throws -> [MovieEntity] {\n        let state = AppPersistence.loadState() ?? AppState()\n        return MovieEntitySource.movies(for: identifiers, from: state).map(MovieEntity.init(movie:))\n    }\n\n    func suggestedEntities() async throws -> [MovieEntity] {\n        let state = AppPersistence.loadState() ?? AppState()\n        return MovieEntitySource.suggested(from: state).map(MovieEntity.init(movie:))\n    }\n}\n"
}

## Code review — feat/movie-action-intents

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, missing tests, CI-blocking lint)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/IntentActionStoreTests.swift:11` — shared-singleton tests are not `.serialized`; they can corrupt each other under Swift Testing's parallel runner**

The two tests both mutate `IntentActionStore.shared` directly (line 14: `store.pendingAction = nil`, line 19: same cleanup). Swift Testing runs tests in a suite in parallel unless the suite declares `@Suite(.serialized)`. The `requestSetsThePendingAction` test clears `pendingAction` at the end with a raw assignment rather than through `consume()`, but if `consumeReturnsAndClearsThePendingAction` starts while the first is between `request()` and the `nil`-clear, the second test's `request()` can be clobbered. The repo already uses `@Suite(.serialized)` for every other suite that touches a shared singleton (`AppDataICloudBackupTests`, `CrashReportStoreTests`, `PeopleActionsTests`). Fix: add `@Suite(.serialized)` to `IntentActionStoreTests`.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/IntentActionStoreTests.swift:12-19` — `requestSetsThePendingAction` would pass even if `request()` were replaced by direct property assignment; the test exercises the wrong contract**

The test sets `pendingAction = nil` before calling `request()`, which means it would pass even if `request` were a no-op and the initial `nil` was never set. The test should start with a non-nil value (e.g. set a sentinel first, then call `request()`, then assert the new value) to prove `request()` actually overwrites an existing pending action. Alternatively, omit the pre-clear and assert both `request()` writes work. This is a weak-test finding that conceals the "overwrite" behaviour that the `markAsSeen`/`addToWishlist` flip test implicitly relies on. Add a test named `requestOverwritesExistingPendingAction` that starts from a non-nil state.

---

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/IntentAction.swift:26` — `pendingAction` is `internal` (default) where `pendingDestination` in `IntentNavigationStore` is also `internal`; fine for now, but the test mutates it directly via `store.pendingAction = nil` which bypasses `consume()`**

Setting `pendingAction` directly in the test teardown (`store.pendingAction = nil` at lines 14 and 19) is weaker than calling `store.consume()`, which is the public API. If cleanup is needed between tests, it should be done through `consume()` to avoid the tests being coupled to the storage field name. Suggested fix: replace `store.pendingAction = nil` with `store.consume()` in teardown. If the property must remain settable from tests for diagnosis purposes, add a `// Testing only` comment.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/models/MovieEntitySource.swift:17-18` — redundant `.map { $0 }` after `.prefix(limit)`**

```swift
.prefix(limit)
.map { $0 }
```

`.prefix` returns `ArraySlice<Movie>`; the intent is to materialise it as `[Movie]`. The idiomatic conversion is `Array(...)` wrapping or `prefix(limit) as [Movie]`. Using `.map { $0 }` is correct but is a non-obvious way to force the type that confuses readers and future agents. Suggested fix: `Array(saved.sorted().compactMap { state.moviesState.movies[$0] }.prefix(limit))`.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/home/HomeView.swift:139-140` — `consume()` is called before `selectedTab = .myLists`; the ordering is fine but asymmetric with SplitView**

In `HomeView` (line 139-140), `consume()` is called and then `selectedTab` is set unconditionally. In `SplitView` (line 168-174), `consume()` is called and then the nav is only set `if selectedMenu != .myLists`. The iOS side always resets the tab to `.myLists` even if the user is already there, which causes a spurious tab-switch animation that flashes back to the same tab. The macOS guard is correct and should be mirrored on iOS:

```swift
intentAction.consume()
if selectedTab != .myLists {
    selectedTab = .myLists
}
```

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/intents/MovieEntity.swift:29` — `DisplayRepresentation(title: "\(title)")` string-interpolates a `String` into a `LocalizedStringResource`**

`DisplayRepresentation.init(title:)` takes a `LocalizedStringResource`. Wrapping `title` in `"\(title)"` creates an unlocalised `LocalizedStringResource` from a plain `String` — this compiles, but it means the entity's Shortcuts/Siri UI label won't benefit from any future localisation of the title. The cleaner and more explicit form is `DisplayRepresentation(title: LocalizedStringResource(stringLiteral: title))`. Not a runtime bug, but wrong intent for a `LocalizedStringResource`-typed parameter.

---

**tvOS: `MovieEntity.swift` and `IntentAction.swift` compile into the tvOS target (pbxproj lines 1747-1748) but `HomeView.swift` on tvOS has no `.onChange(of: intentAction.pendingAction)` wiring**

This is deliberate and mirrors the existing navigation-intent pattern (which is also unwired on tvOS). When the user triggers `AddToWatchlistIntent` from a tvOS Shortcuts automation, the app opens but the action is never dispatched because no view observes `IntentActionStore.pendingAction`. The action silently drops. On iOS and macOS the same intent fires correctly. This is a judgment call. Shipping it as-is is acceptable for Phase 4 given the parity with nav intents, but it should be documented — add a `// TODO(tvOS): IntentActionStore is not observed on tvOS — wiring skipped` comment in `IntentAction.swift` (or in the tvOS `HomeView`) so the gap is visible on the next pass, rather than looking like an accidental omission.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/IntentActionStoreTests.swift` — no test for the `addToWishlist` case in `requestSetsThePendingAction`**

`requestSetsThePendingAction` only exercises `.addToWishlist(movie:)`. The `consumeReturnsAndClearsThePendingAction` only exercises `.markAsSeen(movie:)`. Neither test checks that `request(.addToWishlist)` followed by `consume()` properly returns the action. Adding a paired test `requestWishlistActionCanBeConsumed` would complete the cross-case coverage.

---

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/intents/MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift:75` — `systemImageName: "heart"` on `AddToWatchlistIntent` while the existing `OpenWishlistIntent` uses `"heart.circle"`. Minor inconsistency; consider `"heart.circle"` for visual parity with the My Lists tab icon.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/intents/MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift:84` — `systemImageName: "eye"` is fine; `"checkmark.circle"` might be more evocative for "mark as seen" but this is subjective.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/IntentAction.swift:32` — the comment `/// Posts a pending action. '@MainActor', so 'AppIntent.perform()' reaches it with 'await'.` says `@MainActor` but `request(_:)` itself has no explicit isolation annotation. It inherits `@MainActor` from the class — fine, but the comment would be clearer written as "inherited `@MainActor` from the class" rather than suggesting an explicit annotation on the method.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/MovieEntitySourceTests.swift:16` — the comment on movie id `9` says `"Uncached-but-listed placeholder absent"` but id `9` is present in `movies` and not in `wishlist` or `seenlist`. The intent seems to be testing an id that is in the cache but not in any list (so it won't be suggested). The comment is misleading; rename to something like `makeMovie(id: 9, title: "Cached but unlisted")` and update the comment.

---

### Verdict

**FIX-FIRST** — the `IntentActionStoreTests` suite must be annotated `@Suite(.serialized)` before merging to prevent rare but real parallel-runner corruption of the shared singleton; the other must-fix (the weak `requestSetsThePendingAction` test) is cheap to address alongside it. The tvOS wiring gap needs at least a TODO comment. All other items are low-risk should-fixes or nits.

The pure selection logic is **`MovieEntitySource`** in MovieSwiftFluxCore (unit-tested).\n- **`AddToWatchlistIntent(movie:)` / `MarkAsSeenIntent(movie:)`** (`openAppWhenRun`) post to a new **`@MainActor @Observable IntentActionStore`**, mirroring `IntentNavigationStore`. The iOS `TabbarView` and macOS `SplitView` observe `pendingAction`, dispatch the real `AddToWishlist`/`AddToSeenList` Flux action **through the live store** (so it persists normally instead of being clobbered by the app's 30s archive timer), then surface My Lists.\n- Registered as **parameterized AppShortcuts** (\"Add \\<movie\\> to my watchlist\", \"Mark \\<movie\\> as seen\").\n\n## Notes\n- **tvOS**: the intents/entity compile but — like the existing nav intents — have no app-side wiring there; documented in `IntentAction.swift`.\n- New app/test-target files were added to the `.xcodeproj` (explicit file refs) via the xcodeproj gem.\n\n## Tests\n- `IntentActionStoreTests` (`.serialized`): request, overwrite-existing, consume-returns-and-clears for both cases.\n- `MovieEntitySourceTests`: suggested-entities dedupe/sort/limit + drops uncached ids; id resolution preserves order.\n- The dispatch wiring mirrors the already-UI-tested nav-intent `.onChange`/`consume()` pattern; an end-to-end UI test isn't feasible because the smoke fixture only caches movie 0 (already in both lists), so an observable add would need risky shared-fixture surgery.\n\nVerified: lint clean, all three schemes build + build-for-testing, unit tests pass. ## Code review — feat/liquid-glass-polish

### Must fix (correctness, missing tests, CI-blocking lint)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/discover/DiscoverView.swift:354`** — Undo button `.animation(.spring(), ...)` is not gated on `reduceMotion`

The branch gates five of the Discover floating button animations but leaves the undo button (line 354) with a bare `.animation(.spring(), value: DiscoverUndoState.canUndo(...))`. This is not a pre-existing omission — it sits in the same `actionsButtons` function as all the other gated animations and controls a user-facing spring that appears/disappears the undo affordance. Every other button in that ZStack was updated; this one was missed.

Fix: `.animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(), value: DiscoverUndoState.canUndo(previousMovie: props.lastDiscarded, isDragging: self.draggedViewState.isActive))`

---

### Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/UI/Sources/UI/buttons/BorderedButton.swift:28-29`** — `.symbolEffect(.bounce, value: isOn)` fires on every caller that passes a constant `isOn: false`

`BorderedButton` is used in two non-toggle contexts: the filter button and the "Refill discover" button (both with a hardcoded `isOn: false`). `.symbolEffect(.bounce, value:)` triggers an animation whenever `value` changes. When `isOn` is always `false` the effect never fires, which is fine. But `.symbolVariant(false ? .fill : .none)` resolves to `.none` unconditionally on those call sites, so `heart`/`eye`/`pin` with `isOn: false` will never show `.fill`, which is also correct. The concern is the opposite direction: `BorderedButton` is a public API surface in the `UI` package. Adding animated behavior unconditionally means any future caller that passes a changing `Bool` will get the bounce whether they want it or not. This is a readability / API-contract issue rather than an active correctness bug against current callers.

Fix: Add a comment at the call site (or on `BorderedButton.init`) documenting that `.symbolEffect` fires when `isOn` toggles, so future callers know the contract. Alternatively, expose a `Bool` parameter `animatesSymbol: Bool = true` so non-toggle callers can opt out cleanly.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/EnvironmentKeysTests.swift:16`** — The test suite is `@MainActor` but the `customEnvironmentValuesKeepTheirDefaults` test method has no `@Test` doc comment explaining what regression it guards

CLAUDE.md requires `@Test` methods to have a purpose doc. The suite-level doc comment is good, but the method-level test is bare. This makes it harder for agents and reviewers to understand whether the test is adequate or duplicates existing coverage.

Fix: Add a one-line `/// Pins the @Entry macro defaults so a future edit can't silently change them.` doc comment above `@Test`.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/EnvironmentKeysTests.swift:15-21`** — `selectedOutlineMenu` default is not pinned

The test covers `isRunningUISmokeTests` and `archivedStateSizeDescription`, but not the migrated `FocusedValues.selectedOutlineMenu`. Its `@Entry` default is the implicit `nil` for `Binding<OutlineMenu?>?` — correct, but unasserted. Because `FocusedValues` cannot be instantiated in a plain unit test the same way `EnvironmentValues()` can, this is harder to test, but a comment in the test acknowledging that gap would be clear.

Fix: Add a `// Note: FocusedValues.selectedOutlineMenu default (nil) is implicit in the @Entry Optional; no plain-init test path exists for FocusedValues.` comment so the omission is deliberate rather than accidental.

---

### Nits

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/discover/DiscoverView.swift:215-216`** — The `// Liquid Glass backing for the floating swipe-action button.` comment accurately describes the `primaryActionButton` context, but the modifier is applied inside the button label's ZStack, which means only the two heart/eye primary action buttons get `.glassEffect`. The "Skip" and "Reset" buttons (plain `Button` constructs at lines 275-311) and the undo button (line 344) are structurally identical floating circles but receive no glass treatment, creating an inconsistent visual set. The roadmap intent said "Discover floating buttons". Intentional or oversight worth noting in the PR description.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/discover/DiscoverView.swift:478` and `496`** — The two poster-crossfade animations (`.animation(.easeInOut, value: props.currentMovie?.posterPath)`) are pre-existing and not gated. They animate the full-bleed background poster swap rather than a UI chrome element, so they fall closer to a content transition than a "reduce motion" animation. This is debatable rather than wrong, but worth a conscious call in the PR — the accessibility guidelines do recommend suppressing even content transitions when reduce motion is on.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/discover/DiscoverView.swift:610`** — The macOS `cardDeck` `.animation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.85), value: props.currentMovie?.id)` is also pre-existing and ungated. Same reasoning as above.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the undo button's `.animation(.spring())` at line 354 is an unambiguous omission from the `reduceMotion` gating pass that this branch claims to implement; fix that one line before opening the PR, then the diff is clean to ship.

Task #35 closed — Phase 4 is fully done. Here's the workflow I'm following, which comes from the project's `CLAUDE.md` (it overrides my defaults). Every fix or feature goes through the **same 9-step pipeline**, one PR per logical unit:

## The delivery pipeline

1. **Branch** — cut a `fix/` `feat/` `refactor/` `docs/` `chore/` branch off latest `main`. Never commit to `main`.
2. **TDD (red → green → refactor)** — write the smallest failing test *first*, confirm it fails for the right reason, write the minimum code to pass, then refactor. Test + code land in the **same commit**.
3. **Lint & format** — `./scripts/format.sh` (touched files) and `./scripts/lint.sh --fix` before staging. `lint.sh` runs `swiftlint --fix` then `swiftlint lint --strict` so it matches CI exactly.
4. **Verify with the `verifier` subagent** — runs the same gates CI enforces (SwiftLint + the relevant builds + the test suites that cover the change). I must fix everything it reports and re-run until **PASS** before review.
5. **Pre-PR review with the `code-reviewer` subagent** — address every must-fix (and reasonable should-fix). If a fix changes code, re-run the verifier.
6. **Open a PR** — push, `gh pr create` (always `gh`, never the web UI). Description states what/why/how-tested.
7. **Green CI is the merge gate** — the required checks are `package-tests`, `ios-tests`, `ios-tests-ipad`, `mac-tests`, `tvos-tests`; SwiftLint + CodeQL should also be green. A pending Copilot/automated review is **not** part of the gate.
8. **Address review feedback as it lands** — act on valid points, push, reply, resolve, let CI re-run. Feedback after a green merge is a follow-up.
9. **Merge & clean up** — `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch`, then `git checkout main`, `git pull --ff-only`, delete the local branch.

## On top of that, the roadmap level

The `ROADMAP.md` defines **phases** (1–6), each a set of items. I take them in order, run each item through the 9-step pipeline above as its own PR, and you authorized me to do this **autonomously** — merging through the full pipeline without pausing for per-PR approval. The TaskList you see mirrors that: one task per roadmap item, marked `in_progress` when I start and `completed` when its PR merges.

**Where that leaves us:** Phases 1–4 are complete. I stopped at the Phase 4 boundary because Phases 5–6 weren't part of "finish Phase 4" — that's a natural checkpoint for you to weigh in before I roll into the larger marquee work.

You're right that there's overlap, but there's a real constraint worth separating out, because "lint" and "format" sit on different sides of it:

**Lint** — the verifier already runs it. `verifier.md:64` says `./scripts/lint.sh` is "always run it," same strict exit semantics as CI. So that gate genuinely lives in the verifier (step 4), and my step-3 lint is partly redundant with it.

**Format** — the verifier *can't* run it as currently designed. Its frontmatter and body both pin it as **read-only on source** ("never edit source files") with only `Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`. `swiftformat` and `lint.sh --fix` are *writes* — they mutate files. The verifier can only *report* a violation for me to fix, not auto-correct or reformat. That's why the doc (`verifier.md:82-87`) explicitly calls `swiftformat` advisory-and-non-blocking and leaves the actual formatting to step 3.

So the split today is deliberate:

| | Operation | Who | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step 3 | `swiftformat` + `lint.sh --fix` (mutations / auto-correct) | main agent | before verify |
| Step 4 | `lint.sh` strict + builds + tests (read-only checks) | verifier | the gate |

The reason the *writes* are pulled out front is exactly the verifier's read-only guarantee — if it both edited and verified, it'd be grading its own homework, and it couldn't be the clean pass/fail gate before review.

If what you want is to **fold formatting into the verifier**, that's a real workflow change — I'd need to (a) give the verifier `Edit`/`Write`, (b) drop the "never edits source" guarantee, and (c) update both `CLAUDE.md` step 3/4 and `verifier.md`. I can do that, but it trades away the read-only gate property.

59	## Test-Driven Development (TDD) — write the test first
60	
61	Every behaviour change ships with a test, and the test is written
62	**before** the production code. This applies to bug fixes, new
63	features, refactors that change observable behaviour, and
64	parameterization/modernization passes — anything that isn't pure
65	formatting.
66	
67	The cycle is **red → green → refactor**:
68	
69	1. **RED.** Write the smallest test that captures the next desired
70	   behaviour (or, for a bug, reproduces the bug). Run it. It MUST
71	   fail for the right reason — wrong assertion, missing symbol,
72	   wrong value — not because the harness mis-loaded.
73	2. **GREEN.** Write the minimum production code to make that test
74	   pass. Resist the urge to write code the failing test doesn't
75	   demand.
76	3. **REFACTOR.** Tidy the production code and/or the test while
77	   keeping the suite green. Run the affected suite again at the
78	   end.
79	
80	The test and the code that satisfies it land in the **same commit**.
81	The commit message names what the test covers (e.g.
82	`fix(reducer): clear popularLoading when SetPopular dispatches with
83	empty results — covered by peopleReducerSetPopularClearsLoadingOnEmpty`).
84	
85	This applies to every `fix:`, `feat:`, and `refactor:` commit —
86	reducer changes, view logic, navigation, focus handling, parsing,
87	test-helper rewrites, anything that crosses an assertion boundary.

96	- **Swift packages:** `MovieSwift/Packages/<Name>/Tests/`.
97

99	
100	```

104	    -only-testing:MovieSwiftTests/<TestClassName>

106	
107	For macOS-only logic, use `-scheme MovieSwiftMac` with a macOS

111	
112	If a fix can only be verified visually (layout, animation, focus
113	ring), still note that in the commit message and add at least a
114	structural assertion (e.g. view builds without crashing, the
115	relevant accessibility identifier is present) where possible. The
116	TDD cycle still applies — the failing test is the structural
117	assertion before the visual fix lands.
118	
119	## Lint & format before every commit
120	
121	Run the project's linter and formatter before staging changes. CI
122	runs `./scripts/lint.sh` on every PR (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`),
123	which executes `swiftlint lint --strict` — so the canonical way to
124	match CI locally is `./scripts/lint.sh` (not bare `swiftlint`).
125	Catching violations locally avoids a forced fixup commit + extra CI
126	cycle.
127

131	# Format the files you touched, or run `./scripts/format.sh` to

135	# unrelated files.

138	# Lint the whole repo. `--fix` auto-applies SwiftLint's correctable
139	# rules (trailing whitespace, colon/comma spacing, redundant void

141	# to surface anything autocorrect couldn't fix — same exit semantics
142	# as CI.
143	./scripts/lint.sh --fix

145	
146	The scripts do more than just wire in flags, and there is a parallel
147	wrapper for SwiftFormat:
148	
149	```bash
150	./scripts/format.sh           # rewrite every file under MovieSwift/ in place
151	./scripts/format.sh --check   # lint-only; non-zero exit if anything would change
152	./scripts/lint.sh --fix       # swiftlint --fix, THEN swiftlint lint --strict
153	```
154	
155	Running bare `swiftlint --fix` only applies auto-corrections; it does
156	**not** re-lint, so non-auto-correctable violations — the exact
157	failures CI's strict pass will catch — go undetected locally.
158	`./scripts/lint.sh --fix` performs that second verification pass for
159	you. `format.sh` is a thin wrapper around `swiftformat MovieSwift`
160	that adds the `--check` mode and an install-guard.
161

163	
164	Codebase-wide patterns (SwiftUI multi-trailing-closure builders,
165	long view bodies, TMDB snake_case field names, reducer-pattern
166	cyclomatic complexity) are already relaxed in `.swiftlint.yml` —
167	see the header comment there for the rationale on each tuned
168	threshold. Don't add new global relaxations without a similar note.

**The workflow now reads:** step 3 is **format-only**; the `verifier` subagent (step 4) owns the strict-lint gate. That removes the redundant pre-staging `lint.sh --fix` pass — going forward I format touched files, then let the verifier surface lint violations and fix what it reports.

I made it stick in three places so nothing contradicts:
- `CLAUDE.md` — steps 3 & 4, and the renamed "Format before every commit; lint is the verifier's gate" section
- `.claude/agents/verifier.md` — its description now states it owns the lint gate
- A `feedback` memory ([lint-owned-by-verifier](../../.claude/projects/-Users-scottdensmore-Developer-scottdensmore-movieswiftui/memory/lint-owned-by-verifier.md)) so I follow this in future sessions

It's up as [PR #54](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/54) (docs-only) — CI watcher running, I'll merge once the required checks are green.

One thing worth flagging: the verifier is **read-only by design**, so it can't auto-correct. With lint as its gate, the auto-correctable violations (trailing whitespace, comma spacing, etc.) that `lint.sh --fix` used to silently clean up will now come back as verifier findings I fix by hand or with a reactive `lint.sh --fix`. That's the tradeoff you chose — just noting it so it's not a surprise the first time the verifier flags a pile of whitespace nits.

Found the likely culprit. Both `AddToWatchlistIntent`/`MarkAsSeenIntent` use `@Parameter var movie: MovieEntity` *inside AppShortcut phrases* (`\(\.$movie)`). The App Intents framework has a hard rule: **a parameter referenced in an AppShortcut phrase must be backed by a query conforming to `EntityStringQuery`** (so the spoken/typed value can be resolved). If `MovieEntityQuery` is only an `EntityQuery`, the system can crash at launch during shortcut registration — which builds fine (so CI's build passes) but kills the real app on start. Good — that rules out one of my two suspects. `loadState()` (AppPersistence.swift:24) is fully defensive: a decode failure just returns `nil` and the app starts fresh, so the CodingKeys migration **can't** be the synchronous crash. That leaves the App Intents path as my prime suspect.

## What I found by reading the launch path

The real launch (`.normal`) and CI's launch (`.uiSmokeTests`) diverge at `AppStoreFactory.makeInitialState` ([AppStoreFactory.swift:15](MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/AppStoreFactory.swift:15)) — CI uses an in-memory fixture and never touches your real state or the things that only matter in a real launch. The one Phase-4 addition in that gap that can hard-crash at launch:

**`MovieEntityQuery` is an `EntityQuery`, but it's used as a phrase parameter.** [MovieEntity.swift:33](MovieSwift/Shared/intents/MovieEntity.swift:33) implements `entities(for:)` + `suggestedEntities()` but **not** `entities(matching:)` (i.e. it's not an `EntityStringQuery`). Yet `\(\.$movie)` is embedded in two AppShortcut phrases ([MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift:72,81](MovieSwift/Shared/intents/MovieSwiftAppShortcuts.swift:72)). App Intents **requires** a phrase-parameter's query to conform to `EntityStringQuery`; when it doesn't, the system can fatal-error while registering shortcuts at launch. This builds clean (so CI's build/test stays green) but kills the real app on start.

I'm confident enough to fix it — but a crash like this can also be data- or OS-specific, so let's confirm the signature before I change code rather than fix the wrong thing.

## How to get the definitive signal (fastest first)

1. **Exception breakpoint in Xcode** (seconds): Breakpoint navigator → **+** → *Exception Breakpoint* → All. Re-run (`⌘R`). It stops at the throw; the **console** (bottom pane) prints the message and the **Debug navigator** shows the stack. If I'm right, you'll see `EntityStringQuery` or `AppShortcut … parameter` in it.
2. **Crash report**: Xcode → *Window ▸ Devices and Simulators ▸ View Device Logs*, or `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/MovieSwift-*.ips`.
3. **Stream the log** while launching a sim:

Now I have the **actual** root cause — and it's neither of my guesses. The crash is a **Swift concurrency main-actor assertion**, not App Intents:

```
EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
_dispatch_assert_queue_fail
swift_task_checkIsolatedSwift
_checkExpectedExecutor
MetricKitCrashReporter.didReceive(_:)      ← @MainActor method
__-[MXMetricManager deliverDiagnosticPayload:]_block_invoke   ← called on a background queue
_dispatch_workloop_worker_thread
```

MetricKit invokes the subscriber callback `didReceive(_:)` on a **background queue**, but that method is **`@MainActor`-isolated** (implicitly, under `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`). Under Swift 6 the runtime executor-check traps → SIGTRAP. And it's a **crash loop**: the trap writes a new diagnostic, which MetricKit re-delivers on the next launch → crashes again (hence the cluster of reports at 16:43:26 → 16:44:50).

Why nothing caught it:
- **CI** skips MetricKit entirely — `HomeView.init` only calls `startObserving()` when `!isRunningUISmokeTests` ([HomeView.swift:25](MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/home/HomeView.swift:25)), and the Mac app does the same.
- **My ad-hoc build** had no accumulated MetricKit diagnostics in a fresh `/tmp` bundle, so nothing was delivered in the launch window. Your installed app has a backlog (including the crash-loop reports), so MetricKit delivers immediately on launch → instant re-crash.

**RED confirmed.** The build fails with exactly the isolation error that proves the bug:

```
error: main actor-isolated class property 'shared' cannot be accessed from outside of the actor
warning: call to main actor-isolated instance method 'didReceive' in a synchronous nonisolated context
** TEST BUILD FAILED **
```

That's the compile-time shadow of the runtime SIGTRAP — the type and its callbacks are main-actor-isolated. GREEN — make the class `nonisolated` and correct the now-wrong comment:

> TOOL

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MetricKitCrashReporter.swift",
  "old_string": "// `@unchecked Sendable`: MetricKit invokes the subscriber callbacks on a\n// background queue, so this can't be a @MainActor type. Its only mutable\n// state, `isObserving`, is touched solely by start/stop at app launch on\n// the main thread; the `didReceive` callbacks just write files. We own\n// that confinement, which makes the `shared` singleton safe to share.\nfinal class MetricKitCrashReporter: NSObject, MXMetricManagerSubscriber, @unchecked Sendable {",
  "new_string": "// `nonisolated` + `@unchecked Sendable`: MetricKit invokes the subscriber\n// callbacks on a background queue, so this must NOT be a `@MainActor` type.\n// The project builds with `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`, which\n// would otherwise make this type — and its `didReceive` callbacks — implicitly\n// main-actor-isolated; `@unchecked Sendable` alone does NOT opt out of that.\n// A main-actor callback invoked off the main queue trips the Swift 6 runtime\n// executor check and traps (`EXC_BREAKPOINT`) on the next launch that has a\n// pending payload, which is a launch crash loop. `nonisolated` opts the whole\n// type back out of main-actor isolation. Its only mutable state, `isObserving`,\n// is touched solely by start/stop at app launch on the main thread; the\n// `didReceive` callbacks just write files. We own that confinement, which makes\n// the `shared` singleton safe to share.\nnonisolated final class MetricKitCrashReporter: NSObject, MXMetricManagerSubscriber, @unchecked Sendable {"
}

## Code review — fix/metrickit-mainactor-launch-crash

Note: the branch has no commits; all changes are uncommitted working-tree modifications. The diff is between `HEAD` (which equals `main` at `7efb109`) and the working tree.

---

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MetricKitCrashReporter.swift:23–31` — `isObserving` mutation is nonisolated with no data-race protection; `@unchecked Sendable` comment understates the residual risk**

`startObserving()` and `stopObserving()` mutate `isObserving` from whatever context the caller uses — production calls them from `App.init()` which under `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` runs on the main actor, so the race isn't live today. But because the whole class is now `nonisolated`, the Swift 6 compiler no longer statically enforces that those calls happen on the main actor; a future caller on any queue could race against the read in `guard !isObserving`. The comment on line 17 says "touched solely by start/stop at app launch on the main thread; we own that confinement" — but with the type now `nonisolated`, "we own" means we're relying on a convention the compiler can no longer verify.

Suggested fix (two options, least invasive first):

Option A — document the residual contract explicitly in the comment: note that `startObserving()` / `stopObserving()` must continue to be called from the main actor (they're called from `App.init()` which is main-actor) and that callers must not invoke them from background queues. Add `// Called only from App.init() — main-actor context.` above both methods. This is honest and accurate given the current usage, and keeps the scope of the PR focused.

Option B (stronger) — mark only `startObserving` / `stopObserving` `@MainActor` and leave the `didReceive` overloads implicitly nonisolated. This lets the compiler statically enforce the mutation constraint while solving the original crash: the `MXMetricManagerSubscriber` protocol methods are in an `@objc` NSObject subclass and don't inherit actor isolation from the class declaration. This is actually the tighter fix — `nonisolated` on just the class body was needed to prevent the *protocol witness* from being main-actor; marking start/stop `@MainActor` explicitly would restore the compile-time safety for the mutable flag. Worth discussing, but involves more churn.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MetricKitCrashReporter.swift:8–19` — removed leading file-level comment loses the "hook in once at app launch" usage instruction**

The original comment block began with two paragraphs explaining the usage contract ("Hook in once at app launch by calling `MetricKitCrashReporter.shared.startObserving()`", the MetricKit singleton-retention rationale, and the tvOS no-op note). The replacement doc comment covers the isolation story well but drops the call-site usage instruction. The call sites in `HomeView.swift:26` and `MovieSwiftMacApp.swift:21` are already written, but this is a shared-code type that a future maintainer needs to understand without hunting call sites.

Suggested fix: restore a brief leading `//` block (not a doc comment) that states the usage contract — one to two sentences is sufficient. The elaborate isolation explanation (now in the `///` block on the class) can stay where it is.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/MetricKitCrashReporterTests.swift:30–41` — test does not assert anything observable; a future regression where the callback silently swallowed an error would remain undetected**

The test correctly exercises the isolation boundary (the compile-time guard is the primary value), but the runtime assertion is empty: `reporter.didReceive([] as [MXDiagnosticPayload])` with an empty array does nothing in the loop body, so even if the callback were changed to `fatalError("called on wrong thread")`, the test would still pass because the `fatalError` branch is unreachable for an empty payload.

This is by design — `MXDiagnosticPayload` cannot be constructed in tests. The doc comment (line 34–36) explains this honestly: "An empty payload array exercises the isolation boundary without needing a (non-publicly-constructible) `MXDiagnosticPayload` instance." That rationale is sound and is exactly what the `#expect` harness can't strengthen here. Still, consider whether adding the `didReceive` for `[MXMetricPayload]` variant with the same off-main call would ensure both subscriber overloads are exercised — the crash used the diagnostic variant but the metric variant has the identical isolation exposure.

Suggested fix (nit-level, not blocking): add a second call `reporter.didReceive([] as [MXMetricPayload])` in the same continuation block to cover both callbacks at no extra cost. The compile-time guard it provides is identical.

---

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MetricKitCrashReporter.swift:20` — `final nonisolated class` ordering is unusual; `nonisolated final class` is the canonical keyword order in Swift**

Swift allows both, but every other type modifier (e.g. `@MainActor final class`, `private final class`) puts the modifier before `final`. SwiftLint does not enforce this ordering, so this won't block CI, but it reads oddly. Suggested fix: reorder to `nonisolated final class MetricKitCrashReporter`.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/MetricKitCrashReporterTests.swift:29` — struct `MetricKitCrashReporterTests` has no `@Suite` attribute**

All other test structs in this target use `@Suite` (see `OnboardingFlowTests.swift:8`, `AppBootstrapTests.swift:16`). Without it the struct still works — Swift Testing discovers the `@Test` method — but it is inconsistent with the project's established convention and makes the test harder to filter by suite name in Xcode's test navigator. Suggested fix: add `@Suite` to line 29.

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/MetricKitCrashReporterTests.swift` — `async` on `diagnosticCallbackRunsOffTheMainActor` is needed only for `withCheckedContinuation`; `DispatchQueue.global().async` makes the test non-deterministic in theory**

Under Swift Testing, a `@Test async` function runs on the Swift concurrency cooperative thread pool. `withCheckedContinuation` with a `DispatchQueue.global().async` call is correct here — it properly suspends the test until the background call completes — but a reviewer unfamiliar with the pattern might question why it isn't a `Task.detached`. The comment on line 33 ("Mirror MetricKit's real delivery: off the main actor") explains it; the choice of `DispatchQueue` over `Task.detached` or `withTaskGroup` is intentional because it tests the explicit non-Swift-concurrency path MetricKit actually uses. A one-line code comment noting "DispatchQueue is intentional — mirrors MetricKit's Objective-C GCD delivery" at the `DispatchQueue.global()` call site would make this even clearer.

**pbxproj: `OnboardingFlowTests.swift` is missing from the `MovieSwiftTVTests` sources build phase (`FABB29B9`) while it is present in the iOS and Mac phases — the new test follows the same pattern and is correctly (consistently) absent from tvOS sources for files that would compile away**

Not a new issue introduced by this PR, but confirms the tvOS target has intentional gaps in which test files it builds. The new test's presence in all three targets is correct — the `#if canImport(MetricKit) && !os(tvOS)` guard ensures it compiles to nothing on tvOS.

---

### Answers to the specific questions asked

**1. `nonisolated` on the whole class vs. scoped to `didReceive` overloads only.**

The whole-class `nonisolated` is a valid fix that definitely resolves the crash. The tighter alternative — `@MainActor` on `startObserving`/`stopObserving` and `nonisolated` on the `didReceive` overloads only — is technically superior because it restores compiler-enforced isolation on the mutable `isObserving` flag. The current fix's downside is that `isObserving` is now read and written in nonisolated contexts with no lock, relying on a convention (both callers happen to be main-actor) that the compiler doesn't verify. This is acceptable given the `@unchecked Sendable` annotation explicitly takes ownership, but the comment should make the constraint explicit (see should-fix above). `MXMetricManager.shared.add(self)` is an Objective-C call with no Swift actor annotation; calling it from a nonisolated context is fine — MetricKit manages its own internal thread safety for subscriber registration.

**2. Residual main-actor work in `didReceive`.**

Confirmed no residual main-actor work. `CrashReportStore.writeToDefaultDirectory` is marked `nonisolated enum CrashReportStore` at line 26 of `CrashReportStore.swift`, uses `FileManager.default` (thread-safe for concurrent reads; atomic write flag is set at line 99), and contains no dispatch back to the main thread. The callbacks are safe to run entirely off-main.

**3. `SpotlightStoreObserver` sibling risk.**

`SpotlightStoreObserver` at `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Shared/flux/state/MovieSpotlightIndexer.swift:66` is NOT annotated `nonisolated`, so under `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` it is implicitly `@MainActor`. Its `startObserving` is called from `HomeView.init()` and `MovieSwiftMacApp.init()` which run on the main actor. Crucially, the `onChange` callback from `withObservationTracking` explicitly re-enters the main actor via `Task { @MainActor in ... }` (line 98) before calling `update` or `arm`. So `SpotlightStoreObserver` is safe: it is entirely main-actor-isolated, called from main-actor contexts, and its `CSSearchableIndex` calls happen inside a `@MainActor` task — CoreSpotlight's indexing calls are thread-safe but the pattern is clean. This differs from `MetricKitCrashReporter` because MetricKit's framework-owned callback delivery is outside the app's control; Spotlight's onChange mechanism goes through our own code and the `Task { @MainActor in }` hop is ours.

**4. Test regression guard.**

Yes, the test guards the regression compile-time, which is the strongest possible guarantee here. If someone removed `nonisolated` from the class, the Swift 6 compiler would refuse to call `reporter.didReceive([])` from inside `DispatchQueue.global().async` because `didReceive` would again be main-actor-isolated, and calling a main-actor method from a nonisolated synchronous closure is a Swift 6 compile error (`error: sending '...' risks causing data races`). The test fails the build, not just a runtime assertion. The empty-array approach is sound for this purpose.

The one strengthening worth adding (see should-fix): call both `didReceive` overloads, not just the diagnostic one. The metric payload overload (`[MXMetricPayload]`) has the same isolation and the same off-main delivery risk.

**5. Comment accuracy, pbxproj, lint/readability.**

The pbxproj edits are correct: one `PBXFileReference` entry for the new file, and one `PBXBuildFile` reference per test target (iOS `A1B2C3070000000000000001`, macOS `E4ABCE3F3875BFA94B557F13`, tvOS `FABB29B9F71F5891A08DBCA0`), all pointing at the same `fileRef`. The file is listed under the `MovieSwiftTests` group in the navigator section at line 1242, which is correct. The comment accuracy is good with the one gap noted above (dropped usage instruction). No new `swiftlint:disable` annotations were added.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the crash fix and test are sound, but the `nonisolated` comment should explicitly state that `startObserving`/`stopObserving` must still be called from main-actor context (the compiler can no longer verify this), and both `didReceive` overloads should be exercised in the test; everything else is nit-level.

8	    /// `nonisolated` + `@unchecked Sendable`: MetricKit invokes the subscriber
9	    /// callbacks on a background queue, so this must NOT be a `@MainActor` type.
10	    /// The project builds with `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`, which
11	    /// would otherwise make this type — and its `didReceive` callbacks — implicitly
12	    /// main-actor-isolated; `@unchecked Sendable` alone does NOT opt out of that.
13	    /// A main-actor callback invoked off the main queue trips the Swift 6 runtime
14	    /// executor check and traps (`EXC_BREAKPOINT`) on the next launch that has a
15	    /// pending payload — a launch crash loop. `nonisolated` opts the whole type
16	    /// back out of main-actor isolation. Its only mutable state, `isObserving`, is
17	    /// touched solely by start/stop at app launch on the main thread; the
18	    /// `didReceive` callbacks just write files. We own that confinement, which makes
19	    /// the `shared` singleton safe to share.
20	    final nonisolated class MetricKitCrashReporter: NSObject, MXMetricManagerSubscriber, @unchecked Sendable {
21	        static let shared = MetricKitCrashReporter()
22	
23	        private var isObserving = false
24	
25	        /// Subscribes to MetricKit. Idempotent — calling twice doesn't
26	        /// re-register.
27	        func startObserving() {
28	            guard !isObserving else { return }
29	            MXMetricManager.shared.add(self)
30	            isObserving = true
31	        }
32	
33	        /// Unsubscribes. Useful for tests; production typically never
34	        /// stops observing.
35	        func stopObserving() {
36	            guard isObserving else { return }
37	            MXMetricManager.shared.remove(self)
38	            isObserving = false
39	        }

The CI watcher is running. Here's where things landed:

## Diagnosis → fix

You ran the macOS app; I built it, captured the crash report, and found the real cause — **not** either of my code-reading guesses (App Intents / state decode), but a **Swift 6 main-actor isolation trap**:

- MetricKit delivers `didReceive(_:)` on a **background queue**, but `MetricKitCrashReporter` was implicitly `@MainActor` (the project's `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` default — and `@unchecked Sendable` does *not* opt out of it). Off-main → `EXC_BREAKPOINT`/SIGTRAP → a **crash loop** (each trap writes a diagnostic that's re-delivered next launch).
- **Why CI stayed green:** the UI-smoke launch path skips `startObserving()` and ephemeral CI sims have no payload backlog, so the real delivery path is never exercised. Your installed app had the backlog → instant re-crash.

**Fix:** mark the reporter `nonisolated`. Went through the full pipeline — TDD (compile-time regression guard, red→green proven), verifier PASS, code-reviewer (FIX-FIRST → all should-fixes applied; the two nits turned out to be formatter-owned), re-verified (lint + iOS test + tvOS build green). It's [PR #55](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/55); I'll merge once CI is green.

## Two things worth flagging

1. **Your local crash backlog:** even with this fix deployed, your machine has accumulated `Film-O-Matic-*.ips` reports in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/`. The fix stops *new* crashes; the old reports are harmless but you can clear them.
2. **Stale `Localizable.xcstrings`:** every build regenerates string-catalog entries (the committed catalog is behind the UI source). I reverted that drift from this PR, but it'll keep showing as a dirty file on every build until someone commits the regeneration — a small housekeeping item, separate from this fix.

Want me to spin #2 off as its own cleanup task, and should I keep going to merge #55 when CI passes?

I now have the full picture. The macOS problems are concrete:

1. **`Form`/`Section`** renders as a settings list on macOS — floating headers, no dialog structure.
2. **`SearchField`** is built around a `GeometryReader` + fixed `.frame(height: 44)` for scroll-offset tracking; dropped into a Form row it collapses into that tiny broken box on the right.
3. **"Name:" + TextField** crammed into an `HStack` — misaligned.
4. **"Create"/"Cancel"** are plain colored text rows, not a real button footer.
5. No fixed sheet width and no disabled-Create-when-empty.

(Good news: this view is iOS+macOS only — it's not in the tvOS target, since `SearchField` is `unavailable` there — so the redesign is two platforms, not three.)
