# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite

## Modules
Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance:
- `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams
- `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards
- `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls
- `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth)
- `art` — illustration and generative art
Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance.

**Complexity budget — hard limits:**
- Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box.
- Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp.
- Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams.

If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything.

**Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `<h2 class="sr-only">` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `<title>` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.)

You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat.

## Core Design System

These rules apply to ALL use cases.

### Philosophy
- **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins.
- **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces.
- **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text.
- **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget.

### Streaming
Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early.
- **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last.
- **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately.
- Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream.
- Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS.
- Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead.

### Rules
- No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming)
- No font-size below 11px
- No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths.
- No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects
- No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg)
- **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-serif)`.
- **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--color-text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI.
- **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings.
- **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only.
- The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element.
- Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height.
- No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments.
- When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray.
- **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)` (or `-lg` for cards) in HTML. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill.
- **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides.
- **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above.
- **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits).
- No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.)
- No nested scrolling — auto-fit height.
- Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows.
- **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails.

### CSS Variables
**Backgrounds**: `--color-background-primary` (white), `-secondary` (surfaces), `-tertiary` (page bg), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning`
**Text**: `--color-text-primary` (black), `-secondary` (muted), `-tertiary` (hints), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning`
**Borders**: `--color-border-tertiary` (0.15α, default), `-secondary` (0.3α, hover), `-primary` (0.4α), semantic `-info/-danger/-success/-warning`
**Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-serif`, `--font-mono`
**Layout**: `--border-radius-md` (8px), `--border-radius-lg` (12px — preferred for most components), `--border-radius-xl` (16px)
All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables.

**Dark mode is mandatory** — every color must work in both modes:
- In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes — they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors.
- In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp.
- In HTML: always use CSS variables (--color-text-primary, --color-text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode.
- Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable?

### sendPrompt(text)
A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead.

### Links
`<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly.

## When nothing fits
Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly:
- Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory
- Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object
- All core design system rules still apply
- Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking


## UI components

### Layout width
The widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns — auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width.

### Aesthetic
Flat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai — like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else.

### Tokens
- Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--color-border-tertiary)` (or `-secondary` for emphasis)
- Corner radius: `var(--border-radius-md)` for most elements, `var(--border-radius-lg)` for cards
- Cards: white bg (`var(--color-background-primary)`), 0.5px border, radius-lg, padding 1rem 1.25rem
- Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled — write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width).
- Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px border-secondary, hover bg-secondary, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a ↗ arrow.
- **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts — `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context — integers for counts, 1–2 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step="1"` (or step="0.1" etc.) so the input itself emits round values.
- Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px)
- Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs

### Metric cards
For summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) — surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--color-background-secondary)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border).

### Layout
- Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally
- Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing
- Don't put tables here — output them as markdown in your response text

**Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default — children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp.

**Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (≤700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper.

### Mockup presentation
Contained mockups — mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components — should sit on a background surface (`var(--color-background-secondary)` container with `border-radius: var(--border-radius-lg)` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper.

### 1. Interactive explainer — learn how something works
*"Explain how compound interest works" / "Teach me about sorting algorithms"*

Use HTML for the interactive controls — sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. Whitespace is the container.

```html
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;">
  <label style="font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);">Years</label>
  <input type="range" min="1" max="40" value="20" id="years" style="flex: 1;" />
  <span style="font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; min-width: 24px;" id="years-out">20</span>
</div>

<div style="display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;">
  <span style="font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);">£1,000 →</span>
  <span style="font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500;" id="result">£3,870</span>
</div>

<div style="margin: 2rem 0; position: relative; height: 240px;">
  <canvas id="chart"></canvas>
</div>
```

Use `sendPrompt()` to let users ask follow-ups: `sendPrompt('What if I increase the rate to 10%?')`

### 2. Compare options — decision making
*"Compare pricing and features of these products" / "Help me choose between React and Vue"*

Use HTML. Side-by-side card grid for options. Highlight differences with semantic colors. Interactive elements for filtering or weighting.

- Each option in a card. Use badges for key differentiators. A leading Tabler icon (`<i class="ti ti-NAME">` at 20px, `aria-hidden`) anchors each option visually — pick the most apt name per option.
- Add `sendPrompt()` buttons: `sendPrompt('Tell me more about the Pro plan')`
- Don't put comparison tables inside this tool — output them as regular markdown tables in your response text instead. The tool is for the visual card grid only.
- When one option is recommended or "most popular", accent its card with `border: 2px solid var(--color-border-info)` only (2px is deliberate — the only exception to the 0.5px rule, used to accent featured items) — keep the same background and border as the other cards. Add a small badge (e.g. "Most popular") above or inside the card header using `background: var(--color-background-info); color: var(--color-text-info); font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)`.

### 3. Data record — bounded UI object
*"Show me a Salesforce contact card" / "Create a receipt for this order"*

Use HTML. Wrap the entire thing in a single raised card. All content is sans-serif since it's pure UI. Use an avatar/initials circle for people (see example below).

```html

## Color palette

9 color ramps, each with 7 stops from lightest to darkest. 50 = lightest fill, 100-200 = light fills, 400 = mid tones, 600 = strong/border, 800-900 = text on light fills.

| Class | Ramp | 50 (lightest) | 100 | 200 | 400 | 600 | 800 | 900 (darkest) |
|-------|------|------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|------|
| `c-purple` | Purple | #EEEDFE | #CECBF6 | #AFA9EC | #7F77DD | #534AB7 | #3C3489 | #26215C |
| `c-teal` | Teal | #E1F5EE | #9FE1CB | #5DCAA5 | #1D9E75 | #0F6E56 | #085041 | #04342C |
| `c-coral` | Coral | #FAECE7 | #F5C4B3 | #F0997B | #D85A30 | #993C1D | #712B13 | #4A1B0C |
| `c-pink` | Pink | #FBEAF0 | #F4C0D1 | #ED93B1 | #D4537E | #993556 | #72243E | #4B1528 |
| `c-gray` | Gray | #F1EFE8 | #D3D1C7 | #B4B2A9 | #888780 | #5F5E5A | #444441 | #2C2C2A |
| `c-blue` | Blue | #E6F1FB | #B5D4F4 | #85B7EB | #378ADD | #185FA5 | #0C447C | #042C53 |
| `c-green` | Green | #EAF3DE | #C0DD97 | #97C459 | #639922 | #3B6D11 | #27500A | #173404 |
| `c-amber` | Amber | #FAEEDA | #FAC775 | #EF9F27 | #BA7517 | #854F0B | #633806 | #412402 |
| `c-red` | Red | #FCEBEB | #F7C1C1 | #F09595 | #E24B4A | #A32D2D | #791F1F | #501313 |

**How to assign colors**: Color should encode meaning, not sequence. Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead:
- Group nodes by **category** — all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal.
- For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** — warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert.
- Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps).
- Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp.
- **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept — those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.)

**Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --color-text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** — title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds.

**Light/dark mode quick pick** — use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values:
- **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle**
- **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle**
- Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` — paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke="#..."` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink.

For status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. For categorical coloring in both diagrams and UI, use these ramps.

MovieSwift/Packages/UI/Sources/UI/fields/SearchTextObservable.swift
import SwiftUI
import Combine

// `@MainActor`: this drives a SwiftUI search field and is subclassed by
// main-actor view models in the app target. Isolating it to the main
// actor keeps that hierarchy consistent under the app's default-MainActor
// mode. The debounce pipeline below is scheduled on `DispatchQueue.main`,
// so its sink genuinely runs on the main actor.
@MainActor
open class SearchTextObservable: ObservableObject {
    @Published public var searchText = "" {
        willSet {
            // Forward raw changes immediately for anyone observing the subject
            searchSubject.send(newValue)
        }
        didSet {
            onUpdateText(text: searchText)
        }
    }

    public let searchSubject = PassthroughSubject<String, Never>()

    // Store all subscriptions here to ensure proper lifetime management.
    // No explicit deinit cleanup: each AnyCancellable cancels itself when
    // the set is deallocated, and a nonisolated deinit can't touch this
    // main-actor-isolated, non-Sendable property under the Swift 6 mode.
    private var cancellables = Set<AnyCancellable>()

    public init() {
        // Debounced, distinct, non-empty search text
        searchSubject
            .debounce(for: .milliseconds(500), scheduler: DispatchQueue.main)
            .removeDuplicates()
            .filter { !$0.isEmpty }
            .sink { [weak self] searchText in
                // Hop to the main actor to call the main-actor
                // `onUpdateTextDebounced` hook. `Task { @MainActor }` rather
                // than `MainActor.assumeIsolated` because Combine's GCD
                // scheduling isn't a hard main-actor-executor guarantee; the
                // extra runloop tick is immaterial for an already-debounced
                // search field.
                Task { @MainActor in
                    self?.onUpdateTextDebounced(text: searchText)
                }
            }
            .store(in: &cancellables)
    }

    open func onUpdateText(text: String) {
        /// Overwrite by your subclass to get instant text update.
    }

    open func onUpdateTextDebounced(text: String) {
        /// Overwrite by your subclass to get debounced text update.
    }
}

## Code review — fix/custom-list-form-redesign

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, missing tests, CI-blocking lint)

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:307` — Pre-existing crash reproduced verbatim: `Int.random(in: props.customListsCount ..< 1000 ^ 3)`**

`1000 ^ 3` is bitwise XOR (= `1003`), not exponentiation. The effective range is `customListsCount..<1003`. If a user has created 1003 or more custom lists, `Int.random(in:)` receives an empty or inverted range and the app terminates with a fatal error. The redesign's `submit()` refactor is exactly the right moment to fix this — the old form-splitting obscured it, but the new `submit()` makes it a naked, obvious crash site. You flagged you were carrying it forward intentionally, but shipping a knowingly trap-able path on a PR that touches this exact line is hard to defend. Suggested fix:

```swift
let newId = (props.customLists.keys.max() ?? -1) + 1
let newList = CustomList(id: newId, name: trimmedName, …)
```

Using `max() + 1` is also semantically safer (no collision with existing IDs, no range assertion).

---

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift:15` — `@Suite` removed, diverging from project convention**

The original file had `@Suite @MainActor`. The diff removes `@Suite` (visible in `git show main:…` which shows `@Suite @MainActor struct CustomListTests`). Every other `@MainActor` test suite in the target (`MovieDetailStateTests`, `PeopleActionsTests`, `DiscoverTests`, `AppCompositionTests`, `MoviesListingTests`, etc.) retains `@Suite @MainActor`. Without `@Suite`, the struct still runs (Swift Testing auto-discovers it), but the removal diverges from the codebase-wide pattern with no stated reason. Restore `@Suite`:

```swift
@Suite @MainActor
struct CustomListTests {
```

---

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:229-240` — `bindDispatchSearches` called in `onAppear` captures a stale `props.dispatch`**

`onAppear` fires once when the form appears and re-binds the dispatch closure capturing `props.dispatch` at that snapshot. If the store's `Store` object is replaced or the dispatch function changes between renders (unlikely in practice for this app's in-process store, but architecturally fragile), searches would route through the old closure. All other `ConnectedView`s that use `SearchField` (e.g. `MoviesList`, `FanClubHome`) have the same pattern, so this is not a new regression, but a comment noting the limitation would help future maintainers:

```swift
// `onAppear` fires once; `dispatch` is captured from the initial props.
// In this app the dispatch function is stable for the app's lifetime, so
// this is safe — but rebinding in `body(props:)` every render would be
// more architecturally correct if that assumption ever changes.
```

---

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift` — Missing test: `submit()` trimming is not unit-tested**

`canSubmit(name:)` is well-tested at line 135. But `submit()` independently trims the name before dispatching — `canSubmit` might return `true` for `"  Favorites  "` while `submit` dispatches `"Favorites"`. There is no test that asserts the trimmed name reaches the reducer. The test that should exist:

```swift
@Test func customListFormSubmitTrimmsNameBeforeDispatch() {
    // Construct a form state where listName = "  Favorites  " and
    // invoke submit logic: the dispatched EditCustomList/AddCustomList title
    // should be "Favorites", not "  Favorites  ".
}
```

Since `submit()` is a private view method that touches `props.dispatch` (which requires a live store), the practical approach is to extract the trim-and-dispatch logic into `CustomListFormState` and test the static function directly. Alternatively, document in the `canSubmit` test that the trim contract is shared — but a separate test is cleaner.

---

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:191-208` — Silent "ghost cover" state when `listMovieCover != nil` but `props.coverMovie == nil`**

`coverSection` shows `selectedCover` only when `listMovieCover != nil, let movie = props.coverMovie`. If `listMovieCover` is set (e.g. when editing an existing list whose cover movie hasn't been fetched into `moviesState.movies` yet), both branches are skipped: the selected-cover row doesn't appear, nor does the search field. The user sees only the "Cover" label with blank space beneath it, with no way to remove the cover or search for a replacement. A fallback to the search field when `props.coverMovie == nil` would be safer:

```swift
if listMovieCover != nil, let movie = props.coverMovie {
    selectedCover(movie)
} else {
    // listMovieCover set but movie not yet in state — treat as no cover
    // so the user can search rather than seeing a blank section
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
        searchField
        …
    }
}
```

The current code already does this implicitly — the `else` branch covers the case — but looking at it again: `if listMovieCover != nil, let movie = props.coverMovie` is a compound condition where if `listMovieCover` is `nil` OR `props.coverMovie` is `nil`, the else branch runs. So the else *does* show the search field when `listMovieCover != nil && coverMovie == nil`. The search field would appear with the existing text in `searchTextWrapper.searchText` (empty, unless the user has typed). This is actually fine behavior, not a blank hole. Disregard the must-fix escalation; this is a nit worth a brief inline comment explaining the intentional fallback:

```swift
// Shows the search field when no cover is set, OR when the set cover's
// movie hasn't yet been fetched into state (e.g. on first appear for an
// existing list) — the user can re-search or the section self-heals once
// the movie is in state.
} else {
```

---

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:79` — `@StateObject` annotation on a `ConnectedView` struct: correct, but worth a brief rationale comment**

The switch from `@State` to `@StateObject` is architecturally correct. With `@State`, typing in the inline `TextField` bound to `$searchTextWrapper.searchText` would not cause `StoreConnector` to call `map()` again, so `props.searchedMovies` would lag until the next store change (the debounced `FetchSearch` action). `@StateObject` subscribes `StoreConnector`'s parent to `@Published` changes on the wrapper, so the "No movies found." text and the results strip update immediately on each keystroke. However, all other `ConnectedView`s (`MoviesList`, `FanClubHome`, `CustomListDetail`) use `@State` with `SearchField` providing the reactivity via its own `@ObservedObject`. A comment explaining why this one is different from the others will prevent a future reviewer from "normalizing" it back to `@State`:

```swift
// @StateObject (not @State): the inline TextField binds directly to
// $searchTextWrapper.searchText, so SwiftUI must subscribe to @Published
// changes to re-trigger map() and update props.searchedMovies. Other
// ConnectedViews use @State + SearchField, which provides its own
// @ObservedObject subscription internally.
@StateObject private var searchTextWrapper = CustomListFormSearchWrapper()
```

---

**`MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift` (iOS layout, line 262-275) — No keyboard avoidance on the non-scrollable iOS content area**

The iOS layout is `NavigationStack > VStack(spacing: 0) { content-VStack + Spacer + Divider + footer }`. There is no `ScrollView` wrapping the content. On smaller devices (iPhone SE) with the keyboard raised, the `Spacer` compresses but SwiftUI's default keyboard avoidance might push the footer's Divider behind the keyboard if the content-VStack is taller than the remaining safe area. The name field and search field together with a results strip (150pt poster height) already exceed 300pt, leaving little room before the keyboard's ~300pt footprint. Adding `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` requires a `ScrollView`; alternatively, wrapping only the content VStack in a `ScrollView` (not the footer) would keep the footer anchored and allow the content to scroll when the keyboard is up. This is a layout robustness issue, not a crash, so "should fix" rather than must-fix.

---

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

- `/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:126-143` — The inline `searchField` computed property duplicates the "clear-when-empty" pattern from `SearchField.swift` without the `isSearching` side-effect, which is correct here. But the structural similarity makes the divergence easy to miss. A single-line comment `// Inline replacement for SearchField; no isSearching flag needed here.` would make that deliberate.

- `/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:151-168` — The `selectedCover` helper takes a non-optional `Movie` and is only called from the `let movie = props.coverMovie` bind. The helper's name suggests it could accept optional. Fine as is, but `selectedCover(for movie: Movie)` with the `for:` label would read more clearly at the call site.

- `/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift:97-103` — `customListFormSearchWrapperDoesNotDispatchWithoutInjectedHandler` ends with `#expect(true)`. This test passes vacuously — it asserts nothing about the actual behavior (no crash, no dispatch). The intent is "must not crash", which is meaningful, but `#expect(true)` doesn't communicate that. A comment like `// No assertion needed — the test passes if no crash occurs.` would clarify the intent and avoid a future reader wondering why it's there.

- `/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/custom list/CustomListForm.swift:279-295` — The `header` computed property is defined at the struct level without a `#if os(macOS)` guard, but it is only referenced inside `#if os(macOS)` in `layout(props:)`. The iOS compiler still compiles it. This is harmless (SwiftUI view builders that are never called don't run) but compiling unused view code on iOS is mildly wasteful. Wrapping it in `#if os(macOS)` would match the intent.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — address the `1000 ^ 3` crash site (it lives in the exact line the refactor touched) and restore `@Suite` on `CustomListTests` before merging; the `@StateObject` reasoning comment and the missing trim-dispatch test are strong should-fixes that would block a human reviewer's approval even if they don't block CI.

### Pre-existing failure (not introduced by this change)

`testMyListsCreateCustomListAppearsInListAfterSave` in `MovieSwiftMacUITests` fails both on `main` and on this branch with the same symptom:

```
MovieSwiftMacUITests.swift:519: Failed to get matching snapshot:
No matches found … '"customListForm.nameField" IN identifiers'
```

On `main` the app also fails to present `nameField` ("XCTAssertTrue failed" after the 15 s timeout). On the branch it additionally logs "Lost connection to the application" on one iteration before the retry. The root cause — macOS sheet not surfacing the form's elements to the accessibility tree — exists independently of this change. The cancel flow (`testMyListsCreateCustomListCancelDismissesWithoutSaving`) passes on both baseline and branch.

### Deferred to CI

- `package-tests` / `check_coverage.sh` — change touches only app-level sources (`CustomListForm.swift`, `CustomListTests.swift`), not `MovieSwift/Packages/`. Package coverage numbers are unaffected. CI will run the full coverage gate.
- `ios-tests-ipad` — the layout change is exercised on iPhone above; the iPad CI gate scopes to `testLaunchShowsMainTabs` + `MovieSwiftTests`, which is covered by the unit run above. CI will run it.
- `tvos-tests` — `CustomListForm` is excluded from the tvOS target; the build confirmed no regression. Full tvOS test suite deferred to CI.
- `mac-tests` full suite — macOS UI test for the create-save flow is pre-existing broken on both `main` and branch; all other macOS UI tests deferred to CI.

### Verdict

PASS — ready for code review.

SwiftLint: 0 violations. iOS and macOS compile cleanly. All 27 `CustomListTests` (including both new tests `customListFormCanSubmitRequiresANonBlankName` and `customListFormSanitizedNameTrimsSurroundingWhitespace`) pass on iPhone 17 Pro and macOS. The three iOS UI flows (`testMyListsCreateCustomListShowsForm`, `testMyListsCreateCustomListAppearsInListAfterSave`, `testMyListsCreateCustomListCancelDismissesWithoutSaving`) all pass. > AGENT

I investigated thoroughly, and the finding **inverts the premise of this chore** — here's what's actually true:

**The catalog is already in sync for clean builds.** Three clean builds (iOS + macOS + tvOS) *and* a `build-for-testing` left `Localizable.xcstrings` with **zero diff**. The earlier "every build dirties it" was an incremental/shared-derived-data (or Xcode-IDE) artifact that doesn't reproduce with clean CLI builds.

**There are no translations to protect.** The catalog is **English-only** (`sourceLanguage: en`, no `fr`/`es`/`de`/etc. blocks). It's just a source-string mirror — any missing key falls back to the literal string at runtime, with zero user-facing impact.

**The only "staleness" is cosmetic and harmless.** A few brand-new redesign strings (`"Search for a movie…"`, `"No movies found."`, `"Give your list a name…"`) aren't in the catalog. Adding them isn't a reproducible CLI step — it requires Xcode's IDE "extract" — and since the app is English-only, their absence does nothing.

This is exactly the "extraction is non-deterministic → document the finding instead of fighting it" case the task itself anticipated. **Committing a non-reproducible regeneration of a generated, English-only asset would be churn with no benefit.**

My recommendation: **drop the chore** — delete the empty branch, no PR.

Now I have the complete picture. The macOS rows (`customListsRows`, 443–470) are tap-gesture driven with **no delete path at all** — and the `.onDelete` at line 82 belongs to the iOS-only `customListsSection`, which macOS never uses. So macOS has zero delete capability.

The fix: a macOS context-menu "Delete" + Delete-key support on the highlighted row, both routed through a confirmation alert that dispatches the existing `RemoveCustomList`. Let me see `MyListsPresentation` (for a TDD-able confirmation message) and the state vars:

## Code review — fix/macos-delete-custom-list

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, missing tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:373-374` — `selectedCustomList` is not cleared after deletion**

After the alert's Delete button fires, `highlightedItemId` is cleared (line 374) but `selectedCustomList` is left untouched. In the happy path the user has not opened the detail (so `selectedCustomList` is nil and everything is fine), but consider: user highlights a row and navigates in (double-tap or Return → `selectedCustomList = CustomListNav(id: X)`), Cmd+[ back, row still highlighted, presses Delete key, confirms. At that moment `selectedCustomList` still holds `CustomListNav(id: X)`. The `NavigationStack` is driven by `$selectedCustomList`, so after `RemoveCustomList` commits, the next re-render resolves `selectedCustomList` → `CustomListDetail(listId: X)` where X is now gone from the store, landing on `Text("List not found")` until the user explicitly navigates back. The fix is one line alongside the existing `highlightedItemId` clear:

```swift
if highlightedItemId == list.id { highlightedItemId = nil }
if selectedCustomList?.id == list.id { selectedCustomList = nil }
```

This makes the NavigationStack pop the detail rather than display a stale "List not found" screen.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift:210-219` — the one new test covers only the pure helper; the guard logic in `requestDeleteHighlightedCustomList` has no test**

`requestDeleteHighlightedCustomList` has three distinct branches: returns `.ignored` when the active section is not Custom Lists; returns `.ignored` when no item is highlighted; sets `listPendingDeletion` (and returns `.handled`) when the guard passes. None of these are exercised by the new test. The existing test `myListsDeleteConfirmationMessageNamesTheListAndReassuresAboutMovies` only validates the string helper that feeds the alert message. The TDD rule requires behaviour changes to ship with tests in the same commit. The tests that should exist:

- `myListsRequestDeleteIgnoredWhenSectionIsNotCustomLists` — a `MyListsPresentation`-layer or extracted helper test (or at minimum a comment acknowledging the visual-only gap with a structural assertion) verifying the section guard.
- `myListsRequestDeleteIgnoredWhenNoItemHighlighted` — guard on `highlightedItemId`.

Because this logic lives in a `private func` inside a `ConnectedView`, a unit test requires either making `requestDeleteHighlightedCustomList` `internal` behind a testability flag or extracting the section-guard logic into `MyListsPresentation` (similar to how `deleteConfirmationMessage` was extracted). Extracting is the lower-friction path and consistent with the existing `MyListsPresentation` pattern.

---

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, correctness-adjacent)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:55-59` — `.map(\.self)` on `Set<Int>` is semantically misleading**

`state.moviesState.wishlist` is `Set<Int>`, so `.map(\.self)` converts it to `[Int]` via an identity key-path. This compiles and is correct, but `\.self` as an identity transform on a value type reads as noise — a reader will wonder whether a custom `Hashable` projection was intended. The pre-existing `map { $0 }` was no better, but since the PR touched these lines the idiomatic replacement is `Array(state.moviesState.wishlist)` which makes the Set-to-Array conversion explicit. This is a pre-existing style debt that the PR's reformat surfaced.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:519-527` — context-menu "Open" item has no `Label` / system image, while "Delete List" does**

```swift
Button("Open") { selectedCustomList = CustomListNav(id: list.id) }
Divider()
Button(role: .destructive) { ... } label: { Label("Delete List", systemImage: "trash") }
```

macOS renders context-menu icons from SF Symbols when a `Label` is used. "Delete List" gets a trash icon; "Open" gets none. The inconsistency is minor but slightly unpolished. Suggested fix: `Label("Open", systemImage: "arrow.up.right.square")` (or `"eye"` per project icon conventions).

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:66-101` — macOS dead code in `customListsSection`**

Lines 75–86 (`#if os(macOS)` button block inside `customListsSection`) compile into the macOS target but are unreachable: `customListsSection` is called only from the `#else` branch of `listView` (line 165-198), which is never compiled on macOS. This is pre-existing code that the PR reformatted without removing. It's not introduced by the PR, so not a blocker, but it's a readability hazard — the macOS-specific button handlers here (`.onKeyPress(.return)`, `.onKeyPress(space)`) will mislead anyone reading this file about how macOS navigation actually works. A follow-up should remove the `#if os(macOS)` block inside `customListsSection` or add a comment that `customListsSection` is iOS/tvOS-only.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift:76-78` and `95-97` — pre-existing vacuous tests (`#expect(true)`)**

`customListSearchMovieTextWrapperDoesNotDispatchWithoutInjectedHandler` and `customListFormSearchWrapperDoesNotDispatchWithoutInjectedHandler` both end in `#expect(true)`, which means they pass regardless of what the code under test does. These are pre-existing and not introduced by this PR, but worth a follow-up to add a meaningful structural assertion (e.g. verify no exception is thrown and the wrapper's internal state is unchanged).

---

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:332` — The inline comment `// Delete key removes the highlighted custom list (via confirmation).` is accurate, but the companion doc-comment on `requestDeleteHighlightedCustomList` (lines 382-383) covers the same territory. One or the other is sufficient.
- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:368-379` — The derived `Binding` (`get: { listPendingDeletion != nil }, set: { if !$0 { listPendingDeletion = nil } }`) is the canonical pattern for `alert(isPresented:presenting:)` and is correct. No issue, but extracting it to a computed property `private var isDeletionAlertPresented: Binding<Bool>` would make the `.alert` call at lines 368-379 shorter and self-documenting.
- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:19` — The curly-quote string `""\(list.name)" will be deleted…"` is fine for English but will not localize cleanly in `.xcstrings` interpolation. Acceptable for now given the rest of the file uses hardcoded strings too.

> AGENT

Diagnosis and fix summary while CI runs:

**You were right — custom lists were undeletable on macOS.** The delete logic existed (`RemoveCustomList` reducer) but was only wired to iOS swipe-to-delete (`.onDelete`); the macOS My Lists view uses tap-gesture buttons where `.onDelete` does nothing, so there was no affordance at all.

**Fix ([PR #57](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/57)):** two macOS-native ways to delete, both with a confirmation —
- **Right-click → Delete List** on any custom-list row
- **Delete key** when a row is highlighted

Plus: deleting the list you currently have open now pops back instead of showing a stale detail. iOS keeps its swipe-to-delete unchanged.

Went through the full pipeline — TDD (two new unit tests), verifier PASS, code-reviewer (FIX-FIRST → fixed the open-detail-stale bug + extracted the guard logic to be testable), re-verified across platforms. CI watcher running; I'll merge when green.

One thing worth your call: the **wishlist and seenlist sections have the same macOS gap** (their `.onDelete` is also inert on macOS) — though those are removable elsewhere (the heart/eye toggles on a movie). Want me to extend the same context-menu/Delete-key treatment to them in a follow-up, or leave it since there's another path?

enum MyListsPresentation {
    static func customLists(from customLists: [Int: CustomList]) -> [CustomList] {
        customLists.compactMap(\.value)
    }

    static func sortedMovies(_ movies: [Int], by sort: MoviesSort, state: AppState) -> [Int] {
        movies.sortedMoviesIds(by: sort, state: state)
    }

    /// Confirmation copy for deleting a custom list. Names the list and
    /// reassures that deleting the grouping doesn't remove the movies
    /// themselves from the user's other lists.
    static func deleteConfirmationMessage(for list: CustomList) -> String {
        "“\(list.name)” will be deleted. The movies in it won't be removed from your other lists."
    }

    /// The custom list a macOS Delete-key press should target: the highlighted
    /// row, but only while the Custom Lists section is showing and the
    /// highlighted id actually resolves to a list. Returns `nil` (a no-op) in
    /// every other case so the key press falls through to other handlers.
    static func customListToDelete(highlightedId: Int?,
                                   isCustomListsSection: Bool,
                                   customLists: [CustomList]) -> CustomList? {
        guard isCustomListsSection, let highlightedId else {
            return nil
        }
        return customLists.first { $0.id == highlightedId }
    }
}

No-op\n        /// (so the key falls through) when nothing is highlighted.\n        private func requestDeleteHighlighted(props: Props) -> KeyPress.Result {\n            let section = (MyListsSection(rawValue: selectedList) ?? .wishlist).kind\n            switch MyListsPresentation.highlightedDeletion(section: section, highlightedId: highlightedItemId) {\n            case let .removeFromWishlist(movie):\n                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.RemoveFromWishlist(movie: movie))\n                clearHighlightIfEquals(movie)\n            case let .removeFromSeenlist(movie):\n                props.dispatch(MoviesActions.RemoveFromSeenList(movie: movie))\n                clearHighlightIfEquals(movie)\n            case let .deleteCustomList(id):\n                guard let list = props.customLists.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return .ignored }\n                listPendingDeletion = list\n            case .none:\n                return .ignored\n            }\n            return .handled\n        }\n\n        private func clearHighlightIfEquals(_ id: Int) {\n            if highlightedItemId == id { highlightedItemId = nil }\n        }"

## Code review — fix/macos-delete-wishlist-seenlist

### Design question (addressed inline)

The immediate-removal design for wishlist/seenlist vs. confirmed deletion for custom lists is sound. The rationale is explicitly documented in the inline comment (line 515-518) and mirrors iOS swipe behaviour. Heart/eye toggles make this reversible at any time. No concern here.

---

### Findings

**1. Stale comment on line 368 — Delete key handler**

Line 368 in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift`:

```
// Delete key removes the highlighted custom list (via confirmation).
```

This comment predates the generalization. The handler now also removes wishlist/seenlist movies immediately (without confirmation). The comment only describes the custom-list path and misleads the next reader about what the other two sections do.

**2. Dead `case .customLists: break` branch in `removeMovie` — invites future misuse**

Lines 536-543 in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift`:

```swift
private func removeMovie(id: Int, section: MyListsSection, props: Props) {
    switch section {
    case .wishlist: ...
    case .seenlist: ...
    case .customLists: break      // ← silent no-op
    }
    clearHighlightIfEquals(id)   // ← still runs, clears highlight for nothing
```

`moviesRows` is only ever called with `.wishlist` or `.seenlist` (the two call sites in `currentSectionContent` confirm this), so `.customLists` is unreachable today. But:

- If a future caller adds a third call site passing `.customLists`, `removeMovie` silently does nothing except clear the highlight, with no compiler warning or runtime signal.
- `clearHighlightIfEquals(id)` runs even when `section == .customLists`, which is a spurious state mutation on an unreachable path.

The custom-list context menu's destructive button sets `listPendingDeletion` directly (line 610) and never calls `removeMovie` — that's correct. But since `removeMovie` can structurally receive `.customLists`, it should either `assertionFailure` or use `preconditionFailure` to make the contract explicit, or be constrained to a type that excludes the custom-lists case.

**3. Test gap — `myListsHighlightedDeletionIsNoOpWithoutHighlight` doesn't cover `.seenlist`**

Lines 232-236 in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift`:

```swift
#expect(... section: .wishlist, highlightedId: nil ...) == .none)
#expect(... section: .customLists, highlightedId: nil ...) == .none)
```

`.seenlist` with `highlightedId: nil` is not asserted. The function is a trivial guard, so it's guaranteed to return `.none` for seenlist too — but the test's own comment says "Nothing highlighted → no-op" for all sections, and `.seenlist` is the only one not covered. Add:

```swift
#expect(MyListsPresentation.highlightedDeletion(section: .seenlist, highlightedId: nil) == MyListsPresentation.HighlightedDeletion.none)
```

**4. `ForEach` iteration keyed by `\.offset` rather than `\.element` — identity instability**

Line 486 in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MyLists.swift`:

```swift
ForEach(Array(movieIds.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, id in
```

Keying by offset means SwiftUI identifies rows by position, not by movie id. When a movie is removed from the middle of the list, the rows that follow shift their offsets: SwiftUI will diff the result by positional identity, potentially animating incorrect rows as "removed" and reusing views across different movie ids. The id should be `\.element` (the movie id itself):

```swift
ForEach(Array(movieIds.enumerated()), id: \.element) { _, id in
```

Or, more simply, since `movieIds` is `[Int]` and ids are unique within a list:

```swift
ForEach(movieIds, id: \.self) { id in
```

This bug exists in the code prior to this PR but the PR introduces the delete actions that will now trigger exactly this diffing path on the macOS movie rows. This is a pre-existing issue that this PR's delete affordance now makes user-visible.

**5. Context-menu "Remove from Seenlist" label — "Seenlist" is a product-internal term**

Line 529 in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift`:

```swift
Label("Remove from \(section.title)", systemImage: "trash")
```

`section.title` for `.seenlist` returns `"Seenlist"` (line 311), producing "Remove from Seenlist". The wishlist context menu in `MovieContextMenu` uses "Remove from Wishlist" — so Wishlist is consistent. Whether "Seenlist" is the right user-facing word is a product decision; it's used consistently in the tab label and empty-state copy, so it's consistent here too. This is a nit, not a bug.

**6. `removeMovie` clears highlight even when called from the context menu on a non-highlighted row**

Lines 536-543 in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift`:

```swift
clearHighlightIfEquals(id)
```

A user can right-click a row that is not the highlighted row and choose "Remove from Wishlist". `clearHighlightIfEquals` will only clear if `highlightedItemId == id`, so it won't incorrectly clear a different row's highlight. The guard inside `clearHighlightIfEquals` makes this safe. Not a bug — noting for completeness.

### Must fix (correctness, missing test coverage, stale-comment CI risk)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:540` — `case .customLists: break` in `removeMovie` is unreachable today but silently no-ops if a future call site passes `.customLists`, and `clearHighlightIfEquals` still runs. Add `assertionFailure("removeMovie called for customLists section — route custom-list deletion through listPendingDeletion instead")` (or `preconditionFailure`) to make the contract explicit and surface misuse at development time.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:486` — `ForEach(Array(movieIds.enumerated()), id: \.offset)` keys rows by position. A delete from the middle shifts offsets, causing SwiftUI to diff by wrong identity and animate the wrong rows as removed. Change to `id: \.element` (or use `ForEach(movieIds, id: \.self)`). This pre-existing bug is now user-visible because this PR introduces the delete affordance on these macOS rows.

### Should fix (readability, weak test, stale comment)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:368` — Comment reads "Delete key removes the highlighted custom list (via confirmation)." It predates the generalization. Should read something like: "Delete key removes the highlighted row: movies immediately (wishlist/seenlist), custom lists via confirmation." Otherwise the next reader will think movie sections are untouched by this handler.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwiftTests/CustomListTests.swift:232-236` — `myListsHighlightedDeletionIsNoOpWithoutHighlight` tests `.wishlist` and `.customLists` with `nil` highlight, but not `.seenlist`. The function is trivially correct for all sections (it's a single `guard`), but the test's stated intent ("Nothing highlighted → no-op") should cover all three. Add `#expect(MyListsPresentation.highlightedDeletion(section: .seenlist, highlightedId: nil) == MyListsPresentation.HighlightedDeletion.none)`.

### Nits

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:519-531` — The new context-menu items ("Open", "Remove from …") have no `accessibilityLabel` beyond the `Label` text string. That's actually correct for macOS context menus — `Label` text is the accessibility label. No action needed; calling this out as checked.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/myLists/MyLists.swift:444` — `clearHighlightIfEquals` is a one-liner helper used in two places. The name is clear and the implementation is correct. Consider whether it would read better inlined (`if highlightedItemId == id { highlightedItemId = nil }`) given its brevity, but the helper form is fine.

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — the `ForEach id: \.offset` identity bug will produce incorrect removal animations (wrong rows animate out) the moment the user deletes from a non-last position in a wishlist or seenlist on macOS, and the `case .customLists: break` in `removeMovie` should be an assertion before the function escapes review. Both are one-line fixes; stale comment and missing seenlist-nil test are quick follow-ons.

| Seenlist | right-click → Remove from Seenlist, Delete key | immediate (reversible via 👁 toggle) |

Both delete PRs (#57 custom lists, #58 wishlist/seenlist) went through the full pipeline and are merged; the Delete-key logic is now a single tested section-router, and I cleaned up a latent `ForEach` identity bug along the way. iOS keeps its swipe-to-delete unchanged throughout.

`main` is clean. Worth a quick real-app check on your end (pull `main`, right-click a row in each section) to confirm the affordances feel right, but functionally it's all verified. Whenever you're ready to move on, Phase 5 is still queued.

=== key providers (lines 20-70) ===

    public init(bundle: Bundle = .main) {
        self.bundle = bundle
    }

    public func apiKey() -> String? {
        guard let rawAPIKey = bundle.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "TMDB_API_KEY") as? String else {
            return nil
        }
        let value = rawAPIKey.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !value.isEmpty && value != "$(TMDB_API_KEY)" else {
            return nil
        }
        return value
    }
}

/// Resolves the user-supplied TMDB key from `AppUserDefaults`.
///
/// Returns nil when the stored value is empty or only whitespace so a
/// chained `LayeredAPIKeyProvider` cleanly falls through to the
/// bundled key. The provider re-reads UserDefaults on every
/// `apiKey()` call, so changes the user makes in Settings are picked
/// up by the next API request without needing to reinitialize
/// `APIService.shared`.
public struct UserDefaultsAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding {
    public init() {}

    public func apiKey() -> String? {
        let value = AppUserDefaults.userTMDBAPIKey.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        return value.isEmpty ? nil : value
    }
}

/// Tries each child provider in order and returns the first non-nil
/// key. Used to layer "user-supplied" over "bundled-default" so a
/// user's own TMDB key takes precedence without removing the bundled
/// fallback when the user hasn't entered one.
public struct LayeredAPIKeyProvider: APIKeyProviding {
    private let providers: [APIKeyProviding]

    public init(providers: [APIKeyProviding]) {
        self.providers = providers
    }

    public func apiKey() -> String? {
        for provider in providers {
            if let key = provider.apiKey() {
                return key
            }
        }
        return nil
    }
}

extension APIKeyProviding where Self == LayeredAPIKeyProvider {

> AGENT

Mystery solved — and it's **not a code bug**. Your app's region is set to **Albania (`AL`)**, and TMDB's "Now Playing" is region-filtered. I confirmed it against the live API with your bundled key:

| Region | Now Playing results |
|---|---|
| **AL (Albania)** — your setting | **1** (total: 1) |
| US | 20 (total: 361) |
| GB | 20 (total: 172) |
| FR | 20 (total: 239) |

Albania genuinely has exactly one movie in theaters per TMDB, so the app is faithfully showing one. "Now Playing" is the *only* region-sensitive list (Popular / Top Rated / Trending aren't filtered by region), which is why everything else looks full and only this one looks broken.

The region lives in `user_region` in the app's UserDefaults (set via **Settings → Region** at some point). Two ways to fix:

1. **In the app:** Settings → Region → pick United States (or wherever you actually want).
2. **I can reset it for you** right now (sets `user_region` back to `US`):
   ```
   defaults write com.scottdensmore.film-o-matic-mac user_region US
   ```
   (then relaunch the app)

Want me to run that, or will you set it in Settings? 

One product thought worth flagging separately: when a region legitimately returns 0–1 now-playing titles, the app just shows a near-empty list with no explanation. If you'd like, I could add a small "Few releases for your region — change it in Settings" hint for sparse region-filtered results — but that's a feature, not a fix, so I'll only do it if you want it.

Here's how the pieces fit: the region is set in **Settings → Region** (`SettingsForm`, region picker). Navigation to Settings differs by platform — macOS uses the sidebar (`selectedMenu = .settings`), iOS presents it as a sheet from the gear button in Movies home — but both are reachable, so a "Change region" link is doable on each.

  "new_string": "    public func endpoint() -> APIService.Endpoint {\n        switch self {\n        case .popular: return APIService.Endpoint.popular\n        case .topRated: return APIService.Endpoint.topRated\n        case .upcoming: return APIService.Endpoint.upcoming\n        case .nowPlaying: return APIService.Endpoint.nowPlaying\n        case .trending: return APIService.Endpoint.trending\n        case .genres: return APIService.Endpoint.genres\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether TMDB filters this list by the user's region. Only `nowPlaying`\n    /// and `upcoming` are region-scoped (theatrical schedules differ by\n    /// country), so their result counts can look sparse for small markets;\n    /// the other lists are global. Drives the region indicator in the UI.\n    public var isRegionFiltered: Bool {\n        switch self {\n        case .nowPlaying, .upcoming: return true\n        case .popular, .topRated, .trending, .genres: return false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// One-line caption for the region indicator shown on region-filtered\n    /// lists, e.g. \"In theaters in Albania\". `regionName` is the localized\n    /// country name (see `RegionPresentation.displayName(forRegionCode:)`).\n    public func regionCaption(regionName: String) -> String {\n        switch self {\n        case .nowPlaying:\n            return String(localized: \"In theaters in \\(regionName)\", bundle: .module,\n                          comment: \"Region indicator on the Now Playing list; argument is the country name\")\n        case .upcoming:\n            return String(localized: \"Upcoming in \\(regionName)\", bundle: .module,\n                          comment: \"Region indicator on the Upcoming list; argument is the country name\")\n        case .popular, .topRated, .trending, .genres:\n            return String(localized: \"Results for \\(regionName)\", bundle: .module,\n                          comment: \"Generic region indicator; argument is the country name\")\n        }\n    }\n}"
}

There is no `@AppStorage("user_region")` mirror anywhere, and `AppUserDefaults.region` is a plain computed property backed by `UserDefaults`. `MoviesHomeList.regionBar` reads it in `body` but has no SwiftUI observation hook for it. ## Code review — feat/movies-region-indicator

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, missing tests, CI-blocking lint)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift:48` — `AppUserDefaults.region` is not SwiftUI-observable; the `regionBar` caption will go stale after the user changes region in the presented `SettingsForm` and dismisses.**

`AppUserDefaults.region` is a plain computed property over `UserDefaults.standard` with no `@AppStorage`, `@Published`, or `@Observable` hook. SwiftUI has no mechanism to know the value changed, so `body` is not invalidated when the user picks a different country in the presented sheet and taps Save. `isRegionSettingsPresented` flipping back to `false` re-renders the *outer* VStack (the modifier is on the `VStack`, not the `regionBar`), which does trigger a new `body` call on `MoviesHomeList` because `isRegionSettingsPresented` is `@State`. So in practice the bar *does* refresh — but only because the sheet-dismiss state flip incidentally drives a re-render, not because the region value is observed. This is the exact fragility documented for `userTMDBAPIKey` in `SettingsForm.swift:45–55` (the comment explains why an `@AppStorage` mirror is required there). The same gap exists here: if the dismiss path ever changes (e.g., the sheet is dismissed without flipping `isRegionSettingsPresented` explicitly, or the bar is embedded somewhere that doesn't present a sheet), the caption will silently show the stale region. Fix: add `@AppStorage("user_region") private var displayRegion: String = AppUserDefaults.region` to `MoviesHomeList` and use `displayRegion` in `regionBar` in place of `AppUserDefaults.region`. The key `"user_region"` matches `AppUserDefaults.regionKey`.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/types/MoviesMenu.swift:66–74` and `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` — the three `regionCaption` string keys are absent from the package catalog; they will fall back to raw English at runtime, but the package won't satisfy xcodebuild's "Treat missing keys as warnings" setting and will be a gap for any future translation.**

`String(localized: "In theaters in \(regionName)", bundle: .module)` with a `String` interpoland generates the lookup key `"In theaters in %@"` (Swift's `String.LocalizationValue` represents string interpolands as `%@`). None of `"In theaters in %@"`, `"Upcoming in %@"`, or `"Results for %@"` appear in `/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`. The existing parallel — `" Try again in \(seconds) seconds."` (an `Int` interpoland) — is present in the catalog as `" Try again in %lld seconds."`. The new keys should follow the same pattern and be added to the catalog with `%@` placeholders. This won't crash (English falls through), but it breaks the clean-build-stable invariant the project document states for xcstrings files, will suppress extractable-string tooling, and is a latent bug for any future non-English locale.

Fix: add these three entries to the package's `Localizable.xcstrings`:
```json
"In theaters in %@" : {
  "comment": "Region indicator on the Now Playing list; argument is the country name"
},
"Upcoming in %@" : {
  "comment": "Region indicator on the Upcoming list; argument is the country name"
},
"Results for %@" : {
  "comment": "Generic region indicator; argument is the country name"
}
```

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/MoviesRegionTests.swift:15–22` — `regionCaptionNamesTheRegionPerList` does not test the `popular`/`topRated`/`trending`/`genres` arm of `regionCaption`, leaving the `"Results for %@"` branch uncovered; TDD requires every branch to have at least one assertion.**

The method has three branches (`.nowPlaying`, `.upcoming`, `.popular/.topRated/.trending/.genres`); only the first two are asserted. The `"Results for %@"` branch is dead code in the current UI (those menus return `isRegionFiltered == false` so `regionBar` never shows), which makes it doubly important to have a test: if someone later enables the bar for `.popular`, a misspelled key in this branch would silently produce the wrong text with no test to catch it.

Fix: add `#expect(MoviesMenu.popular.regionCaption(regionName: "Germany").contains("Germany"))` (or any non-filtered case) to `regionCaptionNamesTheRegionPerList`.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift:81–89` — `SettingsForm` is presented as a `fullScreenCover` on iOS even though iOS already has a `fullScreenCover` for `SettingsForm` on `MoviesHome`; if both `isSettingPresented` (gear button) and `isRegionSettingsPresented` (region bar) are true simultaneously, SwiftUI will have two concurrent full-screen covers on the same `NavigationStack` hierarchy, which is undefined behavior and will silently drop one.**

In `MoviesHome.swift:156–162`, a `fullScreenCover(isPresented: $isSettingPresented)` presents `SettingsForm` on the `NavigationStack`. `MoviesHomeList` is a child of that same `NavigationStack`. A user could tap the gear button (opening Settings), then somehow also trigger the "Change" button in an already-visible region bar; or, more realistically, the interaction order matters in automated tests. Two concurrent `fullScreenCover` presentations on the same view hierarchy stack is not supported and one will be silently ignored per Apple's documentation. This is a latent correctness issue. The `macOS` `.sheet` path is safe because macOS `SettingsForm` for the "Change" path is an isolated modal off `MoviesHomeList`'s `VStack`, while the gear-button path in `SplitView` doesn't use `MoviesHomeList`'s `.sheet` at all. The iOS-only gap is the simultaneous-presentation race. Fix options: (a) route "Change" to the same `isSettingPresented` binding on the parent `MoviesHome` (requires lifting state or using a callback), or (b) guard against the race by disabling the "Change" button when `isSettingPresented` is already true — but that binding isn't accessible in `MoviesHomeList`. The cleanest fix is to have `MoviesHomeList` accept an `onChangeRegion: () -> Void` closure (injected by `MoviesHome`) so the host owns the single Settings presentation, identical to how `onClose` works in `SettingsForm`.

---

### 🟡 Should fix (readability, conventions, weak tests)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift:81–89` — on macOS the "Change" button opens `SettingsForm` as a `.sheet` modal anchored to the list, but macOS Settings is already the system-standard way to reach `SettingsForm` (via the `Settings {}` scene in `MovieSwiftMacApp.swift:76–84`), and the sidebar's `OutlineMenu.settings` item renders Settings inline in the detail column. This adds a third settings surface on macOS that is visually inconsistent (modal card) and is not keyboard-accessible from the detail pane.**

The `SplitView` / `OutlineMenu.settingsList` path renders `SettingsForm` in the detail column without a modal, while the new "Change" button opens a floating sheet. On macOS the idiomatic fix is to drive the sidebar to `.settings` selection (firing `selectedMenu = .settings` via a `FocusedValue` or the existing `selectedOutlineMenu` environment binding) or navigate the user to Settings via `NSApp.sendAction(Selector("showSettingsWindow:"), ...)` for the macOS Settings scene. A floating modal sheet for region change is surprising UX on macOS. This is a "should fix" rather than must-fix because it's functional, just inconsistent.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift:43–62` — the `regionBar` has no composite `accessibilityElement` grouping; VoiceOver will read globe icon, caption text, and "Change" button as three separate focus stops with no shared label.**

The `HStack` reads as three distinct elements. Add `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` to the outer `HStack` and an explicit `.accessibilityLabel(...)` or at minimum an `.accessibilityHint("Tap Change to update your region in Settings")` on the `Button`. Without grouping, the globe `Image` gets a generic "globe" announcement that adds noise.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/MoviesRegionTests.swift:6` — none of the three `@Test` methods carry a `@Test("…")` display name or a doc comment, which is flagged by the project guideline ("missing purpose doc").**

The guideline in `CLAUDE.md` requires `@Test` methods to have a purpose doc. None of the three in `MoviesRegionTests` have one. Add display names: `@Test("nowPlaying and upcoming are the only region-filtered menus")`, etc.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Tests/MovieSwiftFluxCoreTests/MoviesRegionTests.swift:27` — `regionDisplayNameResolvesCodesAndFallsBack` asserts `"US" != "US"` but this assertion is locale-dependent: on a device configured for a locale that cannot resolve "US" (e.g., a minimal CI container), `Locale.current.localizedString(forRegionCode: "US")` could theoretically return nil, triggering the fallback to `"US"`, flipping the assertion.**

Fix: also assert that the US result contains a recognizable substring (e.g., `.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("united states")`) so the test is meaningful rather than merely not-equal-to-itself.

---

### 🟢 Nits (optional)

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift:51` — `Button("Change") { … }` uses a bare string literal; a localized `Text` or a `String(localized: "Change")` call would be more consistent with the rest of the file's use of `Text(menu.regionCaption(…))`. It won't cause a warning since the `Button` initializer doesn't require `LocalizedStringKey` on all branches, but it's inconsistent with the project's other button labels which use `LocalizedStringKey` literals.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/Packages/MovieSwiftFluxCore/Sources/MovieSwiftFluxCore/types/RegionPresentation.swift:7` — `RegionPresentation` is a `public enum` with only `static` members, following the project's namespace-via-caseless-enum pattern (same as `AccessibilityID`, `AppUserDefaults`). That's fine, but the name `RegionPresentation` is slightly ambiguous — it could mean "how a region is presented in a picker" or "a presentation that involves a region". `RegionNameFormatter` or `RegionLocalization` would be more immediately clear. Low-cost rename since it's only used in two call sites right now.

- `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/moviesHome/list/MoviesHomeList.swift:57` — `.padding(.horizontal, 16)` and `.padding(.vertical, 6)` use magic numbers. The project uses `16` in several places for horizontal content inset, but a named constant or a comment `// matches MoviesList horizontal inset` would make the intent clear.

---

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — Two correctness issues (stale `AppUserDefaults.region` read without SwiftUI observation, and the potential for two simultaneous `fullScreenCover` presentations on iOS) plus the missing xcstrings catalog entries (which break the clean-xcstrings invariant and suppress future i18n) must be resolved before this is ready to PR.

- **iOS & macOS** read their version/build from build settings via `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` / `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` in Info.plist — but those settings are **static** (version `1.0`, build `1400`), bumped by hand.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/scripts/set_build_number.sh",
  "content": "#!/bin/bash\n#\n# Stamps CFBundleVersion in the built app's Info.plist with the git commit\n# count, so every build is uniquely and monotonically numbered without anyone\n# hand-editing CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION. Run as a \"Run Script\" build phase on\n# each app target (after Info.plist processing, before code signing).\n#\n# The marketing version (CFBundleShortVersionString) is NOT touched here — that\n# stays the single, human-bumped MARKETING_VERSION build setting.\n#\n# Falls back to CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION (then 1) when git can't produce a count\n# — e.g. building from a source export, or a shallow CI checkout — so a build\n# never fails on account of versioning. (For real release builds, CI must do a\n# full clone — `fetch-depth: 0` — or the count will be the shallow depth.)\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nplist=\"${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}\"\nif [ ! -f \"$plist\" ]; then\n    echo \"warning: set_build_number: Info.plist not found at $plist; skipping\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\nbuild_number=\"\"\nif command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    build_number=\"$(git -C \"${SRCROOT}\" rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nfi\n\nif [ -z \"$build_number\" ]; then\n    build_number=\"${CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION:-1}\"\n    echo \"note: set_build_number: git unavailable; using fallback $build_number\"\nfi\n\n/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c \"Set :CFBundleVersion $build_number\" \"$plist\"\necho \"set_build_number: CFBundleVersion = $build_number\"\n"
}

## Verification — chore/auto-build-number

### Gates run

- **SwiftLint** (`./scripts/lint.sh`) — PASS
  Found 0 violations, 0 serious in 203 files.

- **package-tests** (`./scripts/ci/check_coverage.sh`, full) — PASS
  - Backend: 86.13% >= 76.10% threshold
  - MovieSwiftFluxCore: 74.34% >= 52.20% threshold
  - Flux: 90.43% >= 85.00% threshold

- **ios-tests** (build, `XCODE_ONLY_TESTING=MovieSwiftTests`, iPhone 17 Pro) — FAIL

- **ios build-only** (MovieSwift iOS target) — FAIL

- **mac build-only** (MovieSwiftMac target) — FAIL

- **tvOS build-only** (MovieSwiftTV target) — FAIL

### Failures (fix before review)

**All three app targets fail to build — the "Stamp build number from git" build phase is sandboxed out of the plist it needs to write.**

- **ios-tests / ios build / mac build / tvOS build** — `Sandbox: PlistBuddy deny(1) file-write-data …/Info.plist` at the "Stamp build number from git" shell-script build phase in all three targets (iOS, macOS, tvOS)

  - Output (iOS representative):
    ```
    error: Sandbox: PlistBuddy(79652) deny(1) file-write-data …/Debug-iphonesimulator/MovieSwift.app/Info.plist (in target 'MovieSwift' from project 'MovieSwift')
    Set: Entry, ":CFBundleVersion", Does Not Exist
    Error Opening Destination: …/Info.plist [Operation not permitted]
    ** TEST FAILED **
    ```

  - Probable cause: The project has `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES` in both Debug and Release configurations in `/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (lines 2320, 2385). The three `PBXShellScriptBuildPhase` entries for "Stamp build number from git" (UUIDs `029C63A2DFABA0751EAB09D2`, `58EF6CCE8739D0A1385056B0`, `BECB0F7F2DF94239197BAB52`) declare no `outputPaths` at all. Because Xcode's user-script sandbox only grants write access to paths listed as declared outputs, `PlistBuddy`'s attempt to write `${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}` is denied. This affects every build of every target, not just tests.

**Two fixes are needed, either together or as alternates:**

1. **Add the output path declaration** — in each of the three `PBXShellScriptBuildPhase` entries, add `$(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(INFOPLIST_PATH)` to `outputPaths`. This tells the sandbox the phase is allowed to write that file. This is the minimal fix that preserves `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES`.

2. **Or** use `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`-agnostic Xcode build setting injection instead of post-processing the built plist. The idiomatic sandbox-compatible approach is to set `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = $(shell git -C "$(SRCROOT)" rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 1)` directly in the project's build settings (the project file) and remove the shell script phase entirely. This requires no sandbox exception and works with `agvtool` / `xcodebuild` version inspection too.

### Deferred to CI

- **ios-tests-ipad** — not run; build fails before tests could run, and no Swift source changed so the suite is unaffected once the build fix lands.
- **mac-tests (full test suite)** — not run; build fails before test entry. The known macOS UI-runner finalize flake is pre-existing and separate.
- **tvos-tests (full test suite)** — not run for same reason.

### Verdict

FIX-FIRST — 4 gates failing (iOS build, macOS build, tvOS build, ios-tests); all caused by a single root defect: the "Stamp build number from git" build phases write to `${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}` without declaring it as an `outputPaths` entry, and `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES` is set project-wide. The main agent must fix this and re-verify before review.

(The git *read* works — only the write is blocked.)

The standard fix for a git-versioning build phase is to disable script sandboxing on the app targets (they run our own trusted in-repo script). I'll also declare the output path as defense-in-depth:
