Test targets keep the project-level sandbox.\n  t.build_configurations.each do |c|\n    c.build_settings[\"ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING\"] = \"NO\"\n  end\n  # Declare the output so the write is permitted even if sandboxing is later re-enabled.\n  ph = t.shell_script_build_phases.find { |p| p.name == phase_name }\n  if ph\n    ph.output_paths = [\"$(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(INFOPLIST_PATH)\"]\n    puts \"#{t.name}: sandbox NO + outputPaths set\"\n  end\nend\nproj.save\nputs \"saved.\"\n' 2>&1 | tail -6",

## Code review — chore/auto-build-number

### 🔴 Must fix (correctness, CI-blocking)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/.github/workflows/xcodebuild.yml` lines 31, 59, 100, 127, 152 — CI uses `actions/checkout@v4` with the default `fetch-depth: 1` (shallow clone), so `git rev-list --count HEAD` will return `1` on every CI run, not the real commit count.**

The script correctly documents the requirement (`fetch-depth: 0`) and the fallback exists, but the fallback path here is never triggered — git IS available on the runner, so `build_number` is successfully set to `1` on every CI build. Every CI build of every target will ship `CFBundleVersion = 1`. If a real release is ever cut from CI (the most common path), the produced `.ipa` or `.pkg` will have build number `1`, which is lower than the existing `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 1400` on the iOS target — App Store Connect will reject it with "CFBundleVersion must be higher than the previously uploaded build."

Fix: add `fetch-depth: 0` to each `actions/checkout@v4` step in `xcodebuild.yml`. All five job steps need it.

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
```

This is the single highest-priority item. The script's comment is right about the requirement; the workflow just doesn't enforce it.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` lines 2415, 2453 — iOS target `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` is `1400`; macOS and tvOS targets are `1` (added by this diff). The fallback in `set_build_number.sh` reads `${CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION:-1}`, so if git returns an empty count (source export, broken git), iOS stamps `1400` while mac/tvOS stamp `1`. This divergence is silent and produces inconsistent submitted builds.**

Since the git commit count is already 704 and will always be higher than 1 for any real working-tree build, the fallback will never fire locally; but on a source export (e.g., App Store review/notarization flow from an archive without git), mac/tvOS would stamp `1`, which would be an App Store rejection for those platforms. The safer fix is to update `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` to a value that is higher than the last shipped build for all three targets, or to set it to a uniform meaningful sentinel (e.g., `704` — the current count) so the fallback is at least consistent across targets. The underlying design intent (git count wins; this is only a dead-man's switch) is fine, but having divergent stale values waiting to bite is not.

---

### 🟡 Should fix (robustness, correctness under edge cases)

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/scripts/set_build_number.sh` line 26 — `git rev-list --count HEAD` can legitimately return the string `0` for an empty/initial repo. The `[ -z "$build_number" ]` guard on line 29 tests for empty string, not for zero, so a zero count would be accepted and stamped. App Store Connect requires `CFBundleVersion >= 1`.**

The scenario is pathological (an app shipped from an empty repo), but the guard is already there and the fix is trivial: change `[ -z "$build_number" ]` to `[ -z "$build_number" ] || [ "$build_number" -le 0 ]`. More defensively, also validate that `build_number` is a pure integer before passing it to PlistBuddy — if `rev-list` ever emits a warning line mixed with the count (which can happen if `.git` is partially corrupt), PlistBuddy will exit non-zero and `set -e` will fail the build.

Suggested guard:

```bash
if [ -z "$build_number" ] || ! [[ "$build_number" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    build_number="${CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION:-1}"
    echo "note: set_build_number: using fallback $build_number"
fi
```

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` — `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO` is set only on the three app targets; the project-level setting remains `YES` (lines 2324, 2389). The per-target override is correct and surgical — test targets keep sandbox. That's a reasonable trade-off.**

However, there is no inline comment explaining why sandboxing is disabled. Any developer (or future automated reviewer) reading the pbxproj will wonder if this is an accident or a policy decision. The pbxproj format does not support comments next to build settings, so the rationale should live in the commit message and in the script's header. The script header comment (line 5) already says "Run as a 'Run Script' build phase on each app target (after Info.plist processing, before code signing)" but does not mention the sandbox decision. Add a note such as: "Sandboxing is intentionally disabled on the three app targets so the phase can write the built Info.plist at ${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}; declaring outputPaths causes 'Multiple commands produce Info.plist' so the write happens unsandboxed."

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/scripts/set_build_number.sh` line 34 — PlistBuddy exits non-zero if `CFBundleVersion` does not already exist as a key in the plist (it will not create a new key with `Set`, only update an existing one). With `set -euo pipefail`, this immediately fails the build.**

For all three existing targets the key will always be present (either from the source plist or from Xcode's `ProcessInfoPlistFile` phase which precedes this script), so in practice this is fine. But if a future target uses `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = YES` and someone copies this phase, the key may not pre-exist in the generated plist with the expected name. A defensive fix is to use `Add` + `Set` idiom or PlistBuddy's `-x` flag. At minimum, add a comment in the script noting this assumption.

---

**`/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/movieswiftui/MovieSwift/MovieSwift.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` — Phase ordering: the Stamp phase is placed after `Resources` for tvOS/macOS, and after `Embed Frameworks` for iOS (lines 1305, 1328, 1450). This is AFTER `ProcessInfoPlistFile` (which produces the built plist in `${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}`) and BEFORE code signing (which Xcode's build system applies as an implicit post-phase step). The ordering is correct and the plist the script writes is the one that gets signed.**

This is not a problem — confirming it is fine as-is.

That key is an iOS-only key, not a tvOS key, and should not be in a tvOS Info.plist. It is a pre-existing issue, not introduced by this diff, but the tvOS Info.plist is being touched — it is worth cleaning up while the file is already open.**

Run as a \"Run Script\" build phase on\n# each app target (after Info.plist processing, before code signing).\n#\n# The marketing version (CFBundleShortVersionString) is NOT touched here — that\n# stays the single, human-bumped MARKETING_VERSION build setting.\n#\n# Sandboxing: the app targets set ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO so this\n# phase can write the built Info.plist. Declaring the plist as an outputPaths\n# entry isn't an option — it collides with Xcode's own Info.plist processing\n# (\"Multiple commands produce …/Info.plist\") — so the write happens unsandboxed.\n#\n# Falls back to CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION (then 1) when git can't produce a count\n# — e.g. building from a source export, or a shallow CI checkout — so a build\n# never fails on account of versioning. (For real release builds, CI must do a\n# full clone — `fetch-depth: 0` — or the count will be the shallow depth.)\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nplist=\"${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}\"\nif [ ! -f \"$plist\" ]; then\n    echo \"note: set_build_number: Info.plist not found at $plist; skipping\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\nbuild_number=\"\"\nif command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    build_number=\"$(git -C \"${SRCROOT}\" rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nfi\n\n# Accept only a positive integer; otherwise fall back so we never stamp a blank,\n# zero, or warning-polluted value (any of which App Store Connect rejects).\nif ! [[ \"$build_number\" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then\n    build_number=\"${CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION:-1}\"\n    echo \"note: set_build_number: git count unavailable; using fallback $build_number\"\nfi\n\n# PlistBuddy's `Set` only updates an existing key, so fall back to `Add` for the\n# (rare) case where CFBundleVersion isn't already present in the processed plist.\n/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c \"Set :CFBundleVersion $build_number\" \"$plist\" 2>/dev/null \\\n    || /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c \"Add :CFBundleVersion string $build_number\" \"$plist\"\n\necho \"note: set_build_number: CFBundleVersion = $build_number\"\n"
}

> AGENT

The undo mislabel is already clear: **every committed swipe adds to a list** (`.left→wishlist`, `.right→seenlist` — there's no pure "dismiss"), yet `performDiscoverAction` always dispatches `PopRandromDiscover`, whose reducer unconditionally sets `discoverLastDiscarded`. So the "undo last dismiss" affordance appears after an *add*, and tapping it only re-decks the card without removing it from the list. Now let me understand the "stops showing movies" (refill) side — reading `FetchRandomDiscover` and the empty-state UI:

290	    public struct FetchRandomDiscover: AsyncAction {
291	        public var filter: DiscoverFilter?
292	
293	        /// Picks the random page from a `ClosedRange<Int>` after probing
294	        /// `total_pages`. Optional override so unit tests can pin the
295	        /// pick to a known value; `nil` (default) uses
296	        /// `Int.random(in: range)`.
297	        public var randomSource: (@Sendable (ClosedRange<Int>) -> Int)?
298	
299	        public init(
300	            filter: DiscoverFilter? = nil,
301	            randomSource: (@Sendable (ClosedRange<Int>) -> Int)? = nil
302	        ) {
303	            self.filter = filter
304	            self.randomSource = randomSource
305	        }
306	
307	        /// Pure: given a TMDB `total_pages`, pick a random page in
308	        /// `[1, min(total_pages, DiscoverFilter.randomPageCeiling)]`.
309	        ///
310	        /// TMDB's `/discover/movie` returns **HTTP 400** when `page >
311	        /// total_pages` — the old `randomPage()` could pick page 15 for a
312	        /// query that only has 3 pages, which is exactly the failure mode
313	        /// `feature/native-macos-target` was hitting. The fix is to call
314	        /// this AFTER probing page 1 so we know the real ceiling.
315	        ///
316	        /// `randomSource` defaults to `Int.random(in:)`; the parameter
317	        /// exists so unit tests can pin the random pick to a known value.
318	        public static func resolveTargetPage(
319	            totalPages: Int,
320	            randomSource: (ClosedRange<Int>) -> Int = { Int.random(in: $0) }
321	        ) -> Int {
322	            // total_pages is sometimes 0 for completely-empty queries
323	            // (no films matching). In that case page=1 is still the
324	            // valid request — TMDB returns an empty list for page=1
325	            // but 400 for any other page.
326	            let ceiling = min(max(totalPages, 1), DiscoverFilter.randomPageCeiling)
327	            return randomSource(1...ceiling)
328	        }
329	
330	        public func execute(state: FluxState?, dispatch: @escaping DispatchFunction) {
331	            let resolvedFilter = self.filter ?? DiscoverFilter.randomFilter()
332	            let key = LoadingKey.randomDiscover
333	
334	            // Phase 1 — probe with `page=1` to learn total_pages.
335	            //
336	            // We DON'T use `makeTrackedHandler` here because that helper
337	            // dispatches `SetLoadingState(nil)` on success — but on the
338	            // success branch of phase 1 we may still need to fire phase 2.
339	            // Clearing the loading state between phases would briefly
340	            // unblock the UI and look like a flicker. Instead we set
341	            // `.loading` once up-front and clear it only at the end of
342	            // whichever phase produces the final data action.
343	            dispatch(MoviesActions.SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .loading))
344	
345	            APIService.shared.GET(endpoint: .discover,
346	                                  params: resolvedFilter.toParams(page: 1)) { (probeResult: Result<PaginatedResponse<Movie>, APIService.APIError>) in
347	                switch probeResult {
348	                case .failure(let error):
349	                    let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: error)
350	                    dispatch(MoviesActions.SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .failed(failure)))
351	
352	                case .success(let probe):
353	                    let probeTotalPages = probe.totalPages ?? 1
354	                    let targetPage: Int
355	                    if let randomSource = self.randomSource {
356	                        targetPage = FetchRandomDiscover.resolveTargetPage(
357	                            totalPages: probeTotalPages,
358	                            randomSource: randomSource
359	                        )
360	                    } else {
361	                        targetPage = FetchRandomDiscover.resolveTargetPage(totalPages: probeTotalPages)
362	                    }
363	                    if targetPage == 1 {
364	                        // We already have page-1's data; don't waste a request.
365	                        dispatch(MoviesActions.SetLoadingState(key: key, state: nil))
366	                        dispatch(SetRandomDiscover(filter: resolvedFilter, response: probe))
367	                        return
368	                    }
369	
370	                    // Phase 2 — actually fetch the random page now that we know it's in range.
371	                    APIService.shared.GET(endpoint: .discover,
372	                                          params: resolvedFilter.toParams(page: targetPage)) { (result: Result<PaginatedResponse<Movie>, APIService.APIError>) in
373	                        switch result {
374	                        case .failure(let error):
375	                            let failure = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.failure(from: error)
376	                            dispatch(MoviesActions.SetLoadingState(key: key, state: .failed(failure)))
377	                        case .success(let response):
378	                            dispatch(MoviesActions.SetLoadingState(key: key, state: nil))
379	                            dispatch(SetRandomDiscover(filter: resolvedFilter, response: response))
380	                        }
381	                    }
382	                }
383	            }
384	        }

> AGENT

Found both root causes. The "undo last dismiss" text is literally at [DiscoverView.swift:659](MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/discover/DiscoverView.swift:659) (the macOS undo button — you're on macOS). Here's the full diagnosis:

**1. "Stops showing movies" — no auto-refill when the deck empties.** The deck refills (`fetchRandomMovies`) only *as a side effect of a swipe* (and once on appear). When the deck reaches empty — which can happen if you swipe faster than the async refetch, or a refetch hiccups — `currentMovie` is `nil`, the empty state shows, and **nothing auto-refetches**. You're stuck until you manually tap "Refill discover."

**2. The "undo" is mislabeled *and* semantically broken.** Every committed swipe *adds* to a list (`left→wishlist`, `right→seenlist`) — there is no "dismiss." But the reducer's `PopRandromDiscover` unconditionally records `discoverLastDiscarded`, so the undo button appears after *any* swipe, labeled **"Undo last dismiss."** Worse, tapping it (`PushRandomDiscover`) only puts the card back in the deck — it does **not** remove the movie from the wishlist/seenlist you just added it to. So it's a half-undo with a wrong name.

The auto-refill fix is unambiguous (I'll do it). For the undo, there are a few valid product directions and it's your call:

No-op while a fetch has most recently failed (the error\n    /// banner offers a manual retry instead) — avoids a tight refetch loop.\n    private func autoRefillIfEmpty(props: Props) {\n        guard props.movies.isEmpty, props.loadingFailure == nil else { return }\n        fetchRandomMovies(props: props, force: true, filter: props.filter)\n    }"

I've implemented both fixes and the verifier is running in the background. Quick recap while it checks:

**Diagnosis (you're on macOS):**
- **"Stops showing movies"** — when the deck empties, the macOS empty state showed *only* the undo button with no refill and no auto-fetch ([DiscoverView.swift:564](MovieSwift/MovieSwift/views/components/discover/DiscoverView.swift)), so it got stuck.
- **"Undo last dismiss" after seenlist** — every swipe adds to a list, but the pop unconditionally recorded an undo labeled "dismiss," and tapping it only re-decked the card without removing it from the list.

**Fixes:**
- **Auto-refill** when the deck empties (`.onChange(of: movies.isEmpty)` on both platforms, backing off while a fetch error is showing), and the macOS empty state now shows progress instead of just an undo button.
- **True undo**: tracks where each card went (`DiscoverSwipe{movie, wishlist/seenlist/skip}`); undo now removes the movie from that list *and* re-decks it, relabeled **"Undo last swipe."**

Followed TDD on the package layer (reducer + the `undoRemoval` mapping — already green via `swift test`), macOS build + `DiscoverTests` passed. The verifier is now doing the full all-platform + lint + test sweep; I'll report its verdict, run the code-reviewer, and take it through CI → merge.

61	        case missingAPIKey
62	        case server          // 5xx
63	        case unauthorized    // 401
64	        case forbidden       // 403
65	        case decode
66	        case other
67	    }
68	
69	    public let kind: Kind
70	    public let message: String
71	    public let retryActionTitle: String
72	
73	    public init(kind: Kind,
74	         message: String,
75	         retryActionTitle: String = MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter.defaultRetryActionTitle) {
76	        self.kind = kind
77	        self.message = message
78	        self.retryActionTitle = retryActionTitle
79	    }
80	}

> AGENT

CI watcher running on [PR #61](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/61). Summary of the Discover fix:

**Both bugs root-caused and fixed:**
- **"Stops showing movies"** — the deck had no auto-refill; on macOS the empty state showed *only* the undo button. Now it auto-refetches when empty (with a failure/smoke guard so it never tight-loops), and shows progress while refilling.
- **"Undo last dismiss" after seenlist** — every swipe adds to a list, but the undo was mislabeled and only re-decked the card. Now it's a **true undo**: it tracks where each card went and reverses the whole swipe (removes from the list + re-decks), relabeled **"Undo last swipe."**

Full pipeline: TDD on the package layer, verifier (caught swiftformat churn → cleaned up to minimal diffs), code-reviewer FIX-FIRST (pop-by-id robustness + extracted/tested the auto-refill guard) → all addressed and re-verified. I'll merge once CI is green and report.
